It is one of only two three-dimensional copies of the painting, along with another in Lombardy.

Reperti dal Neolithico all'età romana di Santadi e del basso Sulcis: microliti e ceramica cardiali di Cirixì, materiali del vivoli di S'Arriorgiu, Is Solinas e Sant'Anna, della necropoli di Montessu, il deposito votive nuragico della grotto Pirosu-Su Benatzu, dove una stalagmite servizio di altare e venre trovare circa 2.000 articoli in metallo, e gli escovi della forzza Phoenicio-punica di Pani Loriga. Along the only road of the village there are villas and palaces of the XVII-XIX century, the Town Hall and the Market Square with the old cereal warehouses. Among the villas, loved by intellectuals and writers, Villa Find yourself by actress Marta Abba, who called it as the comedy dedicated by Pirandello, then center Pirandelli's studies; from the ridge glimpses among the most beautiful of the Pisan Hills.

Country of red trachyte on the shore of the Tirso, the ancient Forum Traiani, where the hot springs feed the Roman baths of Aquae Ypsitanae, the most important of Sardinia; in the village the Aragonese late-Gothic house and the parish of San Pietro, a short distance from the Romanesque San Lussorio with the paleo-Christian crypt.

A collection that traces three centuries of textile culture in Europe: it is indicated as the world's largest collection of hand-printing blocks on fabric, wood and metal, catalogued and sorted according to style criteria.

Collegiate defined by Lombardy Cultural Heritage as one of the greatest achievements of the first European Romanesque architecture: built between 1025 and 1040 on the remains of a Longobard building, when the Palatine counts of Pavia settled in the castle. Latin cross plan with three naves with protruding transept and three apses, about 60 metres long and 19 metres wide, with alternating pillars and arches; facade and first spans collapsed in the unknown era and the bell tower was rebuilt in the nineteenth century. Behind the altar a staircase descends to the crypt with remains of a previous building; the tradition preserves relics of the Holy Cross donated by Guglielmo de Grossis, who died in Lomello in 1370.

Housed in the former church of Suffragio, it is dedicated to the works of the Petriolese sculptor Diego De Minicis.

Borgo at 514 meters on the Cosentine Tyrrhenian founded by Waldenses from the Piedmont valleys, the only center of Calabria where the Occitan language survives: the Blood Gate recalls the massacre of the Waldenses of 1561, the Museum of peasant civilization keeps Occitan clothes and on the coast there are partly the Luigiane Thermal Baths.

Villa Garnier, the architect's residence, and the buildings he designed: Villa Etelinda, Villa Studio, the church of Terrasanta and Palazzo Garnier, now Town Hall.

Municipality at the southern entrance of the Trompia Valley, birthplace of Pope Paul VI (John Baptist Montini, born here on 26 September 1897): to visit the birthplace and the Paul VI Collection of contemporary art, with about seven thousand works of twentieth century, in addition to the churches of the village of San Vigilio.

Borgo dei Monti Iblei at 820 meters, the highest and coldest municipality in the province of Syracuse: the remains of the Norman castle on Monte Castello, the scenic staircase of Sant'Antonio Abate, the Neviere del Monte Lauro and the gorges of the Stretta.

The thermal plant is still in operation, already active in Roman times: the remains of the ancient complex are located under the current building. It takes its name from the Bourbon general Nunziante who restored it and rises between the rock of Oncino and the volcanic sandy beach of Marina del Sole.

Neo-Romanesque church in a slightly raised position on the road, perhaps born as a chapel in the last quarter of the thirteenth century: the fourteenth-century church remains a part, the medieval tower became bell tower presumably in 1448 and the building was rebuilt in 1900-1901 and consecrated in 1911. In the sails of the working chapel is preserved the cycle of frescoes of 1518 by Gian Paolo Thanner, with Father Eternal blessing, Madonna with Child and Saints, Doctors of the Church and Saint Virgins.

At 670 meters, the villages Ruša and Dolina preserve the historical rural architecture and, between 1993 and 1998, the artists of the association \ Stories from the Lingobards have left works in the villages, even on the seven fountains. The church of San Floriano has an altar of the Madonna of 1777, a work of the Resurrection and a miniature Way of the Cross; from the square of the church opens the view of the valley.

In the House of the Captain (Sale del Capitano) of the Rocchetta, exhibits the collection of the ornithologist Gustavo Adolfo Carlotto with over 700 birds. The entrance is included in the Rocca ticket.

Town of the plain south of Turin linked to hemp and ropes for ships: the thirteenth-century castle today town hall, the palaces of the center, the Cistercian abbey of Casanova and small civic museums, from naval to natural history.

Baroque church with a single nave, probably from the seventeenth century (attested in 1674), in a dominant position in the center of the ancient village of Sciglio on the homonymous stream; originally dedicated to the Most Holy Savior, from the eighteenth century venerates the medical saints Cosma and Damiano. Portale in pietra rosacea del 1758, bell tower of the twentieth century, monumental altar of the sixties.

An easy 3.3 km route (200 m of altitude difference, 1-3 hours) from Punta di Migiandone on a mule track with galleries in the rock, trenches and machine guns stations, to the Fort of Bara (410 m), with cannons and mortars and a plaque on the Battle of Ornavasso in October 1944; view of Lake Maggiore, Mergozzo and the Corni di Nibbio, and continue to the marble quarry.

In the historic center you can visit the house of "Concetta" not me the trust, the house of craftsmanship, the shop of the blacksmith-maniscalco and the ancient straw oven, still working and used in events and recurrences for bread with yeast mother and flour ground at the old mill.

Designed by Giovan Battista Casasopra, pupil of Vittone, built in 1753-1759 and consecrated in 1764: baroque, with a single nave with three chapels connecting on the side and brick facade marked by pilasters and columns. Inside the relics of Santa Giustina on the main altar, frescoes of the vault of Luigi and Rodolfo Morgari (1853 and 1858), organ of 1866 and altarpieces attributed to Antonio Sariga and workshop.

Romanesque church on Piazza Cavour, rebuilt in the 17th century together with a wing of the Monastery of the Visitation, with facade of the 16th century and bell tower of the 11th modified in the 16th century; the Renaissance interior preserves a crucifix of the 15th century. Next to it, the small church of the monastery has 18th century decorations.

Municipality of Alto Mantovano, ancient feud of the Ippoliti with wide autonomy also under the Gonzaga and right to beat coin: Villa Ippoliti has been home to since 1980 the MAM, a museum of modern and contemporary art dedicated to Mantua art and Lombard Chiarismo, and in the village remain the sixteenth-century Palazzo Ippoliti, today seat of the Municipality, and the Palazzo Pigozzi or Pretorio.

On the ground floor of the Park's headquarters, the exhibition   ...The fauna of the Park, opened on May 24, 2008 and renewed over time, is divided into four sections with interactive and multimedia path, the interactive floor ...Sensitive Floor and walls painted by Mario Alimede. Open all year round on weekends (10-12 and 14-17/18.30) and every day from the end of July to the beginning of September and at the end of the year.
It houses an important collection of birds in the pine forest of Candleto, just outside the walls, and is part of an itinerary along with the Oasis of Candleto.
Cable car from Entrèves (1300 m) to the Pavillon du Mont Fréty (2173 m) and Punta Helbronner (3466 m), to the Mont Blanc glaciers.

Rebuilt in 1752-56 on a church mentioned in the 13th century, it preserves the main altar of the workshop of the Fantoni di Rovetta (1767), organ case and cantoria of Grazioso Fantoni (1684), a pulpit of the Fantonian supported by three telamons, canvases by Domenico Carpinoni and Antonio Cifrondi and a altarpiece by Pietro Vecchia; the local stone bell tower was finished in 1786 on a design by Camillo Zigliani.

In the historic centre next to the church of Sant'Ippolito, in the nineteenth-century former town hall, wanted by Monsignor Bellando in 1953: on two mobile floors, domestic objects, sacred art and religious antiquities, working tools, photographs and a small collection of local stones.

It rises on a hill overlooking the Serra d'Ivrea, according to the tradition on the ruins of a temple to the sun god; certain news started from the fourteenth century, was consecrated in 1545, assumed rustic Gothic forms in the sixteenth century and was expanded in 1700. Romanesque façade with pronaos on two columns and frescoes of San Michele; single nave interior with nine altars, 16th century paintings, Baroque presbytery and organ Bossi and Squarcina.

It preserves the original urban layout, with narrow alleys, steps and houses that seem to merge with the rock; in Via Bocchetti the Palaces Pelosi and Spirit have artistic portals and along the alleys a rock in the shape of an elephant, shaped by the wind, is set in a house. From the village the view extends over the wheat fields to the sea of Manfredonia.
Indicated as the first in Europe, it is a museum spread in the historic center that tells the geology of the territory.

Founded in 2003 in the town hall, it tells the geological history of south-western Umbria with marine fossils of the Pleistocene (whale remains, shark teeth, molluscs, sea urchins and corals) and geological and botanical finds of the territory; it also organizes thematic excursions.

The medieval nucleus of the 11th century was surrounded by walls with three doors (via Bonifanti, via Pampanara, via Orologio) closed at night against pirate and Saracen raids: alleys and stone stairs, houses almost overhanging the rock and portals carved by local chisels. The Clock Tower, built by local workers, housed the civic clock; in the rest of the historic center, the portal of Via Giardino, the external stairs and the ancient fountain bas-relief of Vico Vignale.

Erected in 1763 by the will of the Dukes Notarbartolo, founders of the village, it has a monumental eighteenth-century façade on a large staircase, brought back to the original stone with the restoration of 1985. The interior with a single nave, with eighteenth-century stuccoes, preserves canvases from the eighteenth century, an eighteenth-century organ and, at the high altar, the Assumption of the Virgin by Raimondo Bufera di San Cataldo (1842).

In the upper part of the village, between the end of the 12th and the beginning of the 13th century: medieval remains the bell tower, the rest was rebuilt in the 18th century, with two Renaissance portals.

Borgo that appears in 1503 in the Carta della Toscana Marittima di Leonardo da Vinci, among the hilly vineyards of the Strada del Vino della Costa Etrusca (Sangiovese and Trebbiano, with Syrah, Merlot and Vermentino); in September it hosts  "September of...wine" with tastings in the cellars.
Medieval frescoes in an ancient church.

Built around 1134 under Gonario I di Torres on a granite peak about 650 meters away, visible from afar: triple walls in U, central square tower of about 15-16 meters in limestone with red volcanic stone cantonals, a large cistern turned and an underground environment. He died there in 1259 Adelasia di Torres, whose ghost according to the tradition wanders over the towers in full moon nights; passed to the Dorias, the Arboreas and the Aragonese, resisted in 1478 to a siege of more than a year and in 1516 was still in good condition, then decayed. The guided tour of the castle follows the tour of the museum.
A mill frescoed in a mountain village.

Byzantine church built around the middle of the 6th century on a section of the Phoenician- Punic necropolis of Tharros, cross-shaped inscribed with dome on constant-polite plumes of influence, enlarged to three naves in the 11th century; masonry in sandstone blocks of recovery. Free entrance.
The neoclassical codognese, today the place of exhibitions.

Medieval village of the Parma Apennines at 852 meters, the last stop of the Via Francigena in Emilia before the Cisa pass: the Romanesque Cathedral of San Moderanno with its treasure, the ruins of the fortress, the stone village of Corchia with the museum of the painter Martino Jasoni.

At the gates of Mantua, on the banks of the Mincio, the village of Grazie houses the Gothic-Lombard Sanctuary of the Blessed Virgin of Graces (1399-1406), famous for the crocodile hanging at the time and for the National Meeting of the Madonnas of Ferragosto; around, the Mincio Valleys and the places of the battle of Curtatone and Montanara of 1848.
Works of Palma il Giovane and a choir carved in a parish of the Bassa.
The fortress of Frederick II with views of the Euganean Hills.
Military cemetery of the First World War that guards the remains of 14,550 Austro-Hungarian soldiers who fell in this area.

The centre of Salento was built on an ancient Messapian city, of which the megalithic walls (IV-III century BC) and numerous menhirs remain; in the village the Prince's Palace with the Museum of Borgo Terra, the Byzantine church of Santa Marina with the oldest cycle of St. Nicholas and the Baroque churches of the Annunziata and the Immaculate.
A stone's throw from the station.

Oligocene gorge (about 37-26 million years ago) about 4 km long between Persi and Pertuso, on the border with Cantalupo Ligure: a canyon a hundred meters deep and about ten wide, crossed by the Borbera stream. Woods of chestnuts and oaks in the initial section, bare rocks in the final one; deer, deer, birds of prey, blackbird and martin fisherman are seen. From the SP 140 there are many paths to the gorge; the view from above is from Monteggio, and other paths lead to the abandoned villages of Rivarossa and Avi.

It was mentioned already in 1289, and was rebuilt and enlarged in 1667-1670 by the School of the Holy Rosary; façade completed in 1816 by Antonio Marchetti, with the stone statue of the Madonna of about four tons placed in 1873. Inside the fifteen Mysteries of the Flemish Rosary, the main altar in inlaid marble by Angelo Ogna (1707), the frescoes of the choir of Agostino Avanzati and Alessandro Sampilli and a fresco in the left nave.
A walk on the bed between poplar and willow.

Porta della Valle Grana, the land of Castelmagno DOP and the garlic of Caraglio garrison Slow Food; it houses the Red Filatoio of 1676-1678, one of the oldest examples of industrial archaeology in Europe, a medieval historic centre and the sanctuary on the site of the ancient castle.
For the paintings by Giulio Campi and Genovesino.

15th century palace (1443 according to the most beautiful villages and in-lombardia.it, 1456 second italia.it), residence of the Buccelleni, then of the Ginami and the Milesi, today seat of the Municipality: double loggia, Renaissance halls, 17th century frescoes and facade in grey marble of Ardesio. It hosts the MAP, with punches from the families of swordmen Chessers and Ginami and alabards, swords, knives, daggers and Ronconi from the 15th to the 17th century, and the archive with ancient parchments.

Built almost certainly at the end of the ninth century and several times renewed, it has a hut façade and side aisles sloping. Bishop Angelo Mazziotta had it restored in 1445 and is portrayed in the marble sculpture of the sleeping bishop next to the door of the sacristy, enlarged by Fabio Maranta at the end of the sixteenth century; Bishop Gennaro Danza endowed it with the high altar.
Clear sea, islets within reach and a legend of love.

In the village the parish church of San Martino, enlarged between the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, the Oratory of the Battuti and the Oratory of San Sebastiano; near the cemetery the church of Santa Caterina, built in 1653, to thank the saint of protection during an enemy attack.

The village preserves the feudal system collected around the castle, with circular plan with two or three walls still visible; remain a tower and a stretch of the ancient walls. A legend links the castle to the Templars and the Holy Grail.
Village with castle of the X century and some of the most important Etruscan tombs in Tuscany, including the Tomb of the Infernal Quadriga discovered in 2003.

From the village you can climb to the beech and fir woods of Amiata, ideal for trekking and walks; surroundings with the Benedictine churches of Santa Lucia, San Biagio and Santa Flora in Noceto and the ruins of the convent of San Processo.
The parish church on the castle square.
Stairs and passages covered by one of the oldest centers of Tirreno Cosentino.

Urban-rustic villa of Augustan age, at the Lagarian path of the Via Claudia Augusta, discovered during the construction of a childhood school: the urban pars with representative rooms, living rooms and spas decorated with frescoes and mosaics, and the rustic pars for the production activities. The first excavation was conducted in 1973 by Adriano Rigotti; many finds are exhibited at the Museo civico di Rovereto. Accessible to people with motor disabilities.

Castello della Vallesina at about 388 meters, Verdicchio's land: walls of 1509 by Albertino di Giacomo da Cremona, the Clock Tower with the clock of Pietro Mei of 1849, the 19th-century Municipal Theatre that houses the Museum of Mail Art, the only Italian public museum dedicated to this art form, and the Collegiata with the organ Vici of 1776.
A Lombard masterpiece.

Established in 1996 in the deconsecrated chapel of Santa Maria la Scala, it tells the story of Polla through the popular women's clothing between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, with thirteen reconstructions of clothes ordered for occasion (gala and parties, daily use, processions, half party, mourning), from the gala dress of the married woman to the ...suttanèlla, in 2009 the Campania Region recognized it as a museum of regional interest. Visit by reservation, about 45 minutes.

Walk along the lake overlooking Lake Maggiore and the Varesotto lakes; from the public beach you can rent sailing and motor boats. In Belgirate, the Regate Company, founded in 1858 and designated as the first yacht club in Italy, has its headquarters, with historical regattas every year. Free parking; you arrive by train, bus or boat.

In Romanesque-Gothic style, originally called the Church of the Girone, stands on top of the terraces of the village and preserves a bell of 1310; the Franciscan convent, documented since 1549, was suppressed in 1810 and the Municipality bought the church in 1858. Today it is used as an auditorium.

Church perhaps of the XII-XIII century, documented in 1337, consecrated in 1726 and remodelled in neo-Romanic forms in 1855 and 1928, when a fresco of 1421 emerged; it preserves a Madonna with the Child by Claudio Ridolfi (1605), an Immaculate with Saints of G. Pandolfi (1615), a shovel attributed to the Barocci school and the relics of Blessed Publicia.

In the castle, it gathers materials from the Bronze Age to the Middle Ages, with particular attention to the Messapic finds of the settlements of Muro Lieutenant and Muro Maurizio and an important collection of Greek and Roman coins. Admission fee.

Oasis in the Ernici Mountains, it is a karst ghost lake: it was formed in 1800 when debris blocked a swallower, and disappears and reappears depending on whether the debris dissolve or reaccumulate.

Opened in October 2006 in the Franciscan monastery of the 13th century. The Sala Carlo Crivelli exhibits the surviving parts (central register and cusps) of the polyptych painted shortly after 1470 for the church of San Francesco; the Museo Adolfo De Carolis collects about five hundred works of the painter born here (1874-1928), including the oil sketches for the frescoes of the Palazzo del Podestà of Bologna and the xilographies for the Fioretti. The itinerary is completed by Giancarlo Basili's Scenographic Documentation Centre, the Museum of Rural Civilization and the collection of engravings by Domenico Cantatore. It adheres to the Marche Museums Charter.

Borgo del Parco Nazionale della Sila known for the hand weaving of blankets and tapestries and for the ancient silver mines; in the center the Matrice Church with the Norman Bell Tower, the carved stone portals and the Museum of the Silano Craftsmanship in the former Franciscan monastery.
The whole cycle of Friulian wine, from the vineyard to the tavern.

Between the parish church of San Martino and the fortress opens the maze of alleys of the 'borghi', the most prestigious neighborhoods of the ancient Legnago and still today the most characteristic part; in front of the fortress, Piazza della Libertà hosted in the fifteenth century the weekly market, while Piazza San Martino was the area of shops and empori, with the monument to the fallen Rationalist of 1937. The old city was destroyed by the bombings of World War II for about 70%.

Six thousand years of history on a rock on the sea.
The best look on Tolmezzo.
Church and convent of the Dominican friars, founded in 1561; the church, work of Giovanni Tarantino dated 1583, rises at the northern edge of the village.

Cervara is an access to the Regional Natural Park of the Simbruini Mountains, 30,000 hectares, the largest protected area of Lazio, with paths that can be travelled all year round for excursions, mountain bikes and horse riding. The Campaeglio plateau, on the border with Abruzzo, offers in winter cross-country skiing and dog-drawn sleds; Ennio Morricone sought inspiration for over thirty years and in the small cemetery is buried the documentary writer Marino Bruno Vailati.
House with the appearance of a human face that, according to tradition, keeps away spirits and negative influences.
A place of city devotion.
Two red iron carriages in Art Nouveau style, never replaced since 1896, which go up to the castle of Montecatini Alto.

The center grew around the fortified nucleus, with houses in limestone, medieval arches and narrow alleys, and is crossed by the Tratturo Pescasseroli-Candela. Among the residences, the seventeenth-century Palazzo Maraviglia with wooden portal of local manufacture and family coat of arms, and the Palaces Gallo, Caracciolo, Bruno and de Matteis, the latter with a Gothic monophora.
access to the ruins forbidden for safety, visit only from outside; rain, snow or strong wind can limit it
Highest point of the Tonezza plateau, you can reach Passo della Vena for an ancient mule track restored by the Alps; on top a stone base carries a plaque with the names of the 27 visible peaks.
Perfect with the kids.
In the hamlet of Ciareina the Clarea stream fed five mills, still visible and partly preserved, in a wild environment with pools between polished rocks.
The walled hamlet I struggle with its doors.
The civic building of the new city.

12th century cathedral in Piazza Duomo, in the area of the old port, which can be reached by passing under the arches of Via Cathedral. Only the apse retains the original Romanesque system: the rest was largely renovated in Baroque style in the eighteenth century. The best preserved part is the crypt, remained as it was, supported by 10 columns with unusual Roman capitals and 12 pillars that protrude from the perimeter walls; the church preserves the Byzantine icon of the Madonna of Corsignano.
A wild glimpse within walking distance of the village.
The highest viewpoint on the Aniene valley.

From the village a path of about half an hour crosses the chestnut groves and goes up the course of Lambro up to the Menaresta, its source: a natural siphon from which the water flows at intervals. Going up the slope in front, with the entrance hidden by a rock, you will find the Bocc de Pegur, a series of caves communicating with stalagmites.
The Mandelli castle with its four towers.
The ancient defensive outpost on the opposite side of the village; in the Collegiate Church of St. Nicholas a travertine source of 1563.
The building of the late VII or VIII century believed for centuries the palace depicted in the mosaics of St. Apollinare Nuovo; its function is still discussed.
The oldest church in Ussita, of Romanesque origin, consecrated in 1093.
the MiC tab indicates visits on request (tel. 0824 64441) and only partial opening of sections

City of bricks on the hills of the residences, among the most beautiful villages in Italy: the Cathedral known from 868 with the Romanesque crypt, churches and palaces between Renaissance and Baroque and, just outside, the Reserve of Lake Penne, the first WWF oasis of Italy.
The Romanesque in the hills of the Versa valley.
White and pink Gothic.
The Panormite Assumption in the main church.
The mother church of the valley, with the bell tower of 1026.
The valley by bike on the old railway.
The eighteenth-century fortress that looks at the rada.
The traditional costume of the women of Polla.
The walls of the State of the Presidians.

A tourist trail climbs to the top of Monte San Giovanni, where the church and hermitage of San Giovanni in Fistola remain (first half of the 11th century), built on a pre-existing Roman temple dedicated to Giove Pollente.
A walk under the walls of the Fortress.

Small museum in a former shepherd's shelter inside the oasis: stuffed animals of the Sardinian fauna (sardinian deer, deer, wild boar, wild cat, marten, weasel, imperial raven, owl, barbagianni, Sardinian pernice) and a royal eagle in a forest diorama, with a collection of minerals and fossils. Outside there is a charcoal mill and a traditional hut (pinnettu); wild boars, deer and deer used to man are often gathered around the museum. Open every day, October-April 8-16, May-September 8-20; guided tours, numerous groups by reservation.
The fauna of the Friulian Dolomites, to be touched and listened to.
Listing in extension: the guide covers 36 of the 57 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
The view of the Sibillini from the village.
Baroque salons and park in the center of the village.

Baroque panoramic terrace of the early nineteenth century, once known as Tunnu, with wrought iron railings and benches, overlooking the plain of Gela and the Maroglio valley; below opens the avenue with steps dedicated to Angelo D'Arrigo.
Along Via Vannucci, it preserves the Adoration of the Magi del Perugino (1504).

Typical dish are the "cuzzi co' j'ajju" (cuzzi), fresh pasta made by hand with garlic, oil, tomato, chili pepper and local pecorino. In mid-July, the festival de Â Ju SalavaticuÂ, a large round pancake of water, flour, salt and Roman mint, reminds the women who brought it into the baskets to the workers of the fields.
Sea and memory of the landing.
The stone worked between Byzantines and Normans.

In the Borgo del Maglio, on two floors, exhibits the private collection of the antiques Pietro Malossi and works by the engraver Francesco Medici: weapons, furniture, prints, paintings, ancient books, coins and sculptures, with information panels and audioguides. In the village also parking, bar and hostel.

The museum has two sections: a bibliographical, with a historical archive on the island's maritime tradition, and a dedicated to the ex-vote and religious tradition linked to the sea. Open Monday to Saturday 9-13, Sunday closed, without reservation.

Built before 1250 and loved by the Archimanders, it has Gothic-sic portals, a nave partly rebuilt in Baroque style, works of art, noble tombs and frescoes; traditionally converts climbed down its seven steps before baptism.
The high mountain of the Great Paradise.
The rascards.
The oldest painting of the abbey.
Franciscan complex founded in 1500 next to the church of Santa Maria delle Grazie, which preserves carved wooden altars, a 17th century ciborium and a candelabra.

Opened on May 16, 1999 in the medieval tower of Sant'Agnese and in a small adjacent building: stone and metal materials coming largely from the Museo concordiese, and on the top floor manuscripts, prints and photographs of the Portogruaro between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries; it also exhibits two tombstones of the Jewish cemetery. Open Thursday, Saturday and Sunday 10-12; not accessible to people with motor disabilities.
City of the four districts around Piazza del Plebiscito, seat of the Eucharistic Miracle: Santa Maria Maggiore, the Cathedral on the Diocletian Bridge and the Montanare Towers.

Remains of the hexagonal fortress designed in the sixteenth century by Michele Sanmicheli, with thick walls, terrapies, moat and esplanade; the works began in 1525 and lasted about seventy years. After the Unity, the walls were largely demolished from 1887 onwards: only a few stretches remain here and along Via Leopardi.
Baroque intervention of the seventeenth century on an existing structure; the main altar of 1717 is in polychrome marble with inlays.

Documented from 1396, next to the Casa Corazza, it preserves a wooden altar of the eighteenth century and a fresco of the late fourteenth century with three saints, of which it is recognized only St. Bartholomew.
The historic heart of Belluno.

In the Civic Library "Faustino Dalmazzo" is the permanent exhibition "Faustino Dalmazzo" held by the Committee of Memory (born in 2005 in the association "Centallo Viva"), dedicated to the Italian Military Interiors, including the archpriest Don Giuseppe Barbero, a former military chaplain in the Second World War. The Committee shall indicate its opening to the public on Monday 10-12 and 17-19 and Friday 17-19 (tel. OJ L 338, 878, 2475).
The Romanesque portal.
The only sulphur water in Trentino.
Outdoor thermal baths near the city.
The Renaissance cycle of Tamagi.

It is the oldest part, with white stone houses and narrow alleys; the Costarella, a staircase that fishermen used to go down to the port, connects the village to the beaches. There are the Town Hall, in a building of 1773 already summer residence of the bishops of Ancona, a seventeenth-century fountain with five cinnamons fed by a conduit of the ancient Roman aqueduct and the gardens of Piazza Nova, with views of the limestone massif of Conero.
Fraction with particularly well preserved medieval characteristics; along the Arno, in the area, the Nature Reserve Bridge in Buriano and Penna.
The art of torred coral.
Late-Doroma church with restored apse, military bulwark and place of faith.
Fortress built by the Genoese in the 12th century to defend the village.

An isolated nineteenth-century parish church along the road to Concordia and Mirandola; it preserves a marble slab of 12th century ambo with Christ Pantocrator and symbols of the Evangelists. Behind it the villa of the Roses (now Vecchi), also nineteenth century, with a large agricultural courtyard.

A wet area among the volcanic lakes of the Park of Bracciano-Martignano, shelter of water birds loved by birdwatcher (cormorans, royal germans, folagues), near the small crater of the Lagusiello. The park, established in 1999, has trails for all levels.
Sacred silver and finds from prehistory to Normans.
The villa with a view of Rome.
Conventual complex of Norman age not far from the historic center.

From Piazza Vittorio Emanuele, with the fusiform fountain decorated with masks, the arch \"by Ciuchini" introduces to the village: noble palaces including the house of Horatio Romano, accountant of the Farnese, the church of San Michele Arcangelo (probably already existing in 1118), the remains of San Giovanni Decollato, Palazzo Galeotti with a medieval cistern, the church of San Filippo Neri (consecrated in 1718) on the ground floor of Palazzo Farnese and San Rocco, erected by survivors of the plague.
The cycle of Garavaglia on the saints patrons.
The Madonna del Cardellino by Stefano da Putignano.

Square tower of the defensive system of Mura, erected around the IX-X century in front of the Castle to guard the ancient Roman bridge on the Oglio; it was the head of the Bergamo fortifications on the river, with fortified door, wall and moat, at the climax in the first thirteenth century. After the peace of Mura in 1192 it lost importance, it was abandoned in the second fifteenth century and in the seventeenth century it became bell tower with bell cell and large clock; it preserves the original spiral staircase in stone of Sarnico. The outdoor area is freely accessible.
The center of the modern city.
Figurate shelves and wrought iron.
The ancient heart of the country.

Borgo della bassa Vallagarina among vineyards and olive groves, known for its wine and oil, dominated by the Castello di Sabbionara, well of the FAI with frescoes from the Veronese school; in the village the Baroque parish church, the district with decorated portals that climb to the Pieve Vecchia and the House of the Vicar with Roman finds.
The sanctuary where the nuragics carried their bronze.
The neoclassical castle on top of the village.
Plenty of water flowing at the foot of the mountain, in a basin with a small artificial pond: here the stream that gives the name to the valley is born.
The Spanish fort.

The village of Valle Po at the foot of Monte Bracco, with medieval porticos, the fifteenth-century parish church of San Martino and the Borgo Vecchio along the Lea; on the slopes of the Bracco are the hamlet-museum of Balma Boves, built under a huge rock, the rock engravings of the Rocca la Casna and the climbing walls.
The exact place where the patron of the sick was born.
The entrance door to the museums of Seui.
Over 100 bikes of the historic house of Breganze.
Between cliffs in Mediterranean scenery, with blue sea and white dunes fixed by centuries-old junipers, priority habitat of the Habitat Directive subject to conservation actions.
The tower of the Acerbi, with the sixteenth-century bar cage walled outside where the prisoners were exposed to the gogna.

Village in the Frignano Park with Celtic huts with a staircase roof, medieval remains of the Torrione, the oratory of San Rocco, the fountain of Baronio and other fountains; in the surrounding area you can walk through the eighteenth-century Via Vandelli. One of the best preserved huts is in Roncacci - Casoni.

Promontory on the Ionian coast, the ancient Byzantine Asylos: the Aragonese fortress of Le Castella on an islet joined to the coast by a thin tongue of land and the Marine Protected Area Capo Rizzuto, one of the largest in Italy, with ochre sandy beaches.
The Madonna della Rosa and the feast of roses.
Majolica shops dug in the rock.
16th century frescoes in the cardinal's palace.
The castle of the Corderos overlooking the plain.

Regional archaeological museum dedicated to archaeologist and numismatic Antonino Salinas (1841-1914); it was born from the Museum of the Real University (1814), which became a National Museum in 1860, and collects the excavation materials of all Sicily, from Selinunte to Solunto.

Church of medieval origin in the open countryside, about two kilometers from the village on the left side of the valley of the Abatemarco, where around the tenth century flourished a Basilian female romerium; inside a Madonna with Child in mache and frescoes in the apse, above the portal a stone statue of the Madonna.
A small building in the heart of the center.
To understand how men and woods have lived together for centuries.
Eight climbs on the history of the country in the twentieth century, from emigration to the internment of foreign Jews and political refugees; it is part of the Liberation Route Europe circuit.

The largest karst phenomenon of Gargano and Puglia, south of the municipal territory: about 600 meters of maximum diameter, more than 1,800 perimeter and more than 100 meters of depth, born from the collapse of underground cavities and surface corrosion; the red ground floor is cultivated with cereals. Free fruition.
A show that takes your breath away.
The peasant life of the Ibleans.
Built between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, a rare example of aristocratic residence of the late Renaissance.

Ancient marshes reclaimed between the twelfth century and the beginning of the twentieth century, today a naturalistic site of interest with the birdlife of the wetlands. Between canals and cultivated fields you birdwatching and biking.
Romanesque church of the twelfth century with two apses; the baptistery was added in the fifteenth century. The façade has hanging arches in cones and a bezel with cross over the portal.

The territory has over one hundred castles, palaces, noble residences, farms and ruins, mostly of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. A 7.4 km ring (about 3 hours, suitable for strollers) starts from the square of the municipality of San Michele and touches the church of Santa Giustina, the residence Melag, Castel Valentin, the complex of Castel Freudenstein, Castel Moos-Schulthaus, the church of San Sebastiano and the castles Englar and Gandegg, still inhabited, with views of the Sciliar, the Alpe di Siusi and the Latemar.

Tourist village in a plateau in the woods of Sila, on the edge of the National Park, in the municipalities of Taverna, Sorbo San Basile and Zagarise; italia.it indicates it among the most picturesque mountain villages of the region.
Woods and paths above the village.
The old steppath.
Castle in dominant position, contended in the Middle Ages for the control that guaranteed on the territory, along the bike ring of the Sanctuary Retrovato.

Castle built from 1460 by Pirro del Balzo on the model of Castelnuovo di Napoli, with moat and cylindrical towers; in the basement the museum tells Venosa from the fourth century B.C. to the Renaissance, with the cippi of the Auguraculum of Banzi, the Tabula Osco-Bantina and a head of Diadumeno.
In the Upper City, zoological, paleontological, geological and botanical collections with dioramas and reconstructions, a dinosaur room and a section on the animals of Bergamo.
The Lombard fauna seen up close, free.
The patron's 16th century crucifix.
Bernini up close.
Former food warehouse on Piazza del Ferrarese, today one of the most popular cultural spaces in the city dedicated to contemporary arts.

Already existing in 1127, rebuilt in Baroque forms since 1622 and parish seat since 1590; it houses the seventeenth-century statues of St. Michael of Giacomo Colombo and of the Madonna della Neve by Aniello Stallato, a marble altar of 1777, an organ of 1756 and a two-faced stone crucifix carved and painted between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.
Building of 1350 in the village.
Small chapel leaning against a vault frequented already in the Bronze Age; inside a rustic altar and two frescoed kiosks of the fifteenth century.

Medieval village of Madonie at 1,147 meters, natural balcony with three belvedere (Loreto, Carmine and Piazza Duomo) that look from Etna to Palermo; between alleys and squares the Mother Church with the first crucifix of Friar Umile, the elliptical church of the Savior, the Pottino palaces and, in the hamlet Raffo, the salt mine with the Salt Museum.
Neolithic necropolis of domus de Janas, called here forreddos, in the surroundings of the country: testifies to the human presence since prehistory.
Buren and futurist mosaics.
Skiing and biking on the mountain of the house.
The house of Our Lady Sistine.
Along the Foro river, between flora and fauna, you can reach the cliffs and the remains of ancient water mills, where the millers worked with ancient methods until a few decades ago.
The press museum.
The parish church of the patron, with Romanesque-Gothic bell tower and sacristy of the fifteenth century.
The oldest nucleus of the city, a scene from the fourteenth century of festivals, markets and the exhibition of the Sacro Cingolo, with buildings largely fourteenth-century.
the villa is privately owned for residential use; the temple was opened with guided tours of the FAI Delegation of Monza
Inns with pici and boiled all around.
The territory of Alagna is included in the park.

Parish of the diocese of Treviso. The census of the churches of the CEI records a pre-existing structure as early as 1480 and the construction of the building between 1838 and 1841; destroyed in 1918, the church was rebuilt between 1919 and 1923, with the bell tower rebuilt in 1921-1922. The altars were donated in 1927 and 1934 and the presbytery had a structural intervention in 1970.
the MiC tab indicates time: "Closed" every day; contact of the parish priest 085 8561500

Among the last neoclassical churches of Sardinia, of Palladian orientation, according to project of the Nurese Giacomo Galfrè (in charge in 1867): pronao tetrastyle with Tuscanic columns on top of a monumental staircase, inside a Greek cross with dome and lantern. It preserves the altarpiece of Mario Delitala with the Gloria of Sant'Andrea, a seventeenth-century pulpit in inlaid marble and a 16th-century retablo with the Madonna enthroned with the Child.
Blue Flag Sea at the foot of the city of philosophers.
Complete the visit to the square of the sanctuary.
The Patron's crypt.
Gorge around Orvieto where you practice canyoning.
The Lugherras, with central tower and trilobed bastion surrounded by a four-tower wall, and the Battizzonis with mast and three-tower bastion.
An eighteenth-century church with a Crucifixion by Venetian painter Vincenzo Damini and an organ by Hadrian Fedra from 1782, in a monumental wooden chest with golden reliefs.

The frescoes by Benozzo Gozzoli for the tabernacles of the Madonna della Cosse (1484) and the Visitation (1490-91), detached and reassembled in the original dimensions. A "museum for all," accessible.
The best panoramic points of the village, at 917 meters, look north and east over the Madonie and west over the Impera valley.
The fountains and the wash-house under the country.

Stone houses with wooden roofs and tiles, typical medieval rural architecture, between alleys with arches, stairs and caves; the urban layout remained almost unchanged until the mid-Twentieth century. It preserves the fifteenth-century towers of Via Turano and Via Cenci (the latter incorporated into a dwelling) and, in Via Umberto I, columns, friezes and Latin inscriptions of Roman times.
Open-air museum inaugurated on 22 July 2012 in the presence of the bishop of Saluzzo, with free access.

The "porta della Calabria" on the Strait of Messina, from which the ferries depart for Sicily: the Anthropological Naturalistic Museum in Palazzo Arena, the sixteenth-century Torre Cavallo on the cliffs towards Scilla, the seaside village of Cannitello with the felucas of the swordfish and the panoramic village of Piale.
Byzantine iconostasis almost intact.
The grassy hill of 2133 meters in the national park: from Col di Roanza the path 517 climbs in about three and a half hours to the summit, from which on clear days you can see Venice.
A Roman city underwater.
€10 whole / €6 reduced. On the ground floor Sala Alma Mater free

Borgo del Tirreno cosentino about 8 km from Diamante, born in the 11th century around the castle, with a historic center rich in murals and ceramics and an ancient palace that houses the Museo del chiperoncino dell'Accademia Italiana del Peperoncino.
Necropolis of circular tombs at the end of the fourth millennium BC; Italia.it indicates it as the starting point of the recommended route in the archaeological park. Open every day 10-18.
Three thousand-year-old graves dug into the rock.
The fairy tales of the valley.
Play with perspective: to photograph.
Pinerolo's viewpoint.
The treasures of the cathedral.
The big Pollino canyon.
The medieval baptistery next to the Cathedral.
The view of the plain from the churchyard, especially at sunset.

The village is located at the foot of Monte Priora (2,32 m) and Monte Sibilla (2,173 m), in the Sibillini Mountains National Park; Montefortino is a stop of the Grande Anello dei Sibillini, 120 km long trail that can be crossed in nine days.
One of the most beautiful roads in Europe, to be done on foot or by bike.
The oldest space in the cathedral.
In the upper part of the village, next to the amphitheatre.
Walk through painted facades and steps squares.
One of the largest squares in Italy, with the equestrian monument to Vittorio Emanuele II, the Royal Palace and the Arengario.

A stone village of alleys, ramps and steps overlooking the valley of Sacco; the name recalls the "serroni" , the rocky ridges of the Scalambra in the middle of whose slope the first fortified settlement arose in the 6th century. Feud of the Counts of Signs since 1378 and of the Column since 1427.
The coastal road of about 15 km to Torre Faro, along the Pantani di Ganzirri, up to Punta del Faro, north-eastern tip of Sicily with the lighthouse and the Pilone of 250 meters.

Ancient parish church of Bornato dating back to the X-XI centuries, now an archaeological site; the Municipality has set up a visitor path with panels and audio guide (Italian and English) that leads from the castle to the parish. Each year it is the destination of the landscape and archaeological walk on the traces of Christendom in Franciacorta, organized by Pro Loco with the association U.S.P.A.A.A. (€5; info pievesanbartolomeobornato@gmail.com).
Clear sea with a view of the Strait.
The Fortress of the Gonzaga with the synagogue in the palace.
An eighteenth-century sanctuary on an ancient church.
Our Lady of the Finger.
The city of Brunello, closed by walls and dominated by the fourteenth-century Fortress, in the UNESCO landscape of Val d'Orcia.

Route of the Sibillini Mountains National Park of 4-6 km starting from Pievebovigliana, about two and a half hours; the municipal portal connects it to the chestnut and oak woods around Monte San Savino.

The oldest church of Montone, outside the walls in the valley of the Lana stream: built around the year 1000 in Romanesque-Byzantine style and renovated in the sixteenth century, fortified, with three aisles, with frescoes from the Umbrian school in the apse (Annunziata, Madonna on the throne) and the golden wooden edicule that housed the thirteenth century Deposition.
The castle of Casale between the center and the Po, also home to the documentation center on wine and the UNESCO landscape of Monferrato.
It is located in the Sforzesco Castle.
The medieval monastery restored by the pope.
The museum tells the last phase of the war on the Gothic Line, which stops for months along the Seine.
Archaeology and botany on a cliff.

In Vigarano Pieve, perhaps the ancient Vicus Varianus, the parish church rebuilt in 1760-77 according to design by Antonio Foschini; at the entrance of the village the villa Beltrami, rural complex with sixteenth-century tower.
The highest and most spectacular earth pyramids in Europe.
The palaces of the marquisate.

Romanesque church documented from the 8th century and rebuilt in the 12th century, with three portals, including that towards Siena attributed to Giovanni Pisano, a rare example of Lombard style in Tuscany; inside a altarpiece of Sano di Pietro.
18 meters high iron sculpture created in 1962 for the Festival of the Two Worlds, among the first permanent installations of contemporary art in Europe.
A Romanesque countryman.
The Roman mausoleum with the Etna in front.

Municipality of the valley that connects Lake Idro to Garda, around Lake Ledro at 655 meters: on the shore of Molina the village of the Bronze Age, since 2011 UNESCO World Heritage among the alpine arch palafittic sites, in Bezzecca the Garibaldi Museum and the Colle-Ossario of Santo Stefano, in the pine forest of Pur the Ledro Land Art.

The main place of worship of the city, formerly Santa Maria degli Angeli and San Sossio, dates back to the 10th century in Romanesque style and the tradition ties it to the Misenatas who escaped the destruction of Miseno by the Saracens. It preserves the remains of Saint Sossius, patron saint of the city, who arrived in 1807 from the ruins of the church of Miseno, and those of Saint Severino, patron saint of Austria and Bavaria; it has Romanesque crypt, Gothic naves, Renaissance portal and Baroque chapels. It's a national monument.

Porta della Val Codera, valley without roads inhabited all year round, on the shores of Lake Mezzola: the stairway of thousands of steps to the village of Codera, the ethnographic museum of the valley and the Museum of Picapreda, memory of the granite quarries Sanfedelino that paved Milan, Como, Pavia and Bologna.

In the Fortress, it collects traditional boats of Trasimeno, including 13th century monosili obtained from a single trunk of oak, and boats of Piediluco and of the Padule di Fucecchio, in addition to the "fassoi" in marsh plants of the Cabras pond in Sardinia.
A corner of water between lighthouse and sea.
The lazzaretto on the water symbol of the city.

Small medieval village at the foot of Monte Altuino, called Ponza until 1891; on the highlands of Arcinazzo, at about 850 meters, you can visit the remains of the hunting villa of Emperor Traiano with the civic archaeological museum.
The nuraghe with five towers of the Trexenta.

You enter from the Old Gate with the coat of arms of the Municipality of Todi (a marble eagle, memory of the medieval dispute between Todi and Amelia); traces of the medieval fabric on the walls remain and a large cylindrical tower from which the public clock leans. The small town theatre in Liberty style, of the early twentieth century, is well preserved inside.

Protected area of 535 hectares on the eastern edge of Rome, managed since 2016 by the Parco dei Monti Lucretili: Mediterranean maquis, pastures, tufa ditches, ponds and forests of oaks and farnies, with about 240 species of plants (orchids, narcisses) and over 30 species of birds including herons and fishermen martins. There are the site of the ancient Latin city of Ficulea, the remains of a Roman villa at the Casale dell'Inviolata and Roman tombs such as the Sepulchre of the Torraccet (III century AD) and the Torraccia dell'Inviolata, transformed into a tower in the Middle Ages.
The mother church of the village, with thirteenth-century roots.
The large green area along the Po, loved by those who run and pedal, with the Castle of Valentino and the Medieval village.
The museum of the works of the Duomo complex, reported by Visit Tuscany among the attractions of Pisa.
The mills dug in the rock of the Salento farmer.
The memory of the Grappa Resistance.
How he lived and worked a Cistercian abbey.

The old town has seventeen consecrated churches, including the Baroque parish church of San Giacomo, celebrated on July 25, and the Anime church with a wooden pulpit of the eighteenth century. The Palatzos Betzos district, ancient houses and palaces dating back to the 16th-18th century, with the old Spanish prison, is located around the castle's castle.
Jazz and devotion in the country.
Walks and bikes in the green.
Where the Capuchins were born.
In San Martino, almost 50 perfectly functional carriages.
The eighteenth century organ and the Romanesque bell tower.

The Mother Church preserves a wooden crucifix of the seventeenth century attributed to Friar Umile of Petralia; the church of Santa Maria del Gesù houses a Madonna with the Child carved by Giuseppe Gagini; the church of the Crucifix has a valuable late-medieval portal. In the village there are also carved choirs and cornices in 18th century and 18th century golden wood, linked to the intense activity of wood carving lasting until the 18th century.

Crossed by the Villoresi Canal, inaugurated in 1881, Nova Milanese houses in Villa Vertua, reopened in 2024 after the restoration, the civic artistic collection with the Collection of Fire Arts and the donation of the painter Vittorio Viviani; in the village the parish church of Sant'Antonino Martire, the seventeenth-century Villa Manfredini Ferrari Ardicini and the Parco Grugnotorto Villoresi.

Borgo irpino between the valleys of Ufita and Fredane, with an eighteenth-century center rebuilt after the earthquake of 1732: the walk of the Limits with a view over five regions, the former cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta with its hypogeum, the noble palaces, the FriMact museum at Palazzo De Leo and the Roman cisterns of the first century BC.
About 3 kilometers of pebble beach and sand south of Porto San Giorgio, quiet seaside resort among green hills.
The peasant culture.
The promenade starts here.

The stone arched bridge on the Via della Valle Spluga is traditionally known as the Roman bridge, but the current structure derives from successive reconstructions to keep the passage in use. Next to it, the Caurga is a deep gorge dug into the rock by the Rabbiosa stream, with vertical walls and narrow passages; paths, parapets and equipped passages lead to the bridge and to the viewpoints on the gorge, accessible all year round.

The capital of the Orco Valley in Gran Paradiso National Park, elite tourism centre at the end of the 19th century: in the former Grand Hotel of hamlet, it took the visitor centre Homo et Ibex on the ibex, around alpine lakes such as Dres and Serru, the Nivolet road and the mule track of Colle Sià.
Next to the cathedral.
The Duomo of the thirteenth century, with the ceramic basins on the façade that reproduce the constellations of the Bear Major and Minor.
the Park indicates that the site is in state of abandonment and only the ruins remain
The Via Verde, 42 km bike path between Ortona and Vasto, touches the rocky beach of the Foce and, further on, the beach of the Cavalluccio, indicated among the most beautiful of the coast.
open July-August 10-12 and 15-17, in the rest of the year only for events and by reservation

Centre of Nurra about ten kilometers from Alghero, with the Romanesque church of Our Lady of Talia of the twelfth century, the megalithic fortress of Monte Baranta of the Copper Age and over twenty nuraghi in the territory.
MiC card indicates closed every day (aggiornamento 2021)

Built between 1735 and 1742 on a project by Giorgio Massari for the jurist Carlo Cordellina Molin, with an ionic pronao with four columns in homage to Palladio. In 1743 Giambattista Tiepolo frescoed the living room: on the ceiling the Triumph of Intelligence on the Ignorance, on the walls the Family of Dario in front of Alessandro and the Continence of Scipione. Restored by Vittorio Lombardi between 1953 and 1956, he has been from the Province of Vicenza since 1970.

Wide beaches on both sides of the city, awarded in 2024 with Blue Flag and Green Flag for the reception of children. On the beach of the American landing you can see the remains of a means of landing sunk on January 22, 1944.
18th century church built between 1768 and 1783, with convex baroque façade.
The traditions of the high Varaita Valley.

Country in lava stone on the north-eastern side of Mount Etna, starting point of the Mareneve road towards Piano Provenzana: the Mother Church of 1613 with the wooden choir of 1728, Sant'Egidio with the Gothic portal, San Francesco di Paola with a statue of Domenico Gagini, the ethnographic museum and the museum dedicated to Salvatore Incorpora.
The fortress above Pieve.
Public gardens with Mediterranean vegetation and views of Marina Piccola, Via Krupp and the Faraglioni.
The largest historical site in South Tyrol, among galleries and art exhibitions.

The last train of its kind in South Tyrol has been in service since 1907, connecting Soprabolzano to Collalbo with a stop at Maria Assunta in about 18 minutes, every half hour; in Soprabolzano comes the cable car from Bolzano (12 minutes, every 4). Free with RittenCard.
A sulphurous summer bath.
The square of the two Duomi, with the Broletto and the Torre del Pégol; a place of locals and cultural initiatives.
An ancient priory between Camaldolese and Franciscans.
Clear sea under the white village.
The life of the shepherds told in the rooms of the village.

Benedictine community founded before the thirteenth century by Blessed Santuccia Terrabotti of Gubbio; the church of St. Peter was consecrated in 1388. Paid up in 1799, damaged in the last war and renewed since 1956, it preserves Baroque and eighteenth-century interiors, a wooden Crucifix considered miraculous, a wooden choir of the eighteenth century and ancient vestments. It offers hospitality for short spiritual retreats.

The church rises where, around 1600, the Madonna delle Grazie would appear to a young woman of the place; however, the structure could be older, due to the presence of previous frescoes and an icon of the Virgin of the fifteenth century, still object of lively devotion. It preserves a crypt with drainholes for the burial of the dead.
The largest collection of Maria Lai, in her country.
Napoleon's peace.

Country of the Empire Valley was born at an ancient bridge, already the capital of the castle of Bestagno and the place of origin of Pasta Agnesi: on the heights remain the ruins of the castle of Bestagno of the twelfth century, while in the hamlet Villa Guardia there is a wooden group of the Last Supper of the late sixteenth century inspired by Leonardo's Cenacle.

In Ossuccio the church of Santa Maria Maddalena all'Ospedaletto has a famous bell tower: a cell adorned with bricks was built over the Romanesque bell tower, which ended just above the current bifora. In the village also the Oratory of San Giacomo, Romanesque church at an apse (XI-XII century) restored by Pietro Lingeri, with some of the oldest frescoes in the area (XII-XV century).

In the ancient town hall of the mid-nineteenth century, built on the site of the church of St. John, about 600 objects of the population of Armungia collected by a group of girls (first exhibition on December 4, 1982) reconstruct the agropastoral culture of Gerrei, with sections on clothing, female work, agriculture, iron and territory, three small stone houses, a weaving workshop and a multimedia section.

Medieval bridge on the Serio with four arches of increasing width towards the beehive, with a road of about 2.2 meters in steep slope: dated to the thirteenth century and documented by the fourteenth century, it connected Albino with Cene, Val Gandino and Val Cavallina. Dismissed in 1911, it was restored and crossed with the Val Seriana bike path.
About two kilometers from the center: in 1685, when it was a small chapel, the face of Our Lady would pour white drops and the first stone of the largest church was laid.

Wanted by the Duke Galeazzo Maria Sforza and started in 1473 by the Cremonese Bartolomeo Gadio, entirely made of bricks, with three square towers and a cylindrical double apparatus to protrude, an underground room used as a prison and the Tower of the Captain able to defend itself. Private residence of the Print since 1536, was restored by Luca Beltrami in 1886-1895; you enter from a bridge on the rivet.
The Redeemer overlooking the Gulf of Policastro.

Borgo where underground tombs of the 4th century BC were found; the castle, built by the bishops of Arezzo in the 11th century and one of the strongest in Pratomagno, passed to Florence in the second half of the 14th century and was demolished in 1426. According to tradition, Hannibal stayed there during the Punic Wars; there is the church of Santi Margherita and Biagio, documented from the fourteenth century.

The baroque palace transformed in 1999 by Intesa Sanpaolo in the Gallerie d'Italia: three art collections including paintings of the eighteenth century Venetian; free entry on the first Sunday of the month.
The Rimini of the ancient harbor.

On a hill about two kilometers from the village, built according to the source in 1260, restored at the behest of Vittoria Colonna and donated in 1531 by Antonella dei Conti d'Aquino to the Friars Minor Capuchins; to see the cloister and the church of Saints John the Baptist and Evangelist. The library preserves incunabula donated by the literary and musician Giovan Thomaso Cimello.

4 km from the village near the river Fullone, the abbey church was dedicated to Santa Maria on March 3, 1065; Benedictine until 1221, then Cistercian, from the fifteenth century date in commenda and started to decline. The Cistercian phase remains a parlour, scriptorium, staircase to the upper floors and chapter hall.
Medieval alleys between mountain and lake.
Mills and woods of the valley behind the lake.
A planned baroque city, signed in majolica.

Lana is a fresh pasta born at the end of the nineteenth century, when peasants from neighbouring countries built a village of huts on the Colle dei Marcelli: soft wheat flour ground with stone, eggs, water and salt, spread, dried on wooden sticks and cut into triangles; since 2019 it is produced De.Co. and served with cod. The Castelli Romani DOC wine and the polenta pizzas with herbs are also produced; at the end of September the Festival of Grapes and the Typical Products carries allegorical floats decorated with grapes.

Urban plant in \"gjitonia" (near), with groups of houses overlooking small squares called Â"shesh" , eighteenth-century buildings and traditional restored houses; weaving is still part of the life of the country and the Mass is celebrated in Albanian or Greek according to the Byzantine rite.
Under the church of Sant'Eufemia, the mosaic floors of a Byzantine palace, three meters below the road.
15th century frescoes in a Romanesque church.
Sunny balcony secluded from the central valley, with views from the Rosa dei Banchi al Mont Blanc, on the Col Tzecore road towards the Val d'Ayas.
A water sanctuary of three thousand years in a spot landscape.
The main square of the modern center, indicated by the Abruzzo Region among the stops of the visit.
Contemporary architecture on the port.
A Sirani in the heart of Vignola.

In the former Palazzo Opera "Massimino Carrai" is the museum point of the itinerary of the excavation of the Ecomuseum, which follows the alabaster from the quarries of Castellina and Santa Luce to the processing and trade in Volterra. He tells the extract from the Etruscans to date with archive documents, tools of quarry, objects of daily use and testimonies on the life of the quarrymen, in an exhibition that evokes the visit to a quarry. Managed by ASTREA.
The story of the prophet of Amiata.

Country 344 meters in the National Park of Gran Sasso and Monti della Laga, dominated by the Medici castle-palace and crossed by the Tirino, among the clearest rivers in Italy, to be walked by canoe or on foot; along the road stands the Benedictine church of Santa Maria di Cartignano, national monument since 1902.
Ancient canals that serve agriculture and once moved sawmills and washbasins; the Bea del Follo produces energy to warm up the new school near the chapel of Santa Libera.
Acropolis and panorama of the valley.
The stretch that starts from Via Roma and goes up to a viewpoint on the marina.
The only survivor of a missing medieval village.
The most curious dish of the Castles and its wine.
Church built between the 11th and 12th centuries, example of local Romanesque with simple interior; no document sets the date of its foundation with certainty.

The upper part of the village, on the plateau that gives the name to Trebisacce (the small table) surrounded in the sixteenth century by walls against Saracen raids; from the village the view extends over the gulf, so much so that it is worth the name of the balcony of the High Ionian.

Country of the high valley of Volturno, between the Mainarde and the river, linked to the events of the Benedictine abbey of San Vincenzo al Volturno, founded in the eighth century and now archaeological park with the frescoed crypt of the abbot Epifanio; above the modern village the ruins of Rocchetta Alta, abandoned village, and in the village the International Museum of World Wars.
The MiC card indicates the site closed every day
The Black Christ and the Robbian terracotta.
The port and the 1866 cannons still in the wall.

A recently established local park that includes the capital and the hamlets, with high hill forests of maples, poplars, birch, chestnuts and cherry trees among cultivated fields and views of the hills.

The Sele, which was born from the Picentini Mountains and receives Tanagro and Calore, crosses about 15 km of the territory of Eboli; in the natural area of San Miele they nest blackberries, upups and cards and live barbers, chubs and eels. The river is part of the Foce Sele-Tanagro Nature Reserve.
17th century parish church with a lovely brick façade of 1712; the patron saint's feast is celebrated in September.

Medieval village of the Maremma enclosed by Sienese walls among the best preserved in Tuscany, with Palazzo Checco il Bello and the church of San Giovanni Battista; outside it brings the ruins of the abbey of San Bruzio, the Olive of the Strega and the fortified villages of Montiano and Pereta, in the land of Morellino.

Established in 1887 in the former convent of the Alcantarini, it tells the South of Italy from the Paleolithic to the Middle Ages: figurative ceramics, the tomb of the athlete and the Sala degli Ori of Taranto, jewelry to a cantilever and filigree of the IV-III century BC.

The ancient Phoenician Sulky and Punic on the island connected by an isthmus: the Tophet, the Punic necropolis transformed into a hypogeum village, the catacombs under the basilica of the saint and the museum that tells one of the major centers of ancient Sardinia.
The rocks of the Aosta Valley.
Baroque altars and canvases of the Piazza workshop.
Butterfly house where hundreds of tropical butterflies fly free through tropical gardens; the complex also includes the Fairywood and a large insectarius.
A contemporary tribute to those who left.

Park on an area rich in finds, including the tomb of the Basileus, sovereign of the Peuketiantes buried here about 2500 years ago with weapons and symbols of power; the route illustrates the Basilicata between the 6th and 4th century BC with scenic locations and is visited in summer. It includes the ArcheoLab, an interpretation center with three multimedia rooms and final quiz, the Archeotour with contents via QR code and the Archeogame, treasure hunt in the historic center.

On the acropolis the church of St. Peter stands on the podium of the Roman temple of Juno Moneta, of the third century BC, and inside it remain visible the original walls of the cell in square blocks. Below is a large Roman cistern, now used for cultural events.
An icebox that supplied Verona.
Loggia on the sea and a rediscovered shovel.
The first hermitage of San Bruno, in the woods.

The museum of the Cesare Pavese Foundation preserves the writer's legacy; next door, the former church of Saints James and Christopher, where Pavese was baptized, hosts temporary exhibitions. Five large paintings by Ernesto Treccani dedicated to "The moon and the bonfires." Open every day except on holidays 10-12.30 and 14-18; guided tours on Saturdays at 10, 14 and 16 (about 1 hour 45, with Nuto's house and stop at the home).
The amphorae of the Roman ship.

Built in 1678 under Spanish rule, to defend the cove of Longone and Mola, it is named after Governor Ferdinando Foxardo, as recalled by an inscription of the same year. It rises on a promontory on the coast near Naregno and was then transformed into a lighthouse.

Borgo della Valnerina in the National Park of Monti Sibillini, linked to the Benedictine Abbey of Sant'Eutizio, where the famous precian surgical school was born, whose surgeons worked until the sixteenth century throughout Europe; in the territory the medieval castles of Roccanolfi and Todiano.

Double porch born after the 1000 for shops, inns and artisans, with the iconic loggias of the rich in front of churches and palaces and the iconic loggias of the poor; today it hosts more than 80 activities. Nearby, the sixteenth-century Corte Bassa which housed the dukes of Urbino, with porch, sandstone windows and rustic portal, and the Red Court.

Commissioned by Cardinal Pompeo Colonna between 1507 and 1511 and designed by Bramante on the model of the Roman thermal baths, with three spans facade and octagonal niche room; he is part of the Network of the Historical Houses of Lazio.
Built between 1159 and 1163 by Jacopo d'Iseo, it was the seat of the city governor and today houses municipal offices and cultural initiatives.
The baroque façade of the upper village.
The dome of Vittone and the source of San Domenico Savio.
Nineteenth-century building of the custodians of the reclamation works, rectangular plan with central tower; on the back a large garden with exhibition room.

Carlo Antonio Albino's work completed in the first half of the 17th century, with a dome on high octagonal tiburium; it preserves an ancient image of the Crucifix painted on a wall, very venerated, and a Santa Rita by Enrico Groppi.

The Timavo, born in Slovenia, descends into the Karst and re-emerges after about 38 km a few hundred meters from the sea; sacred place cited by Virgilio and Tito Livio, in Roman age with an area of worship of Hercules and Spes Augusta.
The green balcony on the Brianza lakes.
The Gulf from the top of the head.
A mysterious rock between legend and engraved cups.
A church on the historic mule track.

Romanesque-Gothic church that since 1926 has collected works of other sacred buildings, with the 2005 exhibition extended to the convent: the 1309 Crucifix by Giovanni da Rimini, works by Giovanni Baronzio and Benedetto da Maiano, paintings by Giorgio Picchi (1582-86), the rounds of Ottaviano Ubaldini and Federico da Montefeltro attributed to Domenico Rosselli and Francesco by Giorgio Martini, a fourteenth-century window and an Etruscan and Italian archaeological section.
A city under the city.
The medieval village of the city.
The medieval civic square with the Arengo of 1204, the Palazzo del Podestà of the fourteenth century and the fountain described by Leonardo in 1502; Fellini had it rebuilt in Cinecittà for Amarcord.

The convent, founded in 1540, was the house of Padre Pio from September 1916 to his death in September 1968; here he received the stigmata in 1918. Next to it are the ancient church, originally dedicated to Santa Maria degli Angeli and consecrated in 1629, and the church of Santa Maria delle Grazie built on a project by the architect Giuseppe Gentile of Boiano and consecrated on 1 July 1959.
Paintings in the landscape.
The medieval capital with its tower.
Trails between huts and goats above the village.

The thermal city of Valdinievole wanted by the Medici around the sanctuary of Fontenuova: the warm caves Giusti and Parlanti, the birthplace of the poet Giuseppe Giusti, the museums of the Osteria dei Pellegrini and Villa Renatico Martini, and above the village Monsummano Alto.
The balcony on the Tyrrhenian Sea.
Overlooking Piazza XIX Marzo next to Palazzo Caetani, it has an artistic portal and ceramics of Biancini and houses the statue of the patron Saint Rocco carved by Fabio Provinciali.

Borgo dell'Appennino Marche at the foot of Monte Nerone, with the fifteenth-century bridge, the Palazzo Ubaldini by Francesco di Giorgio Martini which houses the smallest theatre of the Marche and, in the underground, the Museum of fossils and minerals, and the ancient Jewish quarter.
after the earthquake of 2016 the old town is partially accessible and some areas are forbidden (red areas)
Three gorges dug from the water in millions of years, with pots of giants up to 12 m wide, reachable with a hiking route.
The Pontormo in the hill.
private property ruin (MiC, abandoned property): visible from outside, access to check

Built by Francesco di Giorgio Martini from the end of the fifteenth century for the Montefeltro-Della Rovere, it was built above the Brancaleoni fortress and enlarged in the sixteenth century by Girolamo Genga, it was the last seat of the Roveresche court. The route of more than 20 rooms exhibits paintings, drawings, prints and cartographic material left by the last Duke Francesco Maria II, with works by Raffaellino del Colle and Barocci, Renaissance ceramic fragments and a ceramic room used by all Italy; the library has about 40,000 volumes, including a Commedia di Dante of 1491, and in the underground there is the Museum of the history of agriculture and craftsmanship. From the loggia of the tower you can see the center and the river; accept the Map Musei Marche.

Central square paved in lava stone, where stands the Town Hall of the early twentieth century on the site of Peculio, the grain reserve that saved citizens from famines. Nearby, in the Cameni district, the church of Sant'Antonio (began in 1601, Baroque façade of 1796) and the Palaces Camardi, Imbesi, Sardo and Saglimboni.

Church on a terrace overlooking the sea, which the Cilento Park dates back to the 6th century; it preserves sacred works of art linked to the devotion of the community. Our Lady of Constantinople is at the center of the seafaring festival where the statue is carried in procession on the water, followed by fishing boats.
The civic and religious heart.
€10 whole; €5 reduced (6-19 years, over 65, residents of the Metropolitan City)

Large water complex of Republican age (1st century BC) in uncertain work, at 911 meters at the highest point of the municipal territory: the galleries collected rain, loose snow and water from a nearby spring, then purified and distributed to the village and its surroundings. Of the eleven rooms, perhaps, there are four, three rooms that can be visited, reached by a non-original entrance.
The glance coming from the valley.
Intelvese and the Madonna di Luini.

Built in 1564 for Vincenzo Grimani, in a style close to the Badoera, perhaps on a project by Palladio or his follower; it rises on a sort of island between the Storcido and a minor canal. Large frescoed rooms with themes of love and fertility, garden with balustrades and niches. Noble floor available on Saturday 15-18 and Sunday 10-12.30 and 15-18.
The theatre of the ancient academy.
Lakes, glaciers and memory of the Great War under Adamello.
Built in 1510-1512 to the west of the village, it houses a wooden altar attributed to the workshop of Simone Lenner; the bell tower has a stone pyramid cusp.
It collects works saved from the churches of the Archdiocese after the earthquake of 2016.

The thermal city of Alto Monferrato, already known to the Romans for its waters: the Bolente that flows about 75 degrees in the middle of the square, the Cathedral, the Palaeologists' Castle with the archaeological museum and the arches of the Roman aqueduct on the Bormida.
The "fiordo" of the Amalfi Coast.

Complex at the bottom of Via Gorini, next to the Torrione, with the chapel of the Suffragio dei Morti and the nearby chapel of San Rocco. The medieval church with a single nave was rebuilt in the eighteenth century: advanced facade, building almost doubled in height, new bell tower and polygonal choir. It preserves a painting by Giovanni Rampana of St. John the Evangelist on the high altar, a great altarpiece by Andrea Celesti with the Virgin intercedes for the souls of purgatory and the cycle of frescoes by Matteo Pedrali (1935) on the life of St. Jerome Emiliani, for which they settled inhabitants of the village.
To pass under the stone arch that inspired Mantegna and, it is said, Dante.
Alleys and feudal squares of an ancient city.

The workshop founded in 1878 by Paolo Ruboli, a Pesaro ceramist who arrived in Gualdo in 1875 to produce gold and ruby majolica, restored and transformed into a museum in 2015 by the last heir Maurizio Tittarelli Ruboli. About 150 majolica in lustro of the family from 1878 to the 1960s, four rooms on the production phases, the room of the majolica (indicated as the last surviving example in the world) and a contemporary section created for the Triennale of Ceramics in 2009. Open Friday-Sunday 10-13 and 15-18.

Borgo with the Arab quarter of the seven Saracen alleys and a long course of churches and palaces between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries, from the Theatre L'Idea to Palazzo Panitteri with the archaeological museum; in the territory the archaeological area of Monte Adranone and the reserve of Monte Genuardo.
On the trail of Graceful in your country.
35 hectares of protected territory along the Farfa River, with small waterfalls, a Roman bridge and woods covered with moss.
A Romanesque jewel isolated from the fields.
Small museum of ancient mountain crafts in the Andonno village, with rooms rebuilt on three levels that tell the daily life of the past centuries. Visits by reservation.
Walk through door, tower and palaces.
Closed Monday; timetables on the museum website
It dates back to the 12th century and is one of the oldest churches in the city.
Baroque church of the eighteenth century annexed to the Benedictine monastery, active since 1655, with frescoes by the Master of Offida.

Amiata mining country with views of the Val di Paglia and Lazio, gathered around the Aldobrandesca fortress and the church of San Nicola; in the territory the Natural Reserve of Monte Penna, the Grotta del Sassocolato, the galleries of Cornacchini, the Rocca Silvana above Selvena and the Villa Sforzesca of Cardinal Alessandro Sforza.

Opened in 2004, it has three routes of different length and altitude, all departing from the museum, passing through the fossiliferous sites overlooking the valley; the longest measures about 9 km and takes about four hours, suitable for children.

The Pinacoteca civica and Archaeological Museum exhibits paintings from the 15th to the 20th century and the rebuilt study of Giuseppe Sacconi, born in Montalto and architect of the Vittoriano; in the Town Hall the Museum of the prisons, with graffiti and drawings of the prisoners, and the museum "L'Acqua, la Terra, la Tela" .
The square with its porticoed buildings with a well of the fourteenth century, dominated by the ruins of the castle.
Two small lakes in an ancient basin of 3,000 hectares at the foot of Terminillo, among reeds and hygrophilous woods: excellent for birdwatching, especially in winter.
One of the very rare surviving golden bronze Roman equestrian groups.
Wooden sculptures and the altarpiece attributed to Ghezzi.
By bike along the Mincio towards Garda.
The mountain that dominates the city and the Gold Conca.
Sanctuary linked to the legend of Machaby miracle.
Ancient wreck forest protected as a protected floristic area; the Centre of Environmental Education of the Selva organizes excursions, guided tours and educational projects.
The walk downtown.

In the 18th-century noble palace of the Ungaros and then of the Capuas, with courtyard and staircase open to three loggia: the history of the valley from Neolithic to the Middle Ages, with the furnishings of the tombs of the Iron Age, vases from Pithekoussai and Cuma, the painted tomb of the warrior of the late IV century BC, finds of the sacred area of Foce and of the Roman villas. Open Tuesday-Friday 9-19, Saturday and holidays 9-14, closed on Monday.
The Biazaci with open doors.
The bike path that connects Marina di Massa to Forte dei Marmi along the coast.
Medieval porticos with views of the castle.
Probably one of the oldest churches in the Lower Modena: a church in Camurana is mentioned in Carlo Magno's donation to the Abbey of Nonantola of about 776.
The sanctuary was born of a miracle of the seventeenth century.
