Rebuilt in 1590 on the design of Brugnoli, Michele Sanmicheli's nephew, instead of a Romanesque church, of which remain the bell tower of 1130; he preserves an octagonal baptistery in marble of 1412 and paintings, including a canvas by Nicolò Giolfino (1476-1555).
Antonello's Ecce Homo from Messina.

Semi-Gothic church consecrated in 1352, with portal of 1429; in the center of the apse a wooden Christ of the late thirteenth century and in the chapel of the Annunciation Umbrian-Marche frescoes of the second half of the fifteenth century.
The abbey on the hill.
The Cagliari of ancient civilizations.
The square as it really is two mornings a week.

Anversa fraction, once an independent feud, a well preserved ridge settlement which is accessed by a Gothic arched gate; there are the parish church of Santa Maria della Snow (16th century) and the church of San Michele Arcangelo (XII century). In 1929 Maurits Cornelis Escher drew a lithograph of it: from the last corner before the village you will find the same view.
A nineteenth-century symbol of the city.

A trail of about 8 km opened in 2019 that descends from the old town towards Attigliano and the site of an ancient Roman river port on the Tiber, where up to the nineteenth century stood a church of San Valentino.
Dolmen of the Bronze Age in the countryside of Corato, in the direction of Bisceglie, included in the Integrated Museum System of the city.
The late Gothic palace on the basin of San Marco, about 1471, seat of the Venice Biennale.
The Phoenician island in the lagoon.

A single nave church upstream of the village, with portal that refers to the 13th-XIV century; the first certain news is of 1324-1325, when they collected the tenth Cistercian monks from France. The fifteenth-century image of the Madonna enthroned with the Child holds the scepter ('mazza') that gives the name; procession back on the first Sunday of July.
Unknown Gothic frescoes a stone's throw from the abbey.
A Renaissance garden at the foot of the castle.
The seventeenth-century ceiling from the hundred paintings.
The central square among the most photographed in Pistoia.
The treasures of the Roman wrecks.

On the hill to the right of the Clanis, in control of the road towards the valley of Saturday: the first elliptical longobard belt with ten semitowers, the second polygonal Norman belt with nine towers and carraia gate, and on top the fortress with the tower-mastio angioina almost 20 meters high; between the walls remains of houses and a large cistern.

Built by the Pisans in the 12th century in the highest part of the village and enlarged in the 15th century by the Appians with four bastions, it was the refuge of the inhabitants during the pirate raids; from the walk the view goes from Monte Capanne to the coast. It houses the Park's Environmental Education Centre, with free admission, on the geology of the Archipelago.
Canoe and bike in the castle crater.
Medieval church along the Via Francigena which preserves a 16th century altarpiece with the crowned Madonna and saints.
Romanesque, small, in colored trachytes.

Museum of shells with over 900,000 specimens, indicated as one of the most important malacological collections in the world, with also some specimens of shark; educational services, guided tours and book shop. Afternoon and seasonal opening: better call first (0735 777550).

A circular centre enclosed by walls, with concentric streets and low houses whitewashed in lime with sharp roofs called "cummerse" , covered with grey stone with chiancarelle. The village was first mentioned at the end of the 11th century; in the 15th century it was part of the principality of Taranto and two centuries later it passed to the Dukes of Martina.

Protected area managed by the Consortium of the Park established in 1995; in Collestatte is located the Documentation Centre of the Park, museum on flora, fauna and history. On the Black, rafting is practiced.

In a small room of the nineteenth-century Palazzo Comunale, paintings by Vincenzo Pagani, Durante Nobili and Giovanni Andrea De Magistris, two frescoes, a bas-relief made of polychrome paper and sacred furnishings by the former convent of San Francesco; after the closing of the parish, there are the Polyptych by Carlo Crivelli, signed and dated 1468 (Madonna with Child among the Saints Giovanni Battista, Lorenzo, Silvestro and Francesco), and the Madonna with Child and angels by Vittore Crivelli. In the Council room a wooden choir of the fifteenth century.
The biodiversity of Prenestini in a sixteenth-century building.

In the hamlet of Torba, at the end of the Olona Valley, stands the Monastery of Torba, well of the FAI: a late antique tower transformed into oratory by Benedictine nuns in the 8th century, with early medieval frescoes and the church of Santa Maria. Since 2011 he has been part, with Castelseprio, of the UNESCO site "I Longobardi" in Italy.
Founded in 1996 by Francesco Stanguellini in the workshop where his father Vittorio built his racing cars: about thirty cars, including the first Sport 750 and 1100 Fiat and the Junior 1100.
A monumental Gothic portal.
A short stop to see the finds of Brendola from the Bronze Age to the Roman.

The narrow streets of the village cross ancient buildings, noble palaces and small churches; next to the streets remain the ruins of the so-called castle, a rectangular building built with boulders made from the walls that surrounded the village.
Ceramics by Galileo Chini.
the Province indicates the castle of private property: visitable during guided tours
A mountain rock sanctuary with 12th century frescoes.
Treasures and history of the diocese of Ogliastra in one path.
the MiC card reports every day as closed: tel. 0984 961001
Sacred and contemporary art in the heart of the city.

Tomb entirely in granite on a hill, dated to 1800 BC and called so for the large overlapping slabs; burial chamber and exedra are respectively 27 and 26 meters long. It is reached by a dirt road about 3 km from the SS 427 towards Calangianus. Open every day 10-18.

A few kilometers from Colonnata, a large quarry dating back to the first century BC in the form of an amphitheater, with cuts, trenches, quarry marks and extraction plans still visible and signs in Italian and English.

In a rural house in Kaberlaba, not far from the center, tells in seven sections, from the water cycle to pollution, the role of water in the life, work and imagination of the plateau; near the museum starts the didactic itinerary "The Ring of Water" .
The footsteps of a dinosaur on a torrent rock.
The mother church of the village, with a sculpture perhaps millenarian.

At the foot of the village, the medieval fountain was fed by an abundant spring and, with two Roman aqueducts of which visible traces remain, distributed water in the area; its structure suggests a spa complex of Roman age.
Historic residence on Piazza Santa Maria, frequented by Händel, with a Salone delle Feste of over 200 square meters; visits from Friday to Sunday, in week by reservation.
The village above the valley.
See bears closely in semi-freedom.
A Roman amphitheatre born in the second century BC

The municipality of Val Leira, where the map has been produced since the 15th century: the Paper Museum in the eighteenth-century paper mill of Acquasanta, the sanctuary of Our Lady of Acquasanta and the sulphur water baths, with the paths of the Park of Beigua and the High Via.
The seaside palace of Posillipo, among the attractions of the hill along with Villa Volpicelli and Via Posillipo.
Village and lake in one stop.
The Etruscan town was built in the 4th century BC on the Tufacian hill of Pianicara, then Roman, with the theater and the spa.

Sacred art next to the cathedral: the Treasure of Canoscio of the V-VI century, a Romanesque palace in gold and silver, a fourteenth-century pastoral and paintings of Pinturicchio, Rosso Fiorentino and Giulio Romano.
The votive church on the hill tied to the legend of the Saracens.
the MiC card indicates the museum closed daily, Pordenone with love indicates visits on request: contact first
It dates back to the early sixteenth century and is a national monument; it preserves an altar in onyx of Mount Maggiore.

Castate di stroni di Rosso Ammonitico sul Monte Borgà, just below the summit of Monte Piave, collected in a space no larger than a football field; in the past these stones served to cover the roofs of the houses of Casso.
Neighborhood designed in the early eighteenth century, a time of fishermen and peasants, with regular road plot around the central Via Independence.
The wooden statues of the Alpine carving workshops between Piedmont and Savoy.
A 17th-century courtyard.

Borgo at the foot of the Teramian side of Gran Sasso, between the Mavone and Ruzzo streams, in the Gran Sasso National Park and Monti della Laga: the Sanctuary of San Gabriele, the Romanesque church of San Giovanni ad Insulam and paths to lakes and hermitages.

About 6 km of galleries 3-4 meters high and 3 wide, with 15 entrances, born as pozzolana quarries to build the first houses of the BPD workers. From November 1943 to June 1944 more than 3,000 people were accommodated, with cellar, infirmary, registry, chapel, common rooms and niches for families; restored since 1985, there is also a living crib.
High example of the Saluzzo Renaissance: it preserves the frescoes in grisaille with the feats of Hercules by the Flemish Hans Clemer and the Madonna della Misericordia.
Stained glass of Morgari and a work of Viviani in the church of the village.
Villa of the sixteenth century, extensively transformed and enlarged in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, with the park and gardens recommended for a walk.
The lake of the village at the entrance of the National Park of the Casentino Forests, fishing destination and walks.
The Tibaldi Palace.
The thermal spring recalled by Dante in Hell: it flows from a small natural crater, visible beyond a transparent parapet but not approachable, and feeds large tanks.
A rare example of noble courtyard of the Novarese countryside.

Country of the Cremasca plain dominated by the Visconteo Castle, built around 1355 by Bernabò Visconti and Regina della Scala as a hunting residence; in the territory the rural village of Gradella, among the most beautiful villages in Italy, the sanctuary of the Madonna del Riposo with its secular hornbeam and the fountains of the Tormo Park.
The fountain of Piazza del Duomo dedicated to the Amenano, the underground river that flows under the city and still emerges in the orchestra of the ancient theatre.

The first stone was laid in 1353 and the enlargement lasted almost two centuries; a very rich Baroque façade with rosette, 16 altars and a 16th century fresco of the Madonna of Constantinople; next to the former convent of the Celestines, today Prefecture.

In Mezzegra, the parish church of Sant'Abbondio has a baroque interior and ceiling painted by Giulio Quaglio; in the hamlet of Bonzanigo, Palazzo Brentano and Palazzo Rosati recall the trade of oil and citrus with Northern Europe.
Ancient urban gate near the Mole and the port, designed by Filippo Marchionni; the papal coat of arms and the friezes were chiseled during the French occupation of the late eighteenth century.
At the former Londres hotel near the town hall, the history of Valdostana beekeeping through tools.
15th-century fortress within walking distance from the centre, with views along the way.
In Civitanova Alta, one of the main monuments of the city, with a theatrical season together with Rossini and Cecchetti.
Listing in extension: the guide covers 6 of the 10 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
One of the parks of the Greek walls of the end of the V-IV century B.C.

Mill on the Foglia known since the sixteenth century, belonged to the Dukes of Urbino and then to the counts Paciotti, who for five centuries macinò wheat and from the twentieth century produced electricity; there were wounded in 1862 two brigands of the Banda Grossi. Recovered since 2002, it hosts a new hydroelectric power station and the Mezzadria Museum since 2018: thirteen rooms of objects of rural culture donated by Adriano Campanari, from the kitchen to the cellar with 18th century press, a 1888 birock and historical turbines. Open Tuesday 15-18 and Saturday 9-12.
The castle of the Sarriod.
To understand the park before going up into the valley.
The bell tower of 36 meters on the plain.
The Battle of Hannibal told in 4D.
Public garden of 1880, called a real botanical garden.

In a historic building under the arcades, born from the private collections of Anna Grandi Müller: over 3,000 objects tell the life of a bourgeois family from 1815 to 1950, with rebuilt rooms including playroom, kitchen with pantry, living room and bedroom.
Beach equipped for families with the Aragonese tower.
Bathroom and trekking in an ice lake.

Public garden in mid-nineteenth-century style, owned by the Municipality, on a terrace overlooking the sea in a park of Mediterranean maquis; from the terrace you can see the Gulf of Naples and the village of Marina di Cassano. In the gardens is partly rebuilt the mosaic nymph of a Roman villa and the ancient greenhouse is today a refreshment point.

Most of the seventeenth-century complex on medieval structures, near the castle: the palace Mattioli was born combining small houses, the Pisapia was the house of the homonymous family. Restored after 1980, in 2009 they revealed mural paintings, some with scenes of 18th century navigation; today, owned by the municipality, they host exhibitions. Visits by reservation.

Reserve in the municipal territory, inside the Lucano Apennines National Park, dominated by the rare white fir with beech and oaks; it hosts rare fauna, it is open all year round, it is a frequent destination for schoolchildren and inside it is home to the ecomuseum center of the white fir.

City of flowers and Festival, between the Medieval Pigna with the sanctuary of the Madonna della Costa, the Casino liberty, the Russian church, the Fort of Santa Tecla and the villas with exotic gardens.
Roman mosaics in Fuorigrotta.
The fortress on the "Wolfstone," retouched by Francesco di Giorgio Martini for Federico da Montefeltro in 1474, today's fairytale museum.
A museum made by children.
The miniature nativity scenes.

Palace of the late seventeenth century bought by Uno Gera in 1966, home of the Civic Museum: art gallery, gipsoteca, ethnographic museum, Risorgimento museum and contemporary art gallery. Access with stairway and elevator.

In an ancient rustic restored at the beginning of the terraced houses where the grandparents of Columbus lived, he exhibits thirty lithographs on the life of the navigator, a wooden model of the Santa Maria Caravella, books, copies of documents of the State Archives and the family tree, with a didactic route for schools. Terrarossa is the starting point of the historic Colombian route of 19 km towards Genoa Quinto, the same route as the ancestors of the navigator; in the hamlet there is also the small chapel of St. Joseph. Tel. 0185 939001.
A village of miners remained deserted.
The rural memory of the Serre in a small civic museum.

Promontory of medieval houses on the lake, about 40 km from Rome: you enter from a door of the sixteenth century with clock and you go up to the Collegiata, overlooking the lake. On the Belvedere the Fountain of the Earth (of the Anguille), symbol of the village; the sixteenth-century Palazzo Baronale, today the town hall, preserves restored frescoes. The name comes from Angularia, a Roman villa built where the shore forms a right corner, whose owner Rutilia Polla raised fish for the market of Rome.
A medieval sanctuary linked to the history of the Carmelites.
Deruta's majolica story.
A Roman bridge in the nature of the Titerno.
Marinar village of the Riviera di Ponente born around the year 1000, with caruggi, arches and bridges covered behind the beach, and the pine forest Bottini above the village.

Borgo Bandiera Arancione, one of the most elegant and intact historic centers of the Roero, overlooking Barbaresco, Alba and the Alps, with the contemporary art of the Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo.
Walk between stairs and lake, better in the late afternoon.
Six hundred million years of history in a downtown building.
The medicinal herbs of the monks.
The fourteenth-century Crucifix of Luke of Tommè.
A convent on the remains of a temple in the woods.
By bike from Jesi Abbey.
The MiC card indicates closed every day without reason: check, tel. 0763 628237.
The church of the den of the persecuted.

In the Palazzo del Podestà, entitled to Pietro Conti, the first president of the Umbria Region, is indicated as the first museum in Italy entirely dedicated to emigration: it tells with voices, sounds, images, documents and objects the Italian emigration from the late nineteenth century to the sixties, with a path backwards from the arrival to the journey to the departure. It is also a study and documentation centre with video library and library. It is part of the unique ticket of the museum (€6). Info: tel. 075 9142445.

Born in the early seventeenth century from the union of two buildings of the noble Luzzago, connected in the eighteenth century by the staircase to two ramps with railing in wrought iron, attributed to the abbot Gaspare Turbini and frescoed probably by Pietro Scalvini; salons and stairs have squares and imaginary landscapes. In 1908 the Di Bagno gave it to the municipality, which has the town hall; the wing of the guest house library and museum, the rider became the Little Theatre after the recovery ended in 2002.
The 14th-century fortress in the centre of the village, home to the archaeological museum of the Roman city of Forum Popili.
Outside the eastern Urbian gate, on the wide homonymous, the convent and the church of the Madonna delle Grazie, the city's patron.
A fourteenth-century church with a baroque face.

The village is surrounded by medieval walls with Porta Maior and Porta San Severino, defensive towers (three rounds and two squares) and remains of a fortress of the fourteenth century; Casa Squarti-Perla has a portal that combines fragments of different eras and in the village remain two proffers in Viterbo style.
Wooden sculptures and canvases of the Zoppo.
The memory of hemp and Arzano fields.

In the Villa Gardella, donated to the Municipality in 1964, it is managed by the Naturalisti Stazzano Group (founded in 1974) and opened to the public around 1980; the fifth room, dedicated to botany, is 1996. It exhibits mainly material of the Ligurian-Piedmontese area: rocks, minerals, fossils, insects, fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals; it preserves over 5,000 leaves of herbarium, including an eighteenth-century herbarium, and more than 10,000 insects. Open on Saturday 15-18, otherwise by appointment (tel. 0143 65303.
Church of the village decorated with frescoes by Martin Figure.
Five falls a stone's throw away.
A portrait of Sora in the early seventeenth century.
The history of the ceramics of Laveno in a palace on the lake.
The cathedral, a stage of the historical and religious core of the city.
The Pirate Tower on the Gulf.
Walk up to the fortress.

Small rural center about 15 km from Taranto, between Valle d'Itria and gulf, located on the two sides of the Lizzitello Vallone and on the eastern edge of the Regional Natural Park Terra delle Gravine. It is famous for its ... Cento Masserie, awarded in 2015 as the European Destination of Excellence EDEN, for the Pianelle Wood, the Torre Cacace and the rock churches of the Basilian monks.
The Esedra square with the colonnade of Gaetano Koch and the fountain of Mario Rutelli with the four bronze nymphs, terminal of the aqueduct of Acqua Marcia.

In the former primary schools of Erto, where the first bodies were collected and recognized in the days after the tragedy, it is one of the most comprehensive documentation centers on Vajont. On the ground floor there is the photographic exhibition "Vajont: images and memories" , the installation "Battito d'ali per la memoria" dedicated to dead children that night and a workshop with 3D models of the valley; on the first floor "A space of memory" in four sections (First, Impact, Emergency, Justice) and the sensory room "9.10.1963 L'Wave" which reconstructs the approximately 240 seconds of the catastrophe. In 2026 it opened 11-18 on weekends, every day from 24 July to 6 September and 9 October.
An ancient construction site stopped for 2,400 years.
In the seventeenth century Palazzo Panichi, finds of the Piceno and Roman age, including the polychrome mosaic with two-faced hermas.
Residency of the Venetian podestà of the late fifteenth century, from 1850 Chamber of Commerce, with the Wheat Hall of 1929 vaulted glass.
The Guelph palace.
Wild paths and orchids in Sabina.
Sacred canvases in the 16th century parish.

Inaugurated by John Paul II in 1990: the harpsichord on which St Alphonsus composed          ♪You descend from the stars ♪, a ceramic nativity scene of Capodimonte, vestments, autograph letters, the wax burial mask and his intact cell; the gallery counts a hundred paintings, including Flemish works of the sixteenth century and Neapolitan of the eighteenth century of the school of Solimena.

Visitable infernot of the country: the infernots are small environments excavated in limestone stone and used for the aging of wine, symbol of the core UNESCO zones "Il Monferrato degli Infernot" . Visits on Sunday 15-18 from April to October, on the other days by reservation (info@monferratodegliinfernot.it); you should call first.

Made by the Grand Dukes of Tuscany to bring water to Livorno, which used it until 1912: it starts from Colognole and runs for about 18 km between the countryside and the woods, with arches also very high, tunnels and tunnels in Parrana, towards Nugola, up to the Cisternino di Pian di Rota and the Cisternone di Livorno. Today it is a route for hiking, cycling or horseback riding to the sea.
Fantoni, Ceruti and Diziani in a single church in the valley.
A village-refuge suspended over the valley.
The "villa of the hundred chimneys" built by Bernardo Buontalenti for Ferdinando I between 1596 and 1600, with rectangular plan with fortifications at the corners, above the village of Artimino.

Promontory with the lighthouse, the point of the mainland closest to Corsica; on the rocks the seventeenth-century chapel of Catalan corals (Ostra Señora de la Peña), reachable by a staircase from Via Aurelia, where on August 5 is celebrated the feast of sailors and fishermen.

Made between 1855 and 1867 on a project by Schellino, considered his most significant work, is a Gothic reinterpreted with pointed spires, handmade bricks and wrought iron gates; restored between 2015 and 2018. Inside the tombs Appiani, Bonari and Cillario of Schellino himself, buried in a modest tomb in the southeast corner; in the right wing of the entrance stands Luigi Einaudi. From the cemetery start the 14 pylons of the Rosary designed by Schellino in 1872, which go up to the sanctuary of Our Lady of Graces.
The rural and river world inside the walls.
Founded in the 13th century, the first Franciscan monastery in the German area, with the wooden altar of Hans Klocker and a 14th century cloister.

The hilly village of the Ciociaria between vineyards and olive groves, about 100 km from Rome, which preserves the design of the medieval castrum with the doors Santa Croce and Sant'Angelo; it was the site of one of the first oil discoveries in Italy, told by the Energy Museum.
Art of the twentieth century.
€6 half day, €10 full day (non-residents)
Romanesque church with three naves of the thirteenth century, with paintings of the Pomarancio and Iacopo Negretti called Palma and a Roman sarcophagus of the third century A.D.

Country of the Majella National Park, historic center of the hand-painted ceramics of Abruzzo, told in the museum of the Convent of Sant'Antonio; in its territory the Grotto of the Colle, the main sanctuary of the Marrucini where the bronze was found, the goddess of Rapino, and the sanctuary of the Madonna of Carpineto, which was the 8th of May of the procession of the Virgins.
A tribute to the Modena tenor.
Two kilometers of canyon at the foot of the Marmolada.

To the southeast of Tomb, on the edge of a terrace of the river Corno, a funerary mound of the castellier culture: a platform of pebbles of about 20 m in diameter and 2 m in height, covered with earth and gravel held by poles and tables (the armed earth) started around 1750 BC and completed between 1620 and 1440 BC. The excavations of the University of Udine (2006-2008) found the skeleton of a young man with two objects related to the processing of metal and the remains of a cow and a horse sacrificed, among the oldest equine remains of Friuli. From here comes the name of the country.
The medieval village whose houses descend as a cascade from the hill to the villa Garzoni; here Carlo Lorenzini passed his childhood and took his pseudonym.

Villa Le Rose and Villa Salterio Erker, together with Villa Passalacqua, have hosted personalities and artists; they are private property and are admired only from the outside, along the theme paths of the village.
Church of Laste in a panoramic position, from which you can dominate much of the upper valley of Cordevole.

It replaced the ancient Santa Maria, chapel next to the castle, seat of the parish founded in 1173 by Manfredo II of Romagnano (the funeral stone is preserved). The new church was decided in 1560 by the prevosto Giacomo Ponte; since 1674 Don Paolo Ponte began restoration and extension lasting about a century, which gave it the present form, and in 1779 it was reconsecrated by Cardinal Costa. In 1890 it had the organ; at the beginning of the twentieth century it was entirely repainted and the main altar rebuilt. Visitable during functions.
About 7 km of golden sand coast with dune stretches where the rare sea lily grows; the view embraces the Gulf of Salerno from Punta Licosa to Capri.
The water sanctuary on the mountain of Siligo.
Beyond the church, built between the thirteenth and sixteenth centuries, today hosts events and conferences.
One of the largest domes in Italy.
The oldest walls on the mountain.
Already church of Santa Maria, the Franciscans moved there in 1292 together with the annexed monastery; it was renamed St. Fortunato in 1352, but the Fallerones still call it St. Francis.
The symbol of Palau and the view of the Mouths.

In Piazza Cavour the Palazzo del Podestà, completed in 1371, with external staircase, and Palazzo Baglioni, where the leader Malatesta Baglioni IV died on Christmas Eve of 1531 (the family ruled Bettona from the XV to the XVII century). In Piazza Garibaldi the Town Hall of the second half of the fourteenth century, with a sixteenth-century wooden choir in the council hall, and the octagonal fountain of 1890 by Garibaldo Mancini, instead of a fifteenth-century well.

Between the new center and the ancient nucleus, of medieval origin, repeatedly damaged by earthquakes and rebuilt in the current forms in the seventeenth century; the bell tower, restored in 1556, preserves the Romanesque structure of the twelfth century and a plaque with the inscription  "sacerdos cerealis" .

Dedicated to the patron dead in 625, it existed already in 835 and was elevated to papal basilica in 1924: Romanesque façade in grey tufa, in the porch whale bones linked to the miracle of the saved child, a side door attributed to the tenth century with columns and classical capitals, the ceiling with paintings by Giambattista Lama (1734). The crypt, the most visited part, has eight columns of marble, paintings by Carlo Amalfi, former seafaring vote and a fresco of the fourteenth-century Madonna delle Grazie, the oldest Marian image of Sorrento.
The palace commissioned in 1474 by Cardinal Bartolomeo Roverella, since 2000 seat of the Pinacoteca dell'Accademia dei Concordi and of the Bishop's Seminary and large temporary exhibitions.
Ideal for families.
The first Italian Gothic.
Small sanctuary along the provincial road for Torre Beretti, which preserves a Renaissance fresco of the school of Gaudenzio Ferrari.
Easy walk with view to the Monviso.
The fortress on the promontory.
A nineteenth-century garden.
Homages to the memory of the young man killed in a beating on September 6, 2020; every year on January 20 is celebrated the Day of Respect.

Town of the plain of the springs of the Biferno at the foot of the Matese, home of the mozzarella fiordilatte, with the cathedral of San Bartolomeo from the thirteenth-century portal and, high on a spur at almost 850 meters, the medieval village of Civita with the remains of the castle Pandono.
The first Crucifix of Friar Umile from Petralia.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 2 of the 10 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
A hamlet chapel with ancient wooden statues carved and painted between the 14th and 16th centuries.
Frantoio that produces organic extra virgin olive oil Garda DOP from Casaliva olives and Gargnà with traditional methods; you can visit, taste and buy oil.
The Liberty in the chapels.
A Roman arch on the Black.
visits by telephone or email (Bracciano Municipality)
The building of the trap on two floors, with loggia, warehouses of salt and floats and a small chapel of Sant'Antonio di Padova, destined to become Museo del Mare.

Visitor centre of the Gran Paradiso National Park in the deconsecrated church of San Francesco, in the historic center: it reconstructs an alpine domestic environment where milk became butter and cheese, tells with an animated theater, a documentary and an interactive sound installation the life of chimney sweeps, men and often children of the valley who in winter went down to work in the city, and presents a plastic of the dams and hydroelectric power plant of the valley of Piantonetto. Open in the summer months and on Christmas and Easter holidays; accessible.
The great Gothic monument of Via Emilia Piacenza.

In Castello D'Aquino, it collects findings from donations and random finds from prehistory to late Middle Ages: neolithic silci and obsidian, italic materials related to the Irpini and Magna Grecia, Roman objects from nearby Aeclanum and medieval ceramics, plus an ethno-anthropological section with sacred objects in wood and objects of the twentieth century.

Artificial basin of 1921 created by a dam on the Scandarello stream, reachable with an easy path; in summer nights the sky not polluted by lights is suitable for falling stars. During World War II, a local girl alerted the mines placed by the Nazis, avoiding the flooding of the Tronto Valley. VisitLazio indicates it as the stage not to be missed.
The Brescian plain before history.
Art of the twentieth century and angels of the Fantoni.
The museum dedicated to Italian emigration, reported by Visit Tuscany among the places of Lucca.
Annunciation architecture at the service of energy.
Water jumps in the woods just a few steps from the center.
Medieval ruins with views of the Piana.

Borgo della Val di Bisenzio grew up around the Badia di San Salvatore, founded in 1073, with its museum; in the territory the Renaissance Villa Vai al Mulinaccio, the town-factory of Briglia, the parish church of Sofignano sulla Calvana and the woods of Monteferrato.
private residence, it opens to the public on very rare occasions; the building is seen only from the outside (FAI)

The centre of the low plain of Brescia, gathered around Palazzo Luzzago di Bagno, home to the town hall and the Archaeological Civic Museum with the only coin known in Italy by the Longobard King Ariperto I, stands out the eighteenth-century parish church of San Lorenzo with a painting of Moretto, the churches of the Discipline and of San Rocco and the neo-Gothic Palazzo Ghirardi.

Small hillside center on the Ionian side of the Serre, with origins that some sources date back to the 8th-IXth century; grew with the Normans and the Carthusian monks, since the 16th century the Turkish raids pushed the population on the hills and under the Bourbons flourished with the processing of silk. Between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries there arose many noble palaces; in the village there is the church of San Pantaleone.

Palace remained unfinished in the center of the village, where Marcantonio Colonna was born, among the architects of the victory of Lepanto (1571); on the main façade there is a Roman sarcophagus in marble of the III-IV century A.D. In his Secrets (The Cantinone) the excavation exhibition on the excavations of Lord Savile Lumley was held.
Walk on a sea and a prehistoric river.
Winter skiing and summer trails under the Cusna.

Municipality of the Brescian plain towards Garda: in Ciliverghe the eighteenth-century Villa Mazzucchelli brings together the museum house of the literary Gianmaria Mazzucchelli and the collections of the Fondazione Giacomini Meo Fiorot.
Recommended for groups

Opened in 1925 in Palazzo Pisani from the collection donated by the local physician and historian Carlo Gaetano Nicastro, it collects archaeological finds from the excavations in the territory of Bovino. Free admission according to the Touring; for the MiC open Saturday and Sunday 10.30-12.30 and 16.30-18.30, in August every day except Monday.
guided tours with reservation required at the Superintendence (0755741230)
The church "vecchia" of Mel, built between 1480 and 1490 with three naves with ten altars, struck by lightning in 1756 and rebuilt; it houses a Pietà by Giovanni da Mel and dello Schiavone.

The village was born around the castle, built around the year 1000, and preserves the original layout with the medieval walls, the entrance tower of the fifteenth century and two sighting towers on the central square; perched on a hill, it probably served as an observatory towards Orvieto.
The maze of rooms in the tuff.
The Pope's summers.

The Romanesque bell tower dates back to the fourteenth century; the new church was started in 1631, finished in 1682 and consecrated on 5 November 1724. The main altar is by Vincenzo Baroncini (1735), the painting decorations by Luigi Morgari (1931).

Less than 2 km from the center along the SS 133, granite fortress of the Bronze Age on a granite dome in a cork wood, with characters of both the nuraghe in corridor and that in tholos: a corridor leads to two oval rooms and a semicircular courtyard. From April to October-November there lives a colony of tiny bats, observable without flash. Admission fee.
The sculptor of the eagles of the Central Station.

A fifteenth-century forge operated by a water wheel still in operation, a rare testimony of the ...bruzafèr... the iron processing once widespread in Franciacorta: a document from 1556 mentions a "mulino della Grotta" and a date of 1430 was visible on an external wall. Between the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries it passed to the Averoldi, who produced agricultural tools there; Andrea Averoldi, among the last blacksmiths in the area, worked with his wife Aldina Barbi until 1984. Purchased by the Municipality in 1997 and open to the public in 1999, it retains its original appearance with hydraulic hammer, stone hydro wind trumpet, pulleys with wooden wheels, wheels and tools, including the 'sappa with horns'; periodically expert craftsmen show live the forging of damask steel blades.
The elliptical square that follows the Roman arena, transformed by Lorenzo Nottolini in the nineteenth century: you enter from arches, pastel houses, bars and trattorias.
An ancient view of the city painted in church.
Built in 3 B.C. by Caius Avilius Caimus, it is 56 metres above the Grand Eyvia stream: great work of Roman civil engineering.
Dedicated to the patron saint of Arzano, it was erected in 1560, enlarged in 1598 with a larger portal on the façade and in 1753, after various works, assumed an appearance similar to the present.
One of the oldest synagogues in the West.
Art, emigration and archaeology in a noble house.
The Sabina's mother church, with the Baglion at the altar.
In the city of the Panini figurines.
the mausoleum is closed to the visits and can only be observed from the outside; dense vegetation in a stretch
Popular devotion in a 17th century church.

The walls of the Greek city in Capo Soprano, a remarkable example of mixed construction technique, with the stretch discovered in excellent condition: Italia.it indicates them as the best preserved example of Greek military architecture.
The most important and characteristic church of the village, dedicated to the patron saint.
A fortification of the Alpine Valley next to a waterfall.

At 683 meters, it is described as the oldest Marian shrine of the Marches and the second most visited after Loreto, called "Little Lourdes of the Sibillini" (Sibillini); the tradition links the first chapel to the apparition of the Madonna to the shepherdella muta Santina, around the year 1000. The present church, with six chapels, was rebuilt from 1603 with decorations by Martino Bonfini by Patrignone, Domenico Malpedi (1634) and Virginio Parodi (1928); since 1897 it has been guarded by the Capuchins.

Large rural house of the fifteenth century, section of the Bersntoler Museum/Museum of the Mòcheni valley restored by the Mòcheni Cultural Institute, which illustrates the scattered settlement in isolated farms typical of the valley: house on two floors with cellar, stables, aia, barn and barn, and around vegetable garden, fertilization, fields, meadows, woods and pastures. Open at 15-17.30: in May and September on Sundays, in June Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays, in July and August every day except Mondays. Suitable for families and schools.
The city of the Punic dead.

3-hectare garden founded by Dr. Antonio Ridella, at about 930-950 meters at the foot of Monte Pietra di Corvo, outskirts of dark volcanic rock. Thanks to a particular microclimate it hosts mountain, subalpine and alpine flora of the Alps, with Apennine, Pyrenean and other chains such as Himalayas and Andes; notable communities of Primula, Saxifraga, Gentiana and Iris. It is recommended to visit it with the staff, who informs about the accessibility and conditions of the trails (tel. +39 0382 597788).

Asti's country with the Romanesque church of San Lorenzo (XI-XII century), restored since 1982 and now home to exhibitions, and the parish church of Santi Giovanni e Lorenzo designed by Filippo Malabayla in 1646; in the Town Hall a permanent exhibition of contemporary art.
The Christmas village of Piazza Rinaldi, with the lighting of the tree in Piazza dei Signori and the Via dei Presepi between churches and historical places.
An almost intact walled village with its four doors.
The popular district beyond the stream, with the birthplace of Toscanini, the Old Hospital, the churches of Santa Croce and the Annunziata and the Ducal Park.
By boat on the underground river, between stalactites and prehistoric stilts.

One-hour-one-and-a-half ring with about 100 meters of altitude difference, accessible to all, among woods, flowering meadows and peat bogs: mountain woods plants, Japanese maples, Asian and aquatic plants, an orchard of lost fruit and panels with passages of the The 2011 Garden of Europe is a flowered amphitheatre that recalls the European Parliament. We start from the visitors center with parking.
A stone village at more than 1,200 meters, leads north of the Park.
Walking in the crater to Lake Mezzano.
The neoclassical theatre of Lotario Tomb dedicated to Verdi, called a small Scala for its shape.
The symbol of the village, with a view of the coast and San Pietro.
An intact alpine valley with stone hamlets.

Outside the village, at the convent of San Giovanni del Palco on the border with Taurano: the excavations of the Soprintendenza of 1981 have brought to light about 1330 m2 of a villa on three levels, dating from the late Republican age to the first century AD, rendered uninhabitable by a landslide. You can see the thermal sector with frigidary, tepidary, calidary and circular laconicum and a nymph with niches in marble tiles and vitreous pasta and a hunting mosaic with deer, dog and amorino.

Ancient Norman village, 'porta dell'Alto Molise', grown along the tratturo Castel di Sangro-Lucera around the Castello d'Alessandro, transformed in the eighteenth century into a noble residence; in the surroundings the tower of Santa Maria dei Vignali between Sannitic fortifications and, beyond the Trigno, the white fir woods of Collemeluccio.
It preserves the sarcophagus of Gaspare Spontini, adorned with a medallion traditionally attributed to Antonio Canova.

Masterpiece of the late Sicilian Baroque on top of a staircase of 250 steps: facade with a 60-metre tower attributed to Rosario Gagliardi, inside with five naves with the polyptych of Bernardino Niger, the Madonna della Neve by Giuliano Mancino and Bartolomeo Berrettaro, the Assunta by Filippo Paladino and a sundial in the floor of the transept.

On the top of Mount Cüsen, with a wide panorama of the Serian Valley, it has been attested since 1565 (visit of Bishop Cornaro) and was wanted by Giacomo Cominelli called Mistrù; for centuries there lived a guardian romantic. The living stone bell tower dates back to 1610, the guardian's house and the eighteenth century Sarnico stone loggia; the church is oriented north-east by the rock and preserves a fresco of the Madonna with Child venerated for almost five centuries. Walk up from San Cristoforo with a steep path on steps or with the mule track "Via di Prècc."
The tomb of the lords of the village and an organ of the sixteenth century.
The black glass of the prehistoric, from the quarry to the sculpture.
museum in preparation, inauguration scheduled for 2026; noble floor open only temporarily with guided tours by reservation (Trentino Cultura)

Dedicated to the German patron saint of the woodsmen, it preserves a cycle of frescoes from the middle of the fifteenth century; the origins are uncertain and could be the first place of worship of the country, consecrated in 1164.
The castle on the hill above the Roman Theatre, reachable by a stairway of 267 steps from Ponte Pietra between ancient houses and climbing, with a view over the whole city.
A water story between Venice and Gonzaga.
The mother church of the militelle baroque.
Walk to the village of wool.

The heart of the city, where the Collegiate and Palazzo del Podestà (or Pretorio) overlook, with the coats of arms on the facade, now the town hall and the venue of exhibitions; there you can play the Game of the Well during the Feasts of Forgiveness, the first weekend of September.
The Vignola ladder, suspended in the void.
Walk on an ancient ocean floor.
The flowering meadows of the Arera in the middle of summer.
The shrine that dominates the city.

Waterfall 30 meters high in all in five jumps, the last of about 15, on the border between Santu Lussurgiu and Bonarcado, in a valley protected as a special conservation area. The name recalls the mills and the galleries for the processing of the cloths operated by the stream; one is preserved next to the major jump. You walk down a mule track with sections of pavement, between holm oaks, oaks, alders and laurel, starting from a stretch on the SP 15.
A garden above the Forums.
Roman stones on the facade.
The Art Nouveau castle that looks at the "Pearl of Friuli."
A thousand years of history in a fortress.
Regional reserve on the mountain above Avezzano, also frequented for paragliding.
A sabaudo castle in the sea in squares of the rice fields.
The bonfire of January 17th.
Neapolis under Forcella.
The laboratory of a sculptor from the 19th century.
Snorkeling coves and rocks.

Small village of Marmilla founded in the seventeenth century under Spanish domination, known for the nuragic complex of Genna Maria, on the hill that dominates from the Gulf of Cagliari to that of Oristano, and for the archaeological museum that exhibits its finds in a nineteenth-century building in the historic center.

In front of Palazzo Di Monte, they were financed in 1550 by Pope Julius III for his brother Baldovino and completed by Count Fabiano after 1556 with 700 shields; they are attributed to Nanni di Baccio Bigio. Five round arches on Corinthian fluted columns, with the coats of arms of the three mountains in laurel crown in the plumes and barrel porch; used for centuries as a covered market, on the upper floor are now exhibits.
Villa Vesuviana that hosted Giacomo Leopardi.
The abbey tower overlooking the valley.

Also known as Loggia Torriana, it was built in 1688 by Count Francesco Ulderico della Torre on a previous Venetian loggia of 1488; meeting place of the nobility and merchant seat with the public weight, since 1939 it hosts on the ground floor the civic stone, with the plaque that recalls the foundation of the Venetian fortress and the inscription of 1479 on Giovanni Emo and the citadel "Emopoli."
Alpeggi del Comune connected by numerous excursions in a landscape of pastures; the Oasis of Segur is the starting point for exploring the mountains of Cavargna.
A Roman slab on a medieval mountain church.

Borgo della Locride on the promontory above the Galizzi torrent: the Pellicano castle where the village was born, the churches rebuilt after the earthquake of 1783 and, towards the coast, the archaeological park of the Roman villa of Naniglio with the large pillar cistern.
In the world of Comiso's great writer.
The first villa built in Frascati, by Bishop Alessandro Rufini, called "La Rufina" (La Rufina), now home to the Vivarium Novum Institute, guided tours on Sundays.

Neoclassical Greek cross church designed by Giovanni Battista Schellino (1859-1886), 46 meters long and 23 meters wide, with an inner peristyle of 24 columns that holds the large dome. It preserves paintings from the XVI-XIX centuries, wooden statues of the Brilla, a Via Crucis of Gaetano Previati and the organ of the brothers Vittino di Centallo, inaugurated in 1883; apse, walls and columns are decorated by the painter Giovanni Albesiano from Dogliano.

The Jewish quarter, where in the middle of the 12th century there lived about two hundred families, expelled in 1541 by edict of Charles V; the streets still remember the past (via La Giudea, via Synagogue, via Mosè da Trani, wide Scolanova).
A path along the coast of Lake Orta, away from noise and traffic, passing through villas, flower gardens and small coves.

Built at the beginning of the fourteenth century in memory of the passage of Saint Francis to Sora in 1219, headed for Egypt; the complex is annexed to a late Baroque palace and the former convent houses the Civic Museum.
At the Sinese Gate, another entrance to the castle, a sixteenth-century tabernacle in polychrome majolica of the Robbiana workshop with the Madonna and Child.
Boats dug in an oak trunk.
Galleries under the streets of the center that tell Massa during the Second World War, with panels and installations.

Ancient fortified village on a hill of tuff at 254 m, about 3 km from the capital, belonged to the abbey of Sant'Antimo and then to Siena, in the fourteenth century divided between Ptolemies and Piccolomini and visited by Pope Pius II in 1459. In addition to the castle, the Pieve di San Donato, the church of the Madonna delle Grazie, ancient wash-houses and fountains and the Itinerary of the Panorami between fields, olive groves and cypresses.
The karst of the Ligurian Alps.

A vast complex, with an area of about 40 times the camp of San Siro, whose first stone was laid on February 6, 1928, wanted by Cardinal Schuster to form the Ambrosian priests away from the city. The 64-metre tower stands out, which since the 1930s has hosted the Observatory of Earth Physics for almost half a century; the library has more than 140,000 volumes and the theology chapel is decorated by A. Bergagna. Library and chapel are to be visited on the occasion of the Feast of the Seminary on 1 May.

The hamlet rises on the ancient Castrum Buccinianum: the castle on the hill, at the confluence of three streams, has three walls and three natural moats and contains Piazza d'Armi, Palazzo Tranquilli and the Piazzetta with the stone arch. On 26 December and 6 January there is the Medieval Itinerant Nativity scene, inspired by Jacopo da Varagine's Legend Aurea and a visit by a cardinal to the castle in 1343; between late May and early June the Sabina Jazz Festival, founded by Bruno Castracucchi.

The construction was started by the Polini brothers in 1723 with the design of a castle-shaped residence with four corner towers; the building was not completed and passed to the Counts Lechi. The complex in red brick is surrounded by greenery and closed by a long wall of belt with turrets. It is one of the places reported in the FAI census "I Places of the Heart" (2010-2022).

Overlooking the Via Arduino, it is a Gothic building on a three-arched porch, with wooden ceiling and terracotta decorations; according to tradition King Arduino stayed there. It is visible only from the outside.
In the Palazzo Pretorio the icons of the 19th and first 20th century donated by journalist Francesco Bigazzi, correspondent from Moscow.
One of the great medieval religious presences of the territory, together with the parish church of San Pietro in Cerreto and the monastery of San Salvatore in Montebona.
The shape of the castle on the cliff.

Founded in 1333 by Guglielmo Sanseverino, lord of Padula, Sanza and Policastro, it preserves many 14th and 15th century buildings, largely restored, including Palazzo Sanseverino and the church of Santa Maria delle Grazie, with a cycle of 15th century frescoes. The heart of town life is Piazza Sandro Pertini, where concerts, fairs and parades are held.
Frescoed salons and a rare Italian garden.

More than a castle a fortified fence: about 470 meters of walls with seven towers (six squares and a semicircular) and an ogival gate of the thirteenth century, which enclose terraced houses along four converging streets on a church of which remains the trace; for the Municipality is the best preserved walls of Abruzzo. Free entrance, not accessible to disabled people.

Cities on the hill between Ancona and Loreto, ancient Roman town hall and bishop's seat: the Romanesque-Gothic cathedral of San Leopardo with baptistery and diocesan museum, the town hall with the Roman statues acephale, the basilica of San Giuseppe da Copertino, the Madonna del Rosario del Guercino in San Marco and more than nine kilometers of underground caves.
Hundreds of whistle-blowers, symbol of the country.
The symbol above the city.
€12, reduced €10, family €34

Easy ring for families (2 hours, 180 m of difference in altitude, all year round) from the Pradielis walkway: hazelnut, maple and ash wood, the village of Crastie after about twenty minutes, Micottis, the view of the Musi bastion and the return along the Torre stream.
The lighthouse on the hill.

In the southwestern corner of Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II, remains of a peripteral temple of the middle of the third century BC, partly incorporated into the foundations of the church of Santa Caterina; on its south side between the end I and the beginning II century A.D. was built a covered theater, with a brick cavea of eleven rows of seats divided into four sectors, excavated in 1892-1893. The only covered theatre documented in Sicily together with that of Catania, hosted concerts, music competitions and public readings.
The elliptical village on the cliff.
Industrial archaeology of the early twentieth century.

Created by the master knifemaker Paolo Pusceddu next to his workshop "Arburesa": the history of Sardinian knifemaking from the Neolithic, with the reproduction of a obsidian dagger, sixteenth-century pieces, horn handles carved with Sardinian fauna, works of knives of Villacidro, Dorgali and Pattada and the reconstruction of the smith's workshop, Pusceddu made in 1986 the largest knife in the world (3.35 m, 80 kg), which was passed in 2002 by a handle wrench of 4.85 m and 295 kg. Saturday and Sunday by reservation.
A theatre born as the home of the people.

Museum of industrial archaeology with ancient spinning mills, documents and uses related to domestic sericulture, spread throughout Calabria until the last century; it is located in the river park together with the ancient spinning mill Gaudio and the dynamic silk museum, expression of the Calabrian textile.
To know the Tarvisio Forest.
Medieval village on the Via Francigena in the Gran San Bernardo valley, which has become an open-air museum with works by internationally renowned artists.
The finds of the caves of the Kronio.
From €6; reduced for families, students and groups; free up to 14 years

House and workshop of the sculptor Ugo Guidi (1912-1977), born in Querceta and professor at the Academy of Fine Arts of Carrara, with his working instruments and about 600 works between sculptures, drawings and temperas: from the marbles of the 1940s to the tufi of the 1950s, to the studies of horses and motherhood and marble totems. It is part of the Memory Houses of Tuscany and hosts contemporary art exhibitions; free visit only by reservation (tel. 348 3020538, museumougoguidi@gmail.com).
19th century buildings linked to the daily life of the village, which can be visited by reservation.

Follina is one of the twelve municipalities of the core areas of the Prosecco hills of Conegliano and Valdobbiadene, UNESCO World Heritage, along the Prosecco road; the territory offers hiking, mountain biking, cycling, horse trekking and Nordic walking.
The double Greek and Latin rite.

Nineteenth-century shrine in a small clearing between the village and the Antica Vetreria, originally the starting point of the Via Crucis that goes up to Santo Stefano; in a niche on the right of the aisle preserves the Madonna and the Child from an ancient medieval capital.
An 11th century parish church in a castle in Valdera.

It exhibits the prehistoric finds of the excavations of Pradis and testimonies of life on the plateau in the bronze and Roman era; in the territory the Cave of Clusantin and the Cave of Rio Secco document the passage of the last Neanderthal hunters. Open at the same time as the caves.

Inaugurated at Palazzo Longhi, a patrician residence of the mid-eighteenth century, on June 24, 1959, a century after the battle of Solferino: it tells the birth of the Movement designed by Henry Dunant, with wooden beds of the late nineteenth century, motor ambulances of the thirties, surgical field irons, philatelic collections and the original text of "A memory of Solferino" .
The early Christian baptistery that named the city.
By bike outside the walls.

Remains of a monumental spa complex of Augustan age, discovered between 1781 and 1788 and excavated again in 1953 and between 1965 and 1970: three large pools with the water supply system (one fully visible), a small theatre or odeon, a building with two apses, thermal baths and a hydraulic network of over 200 meters. From April to October open on Sunday 11-13 and from 15 am to sunset, on other days by reservation; visible from outside.
The fortress of the first fifteenth century on the Bisenzio, with the findings of Gonfienti, one of the major villages of the Bronze Age of northern Italy, then Etruscan and Roman.
15th century monastery near the abbey, indicated as one of the oldest in the region.

Viale Mellano is a walk along the ancient walls that delimits the Old Town overlooking the valley of Stura; the White Avenue, returned to the city in 2012, follows the sixteenth-century wall from the Bastione del Salice to the Porta di San Martino, with traces of the Bastione dell'Annunziata and a panel that indicates names and heights of the peaks of the alpine arch.

In 1572 the village passed to Jerome Theodoli, prelate of the Apostolic Chamber, whose family built a large palace with a small defensive tower, collapsed on the afternoon of November 2, 1969; next stands the Castelluccio district, which takes its name from the tower. For Corpus Domini, in June, from the middle of the nineteenth century the historic center is covered with carpets of flowers on which the procession passes.
Frescoed buildings survived the earthquake and a center returned to its original appearance with reconstruction.
From walkways seen to the sea.
Wet area for summer walks from the valley floor, flanked by a research center with educational activities.
The history of the valley, from mountaineering to rural life.
Modern square indicated as a significant example of rationalist architecture, with the Town Hall, the Civic Tower and the former Fascio House.
The neo-Gothic town hall next to the Palazzo dei Marquisi, information point of the village.
A thousand-year-old Romanesque apse.
From the old town to the summit of the promontory.
Built in the sixteenth century by Cosimo I de' Medici just outside the centre, it hosts exhibitions and events, a park and a walk on the walls overlooking Siena.

Palazzo cinquecentesco traditionally attributed to the Sansovino and probably the residence of the Di Monte, whose coat of arms it bears; since 1761 the headquarters of the Community Chancellery, today it houses the Municipal Historical Archives with over 4000 pre-unitary units. On the façade two orders of five windows and a niche with Madonna and Child; on the side a portal with the coat of arms Baldi and the motto

Country of Salento about 5 km south of Lecce, built on an important Messapico settlement today visitable in the Museo Diffuso managed with the University of Salento. In the historic centre there is the Baronial-Marchesal Palace of Castromediano-Limburg, the Assumption Church and the former Dominican convent.

Outside the village, it is the oldest church of Poggio Mirteto: church, bell tower and crypt are of the thirteenth century. The aisle, with arched ceiling, is frescoed between the 12th and 14th centuries; arch and apse house the Coronation of Maria del Torresani (first half of the 16th century) and there is the cycle of the White Bats, movement arrived in Sabina at the end of the fourteenth century.

More than a kilometer of white sand and very fine, among the most extensive of the Sulcis archipelago, with dunes of junipers, shallow bottom that slopes gently and sheltered bay between tuffy rocks and granite; bar, large parking, rentals, boat excursions and surf school. You can reach in a few minutes from the village towards Punta Maggiore, passing in front of the beach of La Salina, with dunes and a pond that is avifaunistic oasis.
Oratory of the 13th century.

This nineteenth-century villa with a back garden remains intact: it tells the life, tastes and interests of a bourgeois family from the late nineteenth century, with its central salon, rooms furnished in eclectic styles, tempera ceilings with Ligurian themes, mosaic floors and paintings especially from Genoese from the sixteenth to the eighteenth century. It belonged to the Whites, the Raffas and then to the Carbone brothers, it was left to FAI in 1987 by Emanuele and Syria Carbone. Free entry for FAI members.

The mosaic school that has made known Spilimbergo, institute of international fame: you can visit classrooms and workshops, where you can observe techniques and students at work, and the gallery with a chronological path from the Greek-Roman and Byzantine mosaic to the contemporary one, with a section on the artists of Friuli Venezia Giulia on the first floor. Single tour from Monday to Friday 8-12 and 13-16 (last entrance half an hour before), with registration at the entrance to the courtyard; guided tours every day by reservation to the Tourist Information Office (0427 2274), groups up to 50 people with authorized guide.
The balcony on the Adriatic.
Feudal castle of 1200, among the most interesting defensive works in the province of Genoa according to Touring.
The church on the village.
€8 whole; €5 under 35, over 65 and groups; free under 18; combined €12
The tower symbol of civic identity and the noble palace of the village.
The catacombs dating back to the second century AD, among the most fascinating testimonies of the underground Naples.

Ancient tower-door of the village, the only remaining of the three walls, renovated and called ...Parsun in 1693. Originally it had a driveway and a pedestrian poster; the traces of the drawbridge remain. The date 1388 engraved on three terracotta tiles recalls a reconstruction after the battle fought that year in the countryside of Livorno between the Red Count and Facino Dog.

Founded in 1994 in the former middle school of Madonna del Piano, it exhibits about 700 exhibits from prehistory to the early Middle Ages in eight sections plus a lapidary, especially from the excavations of the villa of Casale di Madonna del Piano; among the main pieces the funeral inscription of the child Artemisio (III century A.D.) and a plastic of the settlement on a 1:50 scale. Closed on Monday.
To understand the Palio from the inside.

Easy route from Simaz to Pian dei Cyclameni (2 hours and 50, 200 m of altitude difference, all year round): panoramic view of the high valley of the Tower, the former military range with birch and star broom, the ruins of the Tanatcoda, Tanatcason and Trepetnica barracks, the village of Sriegnibosch with beech and orchids, the Mea stream and well-preserved dry terraces.
The heart of the village, suspended on the Naviglio.
Narrow streets and houses leaned, with the characteristic corzos, arc covered passages built by the maistos de muru, the masons masons.
More than 300 hectares of pine forest between the city and the sea, with paths, bike routes and kayaks in the canal.
A convent complex in the center.
Neo-Gothic building in cast iron and glass, fish market until the late twentieth century, today room for small conventions and exhibitions.

Since 1993 the Fondazione Sartirana Arte has been managing the interior of the castle with one of the most complete museum routes of Lomellina: contemporary silver and artist jewels, and cataloged works including sculptures by Fausto Melotti, Arnaldo Pomodoro, Alik Cavaliere, Marcello Pirro and Paolo Cristiani; exhibitions of painting, sculpture and handicraft are held in the castle. La Pila, an eighteenth-century building for the processing of rice restored as an exhibition space between 1990 and 1996, hosts antiques and vintage design exhibitions and a permanent exhibition dedicated to designer Ken Scott. Italia.it advises you to check the timetables before the visit.

Municipality of the Reggiana plain with a small 1911 municipal theatre decorated by Luigi Pillitu, the neoclassical town hall of 1889 by Giuseppe Aimi and the church of San Giorgio, rebuilt in 1879 with a 36-metre bell tower.
On the edge of the village, overlooking the Germano Valley, it is known for its golden wooden baroque altar and the procession of July 2nd with which the shepherds were welcomed back.
Science and art together.

In the monastery, where in 1465 the German clerics Pannartz and Sweynheym implanted the first typography of Italy: it holds codes, parchments and the first incunabula printed in Italy, with about 100,000 volumes. Access to the library requires the age and identity document.
The viewpoint on the Etruscan Coast.

Opened in 1999 on the first floor of Villa Arbusto, Ischia tells from prehistory to the Roman age through the artifacts of Pithecusae, founded in the eighth century BC by Greci dell'Eubea and dug by Giorgio Buchner since 1952: accessories of the necropolis of San Montano, the crater of the shipwreck of local production and the Cup of Nestor, with an epigram in Euboic alphabet that recalls the Iliad Cup. A section illustrates businesses with Near East, Carthage, Etruria and Sardinia.
The painters of Racconigi.
Walk through palm trees, magnolias, flowerbeds with exotic plants and classical and late liberty palaces, with a view of the Strait; D'Annunzio called it the most beautiful kilometer in Italy.
Romanesque church of 1160, on the outskirts of the village, which was the parish church of Perfugas until the seventeenth century, when Santa Maria degli Angeli replaced it.

Cinta of about 1.9 kilometers in uncertain work, with perfect rectangular plan, with round and square towers and four doors: Porta Napoli to the east, Porta Fiume to the south, Porta Roma to the west and Porta Piedimonte to the north; the doors have been partially restored.

Arch of about 400 meters of fine white sand with pink reflections for the fragments of coral, dunes with centuries-old junipers and granite cliffs at the ends; on the north promontory, the Cappuccino rock, stands a sixteenth-century watchtower. Sea usually calm and shallow that slopes gently; refreshment point, charter boats and parking lots. Crowded in the middle of summer: better May, June, September or October.
Fresh water and brackish water just a stone's throw from the sea.

Tourist center of the Modena Apennines at 791 meters, in panoramic position, announced by the Tower of the Bastille; in the territory the Romanesque parish church of Rocca Santa Maria, the medieval villages of Pompeano and Monfestino, the Museum Garden of the Ancient Rose of Montagnana and the waterfalls of the Bucamante.

Built in the tenth century on a cliff above the Pavone stream, it belonged to the archbishops of Volterra, the Pannocchieschi, the Municipality of Siena and finally to the Barons Sergardi of Siena until the beginning of the twentieth century. The north and east walls retain their original appearance; they include the church of San Niccolò, renovated in the seventeenth century.
The cave houses dug by hand.
The smallest village in the Park, above the lake.

In the hamlet of Torre Paponi, the Baroque parish church of Santi Cosma e Damiano overlooks a small square with a colorful cobblestone; in the hamlet there are also the Oratory of the Annunziata, the Museum of Sacred Art and Confraternities and the Museum of Jar.
The 19th century theater of the village.

Natural park in the Vercelli plain, completely surrounded by rice fields: a planiziale Padano forest predominantly of querco-carpineto on the relief of the Costa, with a black alder anet in the northern marshland and rich in resurgences. According to the Municipality, the rules of care still in force date back to 1275, when the Marquis of Monferrato Guglielmo the Great donated the wood to the families of Trinesi \"participants" .

Romanesque chapel among the orchards with external frescoes and interiors by Giacomino d'Ivrea of 1463; from here comes a crucifix of 12th century goldsmiths today in the museum of the Cathedral of Aosta.

Common at the foot of Mount Avena, known for its brewery founded in 1897; between seventeenth-century villas such as Villa Pasole-Berton and churches born on the ruins of ancient castles, rises to the Passo Croce d'Aune and the sanctuary of Saints Tiburzio and Susanna.
visits to the village of Monte Antuni only with guided tour and by reservation

On the hill preserves the medieval system and the ancient names of the streets: Piazza degli Eroi ("u sieggiu") the Door of Cosenza on the road to Catanzaro and Giudecca with narrow alleys and arches.
The natural mummies of Urbania.

The village rises on a spur of limestone rock on the Valle del Marmo Platano, with houses leaning like in a nativity scene: at the top the Pianello preserves the medieval system with the houses leaning against the ancient walls and traces of Rome, at the bottom a row of Renaissance buildings. In the village you can wind the hierarchy on the places of San Gerardo Maiella.
The relic of the patron next to the palace.
A ghost village in the woods.

About 1 km from the center, on the road to Gricignano-Aversa, the medieval village brings together a 16th century tower without entry to the ground (guards climbed with ropes, whose signs remain on the windowsills), guarded the streets between Aversa, Acerra, Capua and Naples, and an 18th century farmhouse with a large courtyard, aisles and cellars, belonged for a period to the Pignatelli. In 1713 the bridge of Teverolaccio was the scene of a clash with the French. The municipality indicates free access.

Tourist ring from Torre Pellice of 3 hours and 40 with 500 m of difference in altitude, for Ponte Blancio, Colletto, Rocca Budet, Pian di Arbre and Costa Lorens; a variant passes from the house of Giosuè Gianavello to Gianavella, today museum and guesthouse.

Natural monument since 1994: reliefs formed by volcanic activity of 500,000-600,000 years ago, with the Monte Santo torso of cone and Monte Ruju with its volcanic branches; Montiju Tundu, Badde Ortolu and sas Baddes the view sweeps over the terraced valleys dug by streams.

Romanesque-Gothic T-shaped building with three priests and two towers, consecrated in 1338 by the patriarch of Aquileia Bertrando. It preserves an organ of 1792 by G. Callido and is considered an exemplary monument of post-earthquake restoration.

The residence of the lords of Andria, from Del Balzo to Carafa who rebuilt it after 1552: three floors in limestone around courtyards, with chapel, two external monumental stairs and the Carafa coat of arms on the facade.
Built in 1221 by the Municipality of Parma next to the Duomo; for centuries used as a stone quarry for the houses of the village, remains the ruins, restored since 2004.
The "Sistina" of Bormio.
14th century frescoes in the oldest church in the country.
The aperitif in front of the Arena.
Probably of the twelfth century, facade with a hut with rosette and protire on thirteenth-century lions; the Chapel of the Risen Christ is attributed to Bernardino de Lera.
Three hundred frescoes in one of the oldest churches in the upper valley.
The ancient Jewish quarter preserves the synagogue, the oven for unleavened bread and the courtyard for the feast of Sukkot; the 'giro d'aria' dates back to the fifteenth century.
The grave of a king of Lucan from 2500 years ago.

Roman hydraulic work to supply Atheste (Este): a system of tunnels of more than 100 meters dug in the riolite, with walls covered with large tiles, niches for the lamps and a collection basin, the water caput, from which a duct ran for about 10 km. Freed from debris by the municipality in 1970-71, when a poplar wooden boat was found there, and made it more accessible in 1999-2000.
Renaissance villa with frescoes by Raffaello and his school, including the Loggia of Love and Psyche.
€5, reduced €2 (18-25 years)
Faunistic park where you can observe and learn about the most typical animals of the Valdostano alpine environment and the local flora.
The bell tower of 48 meters that marks the village.

Sanctuary village with a church perhaps of Byzantine origin, surrounded by a novenary of more than one hundred muristenes, the houses built in the seventeenth century to accommodate the faithful in the nine days of the feast of the saint.

Reserve with beech, maple, holm oak, willow and chestnut trees and an oak that can reach 40 meters; the Path of the Patriarchs is known for the scallops of secular oaks. Walks from 5 to 15 km, with panoramic views of Etna and the Alcantara Valley.
On the hill, the castle restored in the eighties with the clock tower; below, the church of San Rocco at the bottom of a boulevard of hippocastans.
17th century Sanctuary in Madonna del Monte, destination of the popular feast of August 5, once accompanied by a fair.
Walk on Garda between fishing houses and medieval walls.
The small port from which the ferries depart to the Tremiti Islands; behind it remain the ruins of the abbey of Calena.
The village of fishermen and dried fish.

Church with origins in the IX century, Romanesque in origin and then renovated in several styles, overlooking the lake at the top of the historic center; inside frescoes and, on the main altar, a painting of the Assumption Madonna. Sunday Mass at 11:30.
The fishing village became pearl of Garda.

Romanesque rectorial church of the 10th century on the hill above the center, once part of the manor of Piazza Castello; it has a single nave interior with wooden trusses and frescoes, recently restored, attributed to Martino da Verona and Battista da Vicenza, students of Pisanello. The oldest part is the small crypt on pillars with Roman capitals; from 1855 every August 5th we go up on pilgrimage to Our Lady of the Snow.
One of the oldest churches in the region.
The detective's house that challenged the mob.
Waterfall and mill on the Mignone.
One of the best views of the lake.

Borgo della valle del Cesano that preserves the structure of the castle with walls, arches and towers, grown around the Romanesque-Gothic Benedictine Abbey of San Lorenzo, built with materials of the Roman city of Suasa; in the sixteenth century Palazzo Della Rovere are located the Teatro Tiberini and the civic museums, and in the territory there are the castles of Montalfoglio and San Vito sul Cesano.
Trulli and holm oaks above the plain of olive trees.
open from April to October, entrance only with guided tour fee (in-Lombardy)

The only mountain town in the area, with 17 villages on the slopes of the Apuan Alps, is located in Levigliani: the Antro del Corchia and the Piegata Stone Museum, in Sant'Anna the places of memory of the Nazi massacre of 12 August 1944, the Gold Medal at the Military Valor in 1970.
An Etruscan tomb intact outside the center.
An intact noble residence in Valtellina.
Warm water known for 2,000 years.

Rebuilt from 1764 on a project attributed to Ermenegildo Sintes on medieval remains, with a quadrangular plan of about 50 by 45 meters with angular towers; the earthquake of 1783 caused the south wing to collapse. From its position you can see the Aeolians and the Strait.

Catacombs along the Appian Way to the fifteenth mile, under church and convent of Santa Maria della Stella (mid XVI century, current appearance since 1687), used for burials from the end of the third-beginning IV century; the central crypt was frescoed in successive epochs. Next to the cemetery of cholera, where in 1867 more than 500 citizens were buried. Free admission with voluntary contributions.

Villa built around the middle of the first century BC by the senatorial family of the Saturnini Volusii: the first owner was Q. Volusio, known to Cicero; his son L. Volusio Saturnino, consul in 12 BC, added new mosaics and a great peristyle with a larary with statues of the ancestors. On a panoramic terrace, it develops on two levels separated by a cryptoportico, with atrium, cubicles, triclino and table and mosaic floors restored under roofs. Discovered by chance in 1961 with the work of the Autostrada del Sole, which cut it in two, it was excavated between 1962 and 1971.
The fortress, of early medieval origin (IX century according to Emilia-Romagna Turismo), is the historical symbol of the village and testifies its castle origins; today it houses the Town Hall.
The highest point of the village, with a view to the sea.

About 3 km from the village, Etruscan necropolis used between VII and V century B.C. with chamber graves dug in the rock of tuff: so far about 24 monumental burials have been identified, including the so-called Red Tomb. You can visit with the ticket of the Museo Civita.
The wrought iron with the force of water.
The open arms of Volare on the sea.
The church-fortress of the village.
In the fifteenth-century halls of the Bishop's Palace, with a Saint John attributed to Caravaggio and the Martyrdom of Saint Catherine of Guido Reni.
A Passion made of shells.
The cathedral in the Palladian palaces.

Also called Rocca Aldobrandesca: built in the Middle Ages for the Aldobrandeschi and then passed to the Pisani as a watchtower on the coast and the plain, on a site inhabited since the late Bronze Age. Irregular pentagonal plan connected to the walls, three corner towers of different shape (round, triangular, quadrangular), restored at the end of the twentieth century; in summer it hosts events.
The country of the bread tradition, with the ovens scattered among the houses.
A neo-Gothic façade in the new city.
The cross of Lorraine on the portal.
The fourteenth-century Palazzo della Ragione overlooks the square, with the coeva Torre civica called ""el Campanon" and the 18th-century Duomo.
Free access, preferably with guided tour booked (tel. ) ISBN 949 961864.
Spa resort with a large swimming pool, a natural cave and a path of hot and cold tubs.
Small oratory with frescoes of the sixteenth century.
Casola is known as the land of forgotten herbs and fruits, with a garden of medicinal plants and a long herbal tradition.

Rebuilt in the 17th century on the site of a sixteenth-century church, it has a rectangular plan with two side chapels adorned with eighteenth-century canvases and a large porch facing the facade. A marble tomb with coat of arms recalls the burial of the Avogadro, feudal lords of the place; the organ is of 1814, the work of Giacinto Bruna of Migliano. The bell tower, restored in the early eighteenth century, is made of stone in the lower part and brick with two orders of mullioned windows at the top.

From the first century AD, just outside the eastern door: cylindrical body with dome on a square base of about 13 meters, circular interior with eight niches; it was church of St. John Gerosolimitano from the end of the thirteenth century and votive chapel to the fallen since 1924, and today houses exhibitions. Attribution to the Acili Glabrions is not proven.
A postwar piety story.

The village of Ciociano is on a hill at 850 m, in front of Torre Cajetani, whose name comes from the Latin "tres watchantes" (the three towers of which one remains); the historic center almost all pedestrian looks over Lake Canterno, regional nature reserve.
Villa of Roman age in Malvaccaro, point of the road of ancient Potentia, opened by the Superintendence for guided tours on special occasions.
Thousands of history at the top of the hill.
Understand fossils and excavations of Santu Antine before climbing the hill.
The palace seat of the town hall in Piazza del Duomo, unmistakable for its color.
Church of the XVI century dedicated to Santa Maria Assunta and San Francesco, which in addition to religious services hosts exhibitions, concerts of sacred music and conferences.
The medieval castle.

Built in 1602-1605 on a project by Gherardo Mechini and wanted by Grand Duke Ferdinando I, a Latin cross with portico on three sides; in the lunettes of the loggia the seventeenth-century frescoes by Giovanni da San Giovanni with the Miracles of the Madonna di Fontenuova, inside an Adoration of the Magi by Matteo Rosselli.
In the Gulf of Baratti the necropolis of the only Etruscan city on the sea, with Etruscan settlements, Roman ruins and the medieval fortress.
On the shore of a stream, where farmers grind flour for home or for sale.
The 16th-century triptych found.

Rebuilt at the beginning of the seventeenth century in place of an ancient temple (later portal dated 1611), with brick façade and simple stone portal; single nave interior with four chapels on the side, transept and octagonal dome, eighteenth-century altars and paintings of the seventeenth century.

Location of the MUSE di Trento born in 1899: rocks, minerals and fossils tell with videos, games and installations the geological history of the valley; in summer workshops and excursions to the fossil atoll of Latemar.
