Public market of flavia age, not a temple: porch courtyard with 36 shops and a thòlos in the center; the columns show the holes of marine molluscs that record the rise and descent of the ground for bradisism.

The oldest sanctuary of Senorbì, presumably built in the last quarter of the 13th century as the church of Santa Maria of the village of Segolay, attested from 1215 and disappeared at the end of the 17th century. In square sandstones, it had semicircular apse and unique hall with wooden trusses; the current façade incorporates the Romanesque one with pointed-shaped hanging arches, with a portal and a large sailing bell tower. Party in early August.
Three thousand objects of peasant life re-enacted.
Attached to the Cathedral, it preserves in the chapel of St. Joseph silvereries, vestments, chorals and a 17th century Flemish tapestry.
An ancient royal hunting house between ibex and chamois.
The medieval ruins overlooking the island.
A wild gorge just a stone's throw from the country.
The good living room of the city.

Built between the end of the nineteenth century and the beginning of the twentieth century next to Villa Fortunata, the palace that Armando Raggio had built between 1882 and 1885. It is a hybrid between auditorium and botanical greenhouse: stage in masonry with mouthpiece that preserves traces of floral decorations, iron platea separated from the stage by a curved moulding.
Art nouveau theater of the 1920s, consolidated after the 1980 earthquake and reopened in 1992; 120 square meters stage and room for almost 500 seats.
From the river to the summit of Genzana.
The most famous sight on the towers.

The ancient Allifae in the middle valley of Volturno: the Roman belt almost intact with a rectangular plan with four doors, the amphitheatre discovered in 1976, the mausoleum called "Pantheon of Alife" , the Norman cathedral with the crypt and the national archaeological museum.

Piceno village, home of St. James of Marca (1393-1476): in the historic centre Piazza dell'Aquila, the Benedictine church of St. Leonardo and the oratory on the birthplace of the saint; just outside the sanctuary of Santa Maria delle Grazie, which preserves its body, and the museums with the 61 codes of its library.
The house where according to tradition the poet Quinto Orazio Flacco was born, visible only from the outside; in the center also the statue dedicated to him.

Trabocco in the hamlet of Vallevò, about 10 minutes drive from the center, reached by a wooden footbridge next to the Via Verde dei Trabocchi; the owner tells the story of the overflows, the laws that protect them, how they are built and how the net works. The other overflows of the territory are Punta Cavalluccio, Punta Isolata, Sasso della Cajana and Punta Punciosa.
The 300 nobles.
The shrine of the Fujenti and its secular ex-vote.

At the foot of Mount Cinto, in the Euganean Hills, the municipality houses the Geopaleontological Museum of Cava Bomba with the fossil fishes of 92 million years ago, the path that goes up to the remains of the medieval castle, and in Valnogaredo the eighteenth-century church of San Bartolomeo and the Roman galleries of Mount Vendevolo.
Oak of about 450 years, 30 meters high and with a trunk of 6.5 meters of circumference, national monument since 2000; near the Municipality has realized a small natural amphitheatre.
Built in 1473 by the Lateran canons, a single nave with chapels and fifteenth-century paintings brought to light by the restorations.
The prehistory of the Diano Valley.

Gothic parish with a rectangular plan, with eight chapels, marble altar and once painted by Oreste Parenti in 1902. The bell tower has four bells: the oldest, of 1608, bears the inscription "Seligas." Next to the church there is the grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes; the feast of the patroness, at the end of July, has procession in traditional clothes, dances and poetic competitions.

Tratto di circa 2.6 km tra Fondi e Itri in the limestone gorge of the Aurunci, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2024: without asphalt, it shows in sequence the paved road of the Caracalla age (216 A.D.), the Renaissance road of Philip II of Spain (1568) with epigraphs and bridge rebuilt in 2004, and the Bourbon road of Ferdinand IV (1768). Above the gorge, the Fort of Sant'Andrea, built in 1806, rises on the remains of a late-public sanctuary of Apollo.

Borgo della Grecia Salentina with the Castello de' Monti from the Baroque façade at the entrance of the historic center, the Church Mother of St. Nicholas and the Arc Lucchetti; the monuments have panels in Italian, English and Griko and the village hosts the first stage of the Night of the Taranta.

Scattered municipality of the Strona Valley, near the north-western shore of Lake Orta, formed by the villages of Strona, Luzzogno, Inuggio, Fornero, Forno, Sambughetto and Campello Monti; among woods and alpine pastures offers the sanctuary of the Colletta, the Museum of sacred art of Forno, the caves of Sambughetto and the Walser village of Campello Monti in the Natural Park of Alta Valsesia and Alta Val Strona.
Medieval villages with a view to the sea.

It is reachable on foot with 738 meters of difference in altitude, with views of the plain and the western Alps; other destinations are the Montebracco Cross, the Bric La Plata (1731 m), the Madonna d'Oriente (782 m) in a plateau between high chestnut trees, the Chapel of San Bernardo Agnelli (1125 m, also by mountain bike) and that of San Bernardo di Gilba (1517 m).
The canyon of Sagittarius under the village.

Church of medieval origins, documented in 1174 when Count Guido di Biandrate donated it to the Knights Templar; the present building is eighteenth-century, with a single nave. It is reached with a detour of just over a kilometer from the crossroads of Stroppera, along the route Vie Verdi del Riso.
In the Bourbon castle, it preserves the most significant finds of the wrecks of the Roman age.
From the village you can see the islands.
The Romanesque on the gravina.
museum €3,50, reduced €2; mastio €2
The rocks on the other side.

Homeland of Titian at the foot of the Antelao, with the birthplace of the painter, Titian Square dominated by the Palace of the Magnificent Community (site of the Archaeological Museum) and the Museum of Glass with over 4,000 finds.
Fanzago's bronzes.

Castle documented since 1213, with the first stone walls between the end of the thirteenth and early fourteenth centuries, looted and burned in 1446 by the troops of Sigismondo Malatesta; to the ancient nucleus you enter from an arch under the civic tower, already bell tower of the church of San Rocco (1604-1840). In the village, the late 19th century wash-house with a permanent nativity scene and the public oven of about one hundred loaves.

The promenade with the Art Nouveau buildings of the 1920s, including the Gran Caffè Margherita designed by Alfredo Belluomini and Galileo Chini, the Warehouse Duilio and the Book Gallery, and the great hotel Prince of Piedmont.
The sea under the ancient city.

Scientific and didactic exhibition hosted in the Astronomical Observatory Colle Leone, with sections of paleontology, mineralogy and meteorite: the first illustrates the history of life on the planet, the second exhibits good quality samples and the collection of meteorites completes the path between terrestrial and extraterrestrial environment.
Orange Flag since 2025, the Langhe Sentinel perched on a ridge with the Alps in the background, between UNESCO-listed vineyards and the Pelaverga.

Inaugurated in 2002 in the historic Palazzo Mancini, it is spread over three floors with zampogne from all over the world and different eras, wind instruments, iconographic and literary documentation, historical photographs and the reconstruction of the workshop of the artisans of Scapolesi; there are also an acoustic listening room, a film library and a permanent nativity scene of the Neapolitan school of the Capuan masters of San Gregorio Armeno. A multimedia app allows you to listen to the sounds of the instruments. Timetable indicated by italia.it: Friday-Sunday 10-12 and 16-18.
A sixteenth-century palace with painted loggia, today city hall.
Frescoes from the fifteenth century and a golden altar from the early seventeenth century.

Church of very ancient origins and little documented; it preserves a saints waterworks of 1274, a statue of the Madonna delle Grazie of the fifteenth century and a ciborium of Niccolò da Cornedo of 1438.
View of Lake Pieve.
Cycle path of about 8 km on the old SEFTA railway track that leads directly to Modena, among the vineyards of one of the finest qualities of Lambrusco.

A village nestled between vineyards and mountains at the foot of Cansiglio, heir of the ancient Canipa, with the ruins of the castle built around the Mille; it shares with Polcenigo the UNESCO Palù di Livenza pile-up site and preserves the Museum of cycling      • Toni Pessot • and the Museum of the miner dedicated to emigration to mines.
The cultural hub of the main square.

Viuzze, shops and colorful houses with the workshops of the master ceramicists who paint by hand; the tradition dates back at least to the Middle Ages and was renewed in the twenties of the twentieth century by German craftsmen with a new style inspired by daily gestures. Among the buildings symbolizes the Fabbrica Solimene, designed in the fifties by the architect Soleri.

New land walled on the Panaro and capital of traditional balsamic vinegar: the Rangoni Rocca with the Court of Taste, the Torrione with the Antiquarium and the secret cell of Messer Filippo, the Balsamic Museum in Villa Fabriani and the feast of the Mast Cot in October.
The smallest town in Italy, the most beautiful village in Italy, closed in the gorge of the Dora Baltea under the fort of the nineteenth century, along the Via delle Gallie and Via Francigena.
Gagini's polychrome triptych.
A walk in the village of the alabaster.
Overlooking Piazza Silvestri, it is considered a jewel of Umbrian Romanesque architecture.

Started in 1993 by Centro Studi Piero Ginocchi and opened in 2006: five historic bottling plants, over 15,000 full bottles and more than 80,000 labels; the oldest document is a decree by the Grand Duke of Tuscany of 1583 on the waters of Monte Catini. The mineralogical section exhibits minerals of Verbano Cusio Ossola, including the rare gasparite, roggianite and paraniite, a new species recognized in 1995. Open seasonally or by reservation.

Monumental fountain of the II-I century B.C. of which the architect is known: his signature is written in Greek letters with blue Egyptian glass tiles. Acquired and opened to the public in July 2020, it completed the urban archaeological park.

On the hillside along the road to Valentano remain the traces of the ancient Visentium, set in flames by Urbano IV in 1264, rebuilt and finally abandoned at the beginning of the XIX century; the archaeological park of Monte Bienzo also includes an Etruscan necropolis.
The tower over the upper Panaro valley.
The sanctuary of the Biella Alps.
The big roof.

In the center you can still see traces of the ancient walls that surrounded the village, the clock Tower and the remains of an archaic necropolis. The bronze statue of Zeus (about 530 BC), found in 1961 at the intersection of via Mazzini and via Fabio Pittore, is exhibited at the National Archaeological Museum of Taranto.

In the ski and hiking area of San Martino in Valle (Reinswald), in the eastern Sarentine Alps at 2,460 meters: you climb the cable car and then walk from the Pichlbergalm or Pfnatschalm; in winter a chairlift leads from the Pfnatschalm to the Sattele. 360 degree view all year round, including the Dolomites.

Church of court behind the Reggia, with architecture and furnishings of the last quarter of the eighteenth century; damaged by the earthquake of 2012, reopened in 2013. Three aisles with B stuccoes. Bossi and dome frescoed by D. Muzzi; canvas by P.M. Ferrari, Laurent Pécheux and G. Baldrighi, a Terracotta Pietà by Laurent Guyard (1775) and the Preaching of St Liborius by G. You call on the high altar. The wooden choir by Michel Poncet and Ignazio Marchetti (1775-77) and the organ by Giuseppe Antonio Serassi (1792-96) are among the most remarkable pieces.
In the Neanderthal House of the Circeo.
Opened in 2006, to discover nature with the five senses.
The nineteenth-century villa on the Chiaia Riviera with the museum Diego Aragona Pignatelli Cortes, period furnishings and the museum of carriages in the park.
Medieval irrigation channels: the first of about 1250 brings water from the valley of Saint-Barthélemy, the second of about 1350 was disputed with Torgnon.
Valnerina in canoe or on foot.

Opened in 1998 and titled Don A. Blessed, he tells the story of Western Lessinia in two rooms. The prehistory section exhibits instruments from the Paleolithic lower than the age of metals, many from the Cave of Fumane and from the Riparo Tagliente of Stallavena: flints, engraved bones, painted stones, the cast of a burial of the upper Paleolithic, the "Sciamano" and a skeleton of bison. The section of paleontology shows marine fossils of the Stone quarries of Prun, including curls, ammonites and large sharks, in particular a cretodus of about 2 meters preserved with a sea turtle, perhaps his last meal: it is the most complete fossil known of this shark. Ground floor accessible by wheelchair; open from July to October Friday, Saturday, Sunday and holidays 9.30-18, the rest of the year by reservation.
The sea is just a stone's throw from the archaeological park.
An interior entirely mosaic.

The city of the two seas, a Ligurian village colored on a promontory between the Bay of Silence and the Bay of Fairy tales, with a historical center of painted facades and portals in slate, the MuSel in Palazzo Fascie Rossi, the Rizzi Gallery, the ring of Punta Manara and the seaside village of Riva Trigoso.

Born as a monastery of Saint Mary of the Order of Saint Damian, it took the name of Saint Rosa in the fourteenth century, when the body of the young patron saint was transferred there; it is the goal of the procession of the Machine.

On the hill about 400 meters from the village, in front of Rivalta: parish until the XVI-XVII centuries, then country church and lazzaretto during the cholera of 1894. A unique nave with a barrel vault and, on the altar, a fresco by Antonio Monevi from the late seventeenth century. You can reach it on foot or by bike on a dirt road between the rows starting from the cemetery; the interior is not open to visitors.
The city's most important art museum.
The fortress surrounded by the moat in the center of the village, with the small room of Diana and Atteone frescoed by Parmigianino and the optical chamber.
The catacombs, born on the site of the martyrdom of San Vittorino, are located under the church and are composed of six rooms dug into the rock.

Karst complex in the Alburni massif, on the left of the Tanagro, which occupies the path of an ancient underground river with caves and tunnels for over 2 km. In 1897 there were found remains of two stilts and objects from the Neolithic to the early Iron Age; there is also a newsstand dedicated to St. Michael Archangel. Open to the public since 1932, they visit with a stretch of boat on the Negro river and then on foot between the Wonder Hall, the Throne Hall and the Grand Cave; the route is suitable for all ages. Admission fee, reduced with Touring card; Touring indicates Tuesday-Sunday 10-12 and 14-18, which may vary.

Dedicated to the most illustrious citizen of Dogliani, President Luigi Einaudi, was realized by the Municipality with the Luigi Einaudi Foundations of Rome and Turin and inaugurated on June 25, 2011. It is located in the Town Hall.
Four centuries of Venetian pottery.

The Bergamo Country of the San Martino Valley, between woods and mountains Treasure and Ocone, linked to the oath of the Lombard League of 1167, which tradition places in the abbey of San Giacomo founded in 1079 by Saint Alberto da Prezzate: basilica, cloisters and museum of the monastery, paths between chestnut trees towards Monte Canto and the first social cellar of the province of Bergamo.

The promenade overlooks the Strait of Messina; the beaches, very white, have low seabed and clear waters, and in the summer the marina is filled with colorful wooden fishing boats. In the village there is also the monument to the sisters Bertè, Loredana and Mia Martini, born in Bagnara.
The Madonna of the Rescue of Berrettaro.
Park warns that descriptions are prior to the 2016 earthquake and some areas may be banned
The white truffle in its capital.

Five-arched stone bridge built in 1556 by the Republic of Venice, immediately after the completion of the fortifications, under the Provveditore Iacobo Gauro remembered by a plaque in Via Dante; it is considered the architectural symbol of the city. Under the arch towards Piazza Ferdinando di Savoia there was Pescarezzo, a fixed fish pond; the only structure of this type still visible on Garda, recently restored, can be seen from the Longolago Bonomi.

The oldest district, with houses arranged in semicircle, paved streets in red and black stone, stairs and walls; in the center of the village the parish church of the Assunta and the church of Santa Marta, the patroness celebrated at the end of July. The women of Gadoni weave to the horizontal frame sa burra, traditional carpet born as a blanket.

Teatro dell'Opera dei Pupi founded in 1887 by puparo don Mariano Pennisi and transferred in 1928 to the current headquarters; the adopted son Emanuele Macrì took him on international tours. Acquired and restored by the Region, it houses the Pennisi-Macrì Theatre Collection with puppets and equipment of the Sicilian theatres, with audioguides.
Airons and wetlands among the rice fields.
Middle Ages and measure of time.
Land Art and Arte Povera freely among the meadows.

Municipality of the upper Sarno valley, about 10 km from Pompeii, known for the protohistoric village of Longola, river settlement on artificial islets discovered in 2000; in the village remain palaces of the late nineteenth century and the characteristic rural houses with dome called "vesuvian trullos."
It hosts temporary exhibitions and a film library with a collection of films and photographs.
A Rolli palace with its furnishings.
You can reach itinerary from Tzanté de Bouva; short panoramic walk suitable for children.

Shortly and easily walking distance from the village, the mill operated only with bad weather, when the mountain water was enough to spin the wheel; in the area there are tables, wooden benches and grills.
Castellano's paintings in an ancient romantic.

Ancient capital of the Malaspina of Spino Secco, where Dante was guest in 1306: in the village the Tower of Dante hexagonale, the House of Dante and the Via Dantis, the Museum of Malaspina Archive; in the territory the Castle of Lusuolo with the Museum of Emigration, Montereggio village of the booksellers and the Sanctuary of the Madonna del Monte.
The triptych of Taddeo di Bartolo on the high altar.

Municipality of the Cuneo plain: in the hamlet Roata Chiusani the small museum house dedicated to Cardinal Michele Pellegrino, born in 1903; in the capital, in the Civic Library, the Sala della Memoria with the permanent exhibition on the Italian Military Interiors.
Three centuries of Italian, French and English gardens.

Born in the granary of the farm Bella Foglia and then extended to the farmhouse, it is the work of the elementary master and collector Ettore Guatelli (1921-2000): about 60,000 objects among agricultural tools and craftsmen, furniture, toys, musical instruments, clothes and photographs, arranged on walls and ceilings in geometric compositions, in rooms dedicated to glass, ceramics, tin, shoes, suitcases, watches. Sections on emigration from Parmense to England and on the wanderings of the show. Open Tuesday-Friday 10-13, Saturday and holidays even 15-18, with guided tours.

The tourist portal of the Metropolitan City indicates the Matrix Church, the sanctuary of Our Lady of the Dajna and ten other churches of the village. Among the works mentioned: a mosaic of St. Cyrus in polychrome majolica of the eighteenth century attributed to the Palermo school, a saintly waterworks in white marble of the fourteenth century and the picture of the Madonna of the Tenerance of the seventeenth century.
A journey of over 20 million years in the geology of Marmilla.
Secular chestnuts, a ruined mill and the robbers' cave.
Reserve along the Arno between Laterina and Terranuova Bracciolini, with hiking trails, paths in the green and birdwatching for the many species of birds; a quiet place for a day in nature.

The medieval nucleus, abandoned in the eighties of the twentieth century when the infiltrations of the artificial lake of Monte Pranu made the houses unworkable; there are few restored stone houses and two of the three Baroque arches that closed the village. Behind the church, artisan workshops where to see the work live. The new village is located a few hundred meters away.

In a typical Sicilian house of the mid-nineteenth century in the historic center of Aci Trezza, next to the church of San Giovanni, with courtyard, small vegetable garden and entrance to lava stone arch. The hall      .The earth trembles ... collects photos and posters of the film by Luchino Visconti shot in Aci Trezza with actors from the village; the Room of the Malavoglia documents the world of fishermen of the mid-nineteenth century with tools, everyday objects, photos taken by Giovanni Verga and letters to his brother Pietro.
The house that marks the freedom of the city.
18th century cloister and staircase.

In Villa Fabriani, decorated with frescoes from the early twentieth century and seat of the Consorteria dell'Aceto Balsamico Tradizionale, tells history and production of traditional balsamic vinegar of Modena. The Touring indicates it as a provisional location pending transfer to the Rock.
The terrace on the Umbra valley.
The highest waterfalls of Sardinia, during the periods of fullness.
The medieval heart of the city of pasta.
The former slaughterhouse of the late nineteenth century, active until 1975 and today centre for culture and contemporary art.

Inside the walls, rebuilt in Baroque style between 1753 and 1756 on a more ancient church of which remains the bell tower of the thirteenth century. In the Chapel of the Effects, he preserves the Triptych of the Saviour of 1501, attributed to the school of Antoniazzo Romano.
The quickest way to understand Modena.
The imposing castle dominates the village; its family chapel preserves frescoes by Antonino Ocello da Ceva, marked as not to be missed.
The first inhabitants of the valley.

Inaugurated in 1998 at the initiative of the Municipality of Varese and Comunità Montana della Valcuvia, it occupies an eighteenth-century rural farmhouse known as the "cà della Maria Gill" which was renovated in the nineties by architects Annig Sarian and Gianni Pozzi. He exhibited the works of Floriano Bodini, animator in the post-war era of existential 'realism and author of medals and great public works such as the Paul VI of the Sacred Mount of Varese and the Duomo of Milan and the monument to the quarrymen of Carrara; every year he hosts exhibitions of Italian and foreign artists, workshops, concerts and meetings. Open Saturday and Sunday 10.30-12.30 and 15-18, on other days by appointment.
the Touring Club indicates temporarily closed the Doge's Palace that hosts it and the MiC card reports closed every day
A set of historical environments designed and inhabited by Alessandro Rossi: a nineteenth-century villa, the park and a model farm. The Rossi Park is a romantic garden at the foot of Mount Summano.
Birdwatching and archaeology in the valley of Liri.
A cave of the Basilian monks.
The rooms where the Western Schism began.
Built between 1363 and 1381, it preserves the Madonna delle Grazie by Giovanni da Piamonte (1456), a follower of Piero della Francesca.
Built in the first century B.C. under the hole, it is about 57 meters long: ten parallel rooms with barrel vaults carved into the rock; in the last room the lead fistulae that fed it.
The 18th century church next to the castle.

Medieval village with houses that make up walls, narrow alleys and arched underpasses; the Houses of the Lombards, built by workers of the North between the fifteenth and seventeenth centuries, are fortified houses that exhibited the prestige of the families. Near a carved portal of 1666 with symbols of the cult of San Domenico; the Pazziana Porta, surviving of the walls, leads to a terrace on the Sagittarius and Castrovalva.
The University's headquarters since 1492, with the famous Anatomical Theatre and the chair of Galileo Galilei.

Small village of Alto Molise about 1,000 meters on the slopes of Monte Saraceno, of Sannita origin, with the ancient nucleus framed by the two great rocks of the Morgia of the Tower and the Morgia of the Castle; just south there is the Italic Sanctuary, the most important place of cult of the Sannitic state, with theater, temple and Domus publica.
Before or after visiting Roselle.
In the eighteenth century Villa Henderson, historical finds and a modern didactic itinerary on the evolution and life of the Mediterranean.

Fossils and rocks of Carnia recount over 400 million years of geological evolution of the Carnic Alps, from paleozoic fossils of when the area was covered by the sea up to changes prior to the alpine orogenesis. Panels, interactive teaching tools and laboratories on fossilization, classification and recognition of rocks, with specialized library; it is part of the CarniaMusei network. Times to ask CarniaMusei.
The church of the patron, in stone of the Cucco.
The sanctuary reported by Visit Tuscany in the Prato area.

Opened in 1973 in a room next to the parish church with archaeological and lapidary section (the findings of Agrons of the IV-XVI centuries), since 2010 it has a section in the former social dairy Agrons-Cella (1909-1911), where there are also some dairy equipment: textiles, wooden statues, silverware, vestments and finds of San Martino di Ovaro. The main piece is the wooden group of St. Martin who gives the mantle to the poor, late work of Domenico da Tolmezzo (before 1507), who found the original polychrome with the restoration of 1981-1982. It is part of the CarniaMusei network.
free (15/6-15/9), off-season €5, families €10
It can be reached with an easy walk from the Colle San Carlo; in winter cross-country trails and rackets.
By bike along the Brenta.

On the hydrographic left of the Adige, Cologna Veneta houses in Piazza Duomo, in the palace of the former Monte di Pietà, the Civic Archaeological Museum born in 1896 after the discovery of the necropolis of Baldaria; here ends the cycle path of Treviso-Ostiglia, which from 2025 continues towards Cerea.
Europe's largest salt pans and their water birds.

Just outside the ancient center, a convent with two courtyards of the convent friars, suppressed in the French Decade; the church has golden wooden altars, statues and paintings of the seventeenth century and a 17th century fresco of the Madonna with the Child and Saint Anne.

Reserve at the village gates, made of beech and chestnut woods, peaks and streams. The waterfall comes from a karst spring near the summit of the reliefs and makes a jump of 80 meters, indicated as the highest natural jump of the Apennines; underground open caves, wells and sinkholes. You visit along hiking trails.
The best preserved medieval castle in Tuscany.
The bridge opened in 2009, 466 meters long.

Built in the fifteenth century and still parish church of San Giorgio between the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries, it preserves a remarkable bell tower of the time; the interior with three naves without transept, with rectangular apse, shows frescoes from the fifteenth century that emerge from the plaster and in the apse a Madonna with Child dated 1400. Visitable during religious services.
Where was the Pietà di Palestrina.
The view dedicated to Celeste.

Area of the ancient Mother Church buried by lava in March 1669, of which survived the bell tower called by the mysterious  "U'U Campanarazzu" bell tower. The park, donated to the parish in the sixties by Vespasiano Trigona, Duke of Misterbianco, includes an 8,000 m2 century-old oak grove escaped the cast and the remains of the buried church.
Large blocks of stone carved into the rock that emerge from the ground; they served to press grapes and olives, but according to some hypotheses they would also be pagan altars.

Village along the Via Salaria, on the left of the river Velino at the foot of Mount Nuria covered with woods and chestnut groves, moved downstream in the fourteenth century with the foundation of the  "Borghetto"; it preserves the Flavi Nympheus of a Roman villa of the first century and an ethnographic and naturalistic civic museum in the Town Hall.
The Salento peasant life in a ducal palace.

Born from the donation of the notary Luigi Lechi to the Municipality (2005): 185 paintings, drawings and prints, a hundred porcelains and a library of 1,500 volumes of art history, with the Lombard school from the sixteenth to the eighteenth century and the painting of reality in the center. Among the works the Moretto and seven paintings by Giacomo Ceruti, the Pitocchetto, including ...The woman who makes the stocking (about 1730). More than 1,500 m2 on two floors in the Tabarino Palace, already town hall. Open from Wednesday to Sunday; admission fee.
The hills of Fauglia painted by a post-macchiaiolo.
The unfinished architect of Mole.
Italian and international contemporary art from 1945 to today in the former headquarters of Max Mara, about 2 km from the center (bus 1 or 4).

Artificial wetland born as an example of phytopurification of the waters, recognized by the Region as a special protection zone: real germans, swans, cormorants and herons, along a cycle-naturalistic itinerary. From Mirandola you will find the Chico Mendes cycle path on the old railway.
The Baroque backdrop of the square.
Palaces noble and fifteenth-century views.
The city of the Lombard princes.
Flamingos and bottarga in the large lagoon.
The great Sassu and his horses in the country of childhood.
Mattia Priests in her hometown.
An easy walk to the castles.

Parish church wanted by Duke Pasquale Marotta, the last feudal man of Cerasuolo (dead in 1884), started at the end of the nineteenth century and completed at the beginning of the twentieth century. Destroyed during the Second World War, it was rebuilt thanks to the abbot of Montecassino Gregorio Diamare; damaged by the earthquake of 1984, it had cover and facade restored in 2005. It has three aisles and a stone facade, raised on the road and reached by an external staircase, marked by parasts with doric capitals.
Two united rock churches, six centuries of painting.

Municipality of five villages climbed from the mountain to the sea, Castagnola, Costa, Setta, Ravecca and Anzo, among the most beautiful villages in Italy: towers against pirates, the church of San Martino with the pala di Bernardo Strozzi and the bike path on the old railway track.
The baroque palace seat of the Pinacoteca civica and exhibitions.
Of seventeenth-century origin and dedicated to the Santissimo Salvatore, with baroque portal and bell tower in granite blocks.

Taranto inland town in the Regional Park Terra delle Gravine, divided by the gravina of San Marco in the districts of Terra and Santa Caterina, connected by a dizzying bridge; in the gravines there are about thirty Byzantine rock churches, and the city was the set of the Capernaum of the Gospel according to Matthew of Pasolini (1964).

Under the portico of the Town Hall, built in 1713 for the image of Our Lady frescoed in the sixteenth century by the castle painter Cesare Castagnola, to which between 1708 and 1712 were attributed numerous healings.

Walled city divided in two by the Adda, Orange Flag of Touring: the sixteenth-century walls of about 2 km contain the Casematte, vaulted rooms all connected to each other, next to the parish church of San Bassiano, the Tower of Guado and three museums.
The war told by a painter from the village.

Country of the Val d'Arda mentioned in 844, on a passage of the Arda stream and between the Pliocenic calanques of the "clays of Lugagnano": in its territory the Roman city of Veleia with the forum and the Antiquarium, the church of San Zenone with a canvas by Luigi Crespi and the eighteenth-century Palazzo Gandolfi.
The daily life in the castle, in blocks and majolica.

In the historic Palazzo Ducale, managed by the Accademia Italiana del Peperoncino: salt on tools and objects ('Fantasia of every part') on the geographical origins of the plant, on seeds, spices and sauces, and a video room with posters and satirical cartoons; among the works a lithography by Renato Guttuso and an image from a recipe book of the sixteenth century.
Guttuso in his city, in a 18th century villa.
Cogne's lace.

Small village on the ancient Via Amerina, between Todi and Amelia, among the youngest municipalities in Italy but with protohistoric and Roman settlements; in the hamlet of Dunarobba the Fossil Forest preserves trunks of coniferous giants of the Pliocene, and in the territory rise the castles of Dunarobba, Sismano, Toscolano and Santa Restituta.
The entrance door to the center, with Renaissance and Baroque buildings.

The hamlets preserve numerous churches with works of art and glazed terracottas of the school of Della Robbia: San Lorenzo a Baldignano with crypt of the eleventh century, Sant'Andrea della Torre a Mignano, documented since 1085 and linked to a small fortified village on the road to Verna, the Hermitage of the Madonna del Faggio in Cercetole, of the first fifteenth century, and the churches of Saints James and Christopher in Montalone and Saints Peter and Paul in Valsavignon, with works of the sixteenth century.

Between Grosio and Grosotto, the most important testimony of the ancient populations of Valtellina: the Rupe Magna, discovered in 1966 and among the rocks engraved larger than the Alps, brings more than 5000 figures from the end of the Neolithic to the Iron Age (armed men, animals, cups, geometric shapes) and a double serpentiform figure of about 20 meters. The visit, on barefoot and with the operator of the park, starts from April to October from Tuesday to Sunday at 10.30, 14 and 16; in the park also the Antiquarium Ca' del Cap and a naturalistic path in the chestnut grove.
The café in the square in front of the lake.
opening on request
A palace that hosted an emperor.
The temple of the work.
The square at the foot of the towers with the monument of Augusto Murer to Giacomo Matteotti, born in Rovigo and killed by the fascist regime in 1924.

Municipality of Val di Vara, in the hinterland of La Spezia: in Novà di Zignago was found on 29 December 1827 the first stele statue of Lunigiana, and the territory preserves the Ligurian castle and the ancient Via dei Monti towards Mount Dragonone.
The card of the most beautiful villages in Italy indicates you in restoration
Open only by reservation
The village-fortress on the ridge between Tuscany and Emilia.
Valdostana beekeeping.

In Campocecina, on the Apuan Islands: a quarry on whose walls have been engraved phrases of poets and famous characters for the 2002 Biennale and the park with statues of the international sculpture symposium dedicated to the Shoah.
A 14th century church with precious paintings.

The two fortifications that guard the villages on the banks of the Black: in Precetto a castle on the slope with triangular plan with square watchtower on top, in Matterella a square mast with cylindrical bastions.
The streets with concentric circles of the medieval village.
The casts and paintings that tell the Certosa shipyard closely.

Opened in October 2024 with the permanent collection reordered: over 200 works, from the Gulf Prize founded in 1933 on the idea of Marinetti to donations Cozzani, with works by Lucio Fontana and Marina Abramović. The 1879 building was a female school.

The square houses the statue of Massimiliano I of Habsburg, by Edmund Hofman, remembered as the first foreign monarch in Friuli (Cormons passed to the Habsburgs between 1497 and 1521), and the statue of the Freedom of Marcello Mascherini.
See the potters on the lathe in the caves.

Since 2011 the tower hosts on two floors the exhibition on the history of Glorenza: trade and defence, market and crafts, local curiosities, with panels on the 16th century reconstruction and fortification. From the tower you walk along the path of the round and the blackbirds and you visit the round corner tower. Open from May to September, Tuesday-Friday 14-17 (July and August also Monday afternoon), in October 14-16; free entry with the Reschensee Guest Card.
The villa linked to Maria Callas.

In the Rocca's rooms, it enhances the archaeological heritage of the north-east of Cremona with the findings of about thirty years of research by the Archaeological Group and the discoveries of the Superintendence, in a path from prehistory to the seventeenth century. Closed on Monday, open Tuesday-Friday in the morning and on weekends also in the afternoon.
Chapel of the castle, stage of the Sentieri dei Frescanti del Roero: ceilings in trompe-l'oeil with angels, attributed to the Operts and in baroque style, including an angel showing the Holy Shroud.
The meadows of the Tenda Hill.
A parish church outside of town.
The story of Parabiago and his cabinetmaker Maggiolini.

Crossed from east to west by the Naviglio della Martesana, Cernusco sul Naviglio preserves the eighteenth-century Villa Alari by Giovanni Ruggeri, the Villa Greppi seat of the Town Hall and Villa Uboldo, and a pedestrian historical centre with a path dedicated to silk.

Medieval village of the East Verona among the vineyards of the Soave, closed by the walls of the Scaligere with 24 crenellated towers and dominated by the Castle on Mount Tenda; along Via Roma line up the Palazzo di Giustizia of 1375, the Gothic-Venetian Palazzo Cavalli and the Palazzo del Capitano, seat of the Municipality, while outside the walls stands the sanctuary of the Bassnella, starting point of the walk in the Classic Soave.

Difficult 14.5 km return trip (about 6 hours, 990 m of altitude difference) from the Cauriol Refuge in the Sadole Valley along the Austrian Route, a stone mule track between the remains of tunnels, barracks, walkways, stone stairs, stations and cross-linked roads. On the Italian and Austrian peaks, the peak was contested from winter 1915 to August 1916 and the bombings lowered it by six meters; the summit cross rises between rocks and craters. Exposed traits on porphyric rock.
Pers (494 m) is an uninhabited village, with a chapel near the cemetery; from here the path of the Roman bridge is the ancient road connecting with a stone bridge.

Artificial lake born with the dam 80 meters completed in 1939, about 10 km long with 36 km of shores, about 536 meters at the foot of Mount Navegna, at the edge of the Natural Reserve Monte Navegna and Monte Cervia. You can swim, kayak, canoeing, sailing and SUP, fishing all year round; in Castel di Tora nautical circles rent boats and kayaks.
Built with the stones of the Roman theatre.
Silence and forests.

A village of narrow streets, squares, ancient houses and churches; in Via Torino an relief with a disfigured face, attributed by the belief to an exorcism, and an inscription in a mysterious language. The local ham, without preservatives, remains about twenty days in the big salt, is pressed with the 'prigiotto' and seasoned in the cellar from 12 to 20 months; among the dishes there are the carrati with sheep sauce.
The city of Gaudenzio.
The remains of the ancient stadium under Piazza Navona, of which the square retains its shape.
The village church, the result of a construction site that lasted from the 1920s to the 1940s.
Icon building of Italian rationalist architecture designed by Giuseppe Terragni, behind the Duomo.
The village rises on a rocky spike; the old town, dense with nearby houses, narrow alleys and underpasses, is tightened around the stronghold, once protected by thick walls.
The old town is still partly surrounded by the walls, with churches and remains of previous eras re-used in the buildings; from the viewpoint the view stretches over the Diano Valley.
The ancient Alphaternal Nuceria.
The bread of the 16th century straw oven.
Villa with garden where traditional agricultural tools are exposed.
The tombs of the Corgna.

The Molini sul Lemene have existed since at least 1186; the bridge, documented since 1353 and rebuilt in stone in 1554 under the podestà Giulio Valier, in 1918 was mined by the Austrians in retreat but not destroyed.
The market in front of the church.
The symbol of the village, survived four earthquakes.
The view from the tower over the valleys of the Dolo and the Dragon.
The sixteenth and eighteenth century palaces of a large villa of delights.
The gold and inscriptions of a Lucan city.
Built in the 12th century in the civic center of the city, it has been watching over Cremonesi for 900 years; frescoes by Boccaccino and Romanino and the crypt of Sant'Omobono.

Wood of centuries-old oaks, oaks and oaks between 600 and 900 meters, a few kilometers from the village, inhabited by squirrels, badgers, fairies, wild boars and birds like hawks, peaks and buzzards. Old mule tracks lead to an ancient farmhouse, shelter of shepherds and then of the forestkeepers, today a multifunctional classroom; picnic area, excursions and guided tours.
One of the most venerated relics.

In the cloister of the sanctuary, it is part of the circuit of the Sistine Museums of Piceno: personal objects of the saint and works from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century, including his liturgical set (dress and crucifix), a seal with the name of Jesus and a seventeenth-century wooden bust of Neapolitan school; a section is dedicated to Bishop Eugenio Massi, native of Monteprandone and missionary in China.
A naturalistic museum with live animals in the park.
Arezzo capital of gold.
Three centuries of graces received, painted on a table.
The twentieth century in a manifesto.
A Romanesque church linked to the Vitelli.
Baroque with views of the village.

In the center there are medieval houses with turrets and facades decorated in terracotta and fifteenth-century houses in Via Fornasari and Via Marguati; at the entrance of the road to Molino dei Torti survives an arch of the seventeenth century, one of the gates of the walls (Zibide, Molina, Strad'Alzano, Gualdonasce and Tavernelle). In Piazza Vittorio Veneto there is the birthplace of Matteo Maria Bandello.
The most imposing villa of Pedavena, seen from the outside.

Dedicated to the 'ducks', large torches of fir trunks and broom bundles lit and carried on shoulder in procession along the course on the night of December 24: exhibits several 'droplets, a 4 meters high, reconstructions with costume mannequins, photos of the construction phases and the trophy disputed every year from the five districts. He also recalls the 'Shower taken to St Peter's Square in front of John Paul II in 1996.
The Palazzo del Popolo, in the second half of the 13th century, was transformed into the Victory Theatre, built in 1831 and recently restored.
The most imposing dolmen of Sardinia, a few steps from the village.
The cycling bridge and the track along the second river of Tuscany connect the city to Alberese and Marina di Alberese, entering the Maremma Park.

The town overlooking the narrow Tagliamento, with the ruins of the castle on the hill and the churches of Pinzano and Valeriano that keep frescoes and the first triptych of Pordenone; in Borgo Ampiano there is a mill of the fifteenth century.

The Palazzo Comunale dates back to the fourteenth century and houses the civic art gallery, set up in the hall of the municipal council with works mostly anonymous from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century.
The cathedral wanted by Sixtus V.
The nineteenth-century theatre from the inside spectacular, where Benigni filmed the scene of the audience in "Life is beautiful."

The parish church dates back to the 11th century, in Romanesque style of Lombard taste, and houses the polychrome wooden statue of St. Ambrose of the 15th century, a national monument since 1920. Next to it, the church of Sant'Ambrogio was built from 1893 and completed at the beginning of the twentieth century with the staircase in slate, the facade and the pulpit; damaged in the Second World War and restored in the middle of the century, preserves paintings and the Madonna dei Sette Dolori attributed to the school of Margliano.
Rings marked between hills and villages.
Free Offer

Borgo Ciociano on a rocky hill, surrounded by walls with thirty-six turrets and three surviving gates, dominated by the castle where St. Thomas Aquinas was held prisoner in 1244-45; the name comes from a Benedictine monastery of the sixth century and the village is on the Via Francigena del Sud and on the Way of St. Benedict.
With the Duomo it forms the spiritual triptych of Piazza Castello; the dome is Guarini.
To see the Nestor Cup and the first Greek colony of the West.
Civic museum with a set-up designed to discover the secrets of nature and living forms.
A dry elm that the inhabitants of Villavallelonga consider a real monument of the country.
The ruins of the Arab-Norman castle dominate from above the historic center of Mistretta.
Blue Flag Sea on the Ionian coast.
The Tiepolo father and son.

Spa park of about 130,000 square meters with Italian garden and rare botanical species; the sources, already known in the seventeenth century and appreciated by Alessandro Manzoni, are four: Antica Fonte, Fausta, Igea and Boario. At the entrance the colonnade with the Liberty dome of 1913, symbol of the spa. In addition to bathrooms, mud and wellness area with swimming pools, saunas and salt room, the park hosts the Boario Park Adventure with Tibetan bridge and a slittovia (Alpine Coaster) from the Fausta Pavilion to the high park. Spa hours: Mon-Fri 12:30-22:00, Saturday, Sunday and holidays 10:00-22:00, recommended booking.
Shadow and cool a stone's throw from the beach.
€2.50, reduced €2
Close by, the lost decorations of the Romanesque nave.
Three-jump falls.

In Ginghi, built in 1878 for the vow made after the cholera of 1855, where before a rock with niche housed a statue of the Madonna; inside the picture of the Madonna exhibited from 1915 to 1918 in the church of Braunau, in Austria, where the population of Lavarone had taken refuge.

Palace-fortress built at the beginning of the XVI century by Nicolò Bonafede, born in the village and bishop of Chiusi, today seat of the town hall: the central body is inspired by Palazzo Venezia in Rome, the courtyard to that of the Doge's Palace of Urbino.

Small church in a hamlet on the sides of the Bisalta, entirely frescoed between the fifteenth and eighteenth centuries: cycles of the life of Our Lady and Passion and a universal Judgment inspired by the Sistine Chapel.
A strong house of the fourteenth century.
The novenary among the olive trees.
Parish church of the village, next to the castle, with bell tower built in the mid-18th century.
A spa country of the Crete Senesi, with two establishments and travertine tanks linked to the memory of Garibaldi.

Built by the Monzini family in the mid-18th century with agricultural function, it was transformed into a villa with frescoed ceilings around 1850, on the occasion of a family wedding, and enlarged at the beginning of the twentieth century. The municipal property is home to the Italo Calvino Library; the english park that surrounds it is open to the public.
Secular olive trees and piers with water.

The sixteenth-century church, with a Renaissance bezel portal, is among the few remaining standing after the earthquake of 1694; next door, the monastery founded in 1557 for the Benedictines and finished in 1586 is now the Town Hall, and its portal on Via Roma was the entrance of the inner garden.
Litorale awarded for several years with the Blue Flag of the FEE.
The hamlet is still closed by the historical walls, with its characteristic houses: the hamlet awarded with the Orange Flag of the Touring Club.

Small village in the southernmost part of the Langhe, closed by the Tanaro's handles, between calanchi formed in millennia of erosion and vineyards of Dogliani DOCG; here, in the hamlet Gorrea, was installed in 2010 the first Big Bench of Chris Bangle, and in the ancient Town Hall the historical and ethnographic Museum is located.
The story of the "Tiger of Forlì."
The wildest face of the Langhe, between clays and vineyards.
Works of Guercino, Guido Reni, Lavinia Fontana and Scarsellino, and a Crucifix of the fourteenth century.
The remains of the Sabauda fortress that barred the Stura Valley.
Basilica of the patron, rebuilt in neoclassical style, close to the center; it is in the center of the reenactment of the Corsa alla Sword and Palio.
Paladini's canvases.
Municipality of Montalbano of the wines of Carmignano, with Villa La Ferdinanda to Artimino UNESCO heritage.
A marble comic book.

13th century castle built on the remains of an older building, with crenellated walls, towers, buttresses, moat, drawbridge and underground; inside the Gandini family had built in 1564 a Renaissance villa with frescoed halls, rare example of a Renaissance villa inside a medieval castle, since the 1930s of the Orlando family. The park has an Italian garden and an English garden with centuries-old trees, including a sophora japonica of about 200 years old; you can also visit the nineteenth-century secret cave, the ancient cellars under the main tower and the sacristy of the private chapel of St. Francis with sacred books of the eighteenth century and a Biblia of 1536. Guided tours and tastings for a fee (tel. 030 725006).
Blue Flag Municipality in the regional marine park Riviera dei Cedri, with free beaches and equipped establishments; the promenade is animated by bars and shops.
Easy hike that goes up the stream Ayasse highlighting the geological characteristics of the valley.
The porch on the valley at the entrance of the village.
€5.50, reduced €3

Town of the Torinese to the south of the capital, with the eighteenth-century cathedral designed by Benedetto Alfieri, the sanctuary of the Valinotto by Bernardo Antonio Vittone (1738), the church of the Madonna delle Grazie and a historic center of piazzas and noble palaces such as the House of the Grand Bastard Renato of Savoia.
A unique time travel in Europe (not suitable for everyone).
Low water and comfortable facilities, ideal with children.

Walled city of the Paduan plain, south of the Euganean Hills, with one of the best preserved medieval surroundings in the world: almost two kilometers of fourteenth-century walls with 24 towers, the Castel San Zeno with the civic museum, the Rocca degli Alberi and the Duomo with the Transfiguration of Paolo Veronese.
The castle of Basile and Cunto de li Cunti, today the wine's ecomuseum.
One of the best preserved historical centers of Liguria.
Parish Church designed by Carlo Rainaldi and built in 1666 at the behest of a Prince Borghese, heart of the historic center together with the seventeenth-century Palazzo Borghese.

Since 2019 the artists Ravo and Refreshink paint on the walls of the city subjects inspired by the works of the castle, such as La Carità, Le Tre Grazie and the Archangel Gabriele; the mural "La Carità" by Andrea Ravo Mattoni is in via Milano 17.
A watchtower on the gate of the Bagnone valley.
Baladin beer has been produced in Piozzo since 1996, founded by Teo Musso: the pub overlooks the main square and the production premises are visited with guided tours.
With the Cross of Jerusalem in 1625.

In the Town Hall there are more than 200 exhibits from the 7th century B.C. to the Roman age, found in the territory in the sixties and seventies: vases with black and red figures, Etruscan bronzes and bell towers (calderons, silhouettes, the "pizzipapera"), Corinthian and Ionian ceramics, buccheri and the bronzes of the archaic necropolis of Vico Equense.

Remains of the Roman colony of Abellinum, founded at the end of the II century BC on a Sannite settlement, on the plateau of the Civita along the left bank of Saturday: a stretch of wall in cross-linked work, a public area with spas and hole and a domus of Hellenistic-Pumpian type of about 2,500 m2, perhaps of a freedom of Agrippa. The colony fell after the earthquake of 346 AD and was abandoned during the Greek-Gothic War.

Archaeological, naturalistic and mining museum founded in 1956 in the Palace of the Reverend Apostolic Chamber (1580). With original finds, plastic and reconstructions in four sections (paleontological, archaeological, geominerary and naturalistic) tells the Tolfa Mountains from prehistory to the Renaissance and the extraction of the alum, used in tannery, dyeing and papermaking, from which the village takes its name; the quarries, to whose undertaking the Park attributes the European primacy of capitalist organization in the sixteenth century, were painted by Pietro da Cortona (painting to the Capitolini Museums). Open Tuesday-Saturday 9-13.

It is located in the Palazzo del Vescovado and in the Loggia della Ragione, frescoed around the middle of the sixteenth century; born from the legacy of Andrea Manera and Pacifico Scomazzetto, it has an archaeological section, a gallery from the fifteenth century to today with works by Luca Giordano, Bernardo Strozzi and Bernardo Bellotto, the treasure of the Duomo and the sections dedicated to Caterina Cornaro, Eleonora Duse and Freya Stark.

Borgo della Barbagia di Ollolai, Orange Flag of the Touring, with granite houses arranged amphitheatre at almost 800 meters: the parish church of San Gavino, the Porcu Satta House Museum, the Museum of the Sardinian Flower, the country shrine of Our Lady of Itria and, about 2 km, the lake of Gusana.
The six-seventh-century parish church linked to the Romagnano and the Ponte.
The nature of the Roero.

The agricultural centre of the Bassa Parmense on the Strada del Culatello, a feud and residence of the Rossi until 1817: the Rocca dei Rossi preserves frescoed salt like that of the Golden Ass, and among the fields stands the Romanesque parish church of San Genesio; the village is known for its cooked shoulder and Fortana wine.
The north side of Etna to the craters.
The oldest Romanesque in the country.
The forum of the ancient Teate.
In Valorz you will find the first open-air Kneipp trail in Trentino; from here a ring path passes through the traditional farms and reaches the Valorz waterfalls.
Water and walks in the plain.
Medieval defensive tower of the 14th century, linked to the control of the territory exercised by the castle.

Mother Church of the Castellanza di Teglio, at the foot of the castrum Tilii: under the current building, work of the XV and XVII centuries with three naves with cruising vaults, emerged the foundations of three previous churches, the first of the V-VI century. On the façade there is a marble rosette with the Madonna and the portal of the Rodari of 1506. In the sacred enclosure next to it are the Oratory of the Disciplini Bianchi, with the fifteenth-century fresco of the Danza Macabra, the Oratory of the Black Brothers and the ossuary of the old cemetery.
By bike along the Brembo, from the thermal baths to the village of Tasso.
Church of the historical center that preserves the polychrome wooden statue of the Madonna of Calena, coming from the abbey of Calena, today reduced to ruins behind the marina.
The country seen from above.
The historic heart of the river Dolo.
It collects material on the Alpine troops and military bodies of the territory; a section is located in the former railway station of Ambria.
The museum of the archconfraternity, reported by the City of Cagliari on the itinerary of the sacred art museums of the city.
18th-century ceramic-coated building, on the way to the Regional Ceramic Museum.

In a 13th-century paper mill, the wooden sweaters moved by the hydraulic wheel, the Dutch machine of 1745 and the presses of the eighteenth-century still work with the water of the Canneto stream; you can make by hand a sheet of Amalfi paper.
Summer residence of 1761 with Italian garden on the east bank of the Naviglio Grande.

Fortified village of the Amerino which preserves the walls with crenellated towers and the Porta Amerina with two arches, with the parish church of San Nicolò; in the hamlets the churches of Quadrelli and Casteltodino and, in Castel dell'Aquila, the collection of tools of rural civilization.
The work and life of the Sila of the past.
Lonely spur over Roccaporena where the saint prayed in secret, with a small chapel built in 1919.
The baroque entrance of the village.
All the birds of Sardinia under a roof.
St. Michael the Archangel is a Romanesque church with a Greek cross; San Pietro in Penne has farfensi origins; Santa Maria in Capite Scalorum was built around 1300 around a much older aedicule.

Built at the end of the eighteenth century by the Lembo family on the remains of a medieval castle with towers, after the restoration it was recognized in 2011 "Meraviglia d'Italia" for the architecture and above all for the eighteenth-century frescoes of some rooms on the upper floor, combined with those of the Reggia di Caserta. On the back a hanging garden with snow and an arched walk towards a cylindrical tower; below, underground caves of uncertain dating. The municipality indicates mon-jo opening 10-13 and 14-18.
€10 (one ticket with the archaeological area)
More challenging hike above Miola, reachable for example from the Passo del Redebus, with wide views of the valleys and the plateau.
Church of 1305 dedicated to the patron saint of Picinisco.

Built at the end of the fifteenth century on a project by Bernardino de Lera, with facade in white and pink marble; today the headquarters of the Stauffer Foundation and the Department of Musicology of the University of Pavia.
Under the transept of the cathedral the excavations revealed an ancient use of the site; the museum preserves some of the findings emerged.

A town of medieval origin, mentioned since 1114, on a hill in the Sele valley, dominated by the remains of the baronial castle that houses the Provincial Archaeological Museum of the Upper Sele Valley, with the cultural equipment of ...Oliveto-Cairano.
Visitable with guided tours of the Foundation (Saturday; groups and schools by reservation in the weekdays); the MiC card (Add. 2021) indicates closed every day
The Apennine mines in a hall.
The thermal baths of the Riviera delle Alpi.
The village of Azzinano is decorated with murals depicting the traditional games of the past.
Convention of 2024 for the redevelopment of the building for social and cultural purposes (Comune di Desio)

The village where Ruggiero Leoncavallo grew, which here set Pagliacci: in the Dominican complex of the fifteenth century, now Town Hall, there is the museum dedicated to the composer; above the ancient walls, on the hill of the Serrone, the Cathedral of the Madonna della Serra, founded in 1227.
Small island in front of Pallanza, part of the archipelago of the Borromee Islands, admired from the lakefront.

Founded in 2000 in the former Town Hall of the historic centre, it is dedicated to pre- and protohistoric archaeology and ancient technologies: experimental reconstructions, a tactile collection, the casts of the finds of Vayes, the inside of a neolithic hut and illustrated panels. Open on Sundays (April to November), other days by reservation; guided tour €6.

With 5.4 km2 it is the largest lake in Trentino and gives its name to the village. You swim from May to the end of September on free beaches and equipped shores, with nautical center for sailing, canoeing, windsurfing, rowing, water skiing and diving, and a walk on the banks.

The village where Antonio Gramsci spent his childhood and adolescence, today remembered by the House museum on the main street; around, the Aragonese tower of the fifteenth century, the Romanesque San Palmerio in two-tone stones, St. Peter of Zuri rebuilt stone by stone over Lake Omodeo and the nineteenth-century village of San Serafino.

A small medieval village in the Chietina hills, built around an ancient Norman tower and dominated by the 12th century Ducal Castle, which in September 1943 hosted the royal family fleeing Rome and today houses the Byzantine and Alto-Medieval Abruzzo Museum.

Neoclassical villa of the late eighteenth century and early nineteenth century, perhaps of the Meriggiani family, with park of tall trees. The museum exhibits Roman fragments, the Madonna of the Rosary by Benedetto Nucci, two paintings by Ernst van Schayck and a section of contemporary graphics with 260 sheets and drawings in china, from the donations Ginesi, Garibaldi Jallet and Romiti-Mosullani, the latter with material on the Garibaldi family and on Garibalda Canzio, lived in Castelbellino until 1969.
The medieval road, about 2 km long, is crossed by arches and suspended passages, which runs along the Jewish quarter.
Dedicated to the siege of Turin in 1706 and to Pietro Micca, connected directly to the underground tunnels of countermina.

Considered one of the most original works of Baroque Lecce, it had the present form by the Mesagnese priest-architect Francesco Capodieci; the origins, uncertain, would date back to the fourteenth or fifteenth century. The three-order façade has niches with the apostles, a bas-relief of the Madonna del Carmine and, above the portal, statues of Saint Eleutery, Anthia and Corebo. Inside, with a Latin cross with chapels and altars in finely carved stone, the Adoration of the Shepherds began by Gian Pietro Zullo and completed by Andrea Cunavi and Domenico Pinca, and a Madonna of Carmine by the Neapolitan Giuseppe Bonito.
A page of Bourbon history.
The ancient sea of the Circeo.

The original nucleus, dedicated to St. Christopher, dates back to 1552-1570; the naves are from 1639-1642, the bell tower was completed in 1783 and the facade rebuilt in 1960 by Antonio Valenti. It preserves the Assumption of Antonino Spatafora called the Panormita, dated 1579, and four paintings of the Lombard school of the seventeenth century with Santa Maddalena, Santa Rosalia, Sant'Agata and Santa Caterina.
Built in 1598 at the behest of Cardinal Tolomeo Gallio to host the pilgrims of the feast of the patron.
Art of the twentieth century in a village of valley.
A silk machine remained almost unique in Europe.
Arabic and Norman architecture.

Jewel of the Romanesque Apulian overlooking the sea, in front of the Castle: from the promenade along the castle you can enjoy the best view; on the same square Duomo are located the Diocesan Museum and the Museum of the typewriter.
History and nature above the valley.
The fortress that dominates the city.
The tradition of Ibleo honey.

Destroyed by the earthquake of Belice in January 1968 and rebuilt on a panoramic height by an intuition by Mayor Ludovico Corrao, with the involvement of numerous artists and architects, Gibellina is an open-air museum and is Italian capital of contemporary art 2026: the Great Cretto of Burri on the ruins of the old city, the Star of Consagra, the Mother Church of Quaroni, the MAC and the Museum of Mediterranean Trames.
One of the most eastern peaks of the Pollino massif (1,439 meters), reachable by a path in the vegetation: about 4 hours of excursion accompanied by the guides of the park.
Birdwatching in the conca of crime.

Building on five levels: on the first floor the permanent exhibition on Enotri, Greci and Lucani from the archaic age to the Romanization, on the ground floor and on the second floor temporary exhibitions.
From prehistory to Aeclanum in a castle.
The country's richest art complex.
Pulpit in carved wood, wooden crucifix of the sixteenth century and a very rare Christ in the column of the fourteenth century.
The frescoes of San Giacomo.

Giorgione's birthplace, enclosed in a square of red brick walls erected by Treviso between the 12th and 13th centuries, among the best preserved in Italy: inside the walls the 18th-century Cathedral of Francesco Maria Preti with the Pala di Giorgione, the Giorgione House with the Fregio delle Arti and the Academic Theatre; outside, Piazza Giorgione with the Loggia del Paveion and the large English garden of Villa Revedin Bolasco.
Fortress of 1112 overlooking Sa Costa, around which the new city grew after the abandonment of the ancient one; it offers a panorama of the town.

The village is almost at the western edge of Franciacorta, at the foot of Monte Alto, with views of vineyards and lake and noble buildings of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries; the 18th century parish church with the medieval tower, the ancient parish church of Santa Maria Assunta on the hill and the sanctuary of the Madonna della Snow with the silk, hemp and linen museum.
The place of the martyrdom of San Crescenziano.
An easy cave with thousands of bats.

Walking pass 227 meters long and 36 meters high on the Lima stream, between Mammiano Basso and Popiglio, inaugurated in 1923 after about two years of work: the scaffolding rests on four steel ropes without intermediate supports. Proposed by engineer Vincenzo Douglas Scotti to shorten the route of the workers of Popiglio to the ironworks on the other bank, it was the longest suspended pedestrian bridge in the world until 2006.
€5, reduced €4 (7-14 years)
The traces of a medieval hospice on the way to the pass.

The village is more than 400 meters on the slopes of Mount San Matteo, about 25 km from Sassari, linked to the scholar Giovanni Spano: the Spanish Quadreria with paintings from the fourteenth to the nineteenth century, the complex of San Pietro, the first monumental cemetery of the island and, in the countryside, the Romanesque churches of Salvennor and more than 70 nuragic sites.
The Duomo above Piazza Grande.

Bay between white cliffs and blue-green water, with two calcareous faraglioni a few meters from the shore, the Arch of Diomede and ...The Scissors are about 1 km of beach divided by a spur in the Bay of Faraglioni (sand and gravel) and Zagare Bay (white pebbles and sand), plus the Cala dei Morti reachable only from the sea. Most of the beach is run by hotel establishments: access for guests and with a limited number of daily passes issued by the municipality; you will also arrive by boat from Vieste or Mattinata. Better in the morning, in the afternoon it goes in the shade.
The historic heart of Acceglio.

Reserve of about 57 hectares established in 2000 and managed by WWF Italy: limestone rocks rich in fossils of about 200 million years ago, with three geosites (one of national importance), a cliff of about 35 meters with alofil vegetation and a plateau covered with dwarf palm, the only spontaneous palm of Europe. On the promontory the watchtower, one of the first built on the Sicilian coast, which gives its name to the head and signaled the pirates with fire and smoke; it is the only circular tower of the coast. Suitable for mountain bikes and sunsets.
A sabauda palace in the Rolli.
The statues of the promenade.
One of the most beautiful castles in Tuscany.

Medieval village on a gentle hill just over 200 meters, divided into the districts of Terranova and Terravecchia, with pre-Romanic and Renaissance remains, towers, arches, alleys, stretches of the medieval walls, palaces and the Clock Tower.

Established in 1974, the first of the seven South Tyrolean natural parks, covers 7,288 hectares between Castelrotto, Tires and Fiè (20% of the territory of Castelrotto): it includes the Sciliar massif, the Mountain of Destiny, with the peaks Santner and Euringer, and the Catinaccio; since 2009 it is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Dolomites. The visitor center is in Siusi, in Piazza Oswald von Wolkenstein 6; nature trails and, according to italia.it, the Path of geologists.

Villa at the eastern entrance of the city, which hosted the Duchess Maria Amalia wife of Ferdinand of Bourbon, with furnishings and frescoes of the Seven and Nineteenth Century: today it is home to the municipal library, the ethnographic museum of Val Tidone, with materials on the peasant life, fossils and fragments of Roman objects, and the museum dedicated to Cardinal Agostino Casaroli.

Erected in the Jubilee year 1600 as a thank you to the Virgin for the protection from the plague, a circular plant with a small bell tower of the late seventeenth century; collapsed in 1933, it was rebuilt by the Salusturi Galli family. Feast on the first Sunday of August.
The second largest cathedral in the Baroque city, part of the heritage rebuilt after the earthquake.
To see the accessories of the necropolis of Pezza Petrosa in the palace of the dukes.

A journey on the history of international aviation, with attention to the historical companies of Varesotto, Lombardy and Italian industry, divided into five areas: flight forms, fixed wing, rotating wing, modeling and convertiplani, from the first hot air balloons to planes of the early twentieth century. There are indoor and outdoor areas for children, simulators, library and historical archives. Open from Tuesday to Sunday; free under 2 years and for people with disabilities.

Village of narrow streets, white houses, arches and small squares. The 17th century Mother Church was built by the Knights of Gerosolimitani and dedicated to St. John, with rosette and protyro on the façade; on Piazza Ciaia overlook the Palazzo dei Cavalieri of Malta, renovated in the eighteenth century, and the 16th century Palazzo dell'Università.
Open July 1-10 September, Saturday 16-19.
Earth science to touch with your hand.
Included in the castle ticket (to be checked)
Roman rococo building with Greek cross commissioned by the Columns, inside the cloistered monastery of the Dominicans.
The waters that made the history of the country.
Unpublished times: MiC card indicates closed every day; tel. 0968 81001

The large market covered in a late nineteenth-century building by Angiolo Badaloni, one of the largest historical markets in Europe, with the metal truss ceiling; around the stalls of Piazza Cavallotti.
The heart of the Lauretan pilgrimage.
It preserves a St. Jerome attributed to Guercino.
Archaeology and traditional costume of Tiriolo.
A walk in the center.
In August the IGP potato festival of Montescudo.
The House of the Doges.
The wet areas of the Secchia a stone's throw from Modena.
The baroque lounge of the city.
A walk in the historic center.
The hall built in 1492 for the library of Pius II, frescoed by Pinturicchio, with the choral illuminated by Girolamo da Cremona and Liberale da Verona.
Gothic portico built in the middle of the fifteenth century by Onorato Caetani: it was a municipal seat, business centre and place of public assemblies, with stables under the arches.
In the castle since 2003, tells Vigevano as the center of the footwear and the evolution of the shoe as an object of fashion and design.

The alkaline, sulphurous and sauce-bromo-iodic waters flowing from the slopes of nearby Mount San Paolo feed the hydrotherapy station, with herbal and mud treatments and a wellness centre for medical and aesthetic treatments.

In a rural house in the courtyard of the nineteenth century on two floors and four rooms, with finds from the Nuragic Age to the Spanish domination, many from the backdrops: punic amphorae of the fifth century BC recovered in front of the island of the Cavoli, ex vow and objects of the Phoenician-punic sanctuary of Cuccureddus, Roman materials from the necropolis of Cruccuris and Accu is Traias, and in the last room cannons and azulejos of the Spanish wreck sunk in the fifteenth century near the island of the Cavoli. Open Tuesday-Sunday 9-13 and 16-18.

Seaside town of the coast of Agrigento, called "Dilectissima" by Federico II: on Mount Sant'Angelo the remains of the Hellenistic city of Finziade and the castle, in the 16th century Badia the archaeological museum, in the center the churches of Santa Maria La Nova and San Domenico and the Palazzo of City of Ernesto Basile; along the coast the lighthouse of San Giacomo and the beaches of Mollarella, Marianello, San Nicola and Torre di Gaffe.
A literary source in the countryside.
Genoese fortress of the twelfth century, destroyed in war and partly recovered, surrounded by a garden of Mediterranean plants; from the top the panorama of the village.
The walled village of Montepeloso.

Baroque church of 1686-1734 on the square of the Corallini; the terrace church hosts in summer the International Chamber Music Festival, born after the violinist Sándor Végh discovered its acoustics in 1964.
The view of the gulf from the terraces.
Modern church designed in 1970 by Ludovico Quaroni, with the dome called "Great white sphere."
A chapter of the twentieth century in the square.
The 16th century San Vito.
Romanesque traces in the village of Sant'Ermete.
The long beach of Giannella.
Opera by street artist Alessandra Carloni who portrays Tiburzi on a fairytale background.

Country of the Basso Monferrato on the border between Asti and Turin, dominated by a large castle of medieval origin that houses the Museum of plaster, material obtained here from the seventeenth century; complete the visit the Wine shop, linked to Freisa, and the neoclassical parish church of San Giovanni Battista.
Indicated among the most scenic lakes in the Stura Valley.
The sanctuary of Corniglia.
The Grande Pevero is in the shape of a crescent, the Little Pevero along about half; near there are Cala Granu and the bay of Romazzino, and in front of the Pevero the Li Nibani islands.
A medieval village intact on the Valdarno.

The square with the Palazzo della Ragione and the Torre dell'Orologio, which preserves the original gears of the fifteenth-century astronomical-astrological clock of Bartolomeo Manfredi and houses the Museo del Tempo.
A Byzantine mosaic from the 8th century.
A hermitage in the cave above the water.
The baroque of the village.
40 min tower + 1 h collections

Borgo Bandiera Arancione on the western shore of Lake Como, divided between the upper medieval part, with the cobbled streets and the remains of the castle destroyed in 1523, and the nineteenth-century lakefront with walks, hotels and the Rationalist Lido of 1934; in the hamlet of Loveno the Villa Mylius Vigoni with the English park, behind the Val Sanagra Park.
Along the main street the Fountain of Venus Cyprea, rebuilt in 1614; in the center the ancient Bank of Court, from which you can access the tower whose clock beats the hours from 1885.
A little church on a rock spur.

In the ancient village of San Lorenzo in Monte, the Museum of Art of the Medal tells about the school of Bujesi medalists of the twentieth century and the history of the territory, next to the parish church of San Lorenzo, mentioned already in 792 and frescoed at the end of the fourteenth century.
Beaches equipped for families, with clear waters and low suitable for snorkeling.

Set up in the parish canonical, it exhibits fragments of the stucco decoration that once adorned the central nave of the basilica. It is visited together with the baptistery and the basilica; the complex is part of the parish of Lomello.

Born after the discovery in 1576 of an image of the Madonna and Child in the blade of Santa Margherita, on three levels: the grotto with the marble and silver temple, the intermediate church of the Benedictines with frescoes of the Passion, prophets and sibilles, and the upper church of Cosimo Fanzago with coffered ceiling of 1633.
The heart of the " Marian city" and one of the rare Saints outside Rome.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione from the Ligurian imprint to the confluence of the Neirone with the Lemme, among the vineyards of the Cortese, dominated by the great star fort.

In front of the façade of the cathedral the Oratory of the Rosary, of medieval origin, houses a sculptural retablo of 1700; next to the bell tower the oratory of Santa Croce, of the thirteenth century, preserves wooden furnishings including a retablo and a Deposition.
Wednesday rite at the Fort.

The Via Francigena crosses the village and runs through paths, mule tracks and woods along the river Magra; stage 23, from Pontremoli to Aulla, to Filetto, Virgoletta and Villafranca. The route of Francigena in Lunigiana measures 71 km in three stages.

Town of the plain between Palermo and the Gulf of Castellammare, with the churches of Corso dei Mille (the Mother Church of the Annunziata, San Leonardo with a canvas by Pietro Novelli, San Giuseppe, the Carmine), the Sanctuary of the Madonna del Ponte, the baroque fountain of 1716, the sixteenth-century towers of the countryside, the Poma Lake and the village of Borgo Parrini, a village of artists from colored houses.

Local paintings and sculptures from the 13th to the 19th century, sacred furnishings of the churches affected by the earthquake, illuminated codes of the Bolognese-Paduana school of the Two-Three hundred and, in the Treasury, the monstrance of Nicolò Lionello of 1434 and two bronzes of Girolamo Campagna.
It was partially reopened after the closing of 2003, and exhibits about 200 works from the Bronze Age to the twentieth century.
entrance only with guided tour (suedtirol.info)

Parish of Castellaro dedicated to the patron saint of San Nicola di Bari, renovated in Baroque forms in the seventeenth century on a Romanesque church; it preserves a painting of the saint and a wooden statue of the Virgin of the fifteenth century.
The romantic lake of Vallagarina, between beech and water lilies.

Built from the 16th century on a project by Martino Bassi and modified in the following centuries, it has two towers and a courtyard of honor and is now home to the town hall. Inside cycles of frescoes and stuccoes between XVI and XVIII century of active painters in Milan, including Mattia Bortoloni (in the hall of honor on the ground floor), Carlo Antonio Procaccini, Giovanni Stefano Montalto and Giovanni Paolo Cavagna; In Lombardy he also mentions stuccoes by Andrea Appiani. For Open Villas 2024 guided tours (50 minutes) cost €5, €7 cumulative with Santa Maria in Campo.
A path in the rooms under the roofs of the Cathedral, closed for centuries, overlooking the interior of the Duomo; open from 1 March to 6 January.
The collector's house.
Karst swallower about 180 meters deep, formed by a single vertical well of 10-15 meters of diameter, dug by water in the carbonate rock.
The oldest human remains on the island.
The roots of Paganini in a village of Val di Vara.
The oldest church outside the walls.

Venetian-style palace among the oldest buildings in the city, now home to the Town Hall; behind you lie an Italian garden inside the walls of the historic center and a large park with exceptional tree monuments.
A gallery overlooking the sea.
Among the oldest churches: a large wooden statue attributed to the Bernini school, frescoes attributed to Lorenzo da Viterbo and Umbrian frescoes of the fourteenth century.

In the Cittadella dei Musei, the collection of the magistrate Luigi Cocco (1883-1959) with objects of Sardinian folk culture from the second half of the nineteenth and first half of the twentieth century: carpets, jewelry, furniture, tools and carvings.
The panorama of the village with its medieval walls.
Alpine Christmas in the city.
The large nineteenth-century church of Conoglano.
