Small streets and lanes at the foot of the cliff of the Holy Sudarium, in a place where archaeological research indicates Celtic-ligur settlements since the Bronze Age. In the center and surroundings there are votive chapels from the 16th to the 18th century, including those of the Assumption and of the Saints Rocco and Biagio, and Liberty villas of the early decades of the 20th century.
Perhaps founded in the 12th century and rebuilt in 1820, it preserves a seventeenth-century reliquary in gilded silver with crystals.
Jewel of Cistercian architecture imported from Burgundy: the abbey church with facade and rose window, the capitular hall, the cloister and the lantern that stands out over the landscape.

Born in 1928 from the fusion of Albese and Cassano, along the ancient route of the Roman Via Regina, the municipality preserves the Romanesque church of San Pietro with the leaning bell tower, the Lavandée water museum born in the wash-house of 1822, historic villas and the wooded paths of the Albese Valley towards the Cave of the Cepp.

Rebuilt after the earthquake of 1693 with the funds of Duke Ignazio Migliaccio since 1748, on the current Piazza del Popolo; facade with convex cylindrical tower, Tuscan columns and mechanical clock. The three bronze portals of Romeo Sandrin (2003-2004) depict the Old and New Testaments, the life of Mary and the sacraments.

Borgo del Parco Nazionale del Gargano among the most beautiful villages in Italy, one of the largest historical centers of the promontory: the Civita, Terra and Casale districts with fireplaces and portals, the Norman castle, the fourteenth-century mill of Trappeto Maratea, the necropolis of Monte Tabor and, towards the sea, San Menaio; behind the Umbra Forest.
The medieval village overlooking the sea.
The largest church in Calabria.

Ancient municipal mule track of about 2.5 km and 300 m of difference in altitude between the hamlet Rumer (1100 m) and Aia delle Balme (1400 m), recovered together with the quarries of the Polo extractive, overlooking the area of the three municipalities of the Pietra di Luserna. In some stretches it is steep, with overhanging areas; forbidden to bicycles.
the Municipality indicates that access is not allowed because private property
The medieval heart with views of the Sibillini.
Building of fifteenth century origin with ogival porch on Piazza Duomo.

On the hill above the village, after a fire was rebuilt between 1738 and 1770 and transformed into a Venetian villa by the architect Matteo Lucchesi; it connects to the village a stone staircase of 365 steps. From troubled history, today it appears more like an eighteenth-century palace, not yet completely restored, and it is a panoramic destination for walking.
Square overlooking the city, with the main public buildings on the sides: Palazzo dei Consoli, Palazzo Pretorio and Palazzo Ranghiasci Brancaleoni.
The first cathedral on the hill.
Open only on Friday and Saturday 10-17 and before and third Sunday of the month 9-13 (VisitLatium)
€5, free children up to 6 years
The Gothic in the heart of Merano.
Panorama over Majella and orchids.
The gate of the Senio valley.

Designed in 1849 on the initiative of Beckwith and inaugurated on 17 June 1852, after the emancipation of the Valdese of 17 February 1848; in Romanesque style, with three naves with apse and matroneo, has the facade with two side bell towers. Every year the Synod of Waldensian and Methodist Churches opens.

One of the oldest and largest olive trees in Europe, about 15 meters high, in the hamlet of Canneto along the SP 41; freely accessible with the permission of the owner, in a landscape of olive groves that produce Sabina DOP oil.
One of the oldest documented parishes in the territory.
The great basilica of São Paulo and, not far away, the Centrale Montemartini where since 1997 ancient sculptures of the Capitolini dialogue with the machines of a power plant.

Ancient village on the Lombard shore of Lake Maggiore, dominated by the Fortress Borromeo that houses the Museum of the Doll and the Toy; in the center the Archaeological Museum in the Palazzo del Pretorio, to the south the Bruschera Swamp, the largest reed of the western shore of the lake.

Church of the twentieth century expansion area, with facade in stone blocks of Luserna. The three large, centered windows have lead windows with angels; above the door a high relief depicts Jesus Pantocrator with two young workers in early twentieth century clothes.

At the origin of the village: a small chapel dedicated to St. Vito martyr, built around the fourteenth century, was transformed at the end of the fifteenth century into a fortress and shelter to protect pilgrims from thieves and brigands, and with the increase of pirate raids had also a tower. It looks like a fortified church, more like a bastion, with Arab-Norman architecture; around it in the eighteenth century the houses of the country grew.

Established in 1994, Sardinia's first national park: more than 60 granite and shale islands, more than 20,000 hectares of sea and land and 180 km of coast, with almost a thousand plant species (about fifty endemic), turtles and turtles Caretta caretta. Sports, fishing and diving should be allowed. From Palau the ferry arrives in about 20 minutes.

Born in the seventies after the chance discovery in San Quirico of Roman burials, including a first century A.D. burial tomb with a rich set of glass and fine ceramics, it was inaugurated in 1983 and named after the Germanist Giuseppe Gabetti (1886-1948). Among the findings stands out a sandstone head of the medium Iron age, found in the old walls. Four rooms on the first floor of the Palazzo Comunale tell the territory from prehistory to the Roman age, with panels in Italian and English; Saturday 15-18, Sunday 9-12 and 15-18 (better phone, 0173 70107).

Small village of about 700 inhabitants in the heart of Sila became a village of art and colors.The old town is an open-air museum, with the murals of Francesco Candido on rural life and the works of ArCalabria on doors, windows and walls.
The park with centuries-old trees of the villa that houses the seat of the municipality, with a recovered cave and a navigable pond; the access to the city parks is free.
The 16th-century parish of the country.

Along the CAI 104 mule track, beyond the Stabina stream on a stone donkey-back bridge, the corn, rye and barley mill, active until the eve of World War II, and the hammer with forge, mole and the wind trumpet blowing air into the fire; the wheels are moved by the water of the Grobbia Valley.
The cave in the glacier.

On the hill south-east of the village, on the last slopes of the Serre, the remains of the city destroyed by earthquakes of the late eighteenth century, lying on three hills between two valleys; excavation campaigns are bringing to light the main structures and in August there is a pilgrimage.
The oldest traces of the territory, from the Etruscan era to the Mille.

It occupies the ancient glassworks of the early nineteenth century in the historic center, abandoned in 1968 and restored with the original architecture, example of industrial archaeology and among the few pre-industrial glass plants preserved in Italy. The three-storey route follows the production cycle, from raw materials to hand blowing; on display glasses, bottles, carafes and damsel, some decorated in pure gold, and in the basement a large casting of emerald green glass formed at the closure of the factory. Organize craft workshops.
The children's park.
Two churches of the lower, from Romanesque to Baroque.
The peasant life of the Karst in a stone house remained intact.

Municipality of Friuli hilly overlooking the Tagliamento, with the castle of San Pietro and its parish church, the Mount of Ragogna theater of the battle of 1917 after Caporetto and, in San Giacomo, the civic museums and the Great War.
A 16th century crucifix in the village.
The Romanesque of Nurra and the crib of bread.
A castle of the tenth century under the cliffs of the Cornate of Gerfalco.

Situated on the hill north of Sinnai with traces from the Nuragic Age onwards, including a nuragic temple; from here are finds exposed to the civic museum, like the Punic statue of the god Bes. Wide view of the Gulf of Cagliari and Campidano.
Figures in wax of characters of the history of Piacenza, presented on guided tours rich in anecdotes.
A village of churches in stone.
The story of a city born around a factory.
Medieval hunting casino in the park of Villa Borromeo; on the first floor there are frescoes from the fifteenth century with scenes of bear hunting and falcon.
One of the three museums housed in the castle, dedicated to rural life and traditional crafts of agriculture and pastoralism.

The shell-shaped square was created as a space for civic events, closed by the Palazzo Pubblico and the Torre del Mangia, with the Fonte Gaia, a nineteenth-century copy of the original Jacopo della Quercia.
The bell tower came back up after the earthquake.

The medieval village has a regular system on the tuff hill; according to legend the exiles of Gabi, destroyed by Tarquinio il Superbo, took refuge there. Along the way you will find the Palazzo del Gonfaloniere, the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie, the fountain with Roman bath in Piazza Santa Maria and, in via Fabrini near the Municipality, the ancient public balance with the historical measures of the village guarded by the bust called "Lu Giustu" which depicts Pope Clement IX Rospigliosi.

Country of the Serre on three ridges between Ionian and Tyrrhenian, divided after the earthquake of 1783 in the hamlets of Cellia, Poliolo, Trecroci and Menniti; along the river Milo grows the largest Italian population of Woodwardia rootans, giant fern
An Italian garden with 360 degree views of the Ciociaria.
The peasant civilization of Cuneese inside the castle.

High Ogliastra country on the border with Barbagia, known for the longevity of its inhabitants, with a nuragic heritage of the first floor: the village-sanctuary of S'Arcu 'e is Forros, Sa Carcaredda and Troculu, as well as the park of Santa Barbara, the natural pools of Bau Mela and the lake of the upper Flumendosa near the village of Villanova Strisaili.

It rises on the remains of a Byzantine church with a Greek cross of the 11th century, dedicated to Saint Catherine and consecrated to Saint Leo in the 13th century; enriched under the Sanseverino in the 16th century, restored in the 17th century with Baroque interior. hexagonal bell tower with Romanic triphores, three naves with twelve altars, marble ciborium of 1522 of Tuscan sculptor, baptismal font with the inscription "S." Leo 1592 and frescoes of the vault with the Sacrifice of Abraham and Judith and Holofernes.
Renaissance church overlooking a small canal, with the Madonna dei Miracoli.
Ionian seaside resort, long beach edged by a thick pine forest, known for its services and awarded with the Blue Flag.

Art city of the Brescia plain: the neo-Gothic Bonoris Castle on the hill of San Pancrazio, the Romanesque parish church with the San Pancrazio del Romanino, the eighteenth-century Duomo with its Last Supper, the Lechi Museum with seven paintings by Giacomo Ceruti and a system of seven civic museums.
The medieval village, largely uninhabited after the 1951 flood, with the seventeenth-century church of Santa Susanna; it lives two days in August for the feast of the saint.

On the ground floor of the Town Hall: sections of the medieval walls, remains of houses, a tannery and a warehouse, ceramics, coins, tools and a one-and-a-half-hand sword found in the area of a blacksmith shop. Open on Wednesdays 10-13 and Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays 10-13 and 15-18 (in summer 16-19), with guided tours at 11 am and at 4 pm.
A complete journey into the crafts of rural Sardinia.
A altarpiece by Francesco Guardi in a church in the valley.
The frescoes of Giaquinto in the Lombard castle.
Paths that surround the castle hill, with views of the Pesaro countryside between fields and Mediterranean maquis and up to the sea; the Passeggiata degli amanti turns around the castle.

It rises on the homonymous hill in Goiane and preserves most of the original characters: it was born from a primitive chapel with a single nave, probably Romanesque, with a nave in three bays and a quadrangular presbytery turned into a barrel; between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries were added bell tower, altar, sacristy and guardian's house. It preserves frescoes from the XV and XVI centuries and votive decorations of local artisans; behind the church a park with tables and benches, and on clear days the view reaches up to the Apennines.

Country of the stone of Luserna, born around the year 1000 around the castle of the lords of Bagnolo: the feudal complex of Malingri with castle-forte, palace and park, the neo-Gothic parish church of San Pietro in Vincoli and, at altitude, Montoso with the partisan shrine and the quarries.
MiC card indicates closed every day; open at summer events (Common 0184 208127)

Symbol of the village and rare Italian example of fortified bridge, with original body of the twelfth century; not far away the house where Enrico II Del Carretto signed in 1206 the act of foundation.

The Via Emilia crosses the centre with porticoes, shops and locals; there you will find the Aristide Arzano square with Palazzo Guidobono and Malaspina square. In the center there are also the fifteenth-century Casa del Pozzo, with the Virgin painted by Mario Patri, and Palazzo Garofoli, in the present form of Carlo Riccardi (about 1770), who hosted Napoleon and Pius VII.
A cobblestone cobblestone away from the crowd.

Built between 1664 and 1754 on a project by Antonio Del Grande, it collapsed in 1814 and was rebuilt between 1815 and 1845 by Domenico Palmucci; neoclassical facade of L. Arms between two bell towers. Inside works by Corrado Giaquinto (1739), the ciborium of 1517, a baptismal font of 1490 and a painting of an uncertain author with a Christ with almost feminine traits.

Small hilly town of the Pescarese, in the Val del Fino, with the Museum of Traditions and Rural Arts and a historic centre gathered around Piazza Duca degli Abruzzi and the Baroque church of the Blessed Virgin Mary of the Rescue; in the hamlet of Piccianello rises the neoclassical church of San Rocco (1838).

Chapel of the sixteenth century just outside the walls, built at the request of the Piccolomini so that the Albanians could celebrate the Orthodox rite. Inside sober with a small altar and an icon of the Madonna with the Child; next stood a civic hospital for faithful and pilgrims, expanded in the seventeenth century by the canon Bartolomeo Ciardi and active until the second half of the nineteenth century, and under the road an ancient ossuary with the victims of an epidemic of the sixteenth century.
Botanical garden near the Archaeological Museum, with the path of the Madonnella that offers the view over the whole valley.

In the former fifteenth-century convent of the Hermits of Sant'Agostino, with a cloister of 23 columns with Corinthian capitals, it collects finds from the territory of Buccino: the feminine set of the Tomb of the Ori, chamber tomb of the fourth century BC, and the mosaic of the Banquet Hall in an environment rebuilt with polychrome stuccoes; the route tells the commercial role of Volcei in the Roman age. Open every day 9-14, until 6 pm by reservation. Titled to the Buccina philologist Marcello Gigante.
Delta coastal lagoon, among the richest birdwatching areas in the province.
The country born from the Asinara exodus.
Life and crafts of old.
The old port, used mainly by fishing vessels, is a starting point for exploring the coast of Gargano and the Adriatic; the Swabian-Ange fortress dominates it from the sea.
Two Baroque churches, one with a dome of 46 metres.
Over 1,800 hectares established in 1984 between Tolentino and Urbisaglia: river valleys, low hills and the "Selva" of more than 100 hectares of oak, ash and maple, with roe deer, owls and peaks.

Open-air museum with iron and wood sculptures by twentieth-century artists, including Renato Barisani, Giorgio Bompadre, Sauro Craia and Umberto Peschi, inserted in the streets and landscape; some works have a QR code with presentations. Accessible path.

Isolotto in the middle of the cove between Capo Sant'Andrea and Capo Taormina, protected since 1984 and regional naturalistic museum since 2011, combined with the mainland by a thin tongue of pebbles that with the high tide can end under water. Lady Florence Trevelyan bought it in 1890 and built a house there: the red villa, called Villa Caronia by the last owner, is surrounded by about 1.6 hectares of terraces and Mediterranean maquis, marked in 1970 by De Agostini as a botanical garden.

Borgo dell'alta Val di Vara, the village of origin of the family of Niccolò Paganini, who reminds you of the musician with the Paganinian Festival and with Casa Paganini; also houses a mineral museum with a collection of minerals of the municipal territory.

Born from the collections of the Civic Museum of 1909 and opened by the State in 1968, on two floors: on the ground floor the history of Kroton with athletes, doctors and philosophers and the necropolis of Carrara; on the first floor the sanctuaries, with the treasure of Hera Lacinia, the gold diadem and the bronze nuragic boat of the VII century BC, and the askos shaped as a siren of the fifth century BC.

Museum of Sacred Art of the Diocese of Lucera-Troia in the noble wing of the eighteenth-century Bishop's Palace: the historical bishop's gallery with portraits desired by Mons. Alfonso Maria Freda (1798-1816), relics, relics and much of the Treasury of the Cathedral Chapter.
Museum of the traditional navigation of the Adriatic, with a floating section of ten historical boats moored in the canal port and a section on the ground.

Every second Sunday of the month the antique stalls occupy the main street, from the church of San Rocco to the castle, next to the walls, passing in front of the Duomo and the church of the Discipline.

The historical centre of medieval origin preserves the church of San Pietro Apostolo, among the most valuable buildings, the church of San Francesco built by the Caetani in 1363, and the church of the Annunziata of the XIV century. In July the Festival of the Kingdoms, in honor of the Virgin of Graces, recalls the ancient feast of harvest.
Bermejo's triptych.
A Renaissance palace survived the landslide of 1618.

Ghost village halfway between Palombara Sabina and Moricone, grew around a castle of 1600, with a single access between the most external tower and the church of Santa Maria. It was abandoned after the earthquake of 1901 and its remains were used to build Stazzano Nuovo; from the limestone spur you can see Mount Gennaro and Soratte. Freely accessible.
18th century church built on the remains of a Roman temple.

Sculptures and paintings from the 14th to the 18th century: the fourteenth-century wooden statue of St. Anthony the Abate, the oldest, a Madonna of the Rosary of the fifteenth century, works attributed to Julius Gualio, the Compplanted on Christ who died in 1612, the first wooden Baroque altar of the Shrine of the Guardia and a Last seventeenth-century Supper; historical library with volumes from the 16th to the 19th century.

Parish of the Diocese of Milan (decanated in Vimercate), built between 1924 and 1934, the year in which the frescoes and the interior flooring were executed; the presbytery had a structural intervention in 1974. The CEI card records in 1837 the church of Sant'Ambrogio in Nemus, today deconsecrated, and censisce inside the main altar and lateral altars, side chapels, frescoes, stained glass windows, statues, organ, source, tombstones and inscriptions; outside door, bell tower and parish church.
Wanted in 1260 by Pierre de Sarriod, lord of the Introd, surrounded by a large wooded park and open in summer; near the granaries complex.
Symbol of Biella, from the beginning of the 11th century, among the most interesting examples of Piedmontese Romanesque; on the portal a Roman bas-relief, because under there was a Roman sepulchre.
The castle and the memory of the village.
The baroque monument of the city.
To learn about the flora of Adamello Brenta.
The historic symbol on the Adda.
A baroque villa with frescoes and a museum of peasant civilization.
Ancient medieval nucleus on a panoramic hill, once fortified with walls and Saracen towers; between the alleys the church of Sant'Antonio and the Cathedral of Sant'Ippolito Martire.
Basically accessible

The main square of the village, where in August takes place the animated Tressette, a living game in which 32 girls and 8 boys impersonate the 40 cards; the Civic Tower offers a panoramic view of the village and the surroundings.
The tower built by the emperor between 1217 and 1221 on top of the hill, symbol of the city.
The birds of prey flying under Tyrol Castle.
Built between 1767 and 1773 by the architect Pietro Augustoni on the main square, he holds a fifteenth-century crucifix and statues of the Evangelists of Varlé.
The treasures of the Collegiate.
A frescoed cave inhabited since prehistoric times.

Opened in May 2009 in the old mill in the center of the country and managed by Pro Loco in agreement with the Municipality, it illustrates the phases of the vinification, from the grape harvest to the fermentation to the bottling, and exhibits traditional agricultural tools.
Dry spurs of glacial origin with flora and fauna of the Steppe environments, reachable on foot or by bike.
Marble arch of 1518 with bell tower and clock, next to the church of the SS. Annunziata; the complex is now the seat of the Faculty of Engineering.

Officially inaugurated on 17 November 2000, it collects fifty old tower clock machines, some coming from abroad, which the master watchmaker Salvatore Ricci found and brought back into operation in the course of life; the collection was then purchased by the National Research Council. Since 2007 it has been permanently located in the restored rooms of a nineteenth-century palace in the historic center, between Via Rovagnera and Muro Nuovo, which in the mid-Twentieth century had been an oil mill; the students of the technical institute \Medi-Livatino Â .
The birthplace of the Nobel Prize-winning writer, in the district of Santu Pedru, which preserves the memory of an artist who opened Sardinia to the world.
The Terracotta Complaint of the Fondulis.

Phenomenon of erosion: the morainic clay left by the glaciers is very hard to dry but melts with the rain, and the big boulders protect it, leaving standing columns that grow at every storm and collapse when the boulder falls. You can see in three gorges: the Rio Fosco valley between Longomoso and Santa Maria, Rio Rivellone under Soprabolzano and Rio Gasterer in Auna di Sotto; from Collalbo 30 minutes walk to the panoramic points.

Inaugurated on November 14, 1999 in the premises of the former nursery school in Mairago thanks to the collaboration between the Municipality, Province of Lodi and Fondazione Cariplo, it is managed by the Astrofili Messier 42 Group, born in 1992 in Lodi Vecchio. It includes a dome with the main telescopes and a CCD room for real time viewing and photographing, a videoconference room and two bedrooms (25 beds). The evenings begin with a presentation to the video projector of 30-50 minutes, followed by a visit to the dome; with clear sky you can also see with small telescopes in the courtyard.

On a hill inhabited by the Bronze Age, probably of Lombard origin and documented since 1191: double wall, sixteenth-century bastion and 25 meters high mast. The bishops of Trento, then of Mainardo di Tirolo, were rebuilt in the fifteenth century by the de Federicis, taken by the rebel peasants in 1525 and used as barracks and deposit Austro-Hungarian in the Great War; of the Province since 1992, it has been open to the public since 2014. From summer 2026 free audio guide in Italian, English and German.
Masterpiece of Romanesque and Gothic architecture in the medieval city, restored to its appearance after the 1976 earthquake.

The "castrum" of Andezeno is mentioned in the peace of 1261 between the accounts of Biandrate and the Municipality of Chieri. The nucleus of the 12th century was destroyed in the sixteenth century by the Spanish army; on the top remains the defence tower, then transformed into a bell tower and the clock in the facade, while parts of the structure were incorporated into the omea, Berta and Villa residences.
The 14th-century castle where you can taste the wine of the territory.
At the top of the hill, outside the walls, the fortress reminiscent of the ancient settlement and offers a beautiful view of the village.

On a hill above the Rivosecco valley, a few kilometers from the village, an Italian settlement active from the VII to the II-III century BC: about six hectares surrounded by a high dry wall in some places up to three meters, with polygonal walls, various doors, a cistern excavated in the rock, foundations of huts and terraces; at the foot of the slope a necropolis, damaged by the quarries. It has been proposed as the possible Tarincria "arce."
Woods, farms and a panoramic mountain hut in one ring.

Born from a research of the students of the middle school of Ales (1993-96) with the support of the University of Cagliari, opened in 2002 in the former elementary school of Zeppara and reopened in 2013 after the restoration: handcrafted toys of the Sardinian agropastoral world made with local materials, from the dolls of rags and pumpkin to the carts of asphodelo, trottole and sound instruments, with a carpentry workshop to build them.
Kilometers of sand for everyone.

The territory, in the Regional Natural Park of the Simbruini Mountains, is closed between Monte Tarino (1,959 m) and Monte Autore (1,853 m), with the valley of the Simbrivio; from Vallepietra start hiking trails (683a-d towards Monte Authore, 684 towards Monte Tarinello and the Pozzo della Neve, 685 towards Colle della Tagliata), the Coleman trails towards Jenne and Camerata Nuova and MTB routes.
Courtyard free of charge. Anatomical Theatre: guided tour €12 / €10 reduced, or audioguide €10 / €8 reduced

Church in Goregnis di Vernasso with polygonal Gothic apse at the time ribbed. The golden altar, of 1689, is the work of the engraver Bartolomeo Ortari of Caporetto; the frescoes of the Apostles in the apse are attributed to Bartolomeo da Loka (1530-1535).
Information and contemporary art.
The first Bernini architect.

Domina Piazza Vescovado: built between 1512 and 1536 and renovated in 1760, it preserves in the apse a Madonna delle Grazie by Marco Cardisco (16th century) and in sacristy cupboards and eighteenth-century stuccos. From here starts the walk signposted towards Marina della Lobra.
€3, reduced €1 (6-14 years), free under 6 and with KlausenCard
MiC card (updated 2021) indicates visits only on request and during truffle fairs

Built between 1561 and 1579 on a previous fortress, on a project by Guidetto Guidetti and then by Giovan Domenico Bianchi; here lived Federico Cesi, founder of the Accademia dei Lincei (1603), who hosted Galileo in 1624. On the ground floor mythological vaults inspired by the Metamorphosis of Ovid, on the noble floor wooden coffered ceilings (Throne Room, Emperors' Room, Muse); since 1964 it is of the University of Perugia and hosts guided tours, exhibitions and the Museum of Bees and Honey.
The bridge where the Sile meets the Cagnan, with a plaque that shows the verses of Dante's Paradise on the union of the two rivers.
One of the largest residences in Pompeii, about 3,000 square meters, excavated in the Bourbon age and famous for the mosaic of the Battle of Alessandro.
The entrance door of the Roman Rimini.
Herbs and peasant life of the Velino valley.
Opened in 1938 in the municipal loggia of Ceneda on the collection of Luigi Marson: the trench, the year of Austrian occupation after Caporetto and the final battle of autumn 1918.
The Roman Sulmona.
The exhibition space of Via Pescheria which houses some of the most important art and photography exhibitions in the city.
Castle, gardens and snowfall of the family of Giorgio Gallesio.
The Bourbon hunting palace.
The castle founded by Siena between 1213 and 1219, closed by 570 meters of walls with 14 towers, mentioned by Dante; stop of the Via Francigena.
A Roman villa overlooking the sea.
The gipsoteca of a sculptor of the twentieth century.
To get to know the Marsican bear.
€2, combined museum + guided tour of the reserve €5
The sports complex designed at the end of the 1920s by Renato Ricci, with the Stadio dei Marmi and the Stadio Olimpico on the slopes of Monte Mario.

On three locations: Palazzo del Governore alle Armi, Donjone di Porta Cividale with documents, uniforms and weapons of the garrisons from the Serenissima (1593) to today, and external route on the walls; guided tours.
Two medieval bridges on the stream, visible after 2-3 minutes of path.
Sixteenth-century summer residence of the Counts Rasponi along the Lamone, today home to shows and meetings.

The Museum inaugurated in 2000 preserves the historical and artistic heritage of the Diocese in three sections: archaeological, historical-artistic and sacred art, the "Tesoro dei Papi" with vestments belonging to John XXI and Pius IX.

Born as a Benedictine monastery in the 8th century, in 1216 it was donated to Saint Francis and passed to the Friars Minor; according to tradition Saint Francis and Saint Anthony stayed there. A popular saying binds him to the nearby Mount of Verna.
The 14th-century Certosa and the finds of the island.

More than three kilometers of fine golden sand between Cala di Monte Turno and Cala Sinzias, with water from emerald green to turquoise, deep-sea suitable for snorkeling and diving (cernies and gorgonies) and an oasis of Mediterranean maquis behind; on the promontory stands the nuraghe Gibe Truttiri. Much of the coast is free.
Permanent exhibition on geology, biology and birth of the UNESCO World Heritage Dolomites.

Church in a hut along the road between Vione and Lecanù, with fourteenth-century bell tower on the north side, restored after a period of degradation lasted until the 1930s; tradition binds it to St. Charles Borromeo, with a stone object of veneration.
The starting point for the islands of Trasimeno.
The patron's cathedral.
The great baroque Bergamo in the heart of the village.
The granite sculptures of the Gallura wind.
Fossil, dwarf palms and the tower on the head at sunset.
The hill of farmsteads and cellars that produce the homonymous wine, reachable by the Karl von Ritter promenade with views of the old town.
The nineteenth-century theatre of Corso Canalgrande dedicated to Luciano Pavarotti and Mirella Freni, with the statue of the tenor at the entrance.
The geometric green of the bishops principles.

Guard tower mentioned around the thousand in a donation of San Guido to the Church of Acqui, enlarged after the Saracen incursions and transformed in the fourteenth century into a castle with octagonal tower; in the eighteenth century a second body with cylindrical tower made it a noble residence. Floors in majolica, furnishings and frescoes with coats of arms of the XVI-XVII centuries, cellars with brick vaults. From 1598 to 1922, from 1951 of the Remondini family, which produces wine. Visits according to the official website of the castle.
The medieval heart of Casacalenda.
The shrine in the green just outside the village, with the fifteenth-century image of the Madonna that suckles and the former vows of the faithful.
The seaside village of Agrigento, center of summer town, with fish dinners and events on the seafront.

Castle of probable Longobard origin, modified by the De Capua from the thirteenth century and transformed between 1510 and 1515 by Bartolomeo III in fortress with palace: the portal bears the date 1515 and the Latin motto "If guest, login. Flee, if enemy The cylindrical tower is almost 20 meters high, with crowning of stone bushes, three inner rooms, iron staircase and cistern dug into the rock, on a cliff near the stream Succida that dominates the valley of Fortore.
On the bay of Porto Conte, a nuragic settlement dating back to the 14th century B.C. became one of the oldest commercial ports on the island, with the nearby Roman villa of the 1st century B.C.

Hole dug by water behind the village, with rock walls that almost touch each other; they are a geosite of the UNESCO Geopark of Majella. Legend has it that St. Martin has widened the strait with his elbows to make the shepherds pass towards the mountain, and the "marmittes" in the rock would be the marks left. You will walk along the path H1: to enter the gorges the Park strongly recommends helmet and suitable footwear.

On a rock spur above the valley of Scoltenna-Panaro, about three kilometers from the center, it was a residence and military center of the Montecuccoli, which controlled dozens of towers guarding the streets for Tuscany; the mast is on the highest point, surrounded by three circles of walls. A Gothic portal introduces to the medieval village with the Palazzo del Podestà and the fifteenth-century church of San Lorenzo. The castle, completely restored in 2009, hosts the Montecuccolo Museum Centre with the Donation Raffaele Biolchini, the country rediscovered by Gino Covili and the Naturalistic Museum of Frignano.
The panorama of the Tronto valley.

The early medieval castrum rose on a cliff at the foot of the Martani: the walls and the large door to Piazza Umberto I, decorated with carved stones and the coat of arms of the village, with buildings of the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries. On the square the palace that housed Giuseppe and Anita Garibaldi in 1849; the Town Hall, sixteenth century and restored at the end of the nineteenth century, has an elegant bell tower.
A rococo parish church on the Greek cross.
A centuries-old forest just a stone's throw from the village.
Tratto collinare with steps; you will also arrive by car or train San Luca Express
The peasant life of the Dauni Mountains.
The neoclassical mother church.
Medieval and fifteenth-century works in the historical parish.
The panorama over the entire lake, up to Anguillara and Bracciano.
A children's walk to the castle.
Trecento frescoes and paintings by Claudio Ridolfi.

Local agricultural objects and a rich collection of women's costumes from the Western Alps, including those from Pragelato and Fenestrelle, with typical headphones and multicolored fabrics, and costumes from the Val di Susa and Queyras; the ticket includes a guided tour of about an hour and a half.
The tradition of stone chisels.
Get down into the tunnels of what was the largest copper mine in Europe.

The Lion Gate, which takes its name from a feline head that became the symbol of the maestral, is part of the walls built in the early nineteenth century against the barbarisc pirates. There are still sighting towers and stretches of belt; from Fort Santa Cristina you can see the roofs of the village and the nearby ponds, while Fort Santa Teresa is today a private residence.

On a spur over 1000 m on the Pelago basin, it was of the Longobards and Matilde of Canossa and from 1240 of the Montegarullo; Obizzo made it the Guelph fortress of Frignano until he was defeated in 1408. The arms room became parish church in 1586: in its crypt in 2011 more than 300 bodies were discovered buried between the Five and the eighteenth century, almost one hundred mummified, exhibited with the accessories in the museum of the fortress. In the parish of São Paulo a golden tabernacle of 1603 and a Madonna of the Rosary of G.B. Bertusio (1627); at the foot of the Captain's House.
From the end of the thirteenth century, with fine frescoes.
First century A.D. residence discovered in 1885, with atrium and mosaic floors; an inscription is attached to the mother of the Emperor Vespasian.
Fresh even in summer.
In the center of the old town district, it has a large Baroque façade with local terracotta parishyard and inside works by Gagini and Camarda.

The historic centre, perfectly preserved, maintains important stretches of walls with doors and six towers of the 15th and 16th centuries; you enter it from the Belvedere De Carolis, from which you can see many buildings of the 17th and 18th centuries.
A village with an Arab plant.

Ancient crypt of the church of Santa Maria della Piazza, one of the oldest religious buildings in the country; in 1652 it was donated to the Confraternity of San Giacomo, which had it restored. The 17th-century frescoes depict scenes from the Old and New Testaments, the glory of Mary on the vault and Saint Catherine of Alexandria on the bottom; the trapdoor 'pro confratibus' towards the ancient sepulchre is closed after the 1980 earthquake. Visit by reservation.
The churchyard overlooking the lake.

Opened in 2009 at the initiative of Mgr. Antonino Orrù on the second and third floors of the former Tridentino Seminary, 19th century building: works from the cathedral and other parishes of the diocese, including four bells from the 16th to the 18th century (the oldest cast in 1573 by Pietro Tolo) and two stone lions from the 17th century. Open on midweek holidays; from Monday to Thursday by reservation.
The gastronomic heart of the city.
Three villages in one, over a thousand meters.
Canova to Picasso.

White control tower of Spanish era in front of the port, built in granite and porphyry towards the middle of the sixteenth century; it was part of a chain of coastal towers, of which also remains that of San Gemiliano. The name Arbatax would come from an Arabic expression that means "the fourteenth tower" .
12th century church next to the Rocca Farnese, linked to Cardinal Alessandro Farnese, born in Valentano in 1520; its bells come from the ancient city of Castro.
Stone stele about 4 meters high, dated to the VII-VI century BC, today in the center of Piazza Castello. It was found in 1499 near the church of San Michele, demolished in 1649.
The oldest part of the belt.
The ceramics of the High Ofanto from prehistory to today.
The octagonal church.
The Romanesque of Corneto.
Among the largest medieval districts in Europe.
The history of the lost city of Atella.
Built between 1310 and 1455 and dedicated to the patron saint of the city, with altars and pulpit of relief; next to the Chapel of Santa Barbara (1423-1450).

The most important of the village, with a single nave, with facade with circular carvings and side chapels with the coats of arms of the most influential families. The main altar is in veined marble, perhaps from the early seventeenth century, with a canvas attributed to Pucciarelli; the Virgin of the Rescue is of Peccheneda and the Baroque pulpit in wood, with scenes of the Gospels, is of Fortunato Capero.
Of origin of the 11th century, on the top of the hill, with the bell tower with a dodecagonal plan.
The Renaissance building in Via de' Benci with the collection of English collector Herbert Percy Horne: the Santo Stefano by Giotto, Simone Martini, Filippo Lippi, Beccafumi and Pietro Lorenzetti.

A monastery from the 14th century, which later became a prison, now houses the museum dedicated to the painter Karl Wilhelm Diefenbach, the National Archaeological Museum of Capri and art exhibitions.
A set of churches, cloisters and courtyards that arose in different eras, the oldest religious nucleus in the city, with the Courtyard of Pilate and the Benedictine cloister.

Along the coast of the promontory are the Blue Grotto, the Cave of the Nativity, the Capre, the Fossellone, the Hanging and the Maga Circe, with the coastal places of the Battery, Punta Rossa, the Cava dell'Alabaster and the Precipice; the boat ride around the promontory is among the suggested experiences. In the caves of the Circeo were found traces of human presence of the Middle Paleolithic.
Reachable with a walk from the center.
The eastern Alps are 3,000.
Natural terrace at 206 meters above sea level, on which rises the city.
Late Renaissance complex with five floors frescoed by various artists and the Scala Regia, helical staircase supported by 30 Doric columns.
The largest dome in the diocese.

In the chapel of Sant'Apollonia del Duomo: reliquaries, crosses, glasses and vestments, including the green pivial of San Moderano (perhaps byzantine from the 8th to the 9th century or Lucca from the 12th), a glass of 1517 and a rare glass glass, probably of the 8th century, found in 1971 in a tomb under the presbytery.
The Neanderthals of Mount Fenera.
Walk on the Garda.
Between the sea of the Etruscans and the park of Vulci, with the Etruscan port of Regisvilla and the Pellicone pond in the WWF oasis on the Fiora.
Opened in May 1996, it includes the Pinacoteca della Resistance and a section dedicated to Caldarola Sistina, with space for temporary exhibitions.
The history of the woodsmen at the entrance of the valley.

Started in 1093 under Bishop Girardo da Piacenza and finished in 1120 in Romanesque-Trojan style: it incorporates an earlier church of Santa Maria (1080-1086), still visible in the apse. The rose window (1160-1180), of Arab and Angevin influences, has eleven columns with Corinthian capitals and twenty-two stone tunnel fields; the Gate of the Madonna on the left side was restored in the thirteenth century. Open every day 9-12.30 and 16-20.

The city of the Este Renaissance, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1995: the Castle, the Cathedral, the Erculean Addition with the Diamonds' Palace, the Schifanoia Show of Months and almost 9 km of walls to be turned by bike.
Parish church next to the seventeenth-century Jesuit College: it preserves wooden statues, including the Christ de s'Iscravamentu, and a sixteenth-century retablo called St. Christopher.
Panoramic garden overlooking the gulf, where exhibitions are often held; an elevator descends to Marina Piccola and the port.
A walk along the lakefront leads to the ancient port of Toscolano, surrounded by historic buildings; on the lakefront there is also the large planeland that the inhabitants call
The sketches of the great sculptures.
The otter canyon in Cilento.
Bridge dedicated to Maria Cristina di Savoia, wife of Ferdinand II of Bourbon, destroyed during the war and rebuilt in reinforced concrete in 1946-1947.

Borgo della Tuscia linked to Giulia Farnese, sister of Pope Paul III, who since 1506, was a feudal man for 25 years and renewed it: the Farnese Castle, the sixteenth-century church of Santa Maria and the small Saint Lucia, to which the church of San Filippo Neri is added (1636).

The center preserves the medieval system, with winding streets between houses connected by archivolti, born to defend against rigid mountain winters; the inhabitants have transformed it into an open-air museum with tools of shepherds and peasants, barber tools, home environments, vintage clothes and games exposed in alleys and balconies. The late Baroque Oratory of the Assunta has for its bell tower a late-Roman defensive tower of the fifth century transformed in the thirteenth century in Romanesque bell tower cuspidato with two-fores in terracotta; the parish church of St. Peter the Apostle is of the first half of the seventeenth century, in late Renaissance forms.
17th century wooden statues and an organ from the 18th century.

Born on June 10, 2006 for the centenary of the Nobel in Camillo Golgi, it occupies three floors of the old town hall renovated near the parish and combines materials of the old exhibition and new acquisitions: a rich collection of medical-scientific instruments of epoch, with the reconstruction of a clinic of the late nineteenth century and a histological laboratory. A few meters away is the birthplace with memorial stone; from the museum starts the Camillo Golgi Trail, with 18 biographical panels along the ancient Valeriana street to Aprica.

Of Lombard origin (IX century), it rises on the remains of the Roman theater of Acerrae; in the twelfth century it was decorated with polychrome tarsies of tuff, in the siege of 1421 it was described as "baluardo imprendibile" and at the end of the fifteenth century it became a noble residence, with new rooms, windows and gardens.
Apulian art from the Middle Ages to the twentieth century.
The chapel entirely frescoed by Ferro.

Sabina village about 60 km from Rome built on the remains of Trebula Mutuesca, pre-Roman center of the cults of Feronia, Angitia and Vacuna and then Roman town hall: the amphitheatre rebuilt by Traiano and the findings of the Civic Archaeological Museum, next to the Romanesque sanctuary of Santa Vittoria with its catacombs.

On Sannitic and Roman walls, Longobard fence of the tenth century with towers, enlarged by the Angioini after the earthquake of 1349 with three cylindrical towers and the moat; in the sixteenth century Count Enrico Pando transformed it into a residence and had the halls decorated with horses of his stable, relief painted in front, each with name, age, race and H of Henricus. 14th century staircase, noble floor, loggia, Salone dei Conti and garden; it is home to the National Museum, which also preserves the Polyptych of the Passion of Christ.
An aperitif in Lucca's living room.

In the basement of the ancient church of the Confraternita, he collects works and memories left to the village by Margherita Martini, second wife of illustrator Attilio Mussino, who spent the last years in Vernante founding a free art school open to all; at the cemetery a bas-relief shows Pinocchio crying on his grave.

In 1611 a first building with garden belonged to the Perabò, which in the eighteenth century enlarged the villa; passed to the Melzi d'Eril and in 1850 to the Cagnola, it was transformed into a romantic residence by Luigi Clerichetti (1856-58) for Carlo Cagnola and renovated in 1900-01 by Achille Majnoni d'Intignano for Guido Cagnola, who in 1946 donated it to the Holy See; it is home to the Higher Institute of Religious Studies, today ISSR Blessed Paul VI, and it is also a convention center with hotel and restaurant. The English park, west and north of the villa, has tall trees such as the cedar of Lebanon and the sophora of Japan, a terraced garden closed by a long balcony and a Neo-Medieval tower with terracotta trifores. The park is open from 8 to 19 (April 1-30 September) and from 9 to 16 (October 1 to March 31), with access only from the main entrance; dogs allowed on leash.
A single nave church with stone portal dating back to 1592; inside an octagonal baptismal font of the sixteenth century and the Madonna del Rosario painted in 1583 by Felice Damiani.
The Judgment on the Bisalta.

Small centre rich in historical buildings born with the textile activity started by the Cistercian monks and culminated in the second half of the seventeenth century: Palazzo Barberis-Rusca, at the foot of the abbey, built by Francesco Fadda who from 1666 joined the simple cloths more precious fabrics, and the Bernardi and Tandura palaces.
Rebuilt several times between the Five and the nineteenth century, it preserves a work by Luca Cambiaso.
The history of discovery and the geology of the caves, to complement the visit.

Some caves purchased by the municipality have become ethnographic museum; in one of them the Museum of peasant civilization exhibits tools and objects of common use of rural life.
The pulpit of 1271 and the Gothic tombs.
Walk on the ancient shore of the sea, today in the countryside.

Beaches with free access on grass or white pebbles: the Sabbioni, the largest and equipped with services, rentals and sports areas; the Pini beach (Purfina), more informal and frequented by windsurfers; Punta Lido at the confluence of the streams, close to the center. The Pelèr in the morning and the Hour in the afternoon make regular sailing and windsurfing.
Born from a legacy to the municipality, it collects furniture and works of art acquired in decades by its eclectic benefactor.
The medieval mill that fed the castle.
On a rocky promontory reached by a staircase and surrounded by a loggia of 28 arches, with the Baroque interior and the polyptych of Gaudenzio Ferrari (Supposition of Saint Catherine, 1516-20).

Domina Orvinio from the year 1000: held by the lords of Canemorto until the fifteenth century, enlarged by the Orsini in the sixteenth century (a palace called "Granarone") fortified by the Muti and from 1632 of the Borghese, which in two centuries gave him the present aspect. Cracked walls circling almost all the center, cylindrical mast and rustic portal; inside the halls with wooden ceilings with drawers, frescoes of the late sixteenth century on the exploits of the Barons Muti and traps then transformed into cellars.
Behind the scenes of the frescoes, with lake view.
The mummies of Roccapelago in the castle of Obizzo.
A fountain with imperial legend.
The frescoes of the fourteenth century.

Pre-Roman city on the Amerina street, surrounded by polygonal walls with six doors: the Roman cistern under Piazza Matteotti, the museum with the bronze of Germanico in the former convent of San Francesco, the Duomo with the dodecagonal tower and the noble palaces of the Five and seventeenth centuries.
The city museum housed in the ancient fortress.
The green lung next to the center.
The world of Guareschi and behind the scenes of the films.
The fortress that guards the Fiastra Valley.

One of Sicily's oldest sulphites, excavated perhaps from 1600, owned by the princes of Trabia and Butera; around 1920 it produced about 12% of the world's sulphur with about 3,000 miners. A fire in 1883 killed dozens of workers; the cable car of about 9,800 meters, of 1900, brought sulphur to Ravanusa. Closed in 1975, it was purchased by the Region between 2000 and 2003; it remains a stretch of cable car, castelletti and calcaroni, and in the center of Palladio has restored an interactive didactic path with simulated descent into the well, Tosi engines and the photographic exhibition "Sulfaro and Sulfatari" .
Woods and trails towards Monte Oggioli.
The eighteenth-century door that gives access to the medieval village of Piazzo and to the bridge overlooking Biella Piano.

Ring of about 5 hours from the small church of Sant'Antonio Abate, on the Colle della Fratta from the 12th century, passing through Bolca, Monte Spilecco (where shark teeth were found) and Monte Pergo up to Vestenavecchia, touching the crosses erected between 1894 and 1899 by the pastor Celestino Baldo (1828-1900).

Established in 1989 in the country that has for patron Saint Rufo,     Â tavolarius Â Roman martyrized in 303 and then patron of the letter holders. In five halls documents, Country by Country, the postal systems (logos, uniforms, sacks, historical and current means of transport), with materials sent by the ministries of the post offices of the five continents; the artistic section preserves the unmade sketches of about 400 stamps of Italian and foreign artists. It periodically hosts international exhibitions and exhibitions.

Borgo 651 meters on the southern slopes of Monte Morra, in the Regional Natural Park of the Lucretile Mountains, 51 km from Rome: dominated by the Castle Orsini-Cesi-Borghese, which in 1603 was the seat of the Accademia dei Lincei, preserves the churches of San Nicola di Bari and Santa Lucia and is the starting point of the path to the Pratone di Monte Gennaro.
The painter of the peasants of Abruzzo in his city.
Birdwatching in the plain.
The Jesuit Church was founded in 1701 with an oval plan, whose dome and two bell towers collapsed in December 1933.

Borgo on a hill to the right of the Cesano, known for the Archaeological Park of Suasa, the Roman city with the Domus dei Coiedii and its mosaics, and for the Archaeological Museum "Casagrande" in the Renaissance Palace of the Rovere; in September the Festa della Cipolla.
Medieval village in the municipal territory with the remains of a fortress, the church of the Holy Trinity in St. Francis (XIII century) and that of the Madonna delle Grazie (XV century).
Light sand and sea lilies on the dunes.

Giant bench on the Hill of the Castle above the village, inspired by the motto "Everyone in his own way" engraved also on the bell tower of Coazze. It is reached on foot in 30-40 minutes from the center and offers a wide panorama.
Among the most important examples of rural architecture in Gran Paradiso, today Maison de l'alimentation with an exhibition on traditional products and the evolution of conservation techniques.
The MiC card (updated to May 2020) indicates "Closed" every day; contact 0824 977901, meg@artsanniocampania.it
A fortress of the Swabian age near the sea.

Among Europe's major marine aquariums, opened in 1992 for Colombians: Mediterranean, Caribbean coral reefs, Antarctic waters with penguins and tactile tanks with rays; next to the Biosphere in glass and steel with a tropical forest.

Via Roma is the ancient heart of the city, with porticos, noble palaces and internal courtyards and the weekly market on Wednesday; at its extremes the church of Battuti Rossi and the Bastione del Salice, the rest of the walls that surrounded the city until the Napoleonic age. The Borgo Vecchio, an original nucleus, preserves medieval buildings, narrow alleys and low porticos.

The castle is surrounded by gardens with English and ancient roses, centuries-old trees, a avenue of centuries-old hornbeams, the brolo (ancient walled garden), the secret garden, a fish pond, a glacier, a belvedere and the labyrinth of Minotauro.
The hermitages suspended on the Gulf of Manfredonia.
The ancient underground aqueduct.
The craftsmanship of the world.

The port dates back to the Roman age; today, among colorful buildings overlooking the sea, it is a marina and sports with winter regattas, restaurants and departures for the Pontine Islands. It is one of the favorite places for sunset.
The 16th century Crucifix.
The religious heart of the village.
The giant oaks of the Lucane Dolomites.
Long panoramic walk on the eastern side of the promontory, on the Adriatic, which rises towards the castle.
The Valsassine roots of the Manzoni family.
The fountains of the country of the water.

It rediscovers traditions and ancient crafts with everyday objects and work tools, rebuilding scenes of life disappeared with old maps and vintage photographs. The route is divided into themes: the Lanzo Valleys, the people, agriculture and sheep farming, handicrafts, flora, fauna and mineralogy; curious the collection of nails, once forged in the valley and exported throughout Italy. From May to October the first and third Sundays of the month, 15-18; in the other periods by telephone reservation (333 4825771). Accessible to the disabled.

Rebuilt after 1693, with richly ornate portal, four-column façade, three naves and a precious marble altar; it housed the Annunciation of Antonello da Messina (1474), today at the Museo Bellomo in Syracuse.

Two cylindrical towers remain of the 14th century castle, the environments of the trappet and the south bastion; in 1473 Aldonza Santapau was strangled. In the courtyard the fountain of the Ninfa Zizza of 1607, which marked the arrival of drinking water in the village and recalls the legend of the girl transformed into a spring.
Medieval houses with beautiful portals and stone windows, on the Roman route.

Lake Moncenisio open to the public and members; the fishing is reserved for holders of the card of the US Susa, which can be purchased on site in the wooden house near the lake, where also the good fishing is released.
The first palace of the Medici, where Cosimo il Vecchio and Lorenzo il Magnifico lived, with the Chapel of the Magi of Benozzo Gozzoli.
The colorful heart of Bosa.
Thermal baths powered by sulphurous sources.
From the door starts the course flanked by baroque palaces towards the central square.

Borgo dei Monti Sibillini overlooking Mount Vettore and Mount Sibilla, linked to the legend of the Sibilla: in the center the fourteenth-century civic tower and the church of San Benedetto Abate, from the hamlet of Foce you go up to Lake Pilate, the only natural glacial lake of the Marche.

The pyrite mine, known since the Middle Ages, was an important resource for the country until 1964; the park, inaugurated on July 29, 2008, also in memory of the miners, some of whom lost their lives, is visited along the gallery Leyla, with equipment and materials arranged in a thematic itinerary set up with the Museo Tridentino di Scienze Naturali. The network of tunnels extends for about 40 km until under Bosentino and Vattaro, but most are not accessible. At the Center of mining reception an exhibition of minerals of Trentino and lamps, open from May to August 2026 on Saturday and Sunday 17-19, free admission.
The story of the Granda.

In the heart of the city, at Villa Binetti, it tells two centuries of the Montebellunese footwear district: thousands of shoes, historic objects, sketches, patents and machinery in 11 rooms on two floors, from the nineteenth century to today. Times indicated: Monday-Wednesday 9.30-13, Thursday-Friday 9.30-18, Saturday and Sunday closed.
Medici campaign.
The giant bench.

Built in 1442 to defend the port from pirates, on Greek and Roman remains: almost trapezoidal plant with circular towers at the corners; in the sixteenth century, under the Pignatelli, sugar cane was worked there.
A Romanesque tower in the mountains.

The grapes Avanà, Avarengo and Neretto del Pinerolese Ramie are cultivated on the first slopes of the Germanasca Valley, produced only in Pomaretto and Perosa Argentina. A path crosses the Ramìe vineyards with panels of the municipality on the territory and on the wine, connected to the visit of the Latin School.

The only island of Lake Como, was Roman military garrison, political centre and important religious center of the diocese; theatre of the fight against Barbarossa, then abandoned, from the early twentieth century is archaeological site with Roman columns, early Christian testimonies, fragments of mosaic and remains of various Romanesque churches. The exhibits are exhibited at the Antiquarium of Ossuccio, from which you cross the lake by boat. Island and museum open from March to October.

Porta Alvaro, of the fourteenth century and already mentioned in the statues of 1570, is the main entrance to the historic center; the Porta delle Fonti or San Bernardino is the second historical access, between stone stairs, walls and houses on the hill.
The pilgrimage of every lover.
The parlor of the village, with the fountain of the three saints.
The light of the Mediterranean.
An old town that, seen from the port, looks like a ship ready to sail.
The seistine treasure of the diocese.
Between the walls of the Cultural Pole of Orphans, the history and technology of the book and the press.
The memory of the front.

Small Christian building dedicated to the Saviour, on a rocky spur near the sources, in the form of a small temple tetrastyle in antis with four Corinthian columns and Roman materials of reuse; on the pediment a bas-relief with Latin cross, inside a cell turned to barrels and apse. The dating is discussed (end IV-beginning V century or VII-VIII century, in the Lombard age); the frescoes of the VII-VIII century, with angels around the gemstone cross, Christ in majesty and Saints Peter and Paul, are considered the oldest in Umbria. Since 2011 it is one of the seven UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Italy. Places of power (568-774 A.D.); inspired Francesco di Giorgio Martini, Benozzo Gozzoli and Palladio.
Fortification can be reached along the paths above the city, along with the remains of the romoratory and the church of Sant'Agnese on the homonymous saddle.

Municipality of the Parma Apennines between the Romanesque churches of Sasso and Bazzano, with three small original museums: the Resistance of July 1944, the first museum in the world dedicated to padlocks and the Museum Man-Environment in a house-tower of the thirteenth century.
Borgo on the right of the homonymous stream, also known for the houses-towers and covered passages.

In the square of the Clock, at the beginning of Via Borgo, the nineteenth-century stone fountain with the coat of arms of the village, shaped like a small neoclassical temple that recalls a Pantheon, next to the Clock Tower, among the most valuable architectural elements of the center. Not far away the viewpoint of Piazza Matteotti opens onto the hills of Subappennino Dauno.

Here in 1091 San Bruno built the first monastic settlement, the hermitage of the Tower; the church was consecrated in 1094 by the Archbishop of Palermo Alcherio and in the early sixteenth century there were found the relics of the saint. Between ancient white fir trees and young beech trees, with a granite staircase and the dormitory of San Bruno, is the place of the most tourist and religious attraction of the village; next there is the pond where the saint prayed immersed in the freezing waters in sign of penance. The processions take place on Monday and Tuesday of Pentecost.
Leaders, rural life and nature under the same roof.

Dean's seat of early medieval origins, the current church in classical style dates back to the mid-19th century and forms with the isolated bell tower, the town hall and the houses of the square a harmonious complex. Open every day from 8 am to 6 pm; Sunday Mass at 10 am in German and, from mid-July to August, at 11.15 am in Italian. At the tourist office there is the guide to the churches of Castelrotto and Siusi (€5).

Meadows known for the abundance of flowers, crossed by paths 15 and 15A along the stations of the Way of the Cross, with a biotope pond and views of Sas dla Crusc, Marmolada, Sella, Puez-Odle and Putia. The ring from the sanctuary of La Crusc returns to Badia in 9 km (about 2 hours and 45, 793 meters of descent) passing through the Ütia Ranch from André and the farms of Cialaruns, Alfarëi, Ruac and Fussé.

In an eighteenth-century building, the house of the composer master Canciani houses on three floors a collection of musical instruments that illustrates the history of organ, harpsichord and piano, with eighteenth-century manuscripts of unpublished music and rare ancient books; the tour is guided by his son Daniel Canciani. It is a section of the Ecomuseum Mistirs; visits by reservation (0433 70162).

Medieval fountain in front of the church of San Marco Evangelista, dedicated to the wife of Guiscardo, with three caryatids called Sikelgaita, Virtue and Smorfiosa; restored over time, preserves the water path and part of the sculptures.

The castle overlooking Strada in Casentino and gives its name to the municipality. The counts Guidi held it until 1349, when the inhabitants rebelled and submitted to the Florentine Republic; from the fifteenth century the territory was administered directly from Florence.

Borgo on a hill at 470 meters, the castle that best preserves the medieval appearance among the fortifications of the area: built in 1167 by Count Ghibelline Brandaglia Alberico d'Uguccione, is closed by a belt up to 15 meters high with a turrita door. Inside, the square of the Cisterna with stone and brick houses and the 12th-century castle; from the church on the north side, the view extends over Pratomagno, valleys of the Arno and the Ambra, Valdichiana, Casentino and La Verna.

Natural monument: high cliffs of red porphyry and black diorite emerging from the emerald green sea next to the port of Arbatax, at the foot of the hill of Bellavista; set of the final scene of Large parking lot.
The high-altitude sanctuary.

The present church rises in 1623 on a previous building; the venerated image is a Madonna del Latte di mano populare of the sixteenth century. For the commitment of the parish priest Don Ermelindo Viganò, a short pontifical of 13 October 1949 proclaimed the Virgin of the Ghisallo patron of cyclists: inside the effigy is surrounded by bicycles, shirts, trophies and photographs of champions, and on the square there are the statues of Gino Bartali and Fausto Coppi. It is celebrated on the Easter of cyclists and National Bicycle Day.

Valley almost 4.5 km long in the heart of the Tre Cime Natural Park, from Moso to Rifugio Fondovalle: larch forests and flowered meadows in summer, in winter cross-country skiing or horse-drawn sled. The path 102 is also accessible by bike; the bus 440 and 446 pass alternating every 15 minutes. The Dolomites of Sesto are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Baths over 2,000 years ago.
In La Veulla, alpine animals from recovery centers that cannot return to freedom.
Artificial basin with green waters next to the fort, created in 1940 barring the Isarco river to power a hydroelectric power plant, which dominates the landscape of the valley.
The highest tower in the city can be visited, 218 steps.

Country on the hills of the Aurunci Mountains, which owes its name to the ancient Pre-Roman Ausona (in the Middle Ages it was called Fratte): from the medieval castle, home of the Stone Museum, the view ranges from Montecassino to the Gulf of Gaeta; downstream the Sanctuary of Santa Maria del Piano, above the village the pine forest of Selvacava and Mount Fammera.
The life of a century ago in a thousand objects.
The sea in the city, under the cliffs.
In Marina di Montalto, near Punta delle Murelle, the Etruscan port emerges, which was the economic centre of Vulci.
Consecrated on 18 May 1197 according to an epigraph of 1703; the Byzantine bezel above the portal depicts St Mark between two deacons. It preserves monumental tombs of bishops of the ancient diocese.

Monastery of Benedictines of the fifteenth century, suppressed after the Unity, with bifora fourteenth century and coat of arms Angevin; in the church of San Benedetto valuable paintings and, walled in the municipal seat, the fourteenth-century portal of the disappeared church of San Francesco della Scarpa.
The Palace of Cuba (Cuba Sottana) was built by the Normans; in the neighborhood, used as necropolis at the time of the Punic Wars, a part of the Punic necropolis is still open to visitors.
To the south of the center there are frescoes and ogival windows of the church, mentioned in 1202 together with a nearby hospital.
Church of the historic center; in front, in the yard of San Michele, the Superintendence has highlighted findings on the use of the area between the late antique and medieval ages.

One of the most important centers of Canavese, with the late Dome of 1415 and the octagonal tower of the ancient castle of the Marquises of Monferrato, the prehistoric stele of Lapis Longus in piazza Castello, Palazzo Santa Chiara with its theater and the entrance of the nineteenth-century Canale Cavour on the Po.

In the wholesale fish market on the north pier brings together the Museum of the Maritime Civilization of the Marches, the Museum of the Amphoras, the Museum of the Itticus and the Antiquarium Truentinum.
The Gothic Treviso.
The village of the Madonnas on the Mincio.

Founded in 1867 in the artisan district of Bottonera, next to the bakery of Carlo Moro: on three floors, with pulleys, belts and millstones, he worked day and night until the sixties; today the museum of the cereal cycle, from cleaning to flour.
The Norman mastic that dominates the village.
The stars and the sun from the ... the village of the stars of the Val d'Ega.
The traces of the first inhabitants of the Palermo coast.
The viewpoint on the Aeolians.

Historic nucleus on three main axes, in whose meeting point is the parish church, of medieval origin and rebuilt in the first half of the seventeenth century; the colored houses show the influence of the nearby Liguria. Through the streets and in the park of the Peschiera are exhibited the works of the International Symposium of sculpture on stone, biennial since 2000, sculpted also in the grey sandstone of Carniglia, which was dug from the early twentieth century.
The village church, frescoed in the 1930s.

Started in 1613 in the largest square in the village, it has facade in lava and sandstone attributed to Filippo Vasta and interior with three naves, neoclassical in the naves and baroque in the transept. The wooden choir of 1728 was carved by Giuseppe Turriti, Gioacchino Girelli and Michele and Pietro Orlando; on the main altar a table by Salvatore Mignemi (1756), organ Locatelli of 1903 and works by Salvatore Incorpora, including the twelve apostles in terracotta.
visible only from the outside (MiC card)
The only surviving of the seven gates of the fourteenth-century brick walls of the mid-500s, on the model of the sharp arched doors.
The castle square.

The mining town of Sulcis-Iglesiente in the Geominerario Park of Sardinia: the historic center with the cathedral of Santa Chiara and San Francesco, the mines of Monteponi and Porto Flavia and the coast of Nebida and Masua with the Sugar Pan.

Born in the second half of the thirteenth century with the convent of the Clarisses, it has stuccoes of the eighteenth century, the great painting of the vault of Donato Teodoro and a wooden crucifix.
The Baroque façade of the Jesuits.

At the western end of the coast, Cala Cipolla is a small sheltered creek reachable only on foot; from here a panoramic path rises to the lighthouse of Capo Spartivento, which dominates the southern coast of Sulcis.
The baroque on Signia's hole.
The baptistery of the saint of immigrants.
Romanesque-Gothic monument in Piazza Innocenzo IV, linked in the middle of the thirteenth century to the popes Fieschi Innocenzo IV and Adriano V.
An island-carce became a white donkey reserve.
Cited in 1017 among the goods of the canons of the Arezzo Church, it was transformed in the nineteenth century; it remains the semicircular apse and some original masonry.
A Norman tower turned into an art gallery.
The city of sarcophagi.

In the historic centre, in the former Franciscan convent annexed to the church of Sant'Antonio: four rooms and eight small rooms with a chronological route on the finds collected in the territory from the fifties, from the betelles of the tomb of the giants of Giolve to the architectural elements of nuraghi, from the canalettes of Funtana Oghene to the bronze statue of the priestess of the source of Cantaru Addes, up to milestones, cippi and Roman inscriptions and to the royal copy of the decorated pillar of the

A small artificial lake formed in 1965 by a dam on the Tirino, called the small Atlantis of Abruzzo: the clear waters cover an ancient mill and its silciati and leave in part emerge a paint factory. A diver's destination; those who do not dive see the mill from an electric boat with glass bottom. Balneation prohibited to protect the bird; open Saturday and Sunday 10.30-15.
The Fantoni woods in the parish.
The oldest medieval part, closed by sixteenth-century walls, with the massive tower of the Campano which is the lighthouse to the village.

Medieval water mill in the hamlet of Rijeka, the detached seat of the Museum of Our Earth, still working with pond, closed and original waterfalls fed by the stream Sant'Angelo. For centuries it was one of the five mills of the territory, with a capacity of over 700 quintals of wheat per year; the route reconstructs the life and work of the miller.
A Titian at the top of Sicily.

Val Bregaglia, a few kilometres from Chiavenna, marked by the landslide of 1618 that buried the ancient village: in Prosto survives the Renaissance Palazzo Vertemate Franchi, in Borgonuovo you can visit the excavations of Belfòrt, the multimedia center and the Waterfalls, while the sacristies of Sant'Abbondio house the Museum of Excavations.
All the prehistory and history of Colli Albani in a frescoed villa.
The park of the hills behind the city, with the Leopold aqueduct of the Benedict Valley.

The park surrounds the remains of a synagogue excavated in the 1980s and used between the 4th and 6th centuries AD, the only architectural evidence of the Jewish presence in Calabria at that time and, according to the MiC, the oldest in the West after that of Ostia; the mosaic of the prayer room depicts menorah, palm, cedar and shofar. The museum exhibits the mosaic, a treasure of 3,079 bronze coins in a jug (IV-V century) and a millionaire of 364-367 A.D. Open from Tuesday to Sunday 8.30-14, Monday closed.
A Romanesque Greek cross jewel.

Border village between Lazio and Abruzzo on the ancient via Valeria, feud of the Colonna and then of the Del Drago: the castle of the XI-XII century, the Oratory of the Annunziata of 1422 entirely frescoed, the Roman bridge of San Giorgio and the Museum of Culture in the villa of Ricciotti Garibaldi.
The geosite from which the roofs of Casso came.
It is intended to collect archaeological finds, medieval architectural fragments, fossil collections and period costumes; other medieval fragments are in the gardens behind the Town Hall.
One of the largest churches in the Alps.
The beginning of Spaccanapoli.
A curious neo-Gothic tribute to the Risorgimento.

Village of low and white houses in the north-east of Asinara, at the end of the 25 km road, with an Aragonese tower of the seventeenth century: housed from 1885 to 1997 the penal colony of maximum security, of which remain in the upper part the buildings and bunkers, and today the seat of the park with the Botanical Observatory and a hostel; near, two white sandy beaches, including Sa Murighessa called the beach of the Detainees. You arrive only with the boats authorized by Porto Torres or Stintino.
The symbol of Rome in the world.
The heart of the Serpar rite, documented by the Central Institute for Immaterial Heritage.

Church with bell tower in the historic center, dedicated to the patron saint: the festival, from 20 to 29 September, combines religious, sports and gastronomic events, including the Festival of Pizza Fritta.
The main street of the historic center, porticoed from the sixteenth century, closed by two small squares at the ends.
The Oltregiogo Romanesque.
Flamingos and herons at the gates of Manfredonia.
Romanesque façade partly rebuilt in the Renaissance; the convent complex has a 16th century cloister and houses the civic museum.
The Norman tower that watches over the village.

The smallest system of the UNESCO Dolomites (271 hectares, since 2009): a deep gorge up to 400 meters long and about 8 km long, with at least four waterfalls, which bares the rocks from the late Permian to the Anisic, with traces of the greatest mass extinction of the Earth's history and fossils of footprints of saurians, shells, plants and fishes of about 260 million years ago. The Municipality established the GEOPARC in 2005; from the Visitor Centre of Aldino start the Butterloch geopaths (about 4.6 km, 2h30, to the waterfall) and Gorz (about 6.3 km, 3h20), and daily guided tours in season; compulsory helmet, rentable at the center.
Founded in the thirteenth century, it has a 16th century cloister; the church is an example of provincial architecture of the seventeenth century, with baroque bell tower of the same century.
the bridges are in several municipalities of the valley; routes and accesses not indicated by the source
Climb the tower to see the Valdichiana.
A Roman sarcophagus in a Romanesque church.
In a noble residence of the nineteenth century, it tells the agropastoral and artisan traditions of the territory.
The castle that dominates the Pontina Plain.
The crenellated beast symbol of the country.
The monastery founded in 614 by the Irish monk Colombano, called the northern Montecassino, with the crypt, the saint's sarcophagus and the 12th century pavement mosaic.
A whole village of carved stone.

The alleys of the center are known for the numerous murals and sculptures; in the heart of the village there is Su 'Antaru Vetzu, ancient stone fountain, and the historical districts of 'Astru and 'Antaru vetzu, linked to a station of the Roman military road. Here are also the shops where the masks are still hand carved.

Medieval village of stone houses about 600 meters in the high valley of the Aniene, inside the Parco dei Monti Lucretili, with the Palazzo Borghese, the church of Saint Lucia and the Lagustelli, two karst lakes protected by the Ramsar convention.
Orange Flag of Lake Maggiore with a mild climate, where citrus fruits have been cultivated for centuries, in front of the castles on the water.
By train in the tunnels of the largest manganese mine in Europe.
World War II and Cold War inside a mountain.
The birthplace of the Calabrian prophet.
Circuit of artisan workshops in the historic centre, open on Sundays all year except from 6 January to the first Sunday of March: wood and ceramics, jewelry, lace, watercolors.
Stage 32 of the Via Francigena in Tuscany, on foot among hills, woods and villages from San Gimignano to the castle of Monteriggioni.

Parish church at the foot of the large square tower, symbol of the village: born as a watchtower, used as such until the mid-nineteenth century and then transformed into a bell tower. On the altar there is the oldest representation of the coat of arms of the country.
The village-fortress of the markets in the arcades.
The garden suspended on the ravines.
The works of Jerace and the memory of the city before 1783.
The Cradle of the Challants.

Medieval village of Lunigiana crossed by the Via Francigena, with the church of San Giorgio that houses the stone of Leodegar of 752 and, just outside, the Romanesque parish church of Santo Stefano in Sorano with its archaeological area; in the surroundings the stone villages of Ponticello and Caprio.
The former industrial sheds for the drying of tobacco, opened in 1990, welcome the great pictorial cycles and sculptures of Burri of the last decades, set up by the artist himself.

Monte La Guardia (283 m) is the highest peak of the archipelago: the itinerary starts from the rock of Frisio and passes through Giancos, Sant'Antonio and the Dragonara up to the top in about 3 hours (average difficulty, difference in altitude about 500 m), with the unvisitable ruins of the Old traffic light and the view of the Lighthouse of the Guardia and Palmarola; in spring spontaneous orchids.

The high village, fortified by a double belt, is crossed on a road in pebbles of river: the castle, mentioned for the first time in 1026, has a stone tower and on the tower a 17th century fresco of the Madonna with Child; between the houses stand out the Watchtower and the Tower of the Chaplain, Zanantoni square with the Oratory of San Rocco, the House of Matilde, where according to the tradition stayed Matilde of Canossa, and the House of the Captain (or the Bishop) with the coat of arms frescoed of the Contrari, lords of Savignano since 1409.
A small chest of frescoes behind a wooden door.

The Island of the Sun is the seaside resort of the Adriatic, connected to the mainland by two bridges, with a historic centre of calli and campielli around the early Christian basilica of Sant'Eufemia, the new National Museum of underwater archaeology with the Roman ship Iulia Felix and a lagoon of canals, casoni and islands like Barbana.

Created in 1940 by barring the Salto river to power the hydroelectric power station of Cotilia at the service of the Terni steel works, it is the largest artificial lake in Lazio, with wild banks jagged by coves similar to fjords. The ride by car or by bike crosses oak and chestnut woods; the beaches of Fiumata and Borgo San Pietro take a swim and rent pedalos, canoes and wakeboards, and divers can explore the old submersible village through specialized centres.
The salon is frescoed by an anonymous master, one of the most important profane cycles of late-Gothic painting in Europe, brought to light by the restorations of the FAI.
