The castle on the Appia street, open until the evening of summer.
€7 archaeological area; €10 with the Archaeological Museum; €12 also with the Bandini Museum

Two churches of medieval origin with internal hall enriched with paintings and frescoes; San Domenico is rich in frescoes. In Piazza San Francesco the bronze bust of Angelo Celli by the sculptor Biancini, located in 1959.
Wellness and spa at Cinquale, about 3 km from Forte dei Marmi.
The sanctuary extended over the country.

Attributed to Benedetto Alfieri, it was built between 1749 and 1774 on the initiative of Count Francesco Antonio Ricci, with a baroque plan with an elongated Greek cross and an octagonal tiburian dome; the bell tower (1779-1781) has five bells merged by De Giorgis in 1781. Inside there are three marble altars, twelve paintings with the Apostles of Pietro Montaldo (one dated 1824), the altarpiece of Sebastiano Taricco's Assumption and wooden stands perhaps from Sant'Andrea di Chieri. Open on Saturday 15-18 and Sunday 9.30-12.30, other days by reservation (tel. 0131 996603).

The square of the institutional palaces, with the town hall of Palazzo San Giorgio, built between 1918 and 1921 in Art Nouveau style and attributed to Ernesto Basile, with pilasters, rustic arched windows and a door with coats of arms and clock.
Fountain of 1342 in the square of the church of Sant'Agostino, one of the three that distributed water from the slopes of Monte Erice.
The church of the fourteenth century.
Reading in the streets the organization of an Albanian community.
Outside the walls, with the Romanesque portal of 1295, the rose window, the ancient cloister and a single hall of seven spans.
The Bible of Borso, a masterpiece of the book.
It corresponds to the Roman forum and was the centerpiece of the ancient city.

Center of the High Table on a hill overlooking the Gargano promontory and the first heights of the Dauni Mountains, about 11 km from San Severo, linked to the name of Traiano and the Battle of Civitate of 1053, in which the Normans defeated the papal troops at the Fortore. In the territory the ancient Teanum Apulum with its Roman amphitheatre; in the village the Civic Museum in the seventeenth-century monastery of Sant'Antonio da Padova.
The imposing castle around which the historic centre is gathered houses the Civic Museum, with the only existing bust of Emperor Frederick II.
A crypt you don't forget.

Born in the thirteenth century as a fortification after the sixth crusade (there is a tower, the perimeter walls on the back and on the east side and the supporting stone structure), it was transformed into a residence in 1655 by Duke Fabrizio Caracciolo. It belonged to the Ravaschieri, the Caracciolo and then to the Magno Oliverio, with various modifications after the earthquake. You can see the entrance to the feudal history.

Set up in the monastery of Santa Maria Maddalena delle Clarisse, built in 1586 on the ruins of a previous monastery and enlarged in the eighteenth century; the annexed church, of 1603, has elliptical plan and decorations of Borrominian inspiration. It tells the life of nuns with cups, dishes, clothes, crockery and frames, the \'belief of the pastries \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ The tour is accompanied by a theatricalized audio guide in headphones.
Trekking to the Alta Murgia.
The cathedral on the terrace of cypresses.
The most beautiful sculpted vaults among the rock churches of Massafra.
Public garden at the north edge of the village, overlooking two deep ravines.

In the valley of the Tirino, about 6 km from the village: abbey founded by the Longobard king Desiderio (756-774), church rebuilt and consecrated by Pasquale II in 1117. On the façade is the inscription of the foundation and, upside down, the magic square "ROTAS OPERA TENET AREPO SATOR"; inside three naves and three apses, a ciborium of the thirteenth century with a branch that comes out of the mouths of a dragon and green and turquoise majolicas, unique in Abruzzo, and in the apse the fresco of the first twelfth century with Christ enthroned between the Evangelists and the 24 Vegliards of the Apocalypse.
Almost intact center of streets with stone houses and wooden balconies; in the square the town hall and the beautiful stone fountain of the sixteenth century.
The ancient eel factory, with the Sala dei Fuochi and its 12 chimneys; in autumn we return to cook and marinate the fish.

At the western end of the Gulf of Poets, the village of Roman origin dominated by the Doria Castle and the Gothic church of St. Peter on the tip of the promontory, with the islands Palmaria, Tino and Tinetto: part of the UNESCO site since 1997.
The frescoes of Giacomino.

About 450 square meters dedicated to three areas: ethnography, with hundreds of objects of the peasant world, of the weaving and the work of the foresters; mining activities, with vintage tools, a section on minerals and, outside, a stretch of mine visitable; scientific laboratories, with two rooms of experiments on electromagnetism, sound, gas and radio transmissions designed especially for schools. It also exhibits reproductions of machines inspired by Leonardo's Codex Atlanticus (catapults, mowering wagons, flying machines, mobile bridges) made by Gianfranco Zucchi and granted in comodato by his children.
Last rest of the medieval castle of Da Varano, lords of Camerino, who found refuge in Sefro after the sack of their city in 1259.
A few meters from the castle, about 800 objects among artifacts and sculptures of the Valdostano handicrafts, with a teaching space for children.

Località dello Ionio 28 km from Lecce, known for its golden beaches, Porto Cesareo lives around the marina with the fish market; its sea is one of the largest protected marine areas in Italy, flanked by the reserve Swamp of the Count, and the coast is marked by the sixteenth-century towers of Cesarea, Chianca and Lapillo, as well as the Museum of Marine Biology Pietro Parenzan.
It reconstructs the late 19th century peasant house in three rooms, domestic, handicraft and agricultural, with a detached section dedicated to ceramics.
The convent on the hill.

Great archaeological area with numerous remains of Messapian civilization: traces of the walls of the IV-III century BC of Bastae, center mentioned by Pliny the Elder and Ptolemy and destroyed around 1160 by William the Malo.
Church with frescoed porch, rebuilt in the mid-500s, just outside the castle walls.
In the heart of the Palladian complex.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione on the edge of a morainic basin with two lakes, where the medieval village rises towards the ruins of the castle and the porticoed square of the Count Rosso.
Mountain surgeons required by the courts of Europe.
The Medici fortress of Buontalenti (1590) connected to Boboli, with one of the best views of Florence and contemporary art exhibitions.
The fortress on the Garampo hill dominates the city; inside is the Museum of History of Agriculture.
visits only by appointment (micidiugotognazzi@gmail.com)

Built in the 12th century by the Marquis of Clavesana on the spur of "Petra Lata" it was an autonomous fief in the territory of Oneglia under the protection of Genoa; in 1233 the inhabitants occupied it, passed to the counts of Ventimiglia, then to the Doria and in 1575 to the Savoy. The Province has a castle and two towers in a bad state of conservation.
Palazzolo's sausage, of lean minced pork meat or cubes with spices, chilli and red wine in natural gut; the cavated with pork sauce, ricotta ravioli and caponata.
Tools and objects of the agricultural work of the Bassa, exhibited in the former Castellazzi farm.
The bell tower of the Duomo is almost 90 meters high, symbol of the city, with the Room of the Torresani frescoed and the view on the rooftops of Modena.
MiC card indicates it closed every day (aggiornamento 2021)
A destination of international pilgrimage.
Pale and golden altars outside the walls.

Neoclassical parish church with frescoes by the brothers painters Stolz, the "Danza macabra" by Rudolf Stolz, baptismal font and altarpieces by C. Dusi; the curated cemetery preserves wood and sandstone sculptures. Open every day of the year, 8-19.

Small town of Biellese on a spur of the barracks, dominated by the castle (Rocca dei Cavallari), fortified village castled around the year 1000 with high stone tower, viscontea rock and chapel with fourteenth-century frescoes; in the village the seventeenth-century parish church of Santa Maria Assunta with the memories of the Avogadro.

Built in 1664 as an oratory of the confraternity of the dockers, it has the interior entirely covered with eighteenth-century canvases, mostly of Liborio Riccio da Muro, and wooden stables finely carved; on the marble altar the Madonna between St. Joseph and St. Francis of Assisi of Luca Giordano (1664-65). Opened in 2009 after four years of restoration.
The castle of Frederick II in the Vulture.

Founded in 1884, it preserves the Gozzi Palace of Tiziano, the Madonna and Child by Carlo Crivelli and the Sacred Conversation of Lorenzo Lotto; since 1973 it has been located in Palazzo Bosdari, with a section in the nearby Palazzo Bonomini.
The historical funicular of 1903.
Gothic church with Michael Pacher's altar (1475) and a Romanesque crucifix, open on weekdays from April to October.
The most legendary bike climb in Italy, or the slopes in winter.

Small village in the hinterland of Valvestino, inside the Park Alto Garda Bresciano, Magasa is known for the hamlet of Cima Rest, at 1200 m, with the hay-roofed barns, the ethnographic museum and the astronomical observatory, and for the cheese Tombea, which takes its name from the mountain that dominates the village.

The heart of the city of foundation of 1933, the city of Rationalism is: the piazza porticata of the Town Hall with the civic tower, reference for the whole territory, and around the House of the Fighter, the after-work and the covered market.
Erected in 1513 and rebuilt in the eighteenth century, it preserves a sixteenth-century altarpiece by Grazio Cossali.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for hour 1 of the 4 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.

House inhabited by the Pastorio family for almost six centuries, which hosted Henry Dunant in June 1859: the Hall of Landscapes with monochrome views and imaginary Roman ruins, the Hall of the Coat of Arms, the statue of Francesco Gonzaga by Giovanni Antonio Carra (1610-1617), furnishings, archive, library, paintings, prints, laces, toys and clothes. Open Saturday and Sunday 15-18.30.
Small church outside the walls, already existing in 1112.

Parish Church in the Lower Borgo, mentioned already at the beginning of the fourteenth century: it contains a Madonna del Rosario dated 1561, a statue of St. Dominic, a tooth of the saint in a 15th century reliquary and a beam of the bed from the hermitage of Prato Cardoso.
The park with the remains of the amphitheatre and the antiquarium dedicated to the Roman Milan.
Get lost in the alleys of the ancient village.
Gate of the Norman walls, reachable by alleys to steps from Via Mercato.

Born in 1976 on a collection started in the early 1960s, closed in 2011 and reopened on 30 June 2015 after less than a year of work, it occupies the office building designed in 1968 by Ignazio Gardella. The six-storey route, ordered for Timeline, Beauty and Speed, exhibits 69 models including the A.L.F.A. 24 HP, the 6C 1750 Gran Sport by Tazio Nuvolari, the Juliet and 33 TT 12, with sections on design, cinema, Formula 1 and cars in uniform; closes with virtual reality and a 4D room. Open 10-18, closed on Tuesdays; bookshop, cafeteria and test track.
€5 (with the museums Amedeo Bassi and Vite and Wine)
The Crib of Pollino is designed by Escher.

A path from Magasa climbs towards the Tombea and Caplone mountains along the ancient border between Italy and Austria (the valley was Austrian until 1915-18): military deposits are still excavated in the rock, trenches and masonry stations; from the Bocca di Cablone a military road leads to the Bocca di Campei. On the summit of Tombea (1950 m) a walled compass indicates the names of 34 visible mountains; here the Saxifraga tombeanensis was discovered and royal eagles, deer, ibex and deer are observed.
Small wooded and steep hill near the Mefite area, halfway between Villamaina and Rocca San Felice, with brambles, stingings, brooms and tall trees, especially oaks, elms and poplars.
One of the richest Romanesque sculptural cycles in Molise.
A building on the river.
A small Tuscan baroque in the town square.
Three waterfalls a stone's throw from the village.

It rises on the remains of a temple of the III-I century BC: the church and the bell tower are of the first half of the XII century, the chapel of the Holy Crucifix (second half of the XV century) was commissioned by Cardinal Guillaume d'Estouteville and by Ambrogio Massari, with frescoes of biblical scenes of the late fifteenth century. The cloister of the former Augustinian convent, by Antonio da Como, has 27 marble capitals all different. Convent and cloister are visited by appointment.
The early Christian basilicas.
The story of the Fieschi.
The main monument of the city.
The medieval Virgil.

Made in 1590 by Carlo Emanuele di Savoia to engineer Gabrio Busco, he was shot down after the armistice of Cherasco in 1796. The area can be visited with guided tours organized by the Tourist Office of Demonte.
Crafts and faces of the Teggiano of the past.
The jewels and amulets of the Carthaginians of Trexenta.
Sanctuary built between 1511 and 1514 in Renaissance style, just outside the fortifications, destination of pilgrimages.
Romanesque bell tower and sundial cloister.
A Romanesque church among the oldest in Pisano.

In the hamlets: to Aggi, thirteenth-century lines and frescoes by Matteo da Gualdo; to Acciano, Umbrian anonymous frescoes from the second half of the fifteenth century; to Bagnara, remains of fifteenth-century frescoes by Matteo da Gualdo, three wooden altars from the seventeenth century and an organ from the early eighteenth century; to Boschetto San Giovanni with frescoes from the sixteenth century.
The mill under the house Orsini.

The only Sardinian sanctuary dedicated to the Roman martyr of the third century, of late Byzantine origin, with wooden altar of the seventeenth century; in the restoration of 1996 a Roman furnace for intact bricks emerged. The saint, on Saintus Coiadoras, who marries, is celebrated on 14 February, 8 May and 6 October.
The architecture of today.
Pagani's newsstand that divides the church.
Prehistoric caves that open on the sides of the Pietra di San Marco, next to the historic center.

The house where Giosuè Carducci spent his youth with his family and his father Michele, a doctor; he exhibits works by the artist Antonio Possenti illustrating the poet's most famous poems. The gravestones of his father and brother Dante are still visible in the village cemetery.
The churches of the Easter rites.
The gigantic portrait of San Gennaro painted by the Neapolitan artist Jorit at the entrance of Forcella, historical district near the Duomo.
Walk through alleys in stone.

South of Cala Gonone, among the largest caves in Sardinia, with a development of about 5 km of which 1,200 meters equipped: stalactites and stalagmites reflected in the ponds and an underground salt lake; it was among the last shelters of the monk seal. Guided tour.
The Romanesque in the city.
The oldest building in Moneglia, probably from the 10th century, with frescoes from the 12th to the 18th century restored; on the same square the house of the poet Felice Romani.
The last of the Madonie fir trees.

Ancient elliptical volcanic crater among woods and meadows in the Regional Park of the Roman Castles, 170 meters deep, with paths suitable for everyone. On the dark volcanic beach, about 25 minutes walk from the village, rental of kayak and SUP, bar and departure of boat tours, every hour in season. The artificial emissary of the lake is dated to 396 B.C.
An ancient fountain of Cori Monte where, according to tradition, the Barbarossa granted himself a bath after plundering the city.

In the House of Plevan next to the Duomo, it collects documents and sacred art from the parish and the territory, ordered by typological sections from the 13th to the 20th century; multimedia stations.
The prisoner king's palace.
The fortress of the Falletti that gives the name to the country.
Founded in 1619 by Alessandro Gambalunga, among the first public civic libraries in Italy: the seventeenth-century rooms in walnut, the eighteenth-century room and the Dutch globes.
Castle near Roccalbegna passed from the Aldobrandeschi to the Piccolomini of Siena in 1388; it consists of two large buildings and a mast, mostly covered with ivy.
The story of Todi in the palaces of the square.
The linden of Saint Bernardino.

A hilly village above the Umbrian valley, closed by medieval walls that incorporate Etruscan features of the 6th century BC: in Piazza Cavour the Palazzo del Podestà (1371) with the City Museum and the works of Perugino, the churches of Santa Maria Maggiore, San Crispolto and the Oratory of Sant'Andrea; in the plain the eighteenth-century Villa del Boccaglione.
The largest aquarium on the Adriatic, in the former marine colonies Le Navi.
The voice of the first Italian divo in the music room.
Mediterranean and mountain nature around an ancient hermitage.
The door erected by Claudio in 52 AD with the tomb of the baker Eurisace; near, 9 meters below via Prenestina, the neo-Pythagorean basilica of the first century discovered in 1917.

In the hamlet of San Marco, a large salon exhibits a rich collection of motorcycles, mopeds and scooters ordered by factory and displacement; many pieces have been or still are restored by the owners of the collection. Open Monday to Friday 8-12 and 14-18, closed Saturday and Sunday, without reservation (tel. 0432 868049).
can be visited only by appointment or on regular guided tours
The fortress of Frederick II and the polyptych of the pupil.
The 16th century church of the stonemasons.
The Crucifix attributed to Sangallo.
open from March to December on limited days (Sundays, Saturdays in summer, every day 4-24 August) with mandatory reservation according to the Montana Community
Baroque balconies and covered alleys.

Nuragic village-sanctuary between Barbagia and Ogliastra, from the recent-final Bronze to the early Iron Age: the main megaron temple, about 17 meters long, in granite and shale with temenos and seats, a second temple with two-tone altar today largely at the Nuoro museum, isolated houses and workshops with lead ovens, and not far away a trilobed nuraghe. It is described as the most important metallurgical center of Nuragic Sardinia, with objects from Etruria, Greece and Near East; excavated since 1984 by Maria Ausilia Fadda.

One of the city's symbolic monuments, at the Colle del Sole on the ancient acropolis; also known as Pozzo Sorbello, is an exceptional work of hydraulic engineering of the second half of the third century BC.
The symbol of the city and its opera season.
Austrian architecture.

The top, over 2,000 meters and also referred to as Galzirola, is the highest point in the municipal territory; it is reached from Cavargna or from the area of the oratory and the San Lucio refuge, with a refuge on top and panoramic view of Lake Lugano. Route for experienced hikers; from Cavargna you cross the Sacred Wood, a wide beech wood that acts as a barrier against avalanches.

Oratory in the locality of Campogialli, decorated with cycles of frescoes of the fourteenth century, probably of the workshop of Andrea di Nerio and the Master of Barberino; in the area there was also a manor of the Pazzi del Valdarno.

The ancient Poseidonia, founded at the end of the 7th century BC, part of the UNESCO site of Cilento: three Doric temples, the Roman forum and the National Archaeological Museum with the Tomb of the Diveper.
The place where the memory of Dante in Lunigiana is preserved.
An architecture made of trees.

Country of Agrigentino at the foot of Monte Saraceno, an ancient town inhabited by prehistoric times at the third century BC, now an archaeological area of the Valley of the Temples; the excavations are exhibited in the archaeological museum Salvatore Lauricella, in the historical center.

Country of the Val del Riso marked for centuries by mining activity, with mines opened by the Romans over two thousand years ago; to see the parish church of Santa Maria Assunta with a painting of the Moroni, the ethnographic scientific-minerary Museum, the sixteenth-century sanctuary of the Madonna del Frassino and the mine of Foghera.
A neoclassical villa that preserves the memory of the territory.
The Sardinian Stonehenge, older than the English one.
The Vallombrosana abbey fortified between cypresses and vineyards of Chianti, with the Last Supper of the Ghirlandaio in the refectory.
€6, reduced €3

Born in 1994 on the initiative of the Italian Association of Friends of the Nativity of Giarre, in a noble palace of the nineteenth century, he exhibits about two hundred nativity scenes in Lecce rags, Sicilian and Apulian terracotta, Neapolitan figures and wood of Trentino pine, as well as dioramas on the Sicilian peasant life. Open from 8 December to 6 January every day 16-19.30; in the rest of the year Wednesday, Sunday and holidays 17-19; closed in July and August.

The main church of the village, in white marble and in a raised position, was built from the 15th century where there was a church dedicated to St. John; the current structure with three naves was completed in 1745, the neo-medieval façade dates back to 1884 and the frescoes by Michele Marcucci in the early twentieth century. Next to the bell tower and the square, from which you can see the Piana di Lucca; the patron festival falls on Monday after Pentecost.

Municipality between Pistoia and Prato born as a fortified village of the thirteenth century, destroyed by the Florentines in 1303; to see the Villa Castello Smilea, today municipal seat with the works of Jorio Vivarelli, the crypt of the abbey of San Salvatore in Agna, documented since 772, the parish church with frescoes by Luigi Sabatelli and, at the top, Tobbiana.

On a spur between Portoferraio and Rio, the oldest fortress on the island, of Etruscan origin and transformed by the Pisans, strengthened around 1440; from the top you can see Mount Capanne and, on clear days, Corsica.
The Pontine Islands on the horizon.

Built around 1260 in Angevin age and rebuilt in 1634, with three naves with portal in sandstone dated; bell tower completed in 1960. It preserves the Madonna del Soccorso in marble by Domenico Gagini (1480), the baptismal font by Antonello Gagini (1531), a marble icon of the Gaginian school (1522), the bust of the Most Holy Savior of Hercules Ferrata, a majolica floor of the eighteenth century and a Via Crucis of majolica by Collesano.
The young Treviso.
The mother church of the village, with an ancient retablo.

The park next to Palazzo Tornielli, once private and accessible only from the palace, summer residence of the family, is open to the public since 1920 and has been restored after a long intervention: neo-Gothic architecture, a historic stone glacier, centuries-old trees and autochthonous aromatic plants.

National monument in the hamlet Roselli, begun on April 20, 1636 above a chapel that remembered the appearance of Our Lady to a shepherd; rustic façade with diamond tip and two lateral naves added in the nineteenth century. It houses two wooden sculptures of Neapolitan school: a Crucifix of the mid-sixteenth century and an Annunziata of the eighteenth century.

The Tirino is born from the aquifer system of Campo Imperatore and re-emerges at Lake Capodacqua; with a flow rate of about 6,000 l/s and water at 11 °C is considered one of the most clear rivers in Italy. At the foot of the village, in San Martino, starting point for navigation, the water is emerald green for the transparency that lets the submerged vegetation grow; there live water celery and trout, fishable only You can walk, by mountain bike on the slopes of the Park, by canoe or kayak also with a guide, on horseback or in a carriage (excursions by reservation).
The cartoons of a Milanese liberty decorator.
The most famous Roman mosaics in Sicily.
The panoramic ascent.
The state gallery of the Cittadella dei Musei, in the heart of the fortified district of Castello.
The heart of the village on the ruins of the castle.
The fourteenth-century church was founded next to a hospice for pilgrims, with a small cloister of the fifteenth century.
The Roman Cremona.
The ancient parish of San Martino, a small Romanesque church first mentioned in 1031 in a document from the Abbey of Novalesa, today the Chapel of the Fallen.
The entrance to the old town.

Reserve of 156 hectares on the Trieste Karst at the Slovenian border: karst land partly bushy, mature pinewood of black pine, mixed forest and limestone outskirts with furrowed fields; live there the wild cat and the hedgehog, while brown bear and golden jackal appear only rarely. A path, which starts from the road between Col and Fernetti, climbs to the top where a wooden tower offers a 360 degree view of the sea and Slovenia; a short detour leads to an artificial pond. Information points at the Casa Carsica in Repen and the Town Hall of Col.

Fishing village founded in 1885 by 45 families of Cala d'Oliva, displaced from Asinara to make room for the penal colony; Autonomous municipality since 1988. From 1983 to the end of August, it hosts a regatta of Latin sail gozzos.
Closed to the public since August 25, 2025 for restoration of decorated surfaces and mosaics and for accessibility; reopening to be communicated on official channels
The Roman town of the Appia overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea.

The white city is on the last buttresses of the Murge: the medieval core of the Earth with alleys, whitewashed houses and stairs, the fifteenth-century cathedral at the top of the hill, the Aragonese walls with their towers, the museum that houses the Woman of Ostuni about 25,000 years ago and, less than 10 km away, the marina and the Park of the Coast Dunes.

Fortified city on the southern shore of Garda, where the lake becomes Mincio: the Venetian pentagonal fortress, UNESCO heritage since 2017, you visit entering from Porta Brescia or Porta Verona and walking on the bastions; inside the walls the Ponte dei Voltoni, Piazza Ferdinando di Savoia with the church of San Martino and the remains of the Roman Arilica, the Habsburg military district and the Historical Palazzina, outside the walls the Sanctuary of Madonna del Frassino.
Museum of modern and contemporary art born from the Spoleto Prize, with works by Pino Pascali, Sol LeWitt and Leoncillo Leonardi.
A ring ride around the village.
Temporarily closed according to Visit Tuscany; check with the Casentino Ecomuseum

Country of the plain of Verona crossed by Tartar, the longest river of resurgence in Italy, Isola della Scala is the capital of rice Vialone Nano, with the Rice Fair born in 1967; to see the Scaligera Tower of Mastino II, the Romanesque Sanctuary of Madonna della Bastia (1126), the church of Santo Stefano and the Archaeological Museum in the former church of the Friars.
A rare antis temple in the woods.
The house where Verdi lived and composed.

Set up in the seventeenth-century monastery of Sant'Antonio da Padova, it collects numerous finds; the municipality collaborates in archaeological investigations on Teanum Apulum with its Museum and Archaeological Service.

Rocky gorges dug by the river San Leonardo, where canyoning is practiced by swimming or canoeing and, in some stretches, climbing; on the walls there are artificial caves, castelluccia tombs of the Bronze Age.
Three hundred frescoes and organ doors of Pordenone.
The dungeons and the terrace on the sea.
The baroque chapel all stucco.
Square with a scenic shape in the historic center, with the Duomo and the old Town Loggia.

Sanctuary and shrine of peace at about 700 meters, on the remains of the church of San Martiano a Cella, wanted by Don Adamo Accosa, chaplain of the Alps, and inaugurated in 1958: it is built with stones from about one hundred places affected by the Second World War (from Coutances, Montecassino and El Alamein to Hiroshima and Nagasaki), spires of the Duomo of Milan fallen in the bombings of 1943, a baptismal source by the shutter of a cannon of the battleship Andrea Doria and a crucifix made of weapons. Open every day 9-18:30 from April to October; from November to March Saturday and Sunday 9-17, other days by reservation.
The island of the patron saint of the Gulf.

The village of the average Seriana Valley at the confluence of Nossana nel Serio, whose springs fed for centuries the sweaters (forge documented from the fifteenth century) today told by the Maglio Museo; at the entrance of the village the sanctuary of the Madonna delle Lacrime, linked to the apparition of 2 June 1511 and famous for the embalmed crocodile.

Opened on 28 October 1888 in a building shaped as a three-nave early Christian basilica, it gathers almost only finds of the Roman colony of Iulia Concordia: statues, mosaics, funerary stele, portraits, numerous inscriptions, figurative bronzes, ambers, glass including a cup engraved with Daniele among the lions. Open Monday-Saturday 8.30-19.30, Sunday and holidays 8.30-13.30.

Cell of the Ecomuseum of Biellese opened in 1996 in the buildings of the former Rubino factory, founded in 1896 by Giovan Battista Rubino with his sons Ernesto and Colombo (now Bono Netro). It tells the story of the forge born in the seventeenth century in small workshops, the "boite" along the river Ingagna: tools produced by Rubino and samples, over a thousand drawings, an archive of documents from 1901 to 1964, technical standards for car and motorbike components and an exhibition of historical machinery. Guided tours, workshops and excursions by reservation; collaborate with Fucina Morino in Mongrando. Ecomuseum Contacts: +39 349 3269048.
Great War Trenches on the border ridge.

Opened on July 17, 2005, centenary of the brand, in the former plant in via Zara where in 1905 Corrado Frera started the workshop to build bicycles and motorcycles: the company Anonima Frera produced models appreciated for about thirty years, transformed Tradate from an agricultural village into an industrial town and closed in 1936. One section exhibits 25 motorcycles and 5 Frera bikes, the other bike of historical Lombard and Italian brands such as MV Agusta, Cagiva, Gilera and Moto Guzzi. Open Thursday 20-22, Saturday and Sunday 15-18 (variable hours on holidays and summer); in the library and cafe building.
The parish church of the other historic village.
Cozio's peace arch.
The wild heart of the Apuans.
The square of the living card game.

Piazza in the medieval heart with a long panoramic balcony from Gran Sasso to the Adriatic, overlooking Palazzo Portici and the church of San Lorenzo; between the alleys you can reach Porta Napoli, Palazzo Ronchi and the Ruetta, defined the narrowest street in Italy (about 40 cm).
The Umbrian frescoes of Bontulli.

On the top of the Pausolino hill, it had four doors and twenty towers and is in ruins after the Venetian cannons of 1510; climbing from the Panoramic Carmini Path in the Salin Park, rebuilt stone by stone by the Compagnia delle Mura and inaugurated in 1989, with views from the Grappa to the Euganean and Berici Hills and the Asiago Plateau.
The town hall for over seven centuries: the Salone dei Cinquecento, the Studiolo di Francesco I, the Medici apartments and the Torre di Arnolfo.
An evening under the stars above the caves.

The residence of the early eighteenth century was then enlarged, with a H-shaped plan with courtyard and garden, restored porticos and eighteenth-century molded windows; once attributed to Giuseppe Piermarini, attribution today considered wrong. Renovated, since 1978 it is the seat of the Municipality and can be visited by reservation. It overlooks Piazza Unità d'Italia.
Works and personal objects by Jean-Baptiste Cerlogne (1826-1910), buried next to the facade of the church; in the same place the center studies René Willien on the patois.
The bottom of the Passiria seen from a grenade.

In the historic rooms of the palazzo baronale Picinni-Leopardi, born from an idea of Maurizio Vignati with the Municipality and the Palazzo Picinni-Leopardi Association thanks to the objects donated by citizens: work tools divided by sections (drawing, leather goods, tailoring, joinery, iron, kitchen) that tell who made and used them.
Birdwatching near Ferrara.
The look on the trulli at sunset.

The main centre of Ogliastra, with the port of Arbatax, the Red Porfido Rocks and a coast of about 16 km of beaches and coves such as Cala Moresca, Porto Frailis and Lido di Orrì; inland the archaeological park of S'Ortali' and Monti and in the village the museum of contemporary art On Logu de S'iscultura and the former cathedral of Sant'Andrea.
To be discovered on foot.
The ceramics of Mondovì.
The narrow and wild valley of the Gran Paradiso National Park, dominated by the amphitheatre of the only  "4000" entirely Italian, between paths of the royal hunts and villages of wooden granaries.
The old country emptied from floods and the feast of September 8.
18th century villa belonged to the Sartorio family from 1836 to 1949 and left to the Municipality for will of Anna Sartorio to become a museum.
Romanesque church of the 13th century on Via del Corso, with a copy of San Michele di Guido Reni at the altar and a chapel frescoed with the Flagellation.

Five sections on tobacco cultivation, processing and production and on the festivals and cults related to this crop, plus the section "Pontecorvo" and the history dedicated to tobacconists and smuggling.
Roman mosaics next to the abbey.

It rises on a Benedictine oratory of the 12th century, it is dedicated to Santa Maria Assunta but known as San Francesco for the friars who arrived around 1280; the Romanesque-Gothic ogival portal has three orders of tortile columns with reliefs attributed to Lombard workers. Inside two aisles, wooden ceiling painted by Giuseppe Frigerio da Norcia (1760), frescoes from the 14th to the 16th century and a longobard aquasantiera; in the lower church Franciscan frescoes of the early 15th century, in the 18th century lunettes cloister with the life of St. Francis and an antiquarium of Roman and medieval epigraphs and sculptures.
In the towns of Palazzotto, Villa Santa Lucia and Casale Antonelli remain rustic villas probably begun in the Republican age, with construction phases up to the second century AD.
The silvers of a Pollino community.

Fortified village of the culture of the Friulian castelliers, founded at the beginning of the Ancient Bronze, renovated between Middle and Recent Bronze and frequented again by the second Iron Age: a rectangular terrapieno with bevelled corners, oriented on the cardinal points, 3,5-4 meters high and wide up to about 22, encloses about 2 hectares and is surrounded by a moat at least 13 meters wide. The interior now houses municipal sports facilities; you enter from a single entrance to the northern corner.

Borgo della Val di Fiemme known for its wood craftsmanship and for the about one hundred cribs set up at Christmas in the alleys: in the center the parish church of Sant'Eliseo, the Gothic church of Santi Leonardo and Gottardo and Casa Jellici; in Stava the documentation center and the path of memory on the disaster of 19 July 1985, in Lake Tesero the stadium of the bottom and in Pampeago the art park RespirArt under the Latemar.
Terraced houses, alleys, stairs, fountains and palaces with portals and arches, photographed by Cartier-Bresson, Giacomelli and Berengo Gardin.
Taranto's Ori.

Parish church on Piazza Boiardo with a fifteenth-century bell tower with two windows; it preserves the sixteenth-century polychrome group of Our Lady of the Rosary, a painting by Bartolomeo Passarotti with Saint Catherine of Alexandria and the tomb of Lazarus Spallanzani.

Forest garden open in summer, set up as a didactic area on the site of a forest nursery at the beginning of the twentieth century: it gathers 26 species of trees, shrubs and herbs of the woods of Val di Sole and Trentino, with alpaca and activities for families; there comes the naturalistic path of the Raimondo Fox with installations in QR code.

Jewel of the 11th century Lunigian Romanesque, with stone façade and walls of river pebbles, built along the Via Francigena probably on a medieval building (VIII-IX century); it is mentioned by Sigerico di Canterbury at the end of the 10th century and in a papal bull of 1148. Nearby were found statues-stele of the Bronze Age and the remains of a Roman village.
Private property, not always open to the public: for visits contact the Municipality or ADSI

Medieval village of Val Misa with urban layout of the thirteenth century, remodelled between the late Middle Ages and the modern era and surrounded by walls. The monastery of Santa Maria Maddalena houses the Museum of the monastic arts, and in the center is the Camaldolese church of San Michele.

Medieval village about 1,346 meters in the National Park of Gran Sasso and Monti della Laga, symbol of transhumance, with tower houses, covered passages called sports, the tower of San Marco and a widespread ethnographic museum; from here you go up to Campo Imperatore.

Built in 1489 and consecrated in the presence of Bishop Konrad Reichard; the bell tower was completed 62 years later. Independent parish since 1891; next door, the old canonical church (Altes Widum) of 1495.
The peasant memory of the Apennines between Piedmont and Liguria.

Set up on two floors in the extense castle, it exhibits ceramics from the beginning of the fifteenth century to the second half of the seventeenth century, largely recovered from the drains emptied during the restorations of the sixties: graffite, faenza majolica (sign of the extensive domination), mugs, bowls and engraved cans, with motifs related to the fertility cycle and animals. On the first floor everyday objects such as spoons and home furnishings.

Palace of the eighteenth century wanted by the noble family Malacrida in the upper part of the city, the ancient district Scimicà, considered the most significant example of the rococo in Valtellina. The staircase has a medallion of Gian Pietro Romegialli with the Rat of Ganymede; in the salon of honour, on the first floor, the squares of Giuseppe Coduri said the Vignoli and the vault of Cesare Ligari with the triumph of truth about the lie. Guided tours by reservation at the Tourist Board Porte di Valtellina.
The baroque from Palermo next to the Martorana.

Small fortified village at 616 meters, with narrow alleys and tower houses, dominated by the Mount of Riva. The 18th-century parish church, with a 17th-century bell tower, contains two marble statues from the fourteenth century and paliotti made of Carpigiana stone.
Modern portals on the Baroque façade.
Open only from 1 May to 31 October

A first nucleus is remembered as the church of San Maurizio da Goffredo da Bussero around 1270; in the middle of the fourteenth century the two churches were demolished to make room for the new church, saving the fresco of the Madonna today venerated on the altar of a side chapel, with baroque decorations and polychrome stuccoes of saints, angels and prophets. The presbytery has a cycle of frescoes on the childhood of the Virgin and a large cycle of sixteenth-century Stories of the Virgin. Cardinal Schuster raised him to the sanctuary in 1945; reported in the FAI census "I Luoghi del Cuore" in 2016, 2018, 2020 and 2022.
A nuragic village on the sea.
The Perugino on Trasimeno.
The tree-lined avenue of the thirties connects the port to the cliffs of the Passetto; at the end, in Piazza IV Novembre, the Monument to the Fallen by Guido Cirilli (1927-1930, inaugurated in 1932).
The poet's house in Corso Garibaldi has a marble slab on the façade with the poem "Monete Rossi" (Red Monete), in Montemurro Sinisgalli returned in July 1944 and composed "L'indovino" (The Indovino).
Nuraghe, grave and sacred fountain in one territory.
For those who love to look for the traces of Sanniti and Romans in the countryside.
The most photogenic neighborhood in the city.
Spa town of the Sienese Valdichiana with an Etruscan museum and the ancient village on the hill.

Village gathered around Piazza Nerazio Prisco, on which overlooks the Town Hall and stands the bell tower shaped like a large bottle. The walls of the IX century remain with two doors and three cylindrical towers, the Renaissance Palazzo Attilio of the family that gave a bishop to Termoli and the eighteenth century Palazzo Giacchi, with portals and windows in pink stone; at the entrance of the village a large stone mask, perhaps from a monumental Roman fountain.
The residence of the Farnese in the heart of the village.

Founded in 1966 by Ermanno Leinardi with Italo Utzeri, Ugo Ugo and Tonino Casula, it is located in the former renovated municipal slaughterhouse: two floors lit by a skylight, with a building art room (Sonia Delaunay, Aurelie Nemours, Michel Seuphor and others) and one of abstract art (Capogrossi, Dorazio, Fontana, Bice Lazzari, Veronesi and others), works collected by Leinardi with exchanges between artists.

It rises on Capo Schisò and tells about the Greek colony and the prehistory of the site with materials coming mainly from the excavations begun in 1953. On the ground floor there is the neolithic cup of Stentinello, the Corinthian and Euboic ceramics of the first colony and the masquerade antefixes of silenum, typical production of the city (late VI-V century BC); on the upper floor are the sacred areas, the archaic and classical city, the necropolis and a numismatic toilet. To see the arula with sphinxes faced (530 BC) called "Heidelberg-Naxos" rebuilt in 1997; in the sixteenth-century tower adjacent to the stone and lead anchors recovered in the bay. Open every day 9-19.45.
The rock of the miracle, today altar of a sanctuary.
The place of worship from which the former votes of the museum come.

Arbëreshë municipality of the Greek-Byzantine rite on the hills of the Greek Sila, defined as the most important cultural center of the Albanian colonies of Italy, rose at the Basilian Abbey of Sant'Adriano, founded in the tenth century by St. Nile of Rossano, whose church preserves a mosaic floor and opus sectile, and since 1794 houses the Italian-Albanian College.

Museum of the MUSE built around the remains of a village of the Bronze Age, inhabited between 2200 and 1350 BC and re-emerged in 1929 during the lowering of the lake for hydroelectric works; since 2011 it is part of the prehistoric palafittic sites of the Alpine arch, UNESCO World Heritage. Original finds and, on the shore, huts rebuilt and furnished on catwalks. Open every day: March-June and September-December 9-17, July and August 10-18; family ticket €5 or €10.

Protected area of about 17 hectares established in 2022 and managed by the municipality, which takes its name from the remains of an ancient mill on the river Mignone, with a waterfall and a pond. Along the river Biscione and Mignone grow forests with a black alder tunnel; there are prairies of Agrostis linked to hydrothermal events, a beech wood at unusually low altitude and a maple of exceptional size.

Opened in 2004 by the Alpine Group of Carcare to preserve the memory of an important part of Italian history: letters and postcards from the front, photographs, helmets, uniforms and casings. Open Saturday and Sunday 10-12, without reservation.
Among the vineyards on foot or by bike.
Late sixteenth century church with three arched porch; it preserves the canvas of the Crucifixion with five saints painted by Giovan Battista Lama in 1586.
The abbot's herbarium.
A mammoth born from lignite mines.
A medieval village in Pollino.
Born in 1932 on the left bank of the Po from an idea of Cesare Goria Gatti and Roberto Biscaretti of Ruffia: over 200 cars of 80 brands from all over the world.
Venetian and Neapolitan painting.
Next to the church of the Blessed Redeemer, a short distance from the Cathedral and the Reggia: liturgical furnishings, paintings, ex-vote and sculptures from the churches of the diocese.
A red stone village.
The sanctuary of Feronia is a whole Roman city along the Tiberina.
The grappa of Monferrato, from the still to the glass.
13th century castle near Monte del Lago, the most fearsome military settlement in the area, with seven towers (five survivors), three gates and a massive wall.
The lake on the pass towards France.

In the Villa Tittoni Traversi, since 1999 he has been donating the Milanese sculptor Giuseppe Scalvini (108-2003): 36 sculptures in plaster, wax and bronze, to which in 2003 16 drawings in charcoal and some engravings were added. Scalvini, author of the eagles of the Central Station and Justice of the Tribunal of Milan, realized in 1937 two angels for the Basilica of Desio and participated in the Venice Biennale in 1948 and 1954. In addition to the permanent collection, temporary exhibitions of artists from the twentieth century. Open Friday, Saturday and Sunday 10:30-12:30 and 15:30-18:00; Thursday by appointment.
The accessories of the Vallone necropolis.
A small 15th-century hospital complex in the centre.
House built at the end of the sixteenth century, inside which there is another nuraghe, Su Nuraxi 'e Cresia.
Historic coffee.
Frescoes by Paolo Piazza and the Bronze Age of the plain.
One of the most important museums on the island.
The monumental trees of the Presila.
The medieval aqueduct and the Fontana del Vecchio, among the places indicated by the regional portal.

Among the oldest and most important Romanesque buildings in Valtellina, dedicated to Saints Peter, Paul and Maiolo: it was built in 1078, when Otto and Bonizza of the Comacina Island donated the land to the monks of Cluny, then depended on the priory of Piona and was suppressed in the Napoleonic era. The low bell tower, the semicircular apse in four sectors and part of the southern wall with a round arched portal remain; the restoration is by engineer Antonio Gussa, between 1914 and 1916, and recent excavations have brought to light the walls of the monks' building. It can be reached in 5-10 minutes by mule track from Piagno, between chestnuts and robinias.
Protected area about 12 km from the city, with the valley of Cervaro: birds, deers, wild boars and reptiles.

The old town has slate portals surmounted by bas-reliefs and inscriptions. The parish church of Saints Matthew and Gregory is in neoclassical forms (the Province dates back to the 12th century); the Oratory of the Santissima Annunziata houses a canvas of the Annunciation dated 1545; in the village there is also the small church of San Rocco.
Walls and towers overlooking the lake.

Part of the Latium Historical Houses Network: the fortress, in defence of Anagni, was burned in 1184 and rebuilt on the ruins; since 1427 it was for centuries the Colonna. The Torre Colonna remains with battlements, wounds and walkways and stretches of the walls, particularly suggestive under the snow.

On a terrace overlooking the Naviglio Grande, in the hamlet of Castelletto, the villa has the present eighteenth-century appearance: H-shaped plant on the ground floor, mezzanine and first floor, lower bodies around the courtyard and a staircase that descends to the Naviglio, originally the main entrance. It is considered one of the most sumptuous villas of Naviglio and Milanese and closes the itinerary of the Villas of Delight of Naviglio Grande.
18th century villa with Italian garden of cedars, magnolias and camphors, and rooms with sculptures, stuccoes, majolica and nineteenth century furniture by the cabinetmaker Henry Thomas Peters.
€8, reduced €5 (6-18 years and students up to 25), family €22; guided tour €13
In via San Michele Arcangelo, just outside the cathedral: a corner of the village linked to the fantastic stories of Casertavecchia.

In the monumental complex of St. Bartholomew, one of the two centers of internment for Jews and political prisoners that Campaign hosted in the Second World War: panels and documents on the Shoah and the Jews interned, the reconstruction of a lodging and the place of worship of the camp, a room of pencils, one for each interneth, and the Room of the Fugue, which recalls the escape after September 8, 1943 with the sign "Hebrews transferred," Unknown Destination.

At the Prese dei Rossi, in a grove at the Colle di Castiglione, remains indicated by the municipality as of Celtic times, called "pietrefitte" or "menhir"; the history page of the municipality binds them to druid settlements.
The walled village against Pavia.

From the parking lot of Casera Pramosio (1521 m), reached by Laipacco on the dirt road, the CAI 402 trail leads in about two hours to the lake, next to the Casera Pramosio Alta refuge (1940 m). Along the way the Morgante-Casera Malpasso refuge, an ancient medieval silver mine, quarries disused with marmots, the tombstone of the Carnic carrier Maria Plozner Mentil and remains of military posts.
The church of the saint who gives his name to the village.

It preserves the frescoes above the altar of Giovanni de Gregorio known as the Pietrafesa, painter born in Satriano and active in the first half of the seventeenth century, among the most famous of Basilicata.
The palace of bishops, among the main monuments of the center, preserves a sixteenth-century polyptych with the Madonna and Child and saints of Gerolamo from Santacroce.
Closed for restoration after the earthquake of 2016 according to the Marche Region; the reliquary is exhibited at Palazzo Paradisi
The ancient roots of the coast, from the land and the sea.
One of the largest mountain pastures in Europe, dotted with anemones at the foot of the Gran Paradiso, recognized as natural Italian wonder.
Palazzo Barocco del Seicento, now Town Hall, with frescoes of Montalto and in the hall the painting Â"The chariot of the Aurora" .
Baroque church of the XVII century, next to the Marchionale Castle.
A series of water jumps can be reached on foot from the Sanctuary of the Madonna dell'Acero.
Where Italian organic farming was born.

The medieval village of Castelnuovo Fogliani has grown around a fortress with a tower dated 1377, transformed into a villa in the mid-18th century designed by Luigi Vanvitelli, to which the nearby church of San Biagio is attributed. Neoclassical facade, a hall frescoed by Giuseppe Natali, an oval salon richly decorated with stucco and an Italian garden with geometric parts; in 1925 the last Duchess Sforza Fogliani donated the complex to the Holy See. The Municipality organizes guided tours of about 80 minutes (church, frescoed rooms and garden) on some Sundays from April to October, at 3.30 pm and at 5 pm, with reservation required at 0523 945500.
The Savior's Renaissance triptych.
The country and its fractions told step by step.
The Occitan peasant house as it was.
Hera's treasure.

Artificial basin at 685 m formed by the dam on the Fiastrone (86 m high and 360 m long), at the foot of the Sibillini: the main beach of San Lorenzo al Lago is guarded, there are large stretches of free beach with bathing in the marked areas, two campsites, rental of pedalos, canoes and bikes and the Adventure Park with zipline on the lake. The Nature Path starts from San Lorenzo and follows the right bank for about two hours, with 900 m accessible to people with disabilities.
The church on the bridge.

The heart of the village owes the plant to the work of Baron Alfonso Soderini in the second half of the sixteenth century. The fortress retains the military aspect of the 16th-XVII century, with a square central tower, two round corner towers, garrets and bastions, and a large park with an ancient well; from the mastium the view goes from Gran Sasso to Terminillo to Maiella, and at sunset the lights of the 34 villages around.
The medieval village on foot in half an hour.

On the top of Mount Albagna, in the middle of a morainic arch between small lakes and a park of 11 hectares. In 1640 the hermit Tomaso Barberio built a chapel in San Giuseppe; then became a convent of Teresiani and Carmelitani and sanctuary, was fortified in Napoleonic age and transformed into a noble residence, where Eleonora Duse, Arrigo Boito and Giuseppe Giacosa stayed at the end of the nineteenth century. Restored after long abandonment, today it is a hotel.

Country of the valley of the Esino, stage of the Cappuccini Way, with the civic tower among the most pendant in Italy and, in the woods of the valley of the Acquarella, the hermitage where in 1529 the first general chapter of the Capuchins was held.
The square redesigned by Jean Nouvel, with the Spazio Michelucci, the Scalo Merci Don Gnocchi, the Crystal Serranda by Alessandra Tesi and the facade of the Bellini Chorus by Alberto Garutti.

Born from the association "La Raccolta della Barca Lariana," founded in 1978 to save old boats destined for demolition, the museum opened in 1982 in a nineteenth-century mill. In fourteen halls exhibits about 160 of the more than 350 boats owned (fishing boats, motorboats for racing and tourism, sailing boats, smuggling, military and work) with nets, engines, sails, tools and documents on the Larian nautical, even with increased reality. The most important piece is a gondola built in 1860 on Lake Como, with asymmetrical shapes and the felze of the Venetian tradition. Admission fee, reduced for TCI members and a companion.
From the fort to the observatory, the history of the island.

Dedicated to San Leonardo when it belonged to the Teutonic Knights (1230-1358), then to the Augustinians: portal of the 13th century with Christ between San Leonardo and San Nicola in the lunette and two lions on the sides; on the side portal the coats of arms of the Teutonics, the Angiò and the architect Sergio Bove.

Erected in 1546 in honor of the young martyr protector of Bassano, today in the modern part of the village: a single nave with St. Paul and St. Peter and, on the sides of the apse, frescoes with the life of the saint.
Founded in 1747 by Cardinal Querini in the former bishop's palace; over 500,000 volumes, 1,158 incunabula, 8,386 five hundred and 10,000 manuscripts.
Very wide beach of sand and pebbles, surrounded by palm trees and bergamot, from which you can see the slopes of Etna.
Hike to the hermitage on the Roman temple.
Marine fossils and shells in a quarry returned to nature.
The anatomical theatre and the tomb of Ariosto.
The apartment of the spouses Boschi Di Stefano with masterpieces by Carrà, Fontana, De Chirico, Sironi, De Pisis and Boccioni, part of the circuit Case Museo.
private residence, open from May to October for the occasion of Castles Open
In spring the fair of the plum fungus in Cusercoli.

The castle, purchased by the Municipality of Gubbio in the 13th century, passed to the Papal State in the 17th century and the Kingdom of Italy in 1860. It preserves the remains of the fortress and the walls with the Civic Tower of the 13th century and four doors: of the clock, of the Trione (or of the Rivellino), of Guerrino Gambucci and of the Monument (or of San Lorenzo).
The oldest churches in the territory.

The Ionian Pearl on the Gulf of Squillace, Blue Flag and Green Flag: three kilometers of promenade, the Regional Marine Park of the Bay of Soverato with the seahorses, the Botanical Garden Santicelli, the Tower of Carlo V, the ruins of Soverato Vecchia and, in Soverato Superiore, the Pietà by Antonello Gagini.
The Colonna fortress at the top of the acropolis.

It rises where in 1432 Our Lady appeared to a young woman and where a clear spring of water sprang up, which is located under the high altar and feeds two large pools in the entrance square, surrounded by porticoes for the shelter of pilgrims. The church, with a single nave and Latin cross in classic style, was started in the sixteenth century; the reconstruction is attributed to Pellegrino Tibaldi. He preserves works by Juvara, Cavenaghi, Moriggia and Cavedoni; the most heartfelt festival is the 26th of May, the anniversary of the apparition.
A temple of nuragic water in limestone.
The City of Peace in Vallagarina: the Mart with the dome of Mario Botta, the Futurist Art House of Depero, the Castle with the War Museum and the Bell of the Fallen that plays every evening.

Three meditative paths start from Fraciscio: the first from the Guanella house descends to the banks of the Rabbiosa stream and continues to Gualdera, a place where the saint had the intuition of his vocation; the second passes from the churchyard of the Most Holy Trinity, the third leads to the parish of St. Alexander.

Village of the Piacenza plain on the left bank of the Arda, rebuilt from about 1480 at the will of Gianlodovico Pallavicino as an ideal city of the Renaissance on orthogonal roads; it houses the Collegiate Church with the mausoleum of Pallavicino, the Church of the Annunciation with the frescoes of Pordenone and the Eleonora Duse Theatre.
The frescoes by Vincenzo Manenti.
The botanical garden of the University of Palermo, open-air university museum.

Nuragic well temple in the center, discovered in 1924 by the owner of the land, dated according to the scholars between the middle and the final Bronze: limestone cones laid dry, vestibule with counters-seats, eight steps staircase and circular chamber with trunk of cone, without the roof to tholos; the style recalls the well of Santa Cristina in Paulilatino. Around, traces of a trachyte fence on a temple in antis and a village; the bull bronze found here is at the Sanna Museum in Sassari.
The art of Arbus's "arresoja" .
Palladio's last work, a round temple in miniature.
The Romanesque basilica of the village, marked by Visit Tuscany among the monuments to see in Asciano together with Palazzo Corboli.
The works of Verdi room by room.
Walk on a carpet of prehistoric obsidian.
Born in 2012 on the ground floor of an eighteenth-century house: didactical itinerary on genealogy and the origin of surnames.
Golden sandy beach with lush vegetation.

The 12th century Latin cross church and three naves, with the original rose window on the portal, restored after various earthquakes; paintings by Cristoforo Santanna, Giuseppe Pascaletti and Giuseppe Grana.
From here the Rhine water arrived in Bologna.
Federico II told in sixteen multimedia rooms.

At the crossing between Viù and the Val di Susa the park preserves an ancient network of trails and mule tracks that connected the hamlets and that during the Resistance served to the 17th Brigade Garibaldi. The Nazi Fascist rake of July 2, 1944, in which many young partisans died, is remembered by a tower, a memorial garden and a stone.

Inaugurated on June 18, 1967 in honor of the 600 partisans of the 51 municipalities of the Pinerolese valleys that fell into the Liberation, it was designed by Roberto Gabetti and Aimaro Isola: a 15-metre-high stone hollow tower, with a ladder that rises to a 360° panoramic terrace on the Western Alps and the plain. Here in 1943 the first armed group of the Pinerolese was formed; on 17 October 1943 about 500 German soldiers surrounded St. Bartholomew. Free access to the external structure.

The hilly village of Casalese, among the nine municipalities of the core zone         . Monferrato degli Infernot , of the UNESCO site of the Wine Landscapes of Langhe-Roero and Monferrato (2014); at the top the castle of Nemours, then Sacchi-Nemours, counts of Frassinello, the parish church of the Assunta with the organ of Lingiardi of 1864 and a hell to visit in the village.
A panoramic staircase to the little church on the hill.
A unique work in the world, little known.
A circle of early Christian columns.
The village of Bourbon settlers and houses in the rock.

Country on the plain of the former lake of Bientina, once the largest in Tuscany, with the parish church of Santa Maria Assunta that preserves the remains of Saint Valentino and its Museum of sacred art, the fourteenth-century Mastio and the Museum of the ancient history of the territory in the former oratory of San Girolamo; on the edge of the ancient lake the reserve of Bosco Tanali.
The 18th century pharmacy.

Built in two years, from 1887 to 1889, with the granite of the mountain, in the era of the  "Great Fortifications," together with the batteries of Capo d'Orso and Baragge; it is considered one of the largest fortresses built in Italy in the nineteenth century. On two levels connected by a staircase, with ramparts on granite ridges, barracks, warehouses, powder keg and a monumental ramp towards the shooting area; since 1990 it has passed to the Superintendence and in summer it hosts concerts. Visit only with guide, from the end of March to the beginning of November.

The arched dam, 261 meters high according to Italia.it, was built by Sade since 1957; on the evening of October 9, 1963 a landslide of about 270 million cubic meters from Mount Toc fell into the basin and the wave destroyed Longarone and part of Erto and Casso, with almost 2,000 victims. Today it is a memorial: the Park organizes a guided tour of 50 minutes on the crown (groups of maximum 40, meeting at the square of the memorial church, tickets on VivaTicket or at the information point) and visits of 2-3 hours to the places of memory. Path not suitable for those suffering from vertigo.
At the end of Corso Alfieri, tower of Augustian age elevated in the XI-XII centuries, with the remains of the medieval belt.
Region Marche: historical center, monuments and museums only partially usable
The square where the religious and civil symbols of the city are flanked: the Bishops' Palace, the Civic Tower, the Rector's Palace, the Red Palace and the Cathedral.
Other Tiepolo next to the Duomo.

Set up in the 17th century Casa Eredi Vasina, it tells of the Walser colonization and the daily life of a time with reconstructed environments, original objects and panels: crafts, mountain agriculture, religious and ritual customs, family structure and the Walser language, the "titsch" . Visits by reservation (tel. 0163 55203).

Ethno-anthropological Museum designed and built by Professor Matteo Stuppiello in 1979; after several locations he found a place in a nineteenth-century building, where he exhibits in more rooms about 2,000 objects catalogued in chronological order.
It preserves the incorrupt body of the Blessed Beatrice d'Este and the altarpiece of Giambattista Tiepolo with Santa Tecla who intercedes to free the city from the plague.
The loggia with 143 arches that leads to the sanctuary, indicated as the longest in Italy.
The symbol of the oldest district.
Six paintings of Peccheneda from 1769.
An ancient village towards the Arno.

17th century palace on the Corso, now home to the Town Hall and a Benedictine cloistered monastery, whose nuns carry on the tradition of embroidery. It includes the small church of St. John the Baptist (open to worship in 1633, today deconsecrated), with a fresco of the Baptism of Christ of the Domenichino.
Verzi is the most hilly village in the city: from here start the paths to the top of Monte Carmo (1389 m), the highest peak of the area.
The mother church at the top of the stairway, point of arrival from the lower town.
The monumental olive tree of legends.
The 13th century medieval complex, four buildings around a courtyard, seat of the Galleria d'Arte Moderna Paolo and Adele Giannoni.
The museum dedicated to the Alps, surrounded by greenery along the path that goes up to the Mausoleum of Cesare Battisti.
The cathedral whose interior recalls the great early Christian basilicas of Rome.
By bike between the village, the basilica of Costa Balenae and the sea.
The number one giant bench, where it all started.
The original plasters of Arturo Martini in a 17th century villa.

The name comes from the hold, the handle of the plow. It collects photographs from the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, costumes and military uniforms, rebuilt environments (farm kitchen, room, local for hemp weaving, carpenter's workshop, cellar, classroom) and agricultural tools, telling viticulture, beekeeping, baching and weaving of the hemp of the area.
Family walk.
The heart of the medieval Ferrara, three minutes from the Castle.

In Palazzo Lupieri, a six-seventh-century Carnic style residence, collects the fossils of the Preone valley and illustrates the geological and biological history of the Carnic Prealps: the first room reconstructs with dioramas environments and animals of the territory, the second tells the area from 200 million years ago with some important fossils. It is part of the CarniaMusei network. Summer time indicated by MiC: June-September 16-18 (data 2020, to be verified).
The home design was born on Lake Orta.
Other mosaics next to the basilica.
The wine of the shelter.
The Gothic-Catalan mother church of Villacidro.
A country sanctuary linked to a popular legend.
Octagonal church in the Venice district crowned by a fifty-metre-high dome, with remains of nineteenth-century frescoes.

The square was built at the end of the fifteenth century on a project by Francesco di Giorgio Martini, with powerful containment works; on one side the Data, on the other the ramp of Francesco di Giorgio, above which stands the nineteenth-century theatre, which connects the Mercatale to the historic center.
One hundred thousand years of Val Trebbia in a castle.
A Renaissance door between two towers.

17th century parish church dedicated to Saint Bernardino da Siena, which gives its name to one of the two villages of the village, on the right of the Nure; it preserves stuccoes and frescoes by G.B. Galluzzi of 1716.
For birdwatching.

Ecomuseum of the Sila National Park in the former convent of the Franciscan Friars Minor, dedicated to the handicrafts of Silano, the defence of the soil and the extraction of silver and goldsmithery.
At the Town Hall, a former Franciscan monastery built with funds from the local university under license of Pope Boniface IX of 5 December 1391.

18th century building at the confluence of the torrents Salice and Frido, which housed a hydraulic sawmill and a wool gulcher; renovated in the early 2000s, today it houses a typical restaurant and accommodations.
A Venetian villa became a town hall.

The Lèch dei Giai is a natural lake at 2205 meters at the foot of the Auta peak, reachable from the Franzei Valley with CAI path and easy forest road; another CAI path leads to the panoramic plateau of Val Franzedàz, about 1980 meters, with barns and houses.
Roman Domus with two decorative phases, around the middle of the first century BC and around 100 AD, near the theatre.

A watchtower around the year 1000, owned by the Columns from the 12th to the 19th century, built on a Roman site with irregular hexagonal plan; inside there are traces of the ancient church of St. Peter. At the top of the tower is an astronomical observatory with a new dome and telescope.

Rebuilt in 1758 by the brothers Angelo and Giulio Contarini next to their villa, it has facade with statues and rocaille portal attributed to Antonio Bonazza; inside, with a single nave with rocaille stuccoes, a large fresco on the ceiling of Jacopo Guarana, angels in Bonazza marble on the sides of the main altar and a altarpiece by Domenico Fedeli called the Mayt. Under the altar rests the body of the holy pope Adeodato, donated to the Contarini by Innocent XII.
With works by local artists.
€5, reduced €3 (6-12 years), free under 6 years
The Crucifix of Fra Umile and the Renaissance marbles.

Nuraghe with single tower on a modest relief, with external diameter of about 13 m and preserved walls up to 2 m; the circular chamber has two lateral niches and the door of the staircase opens in the entrance hall, facing south. It collapsed in the Middle-Recent Bronze and was then re-used as a hut, until a violent fire caused its abandonment; the excavation of 1982-1983 returned about a thousand fragments of obsidian, basalt millstones, ceramics and a bronze dagger. It is located about 270 m south-west of the tomb On Cuaddu de Nixias and is an unmanaged site.

Borgo della Maremma viterbese on a plateau of tuff along the Via Clodia, surrounded by Etruscan rock necropolis such as Pian del Vescovo and, towards Barbarano, the archaeological area of San Giovenale excavated by the Swedes since 1956; in the village the collegiate with the tomb of San Vivenzio and the Museum

Oak of caducifoglio of about 400 hectares, Site of Community Importance, frequented for excursions and picnics; inside the Wood of the Fairy tales is a didactic itinerary that tells legends and games of the local folk tradition.
Granite, portals and cellars of the Mandrolisai.
The Romanesque parish from which Erba was born.
The nineteenth-century scientific museum was set up in 1898 and remained almost unchanged.
€5, reduced €4, boys 6-14 years €2
High plateau almost a thousand meters high with views of the Ogliastra, reached through the Scala di San Giorgio.

The village of the Belice Valley linked to the Gattopardo: Palazzo Filangeri Cutò, where Giuseppe Tomasi of Lampedusa spent the summers of childhood and model Donnafugata, with the museum and literary park, the former Mother Church became Museum of Memory of the earthquake of 1968 and the ruins of the ancient country.
Villa with garden, inserted by the municipality among the gardens, villas and parks of the city.

Built around the middle of the fifteenth century by the Brotherhood of the SS. Trinity, which in 1634 welcomed that of the Holy Apostles: from the union comes the asymmetrical form with two communicating naves, the minor closed by the late Renaissance chapel of the Madonna del Carmine. It preserves a wooden altar of the late seventeenth century and a sixteenth-century altar of Vercelli's school with the Trinity and Saints Peter and Paul; baroque bell tower of 1745-1750. Recently restored, open mon-ven 8.30-12.

Halfway to the castle, it dates back to 1262 and was the church of a Franciscan monastery, among the first of Friuli. It contains a portal from the sixteenth century, frescoes fourteenth-century, the Nativity of the Virgin of Egidio Dall'Oglio (XVIII century), an eighteenth-century organ by Giacinto Pescetti, marble altars and eighteenth-century stables.

Ring of about 2 hours and 30 minutes Scalucchia-Spigone-Pineto-Legoreccio-Crovara-Scalucchia between medieval houses and woods with roe deer, linked to the history of Matilde di Canossa; the stream Tassaro houses freshwater shrimps and vairons and a little downstream of Scalucchia forms a waterfall, reachable on foot from the Chichino Mill along the Tassobbio.
The Gothic Last Judgement rediscovered.
History of the Great War and geology on the same path.

Borgo dei Nebrodi linked to San Nicolò Politi, who lived hermitage in a grotto of the territory from 1137 to 1167: the Mother Church preserves its body, the hermitage rises about 2.5 km from the village; above the village rise the Rocks of Crasto, limestone massif with royal eagles and griffon, and the Grotto of Lauro.

Walk under the arcades between Piazza Garibaldi, the urban stretch of the Via Emilia and a stretch of the late-Medieval walls, probably of the late fourteenth century, in bricks tied with mortar and stone. In Piazza Aldo Moro the bronze by Gianni Ferrari tells the legend of the birth of the tortellino, with a giant tortellino of about 50 cm; the Festival of Tortellino is held in September with a reenactment in costume.
Once an ancient castle, today a place of memory destined to cultural space.
The anti-pirate tower symbol of Pozzallo.

A medieval tower from the 15th century at the top of the hill, with a clock considered one of the oldest in Italy: the dial is divided into six hours according to the Italian method and the mechanism, still working, moves the only hand of the hours; every evening it plays 50 chimes in memory of the Spanish siege of 50 days of 1648. Inside, the permanent exhibition "The space of memory" with ancient and current photos of the Eagle before and after the earthquake of 2009 by Roberto Grillo, a stele for victims and a multimedia post on anti-seismic prevention. Not indicated hours: contact the Municipality (0862 85131).

Central of the early twentieth century that transformed the power of the Cellina stream into energy, with original turbines and generators. The multimedia route, in Italian and English, has totem actually increased, a room on the geology of the territory, the construction of the socket and interactive stations on the architecture and the workers of the plant. Visits by reservation through Eupolis.

From the village you climb to the Capo la Serra pass (about 1,600 m) and then to the Campo Imperatore plateau, about 25 km long and defined the largest of the Apennines, with canyons, seasonal lakes and spring blooms; near the Astronomical Observatory at about 2,100 m and the Gran Sasso cable car.
Woods and views of the Limbara.

In the premises of Tenuta Torrione della Colombara, it collects objects donated and restored by the citizens: kitchen and bedroom furnishings, the workshops of the blacksmith, the masquerade and wicker braider, a school hall of epoch, cars and agricultural wagons. In the same estate a modern rice farm shows the rice supply chain, from cultivation to packaging.
The working silk machines, in a spinning mill on the lake.
In the sculptor's workshop.
The Vercelli Book.
The "living room" of the city, built in 1808 and dedicated to the poet Walther von der Vogelweide, with the monument of 1889, elegant coffee, the flower market in spring and the Christmas market.
The ionic sea of the Sardella village.

Managed by the Majella Park in a wing of the former convent of Sant'Antonio, active since 2005: five sections with panels, dioramas and a night forest rebuilt on biology, habits, myth and conservation of the bear. From June to August open every day 10-13 and 17-20; from September to May Saturday 16-19 and Sunday 10-13.
The church was born in the Round.
The lake on foot, between beaches, oratories and villas.
The place of the first stigmata.
The first Christian basilica.
The best known street of the city, reached by the narrow Face of the Centors; Casa Centoris has a Bramantesque façade and an elegant courtyard, which can only be visited on special days.
The miracle of the frescoed wolf twice.
The village of stone and porphyry of the Oltrepò.
The center on the water of the park.
To live the city like the Maceratesi.

Designed by Oscar Niemeyer, who donated the design to the city in 2000, and inaugurated in January 2010: a curved shape that follows the profile of the Coast, a shell on the sea, with about 400 seats under a dome. It hosts concerts and winter shows and screenings on the weekend.
A little jewel of frescoes.

Private collection of more than 200 nautical objects, in an ancient tower house of the village of San Giovanni: Venetian telescopes of the eighteenth century, compasses, sundials, astrolabi, sea chronometers, an armillary sphere and a brass planetarium, with a story of life on ships of the nineteenth century.
MiC card (updated in 2020) indicates "Closed" every day of the week; check before the visit
A chapel among the vineyards transformed into a building with vibrant colorful decoration, inside and outside; the interior is not open to visitors.
A day of spa in Crete.

Via Roma, the ...caruggio is the main street with medieval porticoes, historic shops and restaurants; it ends in Piazza Marconi, dominated by the Basilica of Santo Stefano and the Porticato Brignardello. The old town is made of arcades and colorful houses.
A church in the palaces of power.
The arch of triumph erected in honour of the emperor Charles V, between the two oldest gates at the entrance of the old city; Gian Giacomo dell'Acaya worked there.
The Marian sanctuary of pilgrims with a view from the Circeo agli Aurunci.
Small municipal museum dedicated to rural life.
Museum house dedicated to the missionary of PIME Alberico Crescitelli, born in Altavilla and martyred in China in 1900 during the Boxer revolt.
A place of memory for the victims of the Padule.
The Red Arrow in a monastery.
the MiC card indicates mandatory booking (Wednesday-Sunday 10-12), but the ticket table marks closed every day
In front of the entrance of Villa Ada, one of the largest and oldest in Rome (end II century): about 40,000 burials in 13 km of galleries, with many popes and martyrs.

It dates back to 1220, with successive changes; the bell tower is 1571-73. It preserves an ancient fresco of San Cristoforo, a Virgin with the 17th century Child and a pulpit between the end of the 16th and early 17th century; on the side façade a sundial.
The convent complex with the church of 1568, which at the main altar preserves the Madonna with the Saints Jerome and Cristina of Pietro da Cortona.
Covered walk.

Castles on the heights above the Flaminia: the fortress of Cantiano, on the hill of Sant'Ubaldo, dates back to the IX century and hosted the castle of Gabrielli of Gubbio, which had Cantiano as a fief since 1381; on the top of Colmatrano remain the ruins of a military tower.
The fraction of the mycological exhibition.
The private house of the first king of Italy.
It is the oldest building in the city to survive the earthquake of 1783, and the ashes of over two thousand victims of the earthquake rest there.

Laboratory behind the family pharmacy, active since 1900 as a small pharmaceutical workshop: injectable vials, fruit syrups and registered medicinal products. It exhibits alembics, pestles, mortars and antique instruments; pharmacists Foletto still produce syrups and liqueurs, including Picco Rosso, with tastings. Out of season only by appointment; free entry with the Garda Guest Card.
The village is visited in one morning.

Barbagia village at 660 meters on Mount Genna de Crobu, between the limestone heels and Gennargentu: a museum of natural sciences with about a thousand Sardinian minerals, the nuragic complex of Cuccuru Nolza, the forest of Uatzo crossed by the Green Train.

Founded in 2005 by the volunteers of A.R.T.S. onlus, since 5 May 2013 it has been located in a former factory in the school complex Gianni Roots and is recognized by the Region as Museum Collection since 2014. More than 1,000 m2 of working machinery: one of the few silk torciotes in Italy, with parts designed by Leonardo, a hydraulic wheel of over three meters, looms from the Middle Ages to the mid-Twentieth century, card, gauze machine and follon, an embroidery machine Wuerker of 1926 and a working model of Somet frame, as well as a textile and dyeing garden. Guided tour only (about 60-80 minutes), usually Saturday and Sunday from 15 by reservation; closed in January, July, August and December.
The largest Roman villa in northern Italy, overlooking the lake.
The real home of Pope John, with the objects of his study in the Vatican.
At least six domus de janas on a limestone pitch on the outskirts of the village: the Tomb I,  the tomb of the house
The seventeenth century Bergamo in his painter's house.
