Sandy beach on the border with Tuscany.

Karst complex excavated from an underground stream, discovered in 1934 by Francesco Saverio Majellaro, with remains of Neanderthal, animals, stone instruments and paintings; reopened to the public in 1990.
MiC indicates it as usually closed, open on extraordinary occasions
The stories of prisoners and refugees from the camp of Servigliano.

Settling built entirely under a huge mass of gneiss on Mount Bracco, about 650 meters, in the chestnut woods; settled until the 1950s-sixties, today it is an ecomuseum. You can visit stone houses with flat roofs (used to repair hay and charms), stables, barns, tool store, dryer, sink and bread oven, some houses with original furnishings. It is reached on foot in about half an hour from the hamlet Rocchetta, for mule tracks between secular chestnut trees; guided tours from June to October.
One of the four castles of the municipality, fortress dating back to the time of the birth of Frederick II of Swabia. In front of Rocca Priora a Mare, there is a free beach equipped for dogs.
Alleys dug into the rock.
The market covered in Art Nouveau style where you buy Parmesan, balsamic vinegar and DOP products, with benches for a quick taste.
A single nave church in the Gothic-Franciscan style, passed to the Franciscans in the thirteenth century, with a crucifix on a table by Duccio di Buoninsegna.
In the footsteps of the Patroness of Italy.

Built about the 12th century in front of the church of Santa Maria Ausiliatrice, it is about 15 meters deep, divided into two floors and measuring 6 x 6 meters; it collected water for periods of drought or siege. The two rooms can be visited thanks to routes along the edges, with audio guides in Italian and English.

The village enclosed by ancient walls rises along the slopes of the Poggio Petriccio hill to the medieval castle, overlooking the city and the surroundings; in the center the church of San Giovanni Battista, whose bell tower rests on a circular tower, and near the walls the church of Santa Maria del Giglio.
The neoclassical temple where Dante rests, died in Ravenna in 1321, with the Quadrarch of Braccioforte and the Franciscan cloisters next door.
Clear water mirror that can be reached on foot along the Aniene; the river is also used for rafting, canyoning and stand up paddle.
The grave of a Byzantine empress in the hills.

Cities along the Via Flaminia at the foot of the Nerone and Petrano mountains, with the Medieval Public Palace then residence of Federico da Montefeltro, which houses the Archaeological Museum and the Via Flaminia, the Torrione of Francesco di Giorgio Martini today Centre for Contemporary Sculpture, the Cathedral rebuilt after the earthquake of 1781 and the Roman Bridge Mallio; around forre and waterfalls of Monte Nerone.
The frescoes along the paths.
Green area of tree-lined avenues, ancient garden of Palazzo Altieri.
Church of the hamlet Piagge, where every year on Sunday after July 16 is celebrated the feast of Our Lady, called "day of the consumed" because it fell at the end of a hard work in the fields.

A village perched on the Aso valley near the Parco dei Monti Sibillini, known as the village of longevity, due to the number of centenarians: overhanging houses on the river with walls and bridge, the church of Santa Maria a Terme of the IX century on the remains of a pagan temple, St. Francis and the Museum of sacred art in Palazzo Pascali.
An octagonal architecture among the fields.
The view of Mount Rosa.

Built in the middle of the eighteenth century on the foundations of a fifteenth-century cathedral by the will of the last Patriarch of Aquileia, Daniele Delfino; it houses works of different eras and next stands the 73-metre-high bell tower.

Cities on the southern side of Mount Etna, about 7 km from Catania, rebuilt after the lava of March 29, 1669 destroyed the ancient village; of the buried village remain the bell tower, 'U Campanarazzu', and the excavations of the ancient Mother Church, while in the new center are located the Mother Church with the Sacred Art Museum, the Four Songs and the Carnival Museum.

Also known as Palazzo Farnese-Ridolfi, by the cardinal governors of Lugnano, and "Pennone" because it stands like the pin of a ship: built around 1650, three-storey, with angulars, balustrades and rustic portals in travertine, it is curiously cut into two by the homonymous gallery. It was the residence of the pontifical governor, then barn, mill and bachiculture; restored, it houses the Town Hall.
Outside the center, at the bottom of a tree-lined avenue, it preserves the body and the urn of the patron saint of the city and of the lovers, bishop of Terni martyred in the third century.
A small 18th-century oratory.
The altar of the mother church.
Two intact republican temples.
Fossil of the ancient Tyrrhenian Sea, Neolithic instruments and Roman finds, with audiovisual and photographic material on the history of the territory; open Monday to Saturday in the afternoon.
Taste it with honey or piadina.
The amphitheatre of the Roman Segusio, part of the archaeological park of the city.

It is 2.512 m high between Val Brembana and Val Seriana, among the best view of the Orobie, with views from Presolana to Legione. From Zambla Alta a mule track goes up to the hut Capanna 2000, also suitable for families; beyond the hut the path gets steep on meadows and rocks, with little men and a short stretch equipped not exposed before the summit. The steepest shortcut with path 222; other accesses from the Alpe Arera (parking fee) and via Plassa. In winter only for experienced and equipped hikers.
A historical park and the Etruscan tomb in copy.

The Porta Spoletina is a 14th-century crenellated tower in pink stone overlooking Corso San Giuseppe Leonessano; the Porta Aquilana, to the north, is a remnant of the defensive system wanted by Carlo I d'Angiò.
A place of memory of the Shoah in Piedmont.
Wood and water a stone's throw from the village.
A 17th-century monastery on the cliff.

Borgo on a limestone spur above the valley of the Basento, recognizable from a distance for the Norman tower 27 meters high; it preserves the ancient districts of Rabatana and Saracena, the cathedral wanted by Robert Guiscardo, the Doge's Palace and the monasteries frescoed by Pietro Antonio Ferro. The writer Rocco Scotellaro was born in 1923.
The Etruscans of Cortona.
The console village.

A sixteenth-century fountain near the bridge that connects the old and new cities, the result of several interventions: a counter-façade was added to the ancient façade, facing the south in the eighteenth century. It has three tanks supported each by three putti and three high reliefs with mythological scenes and Latin inscriptions.

Designed by Francesco da Volterra and consecrated in 1575 by Carlo Borromeo: bishop's stables of the seventeenth century, a Holy Family of Lombard school and a 17th century silver palace. On Piazza Mazzini in front of the statue of Ferrante I Gonzaga di Leone Leoni (1564).
A white stone octagon in the middle of the countryside.
Ancient Franciscan monastery a short distance from the village, where the monks of Farfa fled from Sabina found refuge.
the MiC card indicates "closed" every day without hours; contact tel. 0575 445302, biblio@civichiana.it
The palace of the medieval lords of the city: the Acaja chose Pinerolo as the capital of their domains in 1295.
A Teutonic commando intact in the countryside, with frescoes from the thirteenth century.
The Gothic basilica of the historic center can be reached from via Sottoriva, among the main places of worship of the city of Scaligera.
By bike along the river.

Outside the walls, the square was the ancient market: there stands the Paveion, loggia of the grains of 1603 where the negotiations were held; Corso XXIX Aprile is the elegant street of ancient palaces. Inside the walls the Palazzo del Monte di Pietà, which until the twentieth century lent to the poor of the city, today the Municipal Library, and the Palazzetto Preti, the only part built of the eighteenth-century hospital of Preti, seat of exhibitions.
Church of 1486 with a fresco attributed to Pinturicchio.

Opened in 2002 in Palazzo Gervasoni, fifteenth-century building and former convent with cloister in the highest point of the historic center. On three floors about 150 works donated by Don Gianni Bellini, especially painted from the sixteenth to the eighteenth century of Lombard, Venetian, Emilian, Tuscan, Roman and Neapolitan schools: Palma il Giovane, Alessandro Magnasco, Carlo Ceresa, Antonio Cifrondi, Nicolas Regnier, Francesco Cairo, as well as statues, furniture and processional crucifixes.
The square next to Piazza dei Signori, on which the Palazzo Liviano, seat of the Faculty of Letters and Philosophy, faces.

Of medieval origin, with three naves, rises in the green south of the village on the site of a more ancient church documented in 1217 and attributed to San Giulio; the current form dates back to about the second half of the fourteenth century, the late-Romanesque bell tower is dated 1505. Sunday Mass in the summer.
A nineteenth-century mill that still grinds.
The walk to the sea and the square indicated for the sunset on the Riviera.

18th century old town, built after the earthquake of February 5, 1783 that destroyed the ancient Polistena; among the alleys you will find coffee, typical desserts and trattorias with stochus and cutting. In the city are held the feast of the patron saint Marina (17 July), the rites of the Holy Week with the "Seven Words" by Michele Valensise and the "Affruntata," and in July the Night of the Giants Mata and Grifone.

Of Romanesque origins with Baroque façade: it preserves the relics of the patrons and the fifteenth-century altarpiece of the Bergognone.

The 17th century noble villa of the Federici Della Corte, built on a military outpost of the sixteenth century; in the eighteenth century the Peroni di Brescia transformed it into a villa of delight with Baroque furnishings and decorations, and at the end of the nineteenth century the Towers enlarged it. Paolina Calegari Torri and her husband Alessandro made it a cultural living room attended by Giosuè Carducci, Antonio Fogazzaro, Franz Lenbach, Domenico Trentacoste, Bishop Jeremiah Bonomelli and Minister Giuseppe Zanardelli. It is run by the Municipal Library.

Medieval church, national monument, built on the remains of a pagan temple and mentioned already in the Dialogues of St. Gregory the Great; in the apse the Blessing Redeemer, in the hexagonal baptistery frescoes of the late fourteenth century with stories of the Baptist and the Universal Judgment; on June 21 a ray of sun from a window marks the summer solstice.

In the historic center of Zanano, owned by the municipality, it is formed by a northern building older, with the medieval house-tower, and by a south modified in the seventies of the twentieth century. On the first floor, a fresco between the 14th and 15th centuries tells of a clash between Guelphs and Ghibellines in the Trompia Valley, with black bears armed against white bears; in the same room a Madonna enthroned with the Child and St. Martin bishop of the 15th century, and in another room a St. Jerome of 1474. It usually hosts the City's annual Art Prize.

On a hill facing the walls: originally dependent on the abbey of Montesanto, it passed to the Franciscans from the 13th century, who around 1466 built the present complex, still inhabited by the friars minor convents. Convent around a 14th century cloister and church with Romanesque portico; at the high altar the Madonna and Child in polychrome wood by Giovanni di Blusuccio (1489).

Built on the remains of the temple of Athena of 480 BC, of which the Doric columns are still visible inside and outside the building.

On the slope that goes up to the Rocca, with a large glazed wall open to the landscape, exhibits the finds of the ancient settlements of the Rocca and the territory along with its geological and naturalistic characteristics, including the materials of the UNESCO building site of San Sivino. It also organizes guided boat tours around the promontory with a stop at the submerged village.
A walk through the orchards.
An unusual plant.

On the third floor of Palazzo Primoli, the residence of the angler and critic Mario Praz, opened in 1995 and maintained as a nineteenth-century noble house with its collection of furnishings and objects; mandatory booking.

Rebuilt between the late fifteenth and early sixteenth centuries on the remains of a Romanesque church, with interior renovated in the Baroque age and apse restored in the nineteenth century. It preserves a Saint Joseph in glazed terracotta of the workshop of Andrea della Robbia, an Assumption attributed to Saints of Tito, a Madonna with Child and saints of author discussed (Giuseppe Porta or Giovanni Antonio Sogliani) and, in the chapel of St. Joseph, the fifteenth-century wooden crucifix known as "Cristo Nero" with marble frame attributed to the workshop of Matteo Civitali.

In the hamlet Commenda, Castel Negrino is what remains of ancient defensive settlements belonging to the Knights of Malta and the Templars; it meets along the regional cycle route between Mezzago and Ronco Briantino. It is reported in the FAI census (2010-2022) and the route from the sanctuary of Campegorino to Castel Negrino was opened for the FAI Days of Spring 2024.

Ethnoanthropological Museum inaugurated in 2005 and dedicated to the Lucanian arboreal cults, linked to the peasant world; it also serves as a visitor center of the Park of Gallipoli Cognato and has a library on the arboreal cults and a video library on the feasts of May. May combines the top of a holly with a large oak, symbol of fertility and good harvest.
The ancient church of the village, indicated among the things to see.
The central square dominated by the statue of Pope Sixtus V, with around the main buildings of the city.

A single nave church born from an oratory, with a simple façade and a frescoed presbytery with altar of the late eighteenth century; there is preserved the relic of Saint Vitale in a 17th-century metallic bust (the skull, stolen in 1747, was found on 26 December). Every first Sunday of May, the pilgrimage from San Germano Vercellese goes up there for a vow of 1613. Around area equipped with tables, fountain, garden of aromatic plants, tactile path and parking.

It tells the development of ancient Numana and the Riviera del Conero from prehistory to the Roman age, with attention to the trade of the Numana store in the Mediterranean. On the first floor the rich burial of the Queen of Sirolo (VI century BC), with attic and picene ceramics, bronzes, avori, amber jewelry and the remains of a horse and a war chariot, flanked by the picena tomb of a warrior; on the second floor the chronological section, and in closing the collection of Girolamo Rilli. Among the pieces, a Roman tile with a ship engraved in the fresh clay. Times indicated: Tuesday to Saturday 8:30-19:45, Sunday 14-19:45, Monday closed.
Four centuries of life of a villa on the lake, to Enrico Fermi.
The house built in the nineteenth century by the brothers Fausto and Giuseppe Bagatti Valsecchi on the model of the sixteenth-century residences, part of the Case Museo circuit in Milan.

Trapanese Municipality that reaches the sea with the salt pans of Trapani and Paceco, nature reserve managed by the WWF between tanks and windmills; in the hamlet of Nubia, known for its red garlic, the Salt Museum in a seventeenth-century beam, while in the village the Tower of Ligny houses the Prehistoric Museum.

Inaugurated in 1999 by Antonio Marra, it tells the peasant and artisan civilization between the late nineteenth and the sixties of the twentieth century: it rises on the daily life marked by the seasons, religious festivals and work in the fields, with attention to the patriarchal family and the agricultural economy of the Plain. Telephone 0828 982073.
Medieval village surrounded by walls built by Aldobrandeschi, with Piazza del Castello and a fairytale atmosphere: among the most beautiful villages in Italy.
At the highest point of the historic centre, it is the symbol of the ceramics of the Vietrese: the seventeenth-century church has the dome covered with blue and yellow majolica.
In a historic building restored in 2006, it tells the oldest history of Val Vigezzo and Val Grande with local finds, in particular from the Roman and late ancient necropolis of Craveggia.

Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 5 of the 8 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.

Housed in the rooms of Palazzo Casapesenna, it collects archaeological finds recovered in the territory of Tortora, which has returned traces of Enotri, Greci, Lucani, Romani and Longobardi and where many scholars place the ancient Blanda, taken from the consul Quinto Fabio Massimo in 214 BC and then became Blanda Julia. Booking not required; MiC (2020) does not report up-to-date times.
Romanesque on the way of pilgrims.

Ring of 21,34 km, mostly on dirt road, of medium difficulty (about 8 hours, difference in altitude 254 m, between 860 and 1,114 m), which leaves and returns to the Tower of San Michele behind the Certosa. The first stretch, about 5 km to the sanctuary of Santa Maria del Bosco, crosses abetina and beech woods Archiforo, with traces of irons, stonemasons and carbonai.

Ring of about 2 hours (difficulty E) above the localities Gianavella and Tribulèt, where Joshua Gianavello, the "Lion of Rorà," and his had hiding places during the Waldensian resistance of 1655.

The village is dominated by a medieval tower and preserves remains of the castle; in the church of the Madonna Liberatrice a table of Perugino school. In the hamlets (Rotecastello, San Vito in Monte, Pornello, Ripalvella, Poggio Aquilone, Civitella dei Conti, Collelungo) there are medieval towers and castles.

Museum opened in 1966 on Roman structures, with the "Hero" of Cassino and a sword enrolled among the oldest attestations of the name "Roma" (Rome), the area preserves the urban stretch of the Via Latina with Porta Campana, the amphitheatre attributed to Umida Quadratilla, the mausoleum and the theatre.
Artisans at work in the old shops.

Bay on the Gulf of Angels closed by cliffs with eucalyptus and pine trees, rocks and rocks with stretches of amber sand and turquoise water, sheltered from the mistral and suitable for snorkeling and diving; on the western promontory the cylindrical granite tower built in the second half of the XVI century for the Spanish Crown. Parking space, also for campers, at the end of the road.

Borgo di viuzze, arches and glimpses, once fortified: you enter it from three doors, Sea, Low and Over. Churches and manor palaces overlook squares with characteristic names, such as the "giorgia" , an ancient market place, and the "miezzu a curta" , in the center of the old village.
The artificial channel was dug by Giulio Cesare da Varano to drain Lake Plestino on the plateau of Colfiorito; next runs a second channel with travertine walls.

Country of Chierese linked to clay, told by Munlab - Ecomuseo dell'Acilla with its quarry renaturalized, and to the car: since 1982 the Pininfarina Research and Studies Center has been located there, with the Pininfarina Collection.

Wet area of international importance of over 1600 hectares between Cagliari and Quartu, established in 1999 on the former salt pans: since 1993 they nidify the pink flamingos, to be observed on foot, by bike, boat or electric minibus.

In the historic center from 1100, restored between the late eighteenth and nineteenth centuries; in the apse an Annunciation of Buttaragi (1786), in the nave a fresco with the death of Celestino V, the wooden statue of the patron Saint Sebastian with the relics and the golden processional machine of the seventeenth century. For the feast of the patron they throw doughnuts from the bell tower.

Built in 1332-1334 and renovated around 1783, with the chapel of the Madonna del Soccorso, a source of the sixteenth century, a Saint Anthony Abbot of Francesco di Valdambrino, the frescoed crypt and the organ of 1742.
The cathedral where Piero worked in 1473-1474; the painter was buried in 1492 in a chapel of the cloister of the ancient abbey.

In Siolo, it hosts a permanent exhibition on peasant life and kilns, with numerous vintage instruments, and various events; access is linked to the initiatives of the association A.Mu.Si (Friends of the Museum of Siolo).

The ancient area that unites the basilica of Sant'Antonio, the oratory of San Giorgio, Prato della Valle, Santa Giustina and the Botanical Garden, connected by Via Beato Luca Belludi.
Complex in the highest point of the city, residence of the dukes and then military use; from the square a ramp rises to the courtyard passing under the Tower of Bramante.
The medieval castle overlooking Lake Maggiore, with frescoes and views from the tower.

Arbëreshë community born from Albanian refugees who arrived between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, which preserves its language and traditions: the Museum of Costume and Arbëresh Ori in the eighteenth century Cumane Palace and the historic center with the two churches of Santa Maria di Costantinopoli, of Greek and Latin rite.
The symbol of the twinning with Greece.

Volcanic hill of about 600 meters detached from the Jar for erosion: on top the remains of a Punic fortress of the fourth century BC with six towers and a building that tradition considers a temple of Juno, from which would derive the name of the village. There is also a 39-metre deep nuragic sacred well, indicated as the deepest in Sardinia and then re-used in the Christian age, where a rare Roman-era winch was found; next to the remains of the Romanesque church of St. Helena and St. Constantine the Great, celebrated in early August with a procession of one hundred knights.

Born at the end of the seventies in the former primary school of San Martino and renovated in 2018 by the City with volunteers, it has four sections: historical-alpinistica (from the thermal waters of the Renaissance to the Alpine Rescue), naturalistica with diorama, mineralogical and an ethnographic section with the interior of a peasant house of the early twentieth century and agricultural tools and craftsmen. Open in summer and on the main holidays.
Quiet streets with handicraft workshops and galleries made in ancient caves where you buy ceramics; the viewpoint of the Monument to the Bread offers a view that is worth the detour.

Late medieval village of houses leaning one to the other along the hill, with alleys and stairs partly carved into the rock and the Pollino in the background; in 1930 the Dutch engraver M. C. Escher pictured the view. Among the noble palaces the seventeenth-century Palazzo Rocco, Palazzo Cozza with the angular portico, the Palazzo dei Cavalieri Marzano with red facades in the district of Judea, Palazzo Lauria with the Baroque portal and Palazzo Coscia (1793). From Porta Ferrante the view extends over the Pollino and the Maddalena.

Natural park wanted by Pope Gregory XVI around 1834, with natural and artificial waterfalls, caves, terraces and archaeological remains; it is managed by FAI and is visited from March to December in about an hour and a half.

Città d'origine della famiglia di Felice Peretti, pope Sixto V since 1585, 512 meters between the valleys of Aso and Tesino: Piazza Sisto V with the cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, Palazzo Paradisi with the reliquary donated by the pope in 1587, the civic museums in the Town Hall and, in Valdaso, the fortified mill of 1320. Historical center, monuments and museums are partially usable.

In the cathedral of San Clemente, established in 1927: fragments of Exultet of the twelfth century, the Madonna with Child and angels of Gentile da Fabriano (1426-1427), the Madonna in throne signed by Antoniazzo Romano in 1486, the Madonna of the Rosary of Sebastiano Conca and the Velitern Cross, gold reliquary and precious stones of the eleventh-XII century. Closed on Monday; Tuesday-Sunday 9-13 and 15-19.

La Rocca Buitoni is a noble residence of the fourteenth century; Palazzo Cennini was renovated in 1622 by Cardinal Cennini as a summer residence.

Begin around 1143, when the Benedictine monastery founded in the eighth century by the Bavarian duke Tassilo III became a college of canons; it reached almost the present form around 1280, the bell tower was erected between 1320 and 1326 and in 1969 the church was restored to the form of 1250. Three naves with transept and dome at the crossroads, it preserves the fresco of the dome with Creation, the Crucifixion group of about 1250, the crypt and, on the southern portal, a fresco by Michael Pacher of about 1450.
The sunset with views of the Archipelago.
Where gladiators were trained.

Agricultural tools, furnishings and utensils of a 19th century peasant house, linens, alarm clocks collections, purses, mantillas and Borsalino hats, works by local artists, a rebuilt school classroom and documents on emigration and the Great War. Curated by the association Ursaria Amici of the Museum.
A Flemish masterpiece on the Madonie.

In the square stands the bell tower with clock of 1697. Nearby is the House of the Boy, a memory of the criminal jurisdiction, also capital, which the Centurions, princes of the Holy Roman Empire since 1654, exercised over the subjects of Morsasco.
Close-up alpine ungulates, ideal with children.
The residence of the Marquisa Vincenza Roberti, who hosted the Roman poet Giuseppe Gioachino Belli, has a brick facade with embellished mirrors.
Rafting in the gorges of Pollino.

The highest point of Cagliari: 37 meters tower on a terrace 130 meters above sea, built by the Pisans at the beginning of the 14th century and used in the 19th century by Alberto Della Marmora to draw the map of Sardinia.
Founded in 1908, according to the regional catalogue, the largest collection of ceramics in the world: from the Faenza majolica to the works of Picasso, Matisse, Fontana and Burri.
Romanesque parish church in the hamlet of Cisano, well visible from the Gardesana road. It is one of the historical sites included in the virtual tour of the municipality.
The history of radio in original objects.
The Baroque pictorial cycles of the Vallo di Diano.

In the MULA+ pole, over 780 pieces of agricultural tools and artisan crafts tools, with panels on the cycles of wheat and grapes; in the same complex the Museum of Thermalism, set up in the old spa of 1928.
Medieval village of the Val di Cecina, a town of wine and bread, with views from the walls of the Tyrrhenian Sea and the islands.
The civic heart of the village on Topino.
The plants and charcoal trees of the Serre.

The village is closed by a defensive belt of about 650 meters with round and square towers: of the original 25 remain 15, testimony of the ancient Castellum Pastina. You enter from Porta Roma and Porta Napoli; the main square, Piazza del Maggio, is in the highest part of the village and there is the birthplace of Nino Manfredi, which houses photographic exhibitions and a school of theatre. Narrow paved streets, stone houses with wrought iron balconies; the paved road is irregular.

An interactive museum between stars, minerals and fauna of the Piave.

It rose in the middle of the fifteenth century, rebuilt in Baroque forms after the earthquake of the eighteenth century: three-order façade of binated columns and, in the central nave, the golden coffered ceiling of Ferdinando Moscow (1730).
An early medieval church on the ridge of the Asolani Hills.
Founded in 1572, with the oldest part designed by Filippo Juvarra, it houses the Agnesian and Diocesan Library.

An ancient church of the 13th century on the hill, restored thanks to the Committees of Santa Corona; from the effigy of the saint in Piazzale 1° Maggio starts the path-pilgrimage among the chestnut trees to the church. The patron saint's feast is celebrated on May 14.
The memorabilia of movies scattered throughout the country.

It tells the Sinis from the Neolithic to the Roman age: the Neolithic village of Cuccuru is Arrius, the Nuragic finds, Tharros and the lead bars of the Roman wreck of Mal di Ventre. From April 2026 he exhibited the entire statuary complex of Mont'e Prama, nuragic sculptures of 900-700 BC. (Paintings, archers, warriors and models of nuraghe) discovered in 1974, among the oldest stone statues in the Mediterranean.
In 1762, with a trompe-l'œil painted façade in 1857 by the painter Grange, a medieval crypt and a rare bell of the fourteenth century.

Medieval village on the Verona shore of Garda dominated by the Scaligero Castle, National Monument from 1902 and Goethe stage in the ...Travel to Italy. From the village the cable car with rotating cabins rises to Monte Baldo, while to the south, in Cassone, flows the Aril, just 175 meters long.
Plain forest of about 30 hectares.

Village between three rocks (the Castle, the Piesco and the Madonna della Rocca) on the river Melandro, birthplace of the painter Giovanni de Gregorio called the Pietrafesa, with over 500 murals in the historic center and two museums in the Loreti Palace.
The fortress where the author of the Orlando in love was born.

Country of the Peligna Valley built on the ancient Corfinium, capital of the Italian peoples rebels in Rome during the social war, which coined coins with the name "Italy." The Basilica Valvense di San Pelino, one of the most important medieval monuments in Abruzzo, the tower mausoleums known as Morroni along the Tiburtina Valeria and the Archaeological Museum "Antonio De Nino" are worth seeing.
Storks in the plain.

Small centre on a relief from which you can enjoy a wide panorama, which preserves the memory of fortified citadel; called "Borgo degli Immortali" (Borgo degli Immortali), it is part of the international network of the "Blue Zone" of longevity. Among the alleys there is the Largo Greco feritoia, the church of the Collegio di Maria (1738) in Piazza del Popolo and the churches of San Giuliano, San Francesco and San Rocco.

Loreto was rebuilt in a lower position and hidden after the Asti people destroyed the castle in 1255, so much so that today it is not seen from the nearby villages; the parish church of Our Lady of Loreto has an altar attributed to Juvarra. In Burio a castle-fortress remained faithful to the original architectures.
Designed by Adalberto Libera, started in 1956 and consecrated in 1975: a white circular plant, inside twelve columns, one per apostle, and an eighteenth-century wooden crucifix.

Under the village of Poiano flowing salt and sulphurous springs, outlet of an underground canal, with a flow rate of 300-600 liters per second: the water of the river Lucola infiltrates underground and melts chalks and salt.

The historical centre develops with a concentric scheme on the top of the hill around the baronial palace, built in the 11th century when the counts of Palombara held the lordship until the mid-Twentieth century. The church of San Biagio was built in the 11th century on the site of a small older church.
Half a century of contemporary art bell in a convent.

Opened on 15 August 2021 and dedicated to the history, nature and traditions of Villavallelonga, with furnishings in large part of recycled cardboard designed by the architect Rosa Ferrari. The rooms tell the life of the botanist Loreto Grande, recreate a forest in a sensory room and display the costumes of the ugly iconic masquerade of the feast of St. Anthony Abbot, naturalized animals including a large bear, grasses and pictures of the local flora. Summer hours indicated by the Municipality (2024): 10-12 and 16-18.

The nucleus of Mezzane was born around the chapel of Santa Maria de Mezanis, cited in a bull of Pope Urban III of 1186. The parish church dates back to the second half of the sixteenth century, with Baroque façade of 1730-1750 and bell tower of 1829; inside a altarpiece attributed to Andrea del Sarto, a Via Crucis and the bronzes of the ambone and the baptistery of the Brescia artist Oscar di Prata.
The writer's viewpoint.

Country of the Agno valley, 20 km from Vicenza, linked since the century after the thousand to the noble family Trissino: in the park of the castle there are the two surviving villas, including the Villa Trissino Da Porto Marzotto completed in the eighteenth century on a project by Francesco Antonio Muttoni. Also worth seeing is the parish church of Sant'Andrea, the conciliar church of St. Peter and the Tibaldo Museum of Communication.
Large marina with the remains of the eighteenth-century piers and the mighty stone bales in the middle.
Hiking in the woods among the fortifications of the Great War.

On the top of the Esquilino, one of the four papal basilicas, linked to the miracle of snow: the best preserved of the patriarchals, with the mosaics of the Childhood of Jesus of Sixtus III and the apse mosaic of Jacopo Torriti of the thirteenth century.

About a kilometer of white and fine sand, the second longest beach of Elba after Marina di Campo, preserves remains of dunes; it is very equipped, suitable for children and served by the MareBus. The nearby Laconella, less frequented, can be reached on foot with a short dirt road and is suitable for snorkeling.
The public garden created in 1816 and redesigned in 1830, at the intersection with via Zanchini, next to the Rationalist Agricultural Station.

The Regional Park of Alto Garda Bresciano surrounds the village and is a trekking destination: between the itineraries Mount Pizzocolo, Mount Castello di Gaino and the panoramic Sanctuary of Supina; the Way of St. Herculaneum touches all the churches and chapels of the territory.
The great Baroque parish of the village.
Handmade violins and mandolins.

The village of the small fruits is in a wooded and raised position with a view of the Saluzzo plain and the Monviso: in the historic center the Baroque Palazzo Filippa, Gauthier square with the birthplace of the painter Giovanni Borgna and the eighteenth-century parish church of Sant'Andrea; on the slopes, paths towards Pian Pramalano and the chapel of San Bernardo.

The village of Vallesina refounded after the destruction of the fifteenth century with two walls: in the Town Hall, formerly residence of the Counts Fossa Mancini, the civic museum is located; the church of San Sebastiano retains a bust attributed to Mattia della Robbia, and the Path of the Black Crab goes down to the hamlet Macine.

The village at the top of the hill, with one of the most beautiful views of the Roero on the valley of Tanaro, among uphill and local roads that promote wines in the area.

Oratory founded by the grandfather of St. Louis for the Confraternity of the Disciplines, established at the beginning of the sixteenth century; the portal of the Renaissance façade recalls the sermon on the Eucharist held by the Saint on March 3, 1590. Since 2006 it is the church of Santa Maria dei Disciplini della Pace.
Of medieval origin, according to tradition on the temple of the god Neptune (in the subsoil Roman finds have emerged), it was entirely rebuilt between 1738 and 1748 on a project by Carlo Marchionni.

Capital of the Bourbon kingdom and one of the great cities of Europe, with the historic UNESCO World Heritage center, the castles on the gulf, the world-class museums and a millennial subsoil.

The ancient principality (954-1729), Orange Flag, with the Palazzo dei Monaci headquarters of the Mint, the thirteenth-century oratory of San Bernardo and a room of ancient musical instruments.

The walls of the 14th century still contain the old town, where you enter only from Porta San Lorenzo, the only surviving of the three medieval gates, of the 13th century, facing east and incorporated in Palazzo Marinozzi. At the top, the Cassero Garden is the green area of the historic centre.

The village of Barbagia di Belvì at the foot of Mount Sant'Elia, known above all for Nuraghe Nolza, the largest of the Barbagia di Belvì, and for the sixteenth-century parish church of San Bartolomeo.

It rises from 1581 near the place where according to tradition the house of the Gangale family was located, where the future saint Domenico Gangale was born; the interior is frescoed with scenes of his life.

Rest of a fortified structure of six floors and more than 30 meters, reduced to about one sixth after the partial demolition around 1750: it is the only hexagonal tower of Lunigiana, with under the statue of Dante in marble by Arturo Dazzi (1965). The Via Dantis, completed in 2021, is an open-air journey of nine stages from the medieval aqueduct to the tower: totem shaped stele statues with bas-reliefs in Carrara marble by Giampietro Paolo Paita on the songs of the Comedy, with QR code actually increased.

Inaugurated in 2005 next to the Borgo di Pratica, on the ruins of Lavinium, a religious center of the Latins linked to Enea: five thematic rooms from the 10th century BC to the Roman age, with the large statue of Minerva Tritonia (5th century BC), the votive terracotta of the shrine of the goddess and, in the last room, the funeral set of the monument to Enea (sword, spears, sacrificial knife). Multimedia path with holograms and tactile path free of charge upon reservation.

A walk with a view of the islands, animated on weekends and summers by coffee shops, ice cream parlors and restaurants, with beach and port from which boats leave every day for the Isola Maggiore and the Isola Polvese.
An easy walk from an ancient village.

On the first floor of the Bishop's Seminary, a building dating back to the early 20th century, the four sections of the course range from minerals, fossils and Nuragic, Punic and Roman finds to the history of the diocese from the judicial period, to the sacred art of Ogliastra (silver, vestments, parish registers and rare books) and to documents on the arrival of the Salesians. Among the main pieces a parchment in Hebrew and Latin of the thirteenth century found in the binding of a sixteenth-century book, a Madonna of Monserrato in sandstone of the fourteenth century and a small bronze of Hellenistic Hercules.

City founded by the Selinuntini in the 6th century BC, then under Akragas, punic after 409-406 BC and re-colonized by Publius Rupilius in 132 BC; a walls of about 6 km encloses the plateau. The excavations, begun in the fifties, have exposed walls, necropolis, houses and the theatre of the fourth century BC in blocks of marna, facing the sea and protected by a temporary cover. The small Antiquarium at the entrance exhibits figurative ceramics, terracotta statuettes and accessories.

Pieve of the 13th century, rebuilt in the 1930s; preserves a polyptych of the Sienese school of the fourteenth century with the Madonna and Child enthroned among the Saints Bartholomew, Michael and John the Baptist.

The beach symbol of the Conero, reachable only from the sea.
Archaeological area of the Civic Museums with the remains of the Roman gate of the city.

The surviving mast of the Angevin fortress that resisted the sieges of 1361 and 1496 and was destroyed by the earthquake of 1694: originally square plan, four corner towers and moat; the tower recalls the Castel Nuovo of Naples.
The little pebble square in front of the Baroque church.
Symbol of Macomer on a basalt plateau on the slopes of Mount Manai: 15 meters high central tower, four tower bastion and a large village around.
Excursions on the extinct volcano of the obsidian.

A Romanesque church with three naves, with paintings and sculptures from the 16th and 17th centuries, including a Madonna del Rosario by Antonio Stabile, and an octagonal Norman tower older than the church; it houses the body of Saint Faustino, patron saint since the 18th century.
The largest view of the city.
In the palace of the Podestà, the sculpture of the Renaissance: the Davids of Donatello and Verrocchio, Michelangelo, Cellini, Giambologna.

Cittadina della Piana di Gioia Tauro rebuilt after the earthquake of 1783, with the Matrix Church of San Girolamo, the Baroque sanctuary of the Rosario, eighteenth-nineteenth-century palaces and the Town Villa  . Carlo Ruggiero , national monument with botanical garden.

On the hill, probably Celtic fortification then Roman castrum guarding the streets of Ceresio, stands a small Marian church of Romanesque system rebuilt in the eighteenth century, with seventeenth-century decorations and a Madonna with Child traditionally fifteenth-century; higher up a stone with the statue of the Madonna. The Via Crucis of 14 chapels rises from the square, repainted by Franco Vasconi and restored in 1988-89; view of the village, Valceresio, Ceresio and Prealpi.
The fourteenth-century pedestrian bridge that starts from the tower of the Mastio di Castelvecchio, a superb example of 14th century engineering, blown up in 1945 and rebuilt after the war.

The most important monument of San Bonifacio, Romanesque, was rebuilt in 1138 by Abbot Uberto after the earthquake of 1117 and restored at the end of the fourteenth century and in the mid eighteenth century by the Olivetani. It has three aisles and three apses, facade in tuff and terracotta with baroque portal, frescoes of the Giotto school on the life of San Benedetto, a fresco of the fourteenth century of Santa Caterina, a choir in walnut of the fifteenth century, a crypt with 24 columns as wide as the church, Roman finds in the floor and a bell tower-fortility of 1131 with Gothic triples; the cloister preserves Gothic arches of the first fifteenth century. Opening hours: Monday-Saturday 9.30-11.30, Sunday 15-17 (September-March) and 15-18 (April-August).
The red onion countryside with views of the Prealps.
A sanctuary born of a stone.
The heart of city life.
Prehistoric tombs still marked by the red ochre.

Sulfurean waters, salso-bromo-iodiche from the Bojola hot spring, already known in Roman times. The main facilities are the Terme Virgilio (Columbare) and Catullo (historic centre), with inhalations, mud, baths and massages; the Aquaria center has about 3,500 m2 covered and 6,500 m2 of park, with indoor and outdoor pools overlooking the lake open all year round, even in the evening. Booking recommended.
A rare two-arch bridge over Scoltenna.

About 2.5 km from the village, in a wood of holm oaks, six domus de Janas (locally honcheddas) excavated at different levels in granite, between the final Neolithic and the beginning of the Eneolithic (3200-2800 BC). The tomb III, the most characteristic, preserves traces of red plaster, engravings, a cup and a taurine protome in relief on a pillar: one of the very few domus decorated with symbolic motifs of the province of Nuoro. In 2025 it was registered by UNESCO in the World Heritage Site together with 16 other prehistoric Sardinian necropolises.
The town hall, the municipal library and the Antonio Cordici Museum are located on the square.

Set up in the Kursaal Room, built in 1952 and found among the most popular on the Adriatic Riviera in the 1960s: sketches, movie posters, cartoons and satirical drawings of Italian artists, many arrived from the Festival Umorismo nell'Arte, with works by Dario Fo, Milo Manara and Sergio Staino and a room dedicated to Angelo Maria Ricci. Times at 0735 739240.
The lake that turns red in summer.

The center of Costa Viola, under Mount Sant'Elia: the beach of Tonnara with the Scoglio dell'Ulivo, the archaeological park of the Taurians and the museums of the House of Culture Leonida Repaci; at the end of August the Varia, an immaterial UNESCO heritage.
Medieval urbanism and mule trackers.

In a former monastery of the 12th century next to Santa Maria della Verità, inaugurated in 1912: three floors from the Etruscan period to the 19th century, with Etruscan finds, memories of the city and nineteenth-century projects of the Santa Rosa Machine.

Renovated in 1743 by Francesco Maria Ciaraffoni, deconsecrated in 1860, it has the dome frescoed by Francesco Mancini and today houses the Teatro Studio Valeria Moriconi.

The gold of the Cervarese tradition and the goldsmith's shop.
The border tower between two regions.
Church in stone of the sixteenth century with Romanesque-Gothic elements, in panoramic position in the woods above the hamlet of Cravegna.
Works of the painter Pietro Rosa with views of the port of La Spezia and Porto Venere and a self-portrait in the corner tower, in addition to the fragment of a stele statue found at Borseda.
The natural sauna in the cave.

On the hills of Cofino the remains of a Greek temple between the end of the sixth and the beginning of the fourth century B.C., of about 27.50 for 18.10 meters, with colonnade, cell and opistodomum; it is part of the urban archaeological park.
The tower of Carlo V on the sea of Pineto.
A thousand years of self-government in the valley, between paintings and prisons.
About 750 minerals and 170 fossils, with crystals and stones from the Aosta Valley and the world.

Paraments, sculptures, paintings, Neapolitan silvers of the eighteenth century, manuscripts and an archaeological section from the ninth century BC to the fourth AD; the main work is the marble bust of Giuliano l'Apostata, once on the facade of the cathedral.

A small town in eastern Biellese with the village Bonda transformed from the eighties into an open-air gallery of contemporary frescoes and sculptures, and the Museum of the workshop of the Mortigliengo in Mino, dedicated to the traditional crafts of the area.
It dates back to the year 1000 and was renewed in the late eighteenth century; it preserves the Martyrdom of San Lorenzo by Domenico Fiorentino.
Citation already in the Statuti del Duecento, it assumed the current aspect in 1605-1606: four statues of the seasons and twelve mouths for the months of the year.

The ancient market square with the Town Hall of Vittone with wavy lines, the church of Sant'Andrea designed by Gian Lorenzo Bernini, Palazzo Mathis with frescoed rooms, Palazzo Valfrè and Palazzo Garrone.
An almost uninhabited island with the basilica of Santa Maria Assunta and its bell tower, from whose top you can see Burano, and the Devil's Bridge without parapets.

Founded by the Longobards and renovated several times from the Norman age to the eighteenth century: in the courtyard arches with acute sixth, in the loggia of the first floor mythological scenes of the seventeenth century and a fresco of 1710 by Tommaso Giaquinto,  ...Diana and Atteone.
Villa in a large park, owned by Collegio Alberoni, used for events.

It rises on the top of the hill, surrounded by the houses of the village; probably of the thirteenth century, it has been renovated several times and in 1944 it was subjected to the bond of the Fine Arts. Families linked to its walls include the Roots, the Avogadro, the Miroglio, the Frejlino and Scotland. It has lost its imposing circular tower and today has an eighteenth-century façade that hides the medieval structure.
An intact 19th century Romagna interior.
An entire village under a rock, witness to the civilization of the chestnut tree.

Built in the middle of the seventeenth century and enlarged at the end of the eighteenth century and in the first half of the nineteenth century, it has a T-plant with three naves; it preserves a Byzantine fresco of the year Mille and a large fresco with the Virgin with the Child, a kneeling bishop and the archangel Michele who pierces Satan.
The heart of the city of the Pico.
The best preserved Scaliger castle, overlooking the plain.
The view of the Temo and the colored rooftops.

Chapel founded in the Lombard age and named after the Brescia monastery of San Salvatore-Santa Giulia, transformed around the XI-XII century into a single nave church; the mural paintings, attributed to the fourteenth century, remain only in fragments.

Founded in 1872, it combines the Baron's museum house overlooking Piazza Venezia, with antique furnishings and neoclassical sculptures also of Canova, with the modern art gallery arranged by Carlo Scarpa in the sixties.

The church of the patron saint, of Greek imprint, preserves altars and Renaissance and Baroque paintings, including a Madonna of Mercy with an unprecedented Madonna pregnant. Along the coast of Arbus follow the beach of Scivu, with about three kilometers of dunes, Marina di Arbus, about two kilometers long, Portu Maga and Funtanazza, up to Capo Pecora, a diving destination at the southern end.

Valico at 2,652 meters of the Southern Rhaetian Alps in the Stelvio National Park, reached by the panoramic state road 300 and very frequented by cyclists and motorcyclists. Dominated by Mount Gavia, with the White Lake and the Trenches of the Great War; excursions to Punta Gaviola (3,050 m, about 1 hour and 30 by military road) and, for experts, to the Horn of the Three Lords (3,360 m, 3 hours and 30).
The heart of devotion to the saint of Miscano.

Fortress founded by the Republic of Venice in the fifteenth century on the right bank of the Isonzo against Turkish incursions, then capital of a Habsburg county: Venetian walls with towers and gates, Loggia dei Mercanti, Palazzo Torriani with the Spazzapan Gallery, historical squares and cafes.

The eighteenth-century church with a single nave: it houses the Presentation at the Temple of Domenico Bocciardo (1720), the Baptism of Jesus by Anton Maria Maragliano, the Transit of Saint Joseph of the Genoese school of the eighteenth century, two paintings by Francesco Baracca in the presbytery, the Sacred Heart by Luigi Venzano and a canvas by Giannetto Fieschi from 1965 in the choir.

In the historic centre, Palazzo De Sanctis, with its typical stone portal, is the house where Francesco De Sanctis was born on 28 March 1817, a critic and historian of literature. A Museum of Memories was also set up in the context of the Literary Park "Francesco De Sanctis" (1999-2001) with a small collection of its memorabilia.

In a convent of the seventeenth century, the collection donated by Amedeo Lia: liturgical objects, medieval miniatures, archaeological finds and paintings from the fourteenth to the eighteenth century, including the Portrait of Pontormo and the Portrait of a gentleman of Tiziano.
One of the oldest salt mines in Europe.
The alpine lake from which starts the excursion to the lakes of the Autaret Hill, on the Italian-French border.
Sanctuary in the ancient village of the city.

Two churches almost entirely excavated in the Monterrone spur, in the center of the Sasso Caveoso: Santa Maria de Idris has been mentioned since the 14th century, San Giovanni in Monterrone preserves a cycle of frescoes.
18th century parish church dedicated to the saints Faustino and Giovita; it houses the canvas of Saint Lucia del Genovesino (Luigi Miradori), painter of the seventeenth century.

Castle of thirteenth century origin on the border with Giano dell'Umbria; during the Christmas period it houses a living nativity scene with dozens of people, shops and taverns, with the Sacred representation of the Nativity at sunset. There is the church of the Madonna del Ponte.
The medieval village is described as one of the best preserved in the province of Rome; in the square near the Duomo the Belvedere Fountain, where women drew water with traditional jugs.

Patron villa of a vast agricultural sidedone of the first century A.D., referred to as the largest suburban villa in northwestern Italy. The ground floor, part of the monumental entrance, the central courtyard and the large terrace facing south towards the valley, are preserved. Free guided tours with the association Ar.c.A., access on the floor.

Roman billionaire with the names of Emperor M. Opelius Severus Macrinus and his son Diadumeniano, found in Castelbadia (Sonnenburg) in 1857 and today at the entrance of the Museum Mansio Sebatum.

Fraction on a hill near the Salinello valley, 184 meters above sea level and about 10 km from the sea, an autonomous municipality until the French decade (1806-1815); in 1612 Muzio de' Muzij listed it among the castles surrounded by walls. There are still sections of the belt with sharp arches and the ancient entrance door, the Palazzo Striglioni, built between the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries with rooms, gate and railings in Art Nouveau style, and twentieth-century religious newsstands; in the church, recovered since 1996 with interior decorations by Renato Coccia, was restored a seventeenth-century statue of Saint Lucia in painted terracotta.

On the top of the hill that dominates the current town: remains of the ancient shelter, noble palaces of the nineteenth century, houses of the same era, the parish church and the castle. The old 18th-century municipal building, today in abandonment, is remarkable. Pro Loco organizes guided tours from May to September on Sunday from 15 to 18; in other periods by reservation (discover.mazze@prolocomazze.it).
A stage of the right path Po.
Valpiana is a pasture at 1,211 meters for excursions and picnics; with Malga del Doss is the site for which Astronomitaly gave Ossana the recognition of the most beautiful skies in Italy GOLD level.

Wanted in 1463 by Bianca Maria Visconti where in 1441 he married Francesco Sforza, decorated for half a century by the Cremonesi Mannerists, the Campi, Camillo Boccaccino and Bernardino Gatti; wooden choir and sixteenth-century organ case.
The papyri pond in the heart of the city.
The arch of Bari Vecchia tied to the legend of two young lovers hindered by her family: in one night they built an arc to pass from one window to another.
the interior is accessible only to authorized speleologists, the public sees it from outside

Built between 1474 and 1510, with three naves, with Baroque altar, Renaissance frescoes, an eighteenth-century painting of San Biagio and the relics of the patron San Feliciano; on the right of the southern portal a frescoed San Cristoforo, today under the road level for a flood. The 17th century bell tower in local stone.

Port of Rome founded by Traiano as Centumcellae, dominated by the sixteenth-century Fort Michelangelo; a stone's throw away is the National Archaeological Museum in customs of Clement XIII, the historic center around Leandra Square and, on the hills, the Roman Taurine Thermal Baths and the hot tubs of Ficoncella.
Tolfa and the Rock from a giant bench.

Open to visitors on the summer weekends, it preserves the works of art collected by Duke Roberto Ferretti, including pieces from Palazzo Ferretti in Ancona.

From Piazzetta San Michele a dirt track climbs in about twenty minutes to a cross overlooking the Bussento valley and Mount Gelbison, then to a large plateau where there was a Byzantine abbey and to the viewpoint from which, on clear days, you can see the Gulf of Policastro and the Calabrian coast. Two natural caves have been places of worship for centuries: the Cave of San Michele, home of the sanctuary, with concretions, masonry, bas-reliefs and a stone saintly waterworks, where ceramics from the Bronze Age were found, and the Cave of Sant'Angelo. At the beginning of the 11th century, the Longobard Prince Guaimaro III founded the Abbey of St. Angel, whose remains remain.
A museum to be touched, unique of its kind.
At the foot of the Sila Piccola plateau, the territory offers Reventino woods, mountain streams and trails along the watercourses.
Former Benedictine convent used as a theatre in 1686 and renovated in 2002, with three orders of stages and over 200 seats.
Sienese painting away from the Duomo crowd.

The hilly village of Monferrato Casale linked to the Counts Vidua: on the top of the historic center the eighteenth-century Villa Vidua, with the route dedicated to the ... traveler count Carlo Vidua; in the hamlet of San Maurizio the fifteenth-century church founded by Teodoro II of Monferrato, where Empress Sofia is buried.
The judgment on the facade.

Among the largest pre-Roman necropolis in Umbria, in the Tiber River Park between Montecchio and Baschi: chamber tombs excavated in the local limestone ('Matile'), with dromos and side docks, used from the VII to the IV century BC and discovered in 1855 by Domenico Golini. They were sacked in ancient times, they returned weapons and pottery from banquets in the male, jewelry and ointment tombs in the female ones; they showed strong ties with the Etruscan Orvieto.
The oldest stones in the village.
The oldest glass in the West and masterpieces from Tintoretto to Brustolon.
The republic born of a border error.
Between the lakes of Monticolo and Lake Caldaro, paths in the woods covered with moss suitable for families; the best moment is March, when the underwood is covered with snow holes and crocuses.
Built around 1225 under Frederick II of Swabia, it preserves three of the four corner towers and is among the best preserved in Sicily despite the earthquakes of 1693, 1783, 1794 and 1968.

About a kilometer of white sand, fine and soft, with low seabed bordered by rocks, suitable for snorkeling; the bay is dominated by the nuraghe Aleri. Rentals, camping, bar and ample parking also for campers; according to the source is never crowded.

Municipality between hill and Gulf of Squillace: in Roccelletta, in an olive grove, the Museum and National Archaeological Park of Scolacium with the remains of the Roman colony and the Norman basilica of Santa Maria della Roccella; at the top the historical center rebuilt after the earthquake of the eighteenth century.
WWF oasis of 800 hectares with picnic areas and paths, among white firs, beech trees, maples, badgers and lindens; deer, roe deer and wolves, symbol of the reserve can be seen.

Cittadina della Riviera dei Fiori between Bordighera and Camporosso, with about a kilometer of beaches, the sixteenth-century torrione against pirates, the small church of San Rocco on the remains of a Roman temple, the ancient village of Vallecrosia Alta and the Song Museum set up on a steam train.

The village of the stonemasons is located on the hills of Metauro, where the sandstone has been working since the fourteenth century: the center is an open-air museum of portals, niches and carved frames, with the Museum of the territory, the Montefeltresca fortress and, in the surroundings, the walled castles of Sorbolongo and Reforzate.

World-class exhibitions, open until 11pm on Thursday.
Grassi's paintings in a fraternity church.

Small village of Barigadu on a hill at 260 m overlooking Lake Omodeo, with a historic center of houses in red trachite: the Temple of Jupiter on the hill of S'Onnarìu, the Romanesque church of St. Peter, the country shrine of Santa Maria di Ossolo and the house-museum Sa 'Omo' and sa majarza on the witchcraft in Sardinia.
The circle of hamlets between Gothic and Baroque.

The village rises on a cone hill, with paved streets and stone houses; the walls of Castrum with Porta Romana, the main entrance to Rome, and Porta Napoletana or Portella, emergency exit to Naples. At the end of August the Castri Fumonis Ludi evoke the attempted siege of Henry VI of 1186.

At 1550 meters, about 10 minutes from the village of Resia, there is the Adige, the main river of South Tyrol and the second of Italy for length (415 km); here passes the watershed between the Adriatic and the Inn basin and the Danube, towards which flows the nearby Stillebach.

Necropolis discovered in 1983 by extending the municipal road of Ripe, with burials from the Bronze Age (1350-1200 BC) to the Iron Age (about 625-475 BC); in the urn museum and urns in bronze and bone. Archaeological area open in spring and summer, museum by reservation.
The battlefield of Hannibal.

Along the streets of the medieval village there are tower houses and the ancient Loggia dei Mercanti; near Porta Maggiore stands the palace of Gioacchino Pecci, home of the future Pope Leo XIII and today seat of the Town Hall.
