The village, built on five hills with a plant that appears to be a star from a distance, grew around the Ricetto, fortified nucleus of the twelfth century; it preserves tower houses, the Governor's Palace of 1559 and the "sports," arc passages dug under the roads on which the houses rest.

Hesagonal square in the center of the fortress, arms square with the main palaces and the eleven statues of the general providers; it houses the permanent exhibition with the machines to build the fortress in real scale.
In three of the five Community ovens still in use.
The fountain of alley Pula in an exedra of stone of Istria with lion mask and the inscription "Aere civico," and the octagonal one of Piazza Pula of 1903.
The life of transhumance pastors, room by room.

Centro del Logudoro which gave its name to the 'culture of Ozieri' of the final Neolithic: the Cave of San Michele in the village, the Romanesque Basilica of Sant'Antioco di Bisarcio on the plain of Chilivani and a historic center of terraced squares.
Fishermen's village at the foot of the city, reachable from the center through a passage carved into the rock in the third century BC: boats, a small sandy beach and fish restaurants.
Cagliari's roof.
The bell tower with the Gothic mullioned windows.

It takes its name from two large boulders decorated with figures, fallen at the beginning of the Holocaust: from the age of Copper around them grew a megalithic sanctuary. The park occupies about one hectare and is visited in about an hour. Free admission, closed on Mondays.

The oldest church of Sirmione, of Lombard origin (VIII century), on the hill of Mavino among the olive trees; the Romanesque bell tower was renovated in 1070 and the building rebuilt in 1320. Inside the 14th century frescoes and a fourteenth-century altarpiece with the Madonna enthroned with the Child and a saint.

It preserves a fresco of the late fifteenth century with the crucified Christ that comes out of the tomb; after a miraculous event in 1809 the church was rebuilt in neoclassical forms according to the design of G. Lucatelli is declared shrine by the viceroy of Italy Eugenio Beauharnais.
The walk on the walls.

X-XI century tower facing the Orco Valley, part of a Castrum dei San Martino that from the hill to the entrance of the valley controlled the shelter below; rivals Valperga owned instead the Ferranda tower. It was sacked in 1383 during Tuchinaggio, was destroyed in 1552 by the troops of Caesar Maggi in the Spanish money and since then it is a ruin, visible only from the outside.

Romanesque church of the 11th century with two Byzantine domes of different sizes, born from a monastery perhaps of the 8th century, Benedictine complex before 1125 and entrusted in the 13th century to the Knights of Calatrava (1228-1294).

It rises on the Colle Foro, inside the ancient Trebula, where the young Victoria was martyred in the middle of the III century; documented by 817 as the possession of Farfa, it was rebuilt between the XI and XII century and restored by the Orsini in the fifteenth century. Three aisles, bell tower with double windows, marble façade and spolia, a devotional well in the central nave and a ciborium on marble columns; from the right nave you descend to the catacombs with graves dug in the rock, a strigatory sarcophagus and a frescoed archesolio with the martyr.

Piazza Dallo is the heart of the city and in ancient times it had castrum function; in the center there are patrician palaces built between the fifteenth and nineteenth century, including Palazzo Pastore with its park.

The Fortino was built in 1778 by Grand Duke Pietro Leopoldo of Lorraine, following the model of the forts of Marina di Bibbona and Marina di Castagneto, to protect the boarding of the Apuan marble and favor the settlement: around it the town passed from a marble store to a seaside resort. Today it houses the Museum of satire and caricature, a center of conservation and research with original drawings by historical and contemporary authors from all over the world, a library of over 2,500 volumes, video library, multimedia archive and temporary exhibitions.
Wanted by Pope Clement XII in the eighteenth century, designed by Luigi Vanvitelli and completed by Filippo Marchionni, is the gateway from the port to the city.
The origins of the Aquilan diocese.
Walk through ancient stones, narrow alleys and views to the sea.
The Bellunesi's living room.
A church over a Flaminia bridge.
On the ground floor of the archbishop's palace, it houses the Vercelli Book, from the late 10th century, written in ancient Anglo-Saxon prose.
Founded in 1838, the oldest civic institute in Milan, with dinosaurs, minerals and dioramas, in the Gardens of Porta Venezia next to the Planetarium.
Tiso's geodes and those who have been looking for them forever.
12th century church of which you can see the apses from the port.
The history of biomedical district.

Church with annexed convent, originally dedicated to the Sorrowful Virgin and passed in 1858 to the title of the Immaculate Virgin; from the decree of 8 December 1952 it houses the parish of St. Joseph, patron saint of the country. It has neoclassical façade and a single nave with stuccoes and altars, oil paintings of the Cross, of the Sorrows and of Capuchin saints and wooden statues including a San Luigi Gonzaga by Luigi Santifaller from Ortisei, a Christ in the column, a Sorrowful and a Crucifix. In the apse, renovated in 1977, a wooden statue of the Madonna; altar, ambo and baptismal font in marble are the Alberghina brothers of Caltagirone, the wooden tabernacle inlaid is nineteenth century.

An ancient residence in Via Vittorio Veneto with two stone windows: one shows a head with open scissors, perhaps symbol of wool carders, the other a knight who plays the trumpet, with a face in front and one in profile.
Just below the church of San Giorgio are traces of the walls of the ancient castle and a quadrangular tower of the fifteenth century, the last remnant of the ancient fortress.

Village of Porto Viro, a settlement of fishermen with low and colorful houses, a small church of the eighteenth century, a wooded area and an old glacier destination of walks. The port is a starting point for excursions in the lagoon, in the sea and on the river, and the lagoons around lend themselves to the observation of migratory birds.
The lost trades of the Orco and Soana valleys.

Castle of the 12th century strengthened by three circular towers; it houses the museum dedicated to work, crafts and sea life of the 19th century and the permanent exhibition on Ligurian woman 1850-1950.
The Abbey was founded in the 12th century and rebuilt in 1950; it houses an Antiquarium with augustian epigraphs, admired by Theodor Mommsen.
A Renaissance Crucifixion in a former Lazzaretto.
The lake with the submerged bell tower.
The Roman fish ponds dug into the sea.
The residence of the lords of the village.
The old town's cathedral.
One of the first examples of Lombard Romanesque, in a millennial complex.
A forest in the heart of the Tablemaker.
the Municipality indicates it as a former museum, under renovation to accommodate also the municipal library
The sea of Pisa.
Ancient historic coffee that preserves the original furnishings of the early twentieth century and a counter in Liberty style.
Monumental sport.

Dedicated to the nineteenth-century physician and botanist Francesco Minà Palumbo, who collected and classified plant species, reptiles and insects of the Madonie, whose collections the museum preserves.
Cumulation 4 museums €8, reduced €5 (with guided tour)

The largest of the Tuscan villas, about 80,000 square meters, built since 1567 for Cardinal Marco Sittico Altemps: here in 1582 Pope Gregory XIII promulgated the bull "Inter Gravissimas" that introduced the Gregorian calendar. Italian Garden, the Dragon Fountain on the Terrace and tree-lined avenues; since 1981 it has been University of Rome Tor Vergata and is a congress centre.
A century of carpentry became industry.

Anguilla, fried or marinated milk cans, pasta with anguillara broccoli (PAT del Lazio, party at the end of March), sweet or salty fried pizzeria and the Cacio Fiore, pecorino cheese with wild artichoke rennet Slow Food; in mid-June the feast of fish.
Nature of river in the reserve Foce Sele-Tanagro.

Borgo dei Castelli Romani gathered around the seventeenth-century Duomo of the Borghese: the Tuscan villas, with Villa Mondragone where in 1582 the reform of the calendar was promulgated, the astronomical observatory with the laboratory Astrolab, the Borghese Barco with its Roman inscriptions and the wine museum in the old station.
Octagonal tower, unique in Valle d'Aosta, mentioned in 1197 and belonged to the lords of Quart.
A Tintoretto in town.
The sweet of the nuns of Sambuca.
Man Ray to Balla in a 16th century palace.

In the Palazzo Malatestiano, 16 rooms with archaeological sections, ceramics and numismatics, from prehistory to the Roman age, and the art gallery with paintings of the following eras. Closed on Monday.
The tools of traditional cooked wine.
Baroque parish built between 1699 and 1725 on Piazza Matteotti, with white marble altar and rare marble inserts.

The seat of the oldest confraternity of Levanto, next to the remains of the church of Our Lady of the Coast, houses a nineteenth-century organ by Giosuè Agati. At the end of July the Feast of St. James, or Feast of the Sea, brings historical processions, flag-wavers and fires.

Neoclassical, begun in 1845 and completed in 1862 without the two bell towers planned: inside the altar of the Madonna of Pompeii by Angeloronzo Rossi (1909), the Via Crucis in thirteen paintings and the apse fresco by Umberto Colonna, paintings by Mario Colonna and Margherita Deramo; in the bezel of the portal the Madonna of Carmine by Vincenzo Crispo (1954), bronze portals of 1983.

Small medieval village a few kilometers away, with a castle of 1277 with five watchtowers (three well preserved); the main tower became bell tower in 1823 and has a large clock and two bells. Alleys, underground tunnels, walls, arches and medieval frescoes.

About 1.5 km from the centre on the coast towards Leuca, the ruins of the 12th century Basilian cenobius, a great center of culture whose manuscripts are now in the main museums of the world, destroyed by the Turks in 1480.
Orange Flag City of Lake Maggiore, home of San Carlo Borromeo, with the Sancarlone Colossus, the Rocca and a center of churches and porticos in front of Angera.
Where Joy was born.
Mantegna's wounds.

Country of the hinterland of Catania founded in 1810, whose first inhabitants lived in the nearby Fondaco delle Canne along the regia trazzera to Palermo; to see the Museum of the Wheat in the headquarters of the cooperative "La Cerere" , the House of Tea, the only museum of tea in Italy, the Mother Church of 1850 and, in the country, the eighteenth-century Tower of Feudo.
Michelangelo's staircase is a sliding architecture.
The animals up close.
Francesco di Giorgio Martini and contemporary sculpture.

Sulcis center on the south-western coast, born at the end of the sixteenth century as a village of fishermen and coralmakers, in front of the island of San Pietro: the Spanish tower, the trap of Su Pranu still active between May and June, the church of Santa Maria d'Itria and the town beach of Portopaglietto.
The 11th century crypt.
The alabaster quarry thing.

private residence, only guided tours of 60 minutes: without reservation Saturday, Sunday and public holidays, in the weekdays only groups of at least 25 people with reservation 48 hours before; forbidden to photograph inside
A lonely beast on the way back from the throat.

Public park built on the eighteenth-century villa of Cardinal Fabrizio Paolucci, then of the Doria (the palace, bombed in 1944, was demolished in 1951); from Piazza Mazzini you can enjoy the view of the Roman countryside and the park. Underneath the park extends in part the about nine hectares of the villa of Pompeo Magno, built between 61 and 58 BC with the spoils of the mitridatic war and then passed to Augustus. In the summer it hosts the Albano Estate showcase and a bar with outdoor pool.

Parish church at the foot of the village, seventeenth century but of medieval origin: the act for its construction was written by the notary Joseph Cappa on March 28, 1600 and the relics under the altars were consecrated by Bishop Domenico Tagliatatela on October 16, 1736, as recalls a plaque in the right aisle. On the north wall the plaster hides a Roman tombstone and a tile with a stretched thumb; two sundials are on the side and on the back.
The artifacts of Abellinum in the heart of the square.
A thousand years of history in a building passed from castle to monastery.
Where stood the Roman Forum and, until the nineteenth century, the wheat market: Renaissance houses with wooden structure and the Romanesque basilica of San Fedele.
The beautiful Virgin of Camerino.
Sea in town.

One of the most important Etruscan necropolis in central Italy and the only one that shows the entire evolution of Etruscan funerary architecture: from wells and pits of the Iron Age to large orientalizing mounds, to archaic rock tombs with porch, newsstands and chamber, to the Hellenistic nut graves (VII century BC-III century A.D.). Among the most famous tombs are the Tomb of the Deer and the Tomb of the Queen; three entrances along the road of the Quercete (Ciusa-Cima, San Simone and San Giuliano, Caiolo) and numbered paths, reachable on foot from the village with path CAI 103.
The manor around which the village grew.
The most famous bay of the island, seen from the sea.

The company has created theater, castles and museums of all over the world. The visit, of about 2 hours, takes place in a museum-workshop where ancient machinery testify a centuries-old history; reservation through Tourism Turin (Made in Turin).

Straight strip of land along the eastern shore of the lake, about two kilometers long from Varenna to Fiumelatte, with over 900 specimens among rare species, exotic trees and thematic collections: palms, citrus fruits, English roses, rare glycines, oaks, hydrangeas, ferns. Among the ornaments the sculptural group of the Clemenza di Tito by Giovanni Battista Comolli (1830), the last unfinished work of the artist, and a large magnolia stretched over the water.

Designed by Abbot Antonio Marchetti and started in 1757, it is 55 meters high, with rustic base and bell cell with eleven bells; the four dials of the clock have the colors of the four squares of the city. The expected crowning was never realized. Visits only by appointment with the City's Culture Office; no elevator.
The church of Sant'Andrea Apostolo and the castle of Montalvo, Spanish family arrived at the Medici court with Eleonora of Toledo.
The theatre of the painter Fabrianese.
The fortified village with the Romanesque parish church of Saints Philip and James and, not far away, an Etruscan hypogeum of the 6th century BC with traces of a copper mine closed in 1941.
Two exhibition rooms with five pre-Alpine environments recreated in dioramas, eight thematic exhibitors and an environmental education classroom, with activities for children, students and tourists.

The main religious building of the city: it was born from the chapel dedicated to the Annunziata Virgin, for which Charles of Anjou granted land in the fourteenth century, around which the village developed. It preserves the fourteenth-century icon of the Madonna with the Child fished at sea by fishermen off the rock of Rovigliano; every 5 August it is remembered the finding with the "dispute among the fishermen" and 22 October is celebrated the votive feast of the patroness. Open every day 8-12 and 16:30-20.
Dolines and caves half an hour from the centre of Bologna.
A museum that really works, from October to December.
The garden of the simple of the Medical School.
In the Medici Palace, works from the 8th to the 18th century by churches and convents of the territory.
The castle on the gorge.

Medieval village of Oltrepò Pavese restored by private and municipality, with the Baroque parish of San Nicola, the palaces of the Belcredi marquises and the surviving tower of the castle destroyed in 1216; from the church square, the highest point of the village, the view reaches the Alps.
Recognize the places of his paintings.

The village of Monti della Tolfa was born from the quarries of alunite discovered around 1460 by Giovanni da Castro and closed in 1941: the Klitsche de la Grange Museum in the Palace of the Apostolic Chamber, the Way of Miners and the ghost village of Farnesiana, next to the Faggeto, one of the oldest woods of Lazio, and the Trajan Aqueduct of 107 AD.
Quality Vicenza baroque in a hill church.
Historical passage on the Adda, bridge with 11 arches of the 14th century and symbol of the city.
The noble palace returned to the city.
The tower that looked at the Roman bridge, in front of the Castle.

Rural area of the Judicaries above the Terme di Comano, Â small open-air museumÂ: the village of Rango, among the most beautiful villages in Italy since 2006, with the porticos of Christmas markets and the School Museum, the Renaissance parish church of Santa Croce, the 222 naïf murals of Balbido, a village of witches, and the Durone Pass between walnuts and woods.
The great Umbrian painting in one museum.

Borgo del Salento of long ceramic tradition, documented by the Municipal Museum of Ceramics; the historic center collects Palazzo Filomarini, the church of the Immaculate and the Matrice Church, while in a former clay quarry were born the Park of Fossil and the Malacological Museum of Clays.
Indicative morning and afternoon, with pause; limited visit during functions

The main town of the Cusio, lying on the northern shore of Lake Orta and crossed by the Nigoglia, which brings the waters of the lake northwards; home of Gianni Rodari (1920), with the Fantasy Park, the Forum dedicated to industrial history, the church of Sant'Ambrogio and the Roman Porta.
Small local museum with relics dating back to the early twentieth century.
Cumulation €7, reduced €5
Shadow of pine and spring water.

A 13th century monastic complex renovated in the Baroque age, about 800 m above sea level, a national monument from 1873 and dedicated to the Virgin Assumption, St. Bartholomew and St. Bruno. The single nave church has paintings by Filippo Balbi, the chorus of the chorus of the choristers of the late sixteenth century carved by Jacobò and on the vault the  "Gloria" of Blesseds and Saints of Caci (1683); on the square the Palazzo di Innocenzo III houses an important library. The visit is completed by the Italian gardens and the bell tower with three quadrants that mark only the minutes.
Remains of the castle beyond the chapel on the path to Chenal, with some rock carvings nearby.
The entrance door to the natural park.
In the former Municipal Market, it collects ancient objects and tools, some by now forgotten, which have allowed to make documentaries on the customs and traditions of the community.

The old town stands on the slope of a rocky hill; on the only side not protected by rocks runs a belt with thirty-six turrets, partly incorporated in the houses or covered by vegetation. Of the original five doors remain Codarda, Rendola and Scrima.
Like you used to live in medieval Florence.
Enclosed by medieval walls, with numerous towers and palaces such as the Palazzo dei Priori and the Palazzo Comunale with the Sala degli Frescoes.
A stop in the square.

In the Baronial Palace of Vaste, documents the Messapian city from the 4th century BC with sets of sarcophagus tombs (craters, bacils, strigili, the "trozzelle" of the female burials), a capital with funerary column rosettes, a treasure of 150 silver states and 17 lusorias in ivory of Roman age; chronological route from the places of archaic worship to the Middle Ages and virtual reconstruction on large screen.
Church of the seventeenth century in the north of the village, in front of which is the Sovereign Trullo.
Ferruginous water that descends from the 1800 meters of the Citrin valley and flows from the fountain in the town hall square.
The fortress of the Colonna, today home of the sciences of the village.

The complex opened on 23 September 2007 in a 13th century convent, with auditoriums in the former Franciscan church frescoed in the 15th century, archaeological museum, library, environmental education center and botanical garden. The museum tells the valley of Aso with a plastic of about 24 meters and preserves piceni finds, including a helmet with ram protomes and accessories of the necropolis of Contrada Crocifisso (IV century BC), as well as about 500 coins.

Built by the workers of the legion in the early third century, with an axis greater than 113 m and an estimated capacity between 15,000 and 16,000 spectators; in the Middle Ages it was used as a quarry and Christian cemetery. It is located behind the church of São Paulo.

Ghost village on Mount Antuni, reached crossing a small isthmus on the lake and then with a steep climb; the inhabitants left it after the dam of the 1930s, creating the lake, put an end to agriculture and breeding, and was restored in the nineties. Palazzo del Drago (XV-XVI century) rises there, with 365 windows, with hanging gardens overlooking Abruzzo, and a seven-circle maze built with only local materials, first sensory path in a protected area.
Two centuries of pharmacy.
Former church of St. Francis of 1229-34, with Baroque forms of the early seventeenth century.
A fresco attributed to Jerome of John.
The last active ravine on the island, among the very few in Europe.

Outside the village Santa Maria in Cerulis, from the 11th century, is the oldest church of Navelli; at the crossroads of two tractures rise the Renaissance Santa Maria delle Grazie, with Gothic elements in the rose window, and the rural church of the Madonna del Campo.

Park established in 1980 on the right side of the Val di Susa, between about 1,000 and 2,600 meters, to protect forests of white fir, larch and pine cembrian (70% forests, 30% pastures and high altitude prairies); there are recorded more than 600 plant species, about 70 of nesting birds and 21 of mammals, including deer, deer and chamois. From Sauze you go up to Gran Villard and Monfol to the parking lot and picnic area of Serre Blanche (about 1.700 m), or to Clotes and the road of Sportinia to Case Enfer, shortly after the border of the park.

In Fort Arbuticci, about 4 km from the White House, used until the Second World War and then by the Navy: since 2012 it is the first Italian museum entirely dedicated to a historical figure, with a multimedia path on the life and business of Garibaldi. Open Monday to Saturday 8.30-13.45 (last entry 13).

Parish already existed in the sixteenth century; during the Second World War the church was severely damaged and the parish registers were destroyed. It preserves a painting of the Madonna dell'Orto, very venerated, escaped from the fire of 1944.
A wild but comfortable bay to reach.

22 meters high statue, with 19 meters of opening of the arms, in white concrete and scales of Carrara marble, work of the Florentine sculptor Bruno Innocenti, installed in 1965 on commission of the industrial Rivetti; it is reached on a hairpin road and dominates the village from the rocky top of the mountain.
A walk on the embankment overlooking the Euganean and Berici Hills.
The castle on the sanctuary of Venus.
visit only with guided tours
Reachable by excursions, between May and June the wild peony blooms.
Historic and parish center severely damaged by the 2012 earthquake; the church was inaccessible according to the source
The 14th-century Malaspina castle that dominates the village, with the Marine Hall and the Celebration Hall.
A short ascent through the eighteenth-century stations.

Church of the 11th century, originally dedicated to the saints Biagio and Marina and from 1200 to the only Santa Marina; in 1049 Giovanni Shinto and his wife Alfarana donated it to the abbot of Montecassino. On July 17 a procession starts from the church of Sant'Antonino.
Near the archaeological park, it hosts many animal species; in the area nest the griffon.
Discover Cesena Card €13 (entrance to the Fortress)

UNESCO World Heritage with the Reggia: the silk colony wanted by Ferdinand IV since 1778, with manufactures, houses for workers, church and school; the Silk Museum exhibits fabrics and machines, and from the hill the viewpoint dominates all Caserta.

In Piazza Castello, from Roman gate to medieval fortress and castle of the Acajas, then the first Senate of Italy; over seventy thousand works, from the Portrait of Man by Antonello da Messina to the Très belles Heures by Jean de Berry, and the staircase of Juvarra.
Franciscan citadel built since 1310, with the cloister covered with 18th century majolica.

The oldest royal residence in Europe, a 9th century Arab fortress enlarged by the Normans, seat of the kings of Sicily and today of the Regional Assembly: Room of Ruggero with hunting mosaics, Room of Hercules, Pompeiana Room and Chinese Room.
Church with red domes of the Arab-Norman UNESCO itinerary.
